622380716.en: I feel like the warning should either not apply to cases like this, where a shared ref derived from a static mut is immediately dereferenced, or it should also apply to the original `A[i]` operation. The current behavior feels inconsistent to me
622380716.zh: 我觉得警告不应该适用于这样的情况，从静态mut派生的共享ref立即被取消引用，或者它也应该适用于原始的`A[i]`操作。当前行为对我来说感觉不一致

622382170.en: note the `A[i]` operation is a compiler built-in (only when `i: usize`) -- it doesn't actually call any library code, unlike the `get_unchecked` function call
622382170.zh: 请注意`A[i]`操作是内置的编译器（仅当`i: usize`）——它实际上并不调用任何库代码，与`get_unchecked`函数调用

622382223.en: (ignoring panicking on out-of-bounds accesses, which don't access `A`)
622382223.zh: （忽略越界访问的恐慌，这不会访问`A`）

622382375.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/False.20positive.20.60deny.28static_mut_refs.29.60/near/622382170):
```quote
note the `A[i]` operation is a compiler built-in (only when `i: usize`) -- it doesn't actually call any library code, unlike the `get_unchecked` function call
```

Does that matter for reference liveness? I would assume it behaves exactly like a library call for e.g. stacked borrows.
622382375.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/False.20positive.20.60deny.28static_mut_refs.29.60/near/622382170):
```quote
note the `A[i]` operation is a compiler built-in (only when `i: usize`) -- it doesn't actually call any library code, unlike the `get_unchecked` function call
```这对于参考活跃度有影响吗？我认为它的行为与库调用完全相同，例如堆积的借款。

622383489.en: it doesn't create any references, I'm not sure if that makes it behave differently in regards to stacked borrows (I'm too tired at the moment to think it through, sorry)
622383489.zh: 它不会创建任何引用，我不确定这是否会使其在堆积借用方面表现不同（我现在太累了，无法仔细考虑，抱歉）

622408943.en: If there exists a mutable reference to an element of `A` while `a`/`b` is called for a *different* element, `a` does not conflict with that since it only accesses one element, but `b` does conflict since it takes a shared reference to `A` as a whole.  https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=d6e5e38ffdc54fe3c44009e19ec8b0e3 (This example fails under current stacked borrows and tree borrows)
622408943.zh: 如果存在对某个元素的可变引用`A`尽管`a`/`b`被调用为*不同的*元素，`a`与此不冲突，因为它只访问一个元素，但是`b`确实存在冲突，因为它需要共享引用`A`作为一个整体。https://play.rust-lang.org/?version=stable&mode=debug&edition=2024&gist=d6e5e38ffdc54fe3c44009e19ec8b0e3（此示例在当前堆叠借用和树借用下失败）

622499304.en: Wow that kinda sucks. Is that documented anywhere, or is it an implementation detail?
622499304.zh: 哇，这有点糟糕。这是否记录在任何地方，或者是实施细节？

622500530.en: iirc the documentation is generally something like: "just use it through raw pointers, don't create references to mutable statics".
622500530.zh: iirc 文档通常类似于：“只需通过原始指针使用它，不要创建对可变静态的引用”。

622501133.en: so using `A[i]` technically works because it's a compiler built-in, but it's mostly in the same category as calling methods that implicitly make references and stuff so imo you shouldn't do it on mutable statics, use pointers instead.
622501133.zh: 所以使用`A[i]`从技术上讲，它是有效的，因为它是内置的编译器，但它主要与隐式创建引用和内容的调用方法属于同一类别，因此在我看来，您不应该在可变静态上执行此操作，而应使用指针。

622501243.en: makes it much easier to reason about rather than having to remember all the compiler's special sauce exceptions.
622501243.zh: 使得推理变得更加容易，而不必记住所有编译器的特殊酱异常。

605339628.en:
Issue: https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/issues/5159

Basically, the problem is that Android has `padding` field. As you can see, this appears to be implemented correctly for ARMv7: <https://github.com/rust-lang/libc/blob/60297178ac454f730335325c2fa6d37fe93886e2/src/unix/linux_like/android/b32/arm.rs#L44>, but not for ARMv8. I would like someone with more experience to review this and compare it against the Android NDK across all four Android platforms (ARMv7, ARMv8, x86, x86_64).

622443497.en:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/.60ucontext_t.60.20is.20incorrectly.20implemented.20in.20Android.27s.20.60libc.60.2E/near/622374988):
```quote
ucontext is not deprecated. It's part of the kernel ABI for things like signal handlers.
```

Gotcha, that goes against some of the stuff I’ve read online but I guess it’s kinda hard to deprecate a kernel api
622443497.zh:
@_* * Amanieu d 'Antras | 143274 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/.60ucontext_t.60.20is.20incorrectly.20implemented.20in.20Android.27s.20.60libc.60.2E/near/622374988):
```quote
ucontext is not deprecated. It's part of the kernel ABI for things like signal handlers.
```明白了，这违背了我在网上读过的一些内容，但我想很难弃用内核API

622448176.en: It was removed from posix but I think it's still considered fine to use by the platforms that have it
622448176.zh: 它已从posix中删除，但我认为拥有它的平台仍然可以使用它

622448375.en: Well, IIRC there were problems with what it did with the `makecontext` signature that may mean you technically can't use it soundly from either C or Rust. Why posix deprecated the whole thing rather than replacing `makecontext`, I have no idea...
622448375.zh: 好吧， IIRC在处理`makecontext`签名，这可能意味着从技术上讲，您无法从C或Rust中合理使用它。为什么posix不推荐整个事情，而不是替换`makecontext`我不知道

622498443.en:
if that's in reference to `makecontext` only allowing you to pass arguments that are `int`s to the called function, that can be used soundly to pass a pointer, you just have to cast the pointer to `usize`, and then split that into `int`-sized hunks. 

some programmers would pass a `long` or pointer directly, which is UB, though it kinda worked on most 32-bit systems and a few 64-bit systems.
622498443.zh:
如果这是关于`makecontext`仅允许您传递`int`到被调用的函数，可以很好地使用它来传递指针，您只需将指针转换为`usize`，然后将其拆分为`int`-大块头。 

一些程序员会通过一个`long`或指针，这是UB ，尽管它适用于大多数32位系统和少数64位系统。

622499037.en:
e.g. QEMU uses it by passing a pointer as 2 ints:
callee: https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/35500e5c41aec76cde59befe750600dac7a9e37a/util/coroutine-ucontext.c#L148
`makecontext` call: https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/35500e5c41aec76cde59befe750600dac7a9e37a/util/coroutine-ucontext.c#L222-L223
622499037.zh:
例如QEMU 通过将指针作为 2 个整数传递来使用它：
被叫方：https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/35500e5c41aec76cde59befe750600dac7a9e37a/util/coroutine-ucontext.c#L148
`makecontext`称呼：https://github.com/qemu/qemu/blob/35500e5c41aec76cde59befe750600dac7a9e37a/util/coroutine-ucontext.c#L222-L223

622499177.en: but yeah, I agree that's a terrible API.
622499177.zh: 但是，是的，我同意这是一个糟糕的 API。

It's a) ability to debug with standard tools and b) we don't have the means to evaluate phase ordering changes. The latter is more relevant for O2/O3 than O1, because I don't think anyone really cares about O1 upstream. It essentially just does whatever was grandfathered in at some point.

620377919.en:
So, it certainly sounds like opt-level=1 is doing its job, of being an optimization level that makes things noticeably faster without taking as much time as opt-level 2 or 3 to compile.

But that doesn't make it a good default for `dev`. `dev` should build as fast as possible. It should do any optimizations that *make the code faster to compile*, but it already does; opt-level 0 includes some MIR optimizations that are faster than not doing them, because they result in doing less work in compilation.
620377919.zh:
因此，听起来 opt-level=1 确实正在发挥作用，作为一个优化级别，它可以使事情明显更快，而无需花费像 opt-level 2 或 3 那么多的时间来编译。

但这并不能使它成为一个很好的默认值`dev`。`dev`应该尽快构建。它应该做任何优化来*使代码编译速度更快*，但它已经这样做了； opt-level 0 包含一些比不执行更快的 MIR 优化，因为它们会减少编译工作。

620378127.en: If people *want* to turn on optimizations on `dev`, they can. But our defaults should aim for fast builds.
620378127.zh: 如果人们“想要”开启优化`dev`，他们可以。但我们的默认设置应该以快速构建为目标。

620379492.en: opt-level=0 has a dual purpose of compiling as fast as possible and giving maximum debugging fidelity. When these are in conflict you have to pick one or the other. We may have some MIR passes right now that vary behavior based on debug info level but at least in LLVM it's explicit policy to not do that. Between that and "opt level < 0" looking silly, I think it's better to call the "compile as fast as possible at expense of debuggability" optimization level something different than "0" (assuming this level can realistically exist at all).
620379492.zh: opt-level=0 有双重目的：尽可能快地编译并提供最大的调试保真度。当这些发生冲突时，你必须选择其中之一。我们现在可能有一些 MIR 通道，它们会根据调试信息级别改变行为，但至少在 LLVM 中，明确的策略是不这样做。在这和看起来很愚蠢的“opt level < 0”之间，我认为最好将“以牺牲可调试性为代价尽可能快地编译”优化级别称为与“0”不同的东西（假设这个级别实际上可以存在）。

620381158.zh: 是的，如果构建时间是唯一的衡量标准`dev`，我们将完全关闭 debuginfo

620381977.en: The `dev` profile is caught between too many conflicting preferences, same with `release` because it enables *some* optimizations but we still have guidance all over the internet about "oh, do you really want good code? Apply these options instead of using the defaults"

620474138.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/opt-level.201/near/620462564):
```quote
I think my general feeling about not removing #[inline(always)] at opt-level=0 is that opt-level=0 is already too slow for a lot of projects (which is why this thread exists, largely), and making it even slower to make compiles faster is unfortunate, since it will force people towards opt-level=1 which is even slower for compilation.
```

I'm really having trouble grokking this one.  Why isn't it fine to say that if you need non-horrible codegen you should use `opt-level=1`?  Especially if `opt-level=0` is already too runtime-slow for people even *with* inlining of inline-always, which I think this is saying?

That to me sounds like the compilation-speed win for `opt-level=0` from *not* inline-always-ing would be clearly good.
620474138.zh:
@_* * Thom Chiovoloni | 209168 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/opt-level.201/near/620462564):

```我真的很难摸到这个。  为什么不能说，如果你需要非可怕的代码，你应该使用`opt-level=1`?特别是如果`opt-level=0`对于*内联*的人来说，运行时间已经太慢了-总是这样，我认为这是在说吗？

在我看来，这听起来像是编译速度的胜利，`opt-level=0`from * not * inline-always-ing显然是好的。

620655976.en: It can make sense to inline a cold path if it’s sufficiently small and gives more information to the optimizer. That’s why we have `hint::cold_path()`, and an inlinable `#[cold]` call is basically the equivalent of that when it’s needed in multiple places and you don’t want to repeat the actual logic or the `hint::cold_path()` in each of those places.
620655976.zh: 如果冷路径足够小，并且为优化器提供了更多信息，则内联冷路径是有意义的。这就是为什么我们有`hint::cold_path()`和一个内联的`#[cold]`调用基本上等同于在多个地方需要它，并且您不想重复实际的逻辑或`hint::cold_path()`在这些地方的每一个地方。

620663348.en: so to be clear, I think that in most cases the chance to inline cold paths is fine, especially since it's unlikely to happen across crate boundaries, and if the main issue is code size with `panic!` calls, maybe we should have a separate way of tagging those than just always having `#[cold]#[inline(never)]`
620663348.zh: 所以要明确的是，我认为在大多数情况下，内联冷路径的机会很好，特别是因为它不太可能跨越板条箱边界，如果主要问题是代码大小`panic!`也许我们应该有一种单独的方式来标记这些调用，而不是总是`#[cold]#[inline(never)]`

620009690.en:
I made a crate to demonstrate how I think you could do algebraic float operations a bit more ergonomic: https://crates.io/crates/algebraic

My assumption is that it is better to annotate the data itself as being amenable to nondeterministic optimization rather than the operation that is done on the data (the approach I think is taken by crate reassoc). My reasoning is that if, for a given set of floats, you want reordering in operation A, you probably also want reordering in operation B. Curious to hear your thoughts
620009690.zh: 我做了一个板条箱来演示我认为如何进行更符合人体工程学的代数浮点运算：https://crates.io/crates/algebraic我的假设是，最好将数据本身注释为可进行非确定性优化，而不是对数据进行操作（我认为采用的方法是crate reassoc ）。 我的推理是，如果对于一组给定的浮标，您希望在操作A中重新排序，您可能也希望在操作B中重新排序。

620131189.en:
Substituting mathematical functions with approximations is a whole other can of worms. There is no guarantee or bound whatsoever on their precision, at least with algebraic ops you know the output is some mathematically equivalent expression were it not for IEEE754's rounding/nans/infinities. They are genuinely useful for (unless the source material was already carefully written) producing faster (autovectorized) and typically more accurate expressions.

In principle `{ return 0.0; }` is a valid implementation for any function with the approx flag set. Now this is obviously a straw man, but I find it very hard to define what a 'reasonable' amount of approximation is. One use-case might be fine approximating `tanh(x) = x`, another would need `tanh(x) = x - x*x*x / 3`, etc.

620142633.en: FWIW I don’t find “lack of precision guarantee” very convincing as sole reason. The existing algebraic methods also have no such guarantees (not just in the spec, you can construct examples where it gives much worse precision for some inputs). We offer them because they provide a useful balance of “how much does it help performance” and “how likely is it to make precision meaningfully worse or otherwise shoot you in the foot“ in practice despite the lack of guarantees. Likewise, I’d expect any proposal to enable e.g. LLVM’s `afn` flag on `sqrt` to come with some convincing empirical arguments why it’s a useful thing to have and not just a footgun. But if that is established, then I don’t see this as categorically different from the algebraic operators.

620533445.en:
A potentially easier question (but if anyone disagrees, probably best to move it to a new thread), is how much we care about errno. This currently seems to be an undocumented implementation detail on the Rust side, based on whether we go through the llvm intrinsic, or the libm call. When writing these papers we had to look at IR differences between what we generate from rustc, and what we get from clang, to figure out where performance differences come from. In c++ we have `-fno-math-errno` to change that, but in Rust it seems like an implementation detail that users can't change: https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/primitive.f64.html#unspecified-precision-23 

My theory is that we used llvm intrinsics when they were (back then) available and libm otherwise. So some of our float operations just prevent DCE, LICM and other opts, while other float intrinsics allow them. I suggest we fix that, as it seems much less controversial than replacing the opts with some approximations.

I made a draft PR to show the differences: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/162104

620776320.en:
@_**Manuel Drehwald|348574** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/algebraic.20float.20ops/near/620512010):
```quote
https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.13759 Figure 5
```

Note that I'm not doubting that the `algebraic_*` operations help performance. What I'm asking for is the difference for source code readability, ease of authoring, maintainability, etc. of how you access the algebraic operations (`Algebraic<F>` wrapper type with operator overloading vs. the existing methods on primitive types).

From the source code you shared, there's some that seem to hardly use any overloaded operators (e.g. [pressure](https://github.com/ZuseZ4/rust_perf/blob/61da77cf93731c9096583187b82239a26d5e3e8c/src/apps/pressure.rs#L201-L213)) but also some (e.g., [del_dot_vec_2d](https://github.com/ZuseZ4/rust_perf/blob/61da77cf93731c9096583187b82239a26d5e3e8c/src/apps/del_dot_vec_2d.rs#L264-L285) or [matvec_3d_stencil](https://github.com/ZuseZ4/rust_perf/blob/61da77cf93731c9096583187b82239a26d5e3e8c/src/apps/matvec_3d_stencil.rs#L243-L271)) with a lot of `Real` operators. Some thoughts:

1) Those kernels look like a ton of line noise due to all the raw pointer arithmetic interleaved with actual work (no offense, been there done that). I wonder if it's more compelling in code that is overall more tuned for readability and safety.

2) The benchmarks benefits from all the array elements and scalars being typed as `Real` from start to end, so there's no  place where you have to switch back and forth other than for float literals. This makes sense for isolated kernels but is probably less true when embedded in a larger application than a benchmark harness.

620412800.en:
In case it's helpful for anyone using nushell, I have this

```nu
# Get a target->config map
def rustc-target-config [] {
    rustc --print target-list | lines |
        par-each {|tgt| rustc --print cfg --target $tgt | lines | {tgt:$tgt, cfg:$in } } |
        flatten |
        sort
}
```

Then can do things like:

```nu
> let cfg = rustc-target-config
> $cfg | find target_pointer_width | get cfg | sort | uniq
 0   target_pointer_width="16"
 1   target_pointer_width="32"
 2   target_pointer_width="64
```

I use this basically daily to peek at which targets set which cfg

620456081.en:
Think I have it figured out at https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/pull/1305 now. Important bit being running this before anything else to get the right bash

```yaml
    - name: Configure Windows PATH
      if: contains(matrix.target, 'windows-gnu')
      run: |
        # Put the msys bash in PATH so future launches use it rather than the default
        # git bash. This give us access to pacman.
        echo "C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
        echo "C:\msys64\usr\bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
```

Then in the setup script

```sh
# Enable 32-bit tools if needed. Note this must come after existing path entries
# like `/c/mingw64/bin`, otherwise they will be preferred over the host tools.
if [ "$target" = "i686-pc-windows-gnu" ]; then
    PATH="$PATH:/mingw32/bin"
    # Persist this for future jobs
    echo "PATH=$PATH" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
fi

pacman -S --noconfirm mingw-w64-i686-gcc
```

618006597.en:
I've been working on a GBA game and am using the agb crate to so. As part of it, I have a few types of game objects with common interfaces (update, show, take_damage, position, etc...). In my original implementation, to keep code tidy, I was storing game objects together in vectors of type `Box<dyn Enemy>`, as an example.

When running into performance issues, I had a suspicion that the dyn type to be a culprit, because the main bulk of computational work would be on calling these update functions. So, looking into it, I found the crate [enum_dispatch](https://docs.rs/enum_dispatch/latest/enum_dispatch/), and migrating our `Box<dyn Enemy>` types to the `Enemy` enum did give huge performance gains! The limits are now mostly due to hardware constraints on visible sprite counts as opposed to CPU cycles.

I haven't dug into the assembly, but I suspect the gains are due to compiler optimizations becoming available that couldn't be assumed for the dyn type.

So, I wanted to ask out of interest, why isn't there something like this built into the rust language? I know it's not applicable in all situations, particularly in compiled libraries, but in cases when all types are known at compile time, would it not be possible to eliminate these dynamic dispatched traits? Or, would it not be optimial sometimes? I saw this comment, which referenced this being a potential feature as well: https://github.com/rust-lang/goals/issues/257#issuecomment-3155934755

Genuinely curious about all of this, and would love to learn more and maybe hack away on implementation. It has been a while since my college class on compilers so I'm definitely out of my depth, but I am all ears!
618006597.zh:
我一直在开发一款GBA游戏，并且正在使用agb板条箱。作为其中的一部分，我有几种具有通用界面的游戏对象（ UPDATE、SHOW、TAKE_DAMAGE、POSITION等）。在我最初的实现中，为了保持代码整洁，我将游戏对象存储在类型的向量中`Box<dyn Enemy>`，作为示例。

遇到性能问题时，我怀疑dyn类型是罪魁祸首，因为主要的计算工作是调用这些更新函数。 所以，调查了一下，我找到了箱子[ENUM_DISPATCH] （https://docs.rs/enum_dispatch/latest/enum_dispatch/),并迁移我们的`Box<dyn Enemy>`类型到`Enemy`enum确实带来了巨大的性能提升！ 现在，限制主要是由于硬件对可见精灵计数的限制，而不是CPU周期。

我还没有深入挖掘程序集，但我怀疑这些收益是由于编译器优化变得可用，而这些优化无法用于dyn类型。

所以，出于兴趣，我想问，为什么Rust语言中没有这样的内置？ 我知道它并不适用于所有情况，特别是在编译库中，但在编译时已知所有类型的情况下，是否不可能消除这些动态分派的特征？ 或者，有时候这不是最理想的吗？ 我看到了这条评论，其中提到这也是一个潜在的功能：https://github.com/rust-lang/goals/issues/257#issuecomment-3155934755对所有这些都非常好奇，并希望了解更多信息，并可能在实施方面有所收获。 自从我上了大学的编译器课以来已经有一段时间了，所以我肯定超出了我的深度，但我全神贯注！

618008854.en: When *I* use dynamic dispatch, I generally use it deliberately to achieve a specific balance of trade-offs, and I would not appreciate the compiler doing heroics behind my back to undo that. Like sure, don't do indirect calls in every iteration of your hot inner loop! But in a well architected program, there are also many calls sites where static dispatch buys you absolutely nothing performance-wise and costs you a lot (in build times, binary size, cognitive complexity, API fragility, etc. etc.)
618008854.zh: 当*我*使用动态调度时，我通常会故意使用它来实现特定的权衡，我不希望编译器在我背后做英雄般的事情来撤销它。当然，不要在热内部循环的每次迭代中进行间接调用！但在一个精心设计的程序中，也有许多调用站点，静态调度在性能方面绝对不会为您带来任何好处，并且会花费您很多钱（在构建时间、二进制大小、认知复杂性、API脆弱性等方面）。

618009889.en:
Hmm, I totally agree with the build times, and binary size certainly can be an issue, but the cognitive complexity and API fragility have more to do with the status quo (that being, there isn't a way to do this sort of static dispatch without repetitive enum and impls, *or* using a crate like enum_dispatch to hide that away).

If not an automatic optimization, it would be a nice language feature to eliminate the cognitive complexity and API fragility needed to achieve it currently. Like, enum_dispatch is great for what it is, but due to the macro nature it's got some annoying debugging and compiler errors, and some IDE features don't play nice with it (at least in my experience).
618009889.zh:
嗯，我完全同意构建时间，二进制大小当然可能是一个问题，但认知复杂性和API脆弱性更多地与现状有关（也就是说，如果没有重复的枚举和暗示， *或*使用像enum_dispatch这样的crate来隐藏它，就无法执行这种静态调度）。

如果不是自动优化，这将是一个很好的语言功能，以消除当前实现它所需的认知复杂性和API脆弱性。 例如， enum_dispatch非常适合它，但由于宏的性质，它有一些恼人的调试和编译器错误，并且一些IDE功能不能很好地发挥作用（至少在我的经验中）。

618010752.en: For example, instead of doing `Box<dyn MyTrait>`, perhaps `st MyTrait` (st for static, naming things is tough).
618010752.zh: 例如，与其做`Box<dyn MyTrait>`，说不定`st MyTrait`（ st表示静态，命名很难）。

618011238.en: Regarding cognitive complexity and API fragility, I'm not talking about the boilerplate that `enum_dispatch` helps with. That's trivial in my book (which is also why I'm not a fan of using the crate in my own code). In the narrow case where you can just define an enum, you're just swapping a type involving `dyn Trait` for that enum. But if you want to push static dispatch everywhere, you often end up with a lot of code that's generic over `T: Trait`, and then that easily leads to lots and lots of more bounds, more generics, more type-level programming, to be able to express all the non-trivial things happening with and around that `T`. And which APIs need which subset of those bounds often shifts as the code base evolved, which means API breaking changes, while a trait object can often be passed around internally without affecting any public APIs.
618011238.zh: 关于认知复杂性和API脆弱性，我不是在谈论`enum_dispatch`帮助。这在我的书中是微不足道的（这也是为什么我不喜欢在我自己的代码中使用crate的原因）。在可以只定义枚举的狭义情况下，您只需交换`dyn Trait`但是，如果你想将静态调度推到任何地方，你通常会得到很多通用的代码，`T: Trait`，然后这很容易导致更多的边界，更多的泛型，更多的类型级编程，以便能够表达与之相关和周围发生的所有非微不足道的事情`T`。哪些API需要这些界限的哪个子集通常会随着代码库的发展而变化，这意味着API会破坏更改，而trait对象通常可以在内部传递而不会影响任何公共API。

Also, the usual benefit of avoiding indirect branches is better branch prediction which reduces how often CPUs have to unwind mispredicted speculative execution and flush the pipeline. 618016991.en: Meta-comment: I think that finding the right places for `dyn` is the most important part of rust architecture.  For example, it's often really really good to use `BufReader<dyn Read>` because what you really want it *both* kinds: static, inlinable dispatch for the "get me another byte" paths that *don't* usually need to refill the buffer, but polymorphic dispatch when it comes time to get another MB from the don't-care-where to avoid needing to emit all the loading code for *every* kind of `impl Read` that you happen to use.
618016991.zh: 元评论：我认为找到合适的地方`dyn`是防锈架构中最重要的部分。例如，它通常非常适合使用`BufReader<dyn Read>`因为你真正想要的是*两种*类型：静态的、内联的调度，用于*不*通常需要重新填充缓冲区的“get me another byte”路径，但是当需要从don 't-care获取另一个MB时，多态调度，以避免需要发出*每种*类型的所有加载代码`impl Read`你碰巧使用的。

616360082.en:
I maintain the [twox-hash](https://crates.io/crates/twox-hash/) crate, which is a native-Rust implementation of the [xxHash](https://xxhash.com) family of algorithms. Some folks from the icu4x team [noticed](https://github.com/unicode-org/icu4x/issues/8356) that hashing a `Vec` produced different results on 32-bit vs 64-bit systems, and opened [an issue for me](https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/issues/123).

The root cause  is that when you hash a `Vec`, it ultimately uses `write_usize` which writes the bytes of the number as a platform-native chunk of bytes. That changes from 32-bit to 64-bit as the size of `usize` is platform dependent. 

The issue seems to suggest that I should change the code so that the value is consistent on both platforms, but I'm hesitant to do so. At the very least it would require a new semver release as the value for 32-bit hosts would change.

For now, I've suggested that the ICU folks wrap the hasher in one that converts all `usize` to `u64`, which I think would address any immediate issues they have. Hopefully that means there's no urgent fire to put out.

This question is tangentially related to Rust's development as twox-hash is a dependency of the compiler through a few paths, but really I'm asking here to get a broader sense of how people would *expect* such a hasher crate to behave.
616360082.zh:
我维护[twox-hash] （https://crates.io/crates/twox-hash/)crate ，它是[xxHash] （https://xxhash.com)算法家族。icu4x团队的一些人[注意到] （https://github.com/unicode-org/icu4x/issues/8356)哈希算法`Vec`在32位和64位系统上产生了不同的结果，并打开了[对我来说是一个问题] （https://github.com/shepmaster/twox-hash/issues/123).根本原因是当你散列一个`Vec`，它最终使用`write_usize`它将数字的字节写入为平台原生的字节块。从32位变为64位，作为`usize`取决于平台。 

这个问题似乎建议我应该修改代码，以便在两个平台上保持一致，但我对此犹豫不决。 至少它需要一个新的semver版本，因为32位主机的值将发生变化。

目前，我建议ICU人员将哈希器包装在一个将所有`usize` 到 `u64`, which I think would address any immediate issues they have. Hopefully that means there's no urgent fire to put out.

This question is tangentially related to Rust's development as twox-hash is a dependency of the compiler through a few paths, but really I'm asking here to get a broader sense of how people would *expect* such a hasher crate to behave.

616360754.en: Hash consistency is one of those thorny problems where everyone assumes that the phrase means exactly their needs and are surprised when implementations and other users have different needs. I don't think there's a good solution here. Except to clearly document what is and what is not intended to be consistent.
616360754.zh: 哈希一致性是一个棘手的问题：每个人都以为这个说法恰好意味着自己的需求，而当实现和其他用户有不同需求时又会感到意外。我不认为这里有什么好的解决方案，除了明确记录哪些内容应该保持一致、哪些内容不应该保持一致。

616361768.en: vaguely remembered that we actually acount for this sort of thing in hashbrown and found the code for it: https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown/blob/8d9d6c51fe1f9a349f4981c8ef2f69359cd2e708/src/control/tag.rs#L35-L49
616361768.zh: 我隐约记得我们实际上在 hashbrown 里考虑过这类问题，于是找到了相关代码：https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown/blob/8d9d6c51fe1f9a349f4981c8ef2f69359cd2e708/src/control/tag.rs#L35-L49

616361791.en:
From a quick glance it looks like the ICU folks want the hash value of a non-trivial Rust value to be platform-independent and stable over time. Unfortunately that is effectively impossible to achieve with `Hash` because it’s not enough for the `Hasher` to offer stable results for the same sequence of `write_*` method calls, the `Hash` impls involved would also have to guarantee how they call `Hasher` methods, and approximately no impls (including those in core/std and those generated by `derive(Hash)`) promise any such stability.

Personally I think if you want any sort of hash stability, you should completely eschew the standard library’s traits and directly write code feeding bytes into a specific hashing algorithm (make up a new trait if you really must abstract over hashers).
616361791.zh:
粗略看了一下，ICU 的人似乎希望一个非平凡 Rust 值的哈希值与平台无关，并且长期保持稳定。遗憾的是，使用 `Hash` 实际上不可能做到这一点，因为仅仅要求 `Hasher` 对同一系列 `write_*` 方法调用给出稳定结果还不够；相关的 `Hash` 实现也必须保证它们调用 `Hasher` 方法的方式，而几乎没有任何实现（包括 core/std 中的实现以及由 `derive(Hash)` 生成的实现）承诺提供这样的稳定性。

我个人认为，如果你需要任何形式的哈希稳定性，就应该完全避开标准库的 trait，直接编写代码，将字节输入到某个特定的哈希算法中（如果确实必须对不同哈希器进行抽象，那就自己定义一个新的 trait）。

616362876.en:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Feedback.20on.20making.20twox-hash.20treat.20usize.20as.20u64.20by.20default/near/616361768):
```quote
vaguely remembered that we actually acount for this sort of thing in hashbrown and found the code for it: https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown/blob/8d9d6c51fe1f9a349f4981c8ef2f69359cd2e708/src/control/tag.rs#L35-L49
```

I think that’s something different: hashbrown has to deal with hashers that use usize *state* and therefore only have effectively 32 bit hash results, the ask here is about widening usize *inputs* to the hasher (and IIRC each xxhash variant has fixed state/output size)
616362876.zh:
@_**Clar Fon|330161** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Feedback.20on.20making.20twox-hash.20treat.20usize.20as.20u64.20by.20default/near/616361768)：
```quote
我隐约记得我们实际上在 hashbrown 里考虑过这类问题，于是找到了相关代码：https://github.com/rust-lang/hashbrown/blob/8d9d6c51fe1f9a349f4981c8ef2f69359cd2e708/src/control/tag.rs#L35-L49
```

我觉得那是另一回事：hashbrown 必须处理使用 usize 作为*状态*、因而实际上只能产生 32 位哈希结果的哈希器；这里讨论的是将 usize *输入*扩展后再传给哈希器（而且如果我没记错的话，每个 xxhash 变体都有固定的状态大小和输出大小）。

616363746.en: [`rustc-stable-hash`](https://lib.rs/crates/rustc-stable-hash) provides a generic [`StableHasher<H>`](rustc_stable_hash::StableHasher) that abstract over the target differences (little-endian vs big-endian, usize size). I would advise for using this solution or something similar and not to modify your algorithms.
616363746.zh: [`rustc-stable-hash`](https://lib.rs/crates/rustc-stable-hash) 提供了通用的 [`StableHasher<H>`](rustc_stable_hash::StableHasher)，用于抽象掉目标平台之间的差异（小端与大端、usize 大小）。我建议使用这个方案或类似方案，而不要修改你的算法。

616365160.en: If anything, I’d consider adding *more* platform differences (or even per-run) to the `Hasher` impls to shake out unwarranted stability assumptions even earlier (many things are never tested on big endian, and continuous testing on 32 bit targets is also getting less common). It looks like this is hard to do in the current API because the types that implement `Hasher` also have other APIs that can be stable, but maybe that’s something to consider for the next semver breaking release
616365160.zh: 如果要说有什么不同的话，我反而会考虑在 `Hasher` 的实现中加入*更多*平台差异（甚至让差异随运行而变化），以便更早地暴露那些没有依据的稳定性假设（很多东西从未在大端平台上测试过，而对 32 位目标进行持续测试也越来越少见）。考虑到实现 `Hasher` 的类型通常还有其他 API，而这些 API 可能需要保持稳定，这在当前 API 中似乎很难做到；不过，也许可以把它作为下一次 semver 破坏性版本发布时要考虑的事项。

619077952.en: Any chance of this being an LLVM version mismatch? The compiler was recently bumped to LLVM 23, and if it's run against an LLVM 22 dynamic library floating around somewhere, you'll get that segfault.

619187980.en:
That sounds like the problem then. rustc does support older LLVM versions, but it must be compiled against the same major version of LLVM which will be used at runtime, as different major versions are ABI-incompatible.

This is the fourth time I've seen this happen since the LLVM 23 bump, so I opened a PR to add a check so that future civilizations get a friendlier error:  https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/161788
619187980.zh:
那听起来问题就出在这里了。rustc 确实支持较旧版本的 LLVM，但它必须使用与运行时加载的 LLVM 相同的主版本进行编译，因为不同主版本之间的 ABI 不兼容。

自从升级到 LLVM 23 以来，这是我第四次看到这种情况了，所以我开了一个 PR，加入检查，让后世的人能看到更友好的错误信息：https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/161788

620226712.en:
We currently have the following list of `target_arch` values getting set for mips targets:

```text
 #                   tgt                             cfg
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  0   mips-mti-none-elf                      target_arch="mips"
  1   mips-unknown-linux-gnu                 target_arch="mips"
  2   mips-unknown-linux-musl                target_arch="mips"
  3   mips-unknown-linux-uclibc              target_arch="mips"
  4   mips64-openwrt-linux-musl              target_arch="mips64"
  5   mips64-unknown-linux-gnuabi64          target_arch="mips64"
  6   mips64-unknown-linux-muslabi64         target_arch="mips64"
  7   mips64el-unknown-linux-gnuabi64        target_arch="mips64"
  8   mips64el-unknown-linux-muslabi64       target_arch="mips64"
  9   mipsel-mti-none-elf                    target_arch="mips"
 10   mipsel-sony-psp                        target_arch="mips"
 11   mipsel-sony-psx                        target_arch="mips"
 12   mipsel-unknown-linux-gnu               target_arch="mips"
 13   mipsel-unknown-linux-musl              target_arch="mips"
 14   mipsel-unknown-linux-uclibc            target_arch="mips"
 15   mipsel-unknown-netbsd                  target_arch="mips"
 16   mipsel-unknown-none                    target_arch="mips"
 17   mipsisa32r6-unknown-linux-gnu          target_arch="mips32r6"
 18   mipsisa32r6el-unknown-linux-gnu        target_arch="mips32r6"
 19   mipsisa64r6-unknown-linux-gnuabi64     target_arch="mips64r6"
 20   mipsisa64r6el-unknown-linux-gnuabi64   target_arch="mips64r6"
```

Does it really make sense to set a `mips32r6` and `mips64r6` `target_arch`, rather than reusing `mips` and `mips64`? Reading through section 2.3.6 at https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/downloads-mips/documents/MD00083-2B-MIPS64INT-AFP-06.01.pdf it seems like there are instruction differences that you need to be aware of writing asm, but otherwise don't matter.

It feels like this could be something encoded via `target_abi` now that we have it.

(Added in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/58941, for context)
620226712.zh:
目前，mips 目标会设置为以下这些 `target_arch` 值：

```text
 #                   tgt                             cfg
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  0   mips-mti-none-elf                      target_arch="mips"
  1   mips-unknown-linux-gnu                 target_arch="mips"
  2   mips-unknown-linux-musl                target_arch="mips"
  3   mips-unknown-linux-uclibc              target_arch="mips"
  4   mips64-openwrt-linux-musl              target_arch="mips64"
  5   mips64-unknown-linux-gnuabi64          target_arch="mips64"
  6   mips64-unknown-linux-muslabi64         target_arch="mips64"
  7   mips64el-unknown-linux-gnuabi64        target_arch="mips64"
  8   mips64el-unknown-linux-muslabi64       target_arch="mips64"
  9   mipsel-mti-none-elf                    target_arch="mips"
 10   mipsel-sony-psp                        target_arch="mips"
 11   mipsel-sony-psx                        target_arch="mips"
 12   mipsel-unknown-linux-gnu               target_arch="mips"
 13   mipsel-unknown-linux-musl              target_arch="mips"
 14   mipsel-unknown-linux-uclibc            target_arch="mips"
 15   mipsel-unknown-netbsd                  target_arch="mips"
 16   mipsel-unknown-none                    target_arch="mips"
 17   mipsisa32r6-unknown-linux-gnu          target_arch="mips32r6"
 18   mipsisa32r6el-unknown-linux-gnu        target_arch="mips32r6"
 19   mipsisa64r6-unknown-linux-gnuabi64     target_arch="mips64r6"
 20   mipsisa64r6el-unknown-linux-gnuabi64   target_arch="mips64r6"
```

与其设置 `mips32r6` 和 `mips64r6` 这两个 `target_arch`，而不是复用 `mips` 和 `mips64`，这样做真的合理吗？阅读 https://s3-eu-west-1.amazonaws.com/downloads-mips/documents/MD00083-2B-MIPS64INT-AFP-06.01.pdf 第 2.3.6 节后，我觉得其中确实存在一些指令差异，编写 asm 时需要注意，但除此之外似乎并不重要。

感觉现在既然已经有了 `target_abi`，这件事可以通过它来编码。

（相关背景：添加于 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/58941）

620227888.en: Asking because all the code I've come across should be treating these like mips targets, but fails to because it doesn't match `any(target_arch = "mips", target_arch = "mips64")`. For prior art, Clang has pretty much the same definitions (`__mips__`, `__mips`, `__mips64`, `__mips64__`) on both and only seems to differentiate with `#define _MIPS_ARCH "mips32r6" https://clang.godbolt.org/z/s343xK53x
620227888.zh: 之所以问这个，是因为我遇到的所有代码似乎都应该把这些当作 mips 目标处理，但由于它们不匹配 `any(target_arch = "mips", target_arch = "mips64")`，所以无法正常工作。作为先例，Clang 对两者基本使用相同的定义（`__mips__`、`__mips`、`__mips64`、`__mips64__`），似乎只有通过 `#define _MIPS_ARCH "mips32r6" https://clang.godbolt.org/z/s343xK53` 才会加以区分。

620227907.en: I'd worry a bit about the asm but it's still unstable
620227907.zh: 我会有点担心 asm，不过它目前仍然是不稳定的。

620228225.en: Cc maintainers @**chenx97**  @**Fearyncess**, and @**Aelin** for mips familiarity
620228225.zh: 抄送熟悉 mips 的维护者 @**chenx97**、@**Fearyncess** 和 @**Aelin**

620229394.en: We do set `target_abi="abi64"` on some of these but I believe that can be multivalued
620229394.zh: 我们确实在其中一些目标上设置了 `target_abi="abi64"`，但我认为它可以有多个值。

620246403.en: mips64r6 is a bunch of breaking changes to mips64 and I believe it should be a separate `target_arch`, yes
620246403.zh: mips64r6 对 mips64 做了许多破坏性修改，我认为它应该是一个独立的 `target_arch`，没错。

620246865.en: From a user POV I'd expect to be able to write assembly that's gated by a `#[cfg(target_arch)]` as long as I'm not using instructions that aren't part of the baseline. With mips64r6 and mips64 that's no longer the case if they had the same `target_arch`
620246865.zh: 从用户的角度来看，只要我没有使用不属于基线的指令，我会期望自己能够编写由 `#[cfg(target_arch)]` 控制的汇编代码。如果 mips64r6 和 mips64 使用相同的 `target_arch`，那就无法再保证这一点了。

620282353.en: These "revisions" make entirely different processors instead of being an "ABI" difference. One **redefines** *opcodes* defined in another.
620282353.zh: 这些“修订版”实际上造就了完全不同的处理器，而不只是“ABI”差异。其中一个版本还会**重新定义**另一个版本中定义的 *opcode*。

620282882.en: See also #**t-compiler/major changes>Add New Values To MIPS_ALLOWED_FEATURES compiler-team#595@337942966**
620282882.zh: 另请参见 #**t-compiler/major changes>Add New Values To MIPS_ALLOWED_FEATURES compiler-team#595@337942966**

620475245.en: Yes, the ISA having an instruction-level difference was what persuaded me, reluctantly, to conclude that they're different ISAs.
620475245.zh: 是的，正是 ISA 在指令层面的差异，让我不情愿地得出了它们属于不同 ISA 这一结论。

620509422.en: That all makes sense. It's just kind of too bad that the configuration gets messier
620509422.zh: 这些都说得通。只是配置会变得更加繁琐，多少有点遗憾。

620509571.en: Perhaps we could be setting `target_family = "mips32"`, `target_family = "mips64"`, `target_family = "mips"` (any mips)
620509571.zh: 或许我们可以设置 `target_family = "mips32"`、`target_family = "mips64"` 和 `target_family = "mips"`（任意 mips）。

620590430.en: Yes, `target_family` seems like the right thing here, especially for "any mips".
620590430.zh: 是的，`target_family` 在这里似乎是正确的做法，尤其是对于“任意 mips”这种情况。

620594299.en: Quite honestly I wouldn't mind that sort of thing for all similar targets. Seems almost as common to need something like `any(target_arch = "powerpc", target_arch = "powerpc64")`, `any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64")` etc. as for a single arch
620594299.zh: 说实话，如果所有类似的目标都采用这种做法，我也不会介意。需要写类似 `any(target_arch = "powerpc", target_arch = "powerpc64")`、`any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64")` 的情况，似乎几乎和只针对单个架构一样常见。

620602596.en: With `powerpc` I believe we don't actually differentiate in `target_arch` for SPE at the moment, which has opcode overlaps with AltiVec. This is quite inconsistent
620602596.zh: 对于 `powerpc`，据我所知，我们目前实际上不会在 `target_arch` 中区分 SPE，而 SPE 的 opcode 与 AltiVec 存在重叠。这种情况相当不一致。

620602869.en: But then I also vaguely remember that the SPE targets don't enable SPE, so perhaps they should just be removed
620602869.zh: 不过我又隐约记得，SPE 目标并没有启用 SPE，所以也许它们应该直接被移除。

620606776.en: AltiVec is an extension on top of the base ISA, right? That conflict is similar to how on RISC-V some extensions conflict with each other. That is different from MIPS where instructions in the base isa changed and thus even proper `#[cfg(target_feature = "...")]` around the inline asm wouldn't help.
620606776.zh: AltiVec 是在基础 ISA 之上的扩展，对吧？这种冲突类似于 RISC-V 上某些扩展彼此冲突的情况。这与 MIPS 不同，后者修改了基础 ISA 中的指令，因此即使在内联 asm 外围使用恰当的 `#[cfg(target_feature = "...")]` 也无济于事。

620630642.en: For `powerpc` it is, yes. I didn't know we already had such a situation on RISC-V, in that case it's fine
620630642.zh: 对于 `powerpc` 来说，确实如此。我之前不知道 RISC-V 上已经存在这种情况；既然如此，那就没问题了。

606382523.en:
While I have no objection to dropping i686 host tools, demoing to tier 2 is a worry.

To quote a colleague "x86 will outlive the sun" - building apps as i686 is still very important, especially if you want to support older versions of Windows. x64 emulation for Arm64 is only supported on Win11, so i686 is the only thing guaranteed to work on any version or arch of Windows.
606382523.zh:
虽然我不反对移除 i686 主机工具，但降到 Tier 2 让我有些担心。

引用一位同事的话：“x86 会比太阳活得更久。” 构建 i686 应用仍然非常重要，尤其是如果你想支持较旧版本的 Windows。Arm64 上的 x64 模拟仅在 Win11 上受支持，因此 i686 是唯一能保证在任何 Windows 版本或架构上都能运行的方案。

606382934.en: imo we should eventually move both `i686-pc-windows-gnullvm` and `i686-pc-windows-msvc` to tier 1 without host tools.
606382934.zh: 我认为最终我们应该把 `i686-pc-windows-gnullvm` 和 `i686-pc-windows-msvc` 都提升到 Tier 1，但不提供主机工具。

606383012.en: and `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` to tier 1 with host tools
606383012.zh: 并且把 `x86_64-pc-windows-gnullvm` 提升到 Tier 1，同时提供主机工具。

606385879.en: Demoting to tier 2 doesn't necessarily mean we stop running tests. We do test a number of tier 2 targets, we just make no guarantees. Having something official that's between "it builds" and full tier 1 host/target support might be useful though.
606385879.zh: 降到 Tier 2 并不一定意味着我们会停止运行测试。我们确实会测试一些 Tier 2 目标，只是不会提供任何保证。不过，有一个介于“能构建”和完整的 Tier 1 主机/目标支持之间的官方级别，或许会很有用。

606387359.en:
@_**Daniel Paoliello|391982** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606382523):
```quote
While I have no objection to dropping i686 host tools, demoing to tier 2 is a worry.

To quote a colleague "x86 will outlive the sun" - building apps as i686 is still very important, especially if you want to support older versions of Windows. x64 emulation for Arm64 is only supported on Win11, so i686 is the only thing guaranteed to work on any version or arch of Windows.
```

we don't really support older versions of windows though at tier 1, we only really support windows 10.
606387359.zh:
@_**Daniel Paoliello|391982** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606382523)：
```quote
虽然我不反对移除 i686 主机工具，但降到 Tier 2 让我有些担心。

引用一位同事的话：“x86 会比太阳活得更久。” 构建 i686 应用仍然非常重要，尤其是如果你想支持较旧版本的 Windows。Arm64 上的 x64 模拟仅在 Win11 上受支持，因此 i686 是唯一能保证在任何 Windows 版本或架构上都能运行的方案。
```

不过，我们在 Tier 1 中其实并不支持较旧版本的 Windows，我们真正支持的只有 Windows 10。

606389442.en: Hm yeah, I do wonder if we should consider T1 (but no host tools)
606389442.zh: 嗯，确实。我倒想知道，我们是否应该考虑 T1（但不提供主机工具）。

606390744.en: I think the RISC-V targets were interested in having the target be T1 without host tools, and then the host tools at T2. Seems like that might work here too
606390744.zh: 我记得 RISC-V 目标似乎有意让目标本身进入 T1，但主机工具放在 T2。这里采用同样的方式似乎也行。

606402767.en:
i686 code runs fine on x64 Windows 11, and might be useful if you need to link against some proprietary 32-bit DLL you’ve been given. 

But the host tools do not seem useful because I don’t know how much you can compile with just 2GB of virtual address space per process.
606402767.zh:
i686 代码在 x64 Windows 11 上运行得很好；如果你需要链接到别人提供给你的某个专有 32 位 DLL，它也可能会派上用场。

但主机工具似乎没什么用，因为我不知道只靠每个进程 2GB 的虚拟地址空间，你究竟能编译多大的东西。

606406385.en: You can get more than 2GB when the binary is large address aware, but for a compiler, it's...not much change. On the C++ side, the STL maintainer is also pushing for dropping the x86 host tools and only leaving amd64_x86 (aka the 64-bit compiler binary that outputs 32 bit code) as "My compiler is running out of heap" is not a great user experience
606406385.zh: 如果二进制启用了大地址感知（large address aware），可以获得超过 2GB 的空间；但对于编译器来说……变化并不大。在 C++ 这边，STL 维护者也在推动移除 x86 主机工具，只保留 amd64_x86（也就是生成 32 位代码的 64 位编译器二进制），因为“我的编译器耗尽堆空间了”并不是很好的用户体验。

606410928.en:
> the target not exactly having a future by the OS vendor

This is not entirely true; the host tools don't, but there are no (public) deprecation plans for WOW64. That being said, I don't think running host tools on 32-bit Windows editions is relevant anymore, and that we should drop the host tools.

i686-msvc is in a bit of a funny situation: It leeches its maintenance off of x86-64, which works fine for the library side, and the interest in that target is much more skewed towards the enterprise space - there is still a lot of software only providing 32-bit builds, and if you have to interoperate with that, you need the ability to compile 32-bit code. It also generally works, as opposed to, say, the GNU version.

Assuming the i686-msvc CI seizing up doesn't become a more regular occurrence, and with only this issue in mind, I'd be in favor of dropping it to T1 without host tools. I think a demotion to T2 (which, even if we run tests, signals a level of instability simply due to its neighborhood currently not present in the target) would only fit at this moment if we also want to clean out some of the legacy brokenness in 32-bit tier 1 targets, like the wonders of x87 or alignment issues (like MSVC aligning i64 to 4 bytes if it's on the stack).
606410928.zh:
> 该目标在操作系统厂商那里前景并不明朗

这并不完全正确；没有前景的是主机工具，但目前并没有关于弃用 WOW64 的（公开）计划。话虽如此，我认为在 32 位 Windows 版本上运行主机工具已经不再有意义，我们应该移除主机工具。

i686-msvc 的处境有点特殊：它在库这一侧借用了 x86-64 的维护成果，而后者运行良好；同时，对该目标感兴趣的用户更多地集中在企业领域——仍然有大量软件只提供 32 位构建，如果你必须与这类软件互操作，就需要能够编译 32 位代码。与 GNU 版本不同的是，它通常确实能正常工作。

假设 i686-msvc CI 卡死不会变成更频繁发生的情况，那么仅考虑这一个问题，我会赞成将它保留在 T1，但不提供主机工具。我认为此时降到 T2 并不合适（即使我们仍然运行测试，也会因为它目前所在的目标类别而传递出不稳定的信号），除非我们还想清理 32 位 Tier 1 目标中的一些历史遗留问题，比如 x87 的种种问题，或对齐问题（例如 MSVC 在 i64 位于栈上时会将其按 4 字节对齐）。

606411582.en: if we have the target (partially) to support legacy windows code, why would we go out of our way to break legacy windows code that uses x87 or those MSVC alignment issues?
606411582.zh: 如果我们保留这个目标，部分原因是为了支持旧版 Windows 代码，那为什么还要特意破坏使用 x87 或存在这些 MSVC 对齐问题的旧版 Windows 代码？

606412028.en: admittedly x87 (other than missing `c_long_double`) isn't really a problem for FFI with other code, it's mostly a problem in function bodies that want to do fp arithmetic and have to use x87's broken `f32`/`f64` support; i686 Rust targets already use SSE2 for fp arithmetic precisely to avoid those issues.
606412028.zh: 话虽如此，除了缺少 `c_long_double` 之外，x87 对与其他代码进行 FFI 来说其实并不算什么问题；它主要影响那些需要进行浮点运算、因而不得不使用 x87 那套有问题的 `f32`/`f64` 支持的函数体。i686 Rust 目标已经使用 SSE2 进行浮点运算，正是为了规避这些问题。

606412704.en: The C calling convention still mandates that fp return values are returned in `st(0)`, which can do funny things like https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/115567
606412704.zh: C 调用约定仍然规定浮点返回值要放在 `st(0)` 中，这可能会导致一些奇怪的问题，比如 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/115567

@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [schrieb](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606411582):
```quote
if we have the target (partially) to support legacy windows code, why would we go out of our way to break legacy windows code that uses x87 or those MSVC alignment issues?
```

We shouldn't break it, I meant it as "maybe we'd want to demote it (and eventually the Linux equivalent) to T2 so that we can have all T1 targets always have reasonable floating point operations etc, if not, keep it at T1 for now"

```quote
如果我们保留这个目标，部分原因是为了支持旧版 Windows 代码，那为什么还要特意破坏使用 x87 或存在这些 MSVC 对齐问题的旧版 Windows 代码？
```

我们不应该破坏它们，我的意思是：“也许我们会希望把它（以及最终 Linux 上的对应目标）降到 T2，这样所有 T1 目标就都能始终提供合理的浮点运算等功能；如果不这么做，那目前就先保留在 T1。”

606413683.zh: 毕竟，它们是仅有的带有“这可能是不健全的”注释的 T1 目标。

TBH, I think we should never have any 32-bit *hosts* as "with host tools" at tier 1.  There's a bunch of stuff that definitely has bugs if you cross-compile from 32-bit host to 64-bit target, for example.  And I think we should just "won't fix" any bugs related to having <3GB of address space while running rustc.

We can still consider "excessive memory usage" bugs, but I think we should just pre-emptively decide not to care about 32-bit address space for *host tools*.

@_**Fulgen|644580** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606406385):
```quote
You can get more than 2GB when the binary is large address aware, but for a compiler, it's...not much change. 
```

Yeah, I consider the difference between 2GB and 3GB here completely irrelevant.
606784620.zh:
@_**Jonathan 'theJPster' Pallant|203633** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606402767)：
```quote
但主机工具似乎没什么用，因为我不知道每个进程只有 2GB 虚拟地址空间时到底能编译多少东西。
```

说实话，我觉得 Tier 1 根本不应该有任何 32 位*主机*被标记为“带主机工具”。比如，从 32 位主机交叉编译到 64 位 target 时，有一大堆东西肯定会出 bug。而且我认为，对于运行 rustc 时地址空间小于 3GB 所导致的任何 bug，我们都应该直接标记为“不会修复”。

“内存使用过高”相关的 bug 仍然可以考虑，但我觉得我们应该提前决定：对于*主机工具*的 32 位地址空间问题，我们就不必操心了。

@_**Fulgen|644580** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/606406385)：
```quote
如果二进制文件启用了大地址感知，那么在 32 位进程中可以获得超过 2GB 的内存，但对于编译器来说……变化并不大。
```

是的，我认为这里 2GB 和 3GB 之间的差异完全无关紧要。

606785955.en: Yea, I don't think providing the host tools at all is worth it. They're only required for people running the 32-bit version of Windows 10.
606785955.zh: 是啊，我觉得根本不值得提供主机工具。它们只对运行 32 位 Windows 10 的用户有用。

606785963.en: (You can technically use file mappings to allocate more memory in a 32-bit process on a 64-bit OS and only map what you need into the address space, but...no. Just no.)
606785963.zh: （从技术上讲，在 64 位操作系统上的 32 位进程中，可以使用文件映射来分配更多内存，只把需要的部分映射到地址空间里，但……不。真的别这么做。）

606796376.en: Also, I'm worried that keeping them at tier 2 and shipped will just cause user frustration in the long run  - they'd still be there, people would still use them as if they were tier 1, and have to deal with the switch to `--target` anyway when stuff would eventually break.
606796376.zh: 另外，我担心把它们保留在 Tier 2 并随发行版一起提供，长远来看只会让用户感到挫败——它们依然存在，用户也依然会把它们当作 Tier 1 来使用，而等到最终出问题时，他们还得处理切换到 `--target` 的问题。

606798557.en: maybe we should make a version of the compiler that is x86_64 but targets i686 by default?
606798557.zh: 也许我们应该做一个 x86_64 版本的编译器，但默认以 i686 为 target？

606799086.en: That seems like a thing that would add confusion and complication — particularly around the compilation of build scripts, proc-macros and `"host-tuple"`
606799086.zh: 这似乎会增加困惑和复杂性——尤其是在编译构建脚本、proc-macros 和 `"host-tuple"` 时。

606800501.en: As said above, we can simply fix this in rustup by not allowing i686 host toolchain to be installed on a 64-bit Windows (`--force-non-host-toolchain` can be used to override).
606800501.zh: 正如上面所说，我们完全可以在 rustup 中解决这个问题：不允许在 64 位 Windows 上安装 i686 主机工具链（可以使用 `--force-non-host-toolchain` 来覆盖这一限制）。

609292935.en: So, with MSVC 64-bit debugger cannot properly debug 32-bit binaries?
609292935.zh: 所以，使用 MSVC 的 64 位调试器无法正确调试 32 位二进制文件吗？

609293220.en:
Normally (in Visual Studio or windbg) it autoswitches to the 32-bit debugger. If you explicitely force the 64-bit debugger it can properly debug it, but you're debugging it from a 64-bit point of view, which exposes you to all the WOW64 stuff like how it does CPU mode switching from 32bit to 64bit for syscalls etc. Not useful, and generally not done.

And also not really what we care about if we want to test debuginfo.
609293220.zh:
通常情况下（在 Visual Studio 或 windbg 中），它会自动切换到 32 位调试器。如果你明确强制使用 64 位调试器，它确实可以正确调试，但你是在从 64 位的视角进行调试，这会让你暴露在各种 WOW64 细节之下，比如系统调用时它如何把 CPU 模式从 32 位切换到 64 位等。没什么用，而且通常也不会这么做。

另外，如果我们想测试 debuginfo，这也并不是我们真正关心的内容。

609625195.en:
okay, the opinion is actually stronger against maintaining host tools whatsoever based on the poll responses. some people are leaning towards it but there are way more people in the "it should be std only" buckets. some of them are doubled up between "std, tier 1" and "std 1, host 2" but I am assuming that signifies "both of these are fine to me".

I think it makes more sense also in terms of addressing the target's ongoing maintenance costs, having reflected on it, which is probably informing the preferences here.
609625195.zh: 好吧，根据投票结果，大家实际上更强烈地反对维护 host tools。确实有些人倾向于保留它，但更多人选择了“应该只有 std”的选项。有些人同时选了“std，tier 1”和“std 1，host 2”，但我猜这表示“这两种方案对我来说都可以”。我仔细想了想，觉得这样对于解决该 target 持续产生的维护成本也更合理；这可能正是大家形成这些偏好的原因。

609625375.en: I think it makes more sense to just plain RFC dropping the host tools entirely also as we can add a tier 2 target, including host tools, much more readily.
609625375.zh: 我觉得直接发起一个 RFC，彻底移除 host tools，会更合理；毕竟我们可以更容易地添加一个包含 host tools 的 tier 2 target。

609629389.en: Yeah, that makes full sense to me now, thinking about it. If we allow targets to have multiple tiers for host tools and std support, then an MCP, logically, can add such tier 2 support to a target that is any other tier in any other way.
609629389.zh: 是的，现在想想，这完全说得通。如果允许 target 在 host tools 和 std 支持方面分别拥有不同的 tier，那么从逻辑上讲，MCP 就可以为一个以其他方式处于任意 tier 的 target 添加这样的 tier 2 支持。

609629413.en: tier 2 std can become tier 2 std + tier 2 host, tier 1 std can become tier 1 std + tier 2 host, etc.
609629413.zh: tier 2 std 可以变成 tier 2 std + tier 2 host，tier 1 std 可以变成 tier 1 std + tier 2 host，等等。

609629439.en: we just bundle the two usually
609629439.zh: 我们通常只是把这两者捆在一起。

609629456.en: So yeah, if people want tier 2 host tools support they can pursue it after.
609629456.zh: 所以，如果有人想要 tier 2 host tools 支持，之后再推进就行。

611146799.en:

Likewise I usually just revise things on other people's docs if they've given edit access if it's something communal like a meeting agenda (esp. if I'm just fixing typos or something). 611939546.zh:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Demoting.20.60i686-pc-windows-msvc.60.20to.20Tier.202.3F/near/611145400)：

```

考虑到我们还把 `i686-unknown-linux-gnu` 完整地保留在 Tier 1，把论点很大程度建立在地址空间太小这一点上，确实有点奇怪。

611941336.en: true, but all the address space arguments apply equally to both of our 32bit tier 1 with host tools targets
611941336.zh: 没错，但所有关于地址空间的论点同样适用于我们这两个带宿主工具的 32 位 Tier 1 目标。

611941422.en: (and we have a bunch of 32bit tier 2 with host tools as well)
611941422.zh: （而且我们还有一大批带宿主工具的 32 位 Tier 2 目标。）

611950032.en:
Not entirely equally - running the i686-msvc host tools is only supported on Windows 10 (which is already EOL) or newer, so the only scenario where they are required is running on Windows 10 32-bit which has no upgrade path as Windows 11 only ships 64-bit builds, so it's an address space headache for a very very tiny gain, if any. (Also it caused problems in CI.)

In contrast there are still 32-bit Linux distros out in the wild and running on older device (though, given the usage statistics, apparently with not much Rust usage).
611950032.zh:
也不完全一样——i686-msvc 宿主工具只支持在 Windows 10（而它已经停止支持）或更新版本上运行，所以唯一需要它们的场景，就是在 32 位 Windows 10 上运行；但 Windows 11 只提供 64 位版本，因此没有升级路径。为了几乎没有、即使有也非常微小的收益，却要面对地址空间问题，实在不划算。（而且它还给 CI 带来了问题。）

相比之下，市面上仍然有 32 位 Linux 发行版，也仍有人在较旧的设备上运行 Linux（不过从使用统计来看，显然 Rust 的使用并不多）。

611961066.en: @**RalfJ** Not really the same, because they are effectively cross-compiled.
611961066.zh: @**RalfJ** 不太一样，因为它们实际上是交叉编译的。

611961216.en: dist-i686-linux builds using a 64-bit host toolchain. Not like i686-windows-gnu, which uses a 32-bit host toolchain. (No idea what i686-windows-msvc does.)
611961216.zh: dist-i686-linux 使用 64 位宿主工具链进行构建。不像 i686-windows-gnu，后者使用 32 位宿主工具链。（不知道 i686-windows-msvc 的情况。）

611962128.en: Though really, the actual difference is just that Windows sucks and nobody wants to deal with issues on it.
611962128.zh: 不过说到底，实际区别就是 Windows 太拉了，没人想处理它上面的各种问题。

those are all valid arguments but the RFC chooses to put the "it's 32bit" argument front and center.

611963869.zh: Debian 使用 i686 编译 i686（但据我所知，实际是在 x86_64 上执行）。不过从 Trixie 开始，我们已经不再构建 mingw 部分了

611964309.zh: 据我所知，armel、armhf、powerpc、x32 和 hurd-i686 也一样——不过除了 armel 和 armhf 之外，它们都不是正式的发行版架构，而且 Trixie 之后 armel 也不再是了

564142853.en:
Howdy t-compiler, I'm looking for insights to help shape a survey about debugging support in Rust. I've got two questions for you, and I'd appreciate any information you can offer.

1. Are there any particular RFCs or other work on the compiler you think could have a significant impact on the debugger experience? For better or for worse.
2. Is there anything in particular you'd like to know about Rust users experiences with debuggers to help guide development?
564142853.zh:
嗨，t-compiler，我想收集一些见解，以帮助设计一份关于 Rust 调试支持的调查问卷。我有两个问题，希望你们能提供任何相关信息。

1. 你认为有哪些特定的 RFC 或其他编译器方面的工作，可能会对调试器体验产生重大影响？无论是积极影响还是消极影响。
2. 为了指导后续开发，关于 Rust 用户使用调试器的体验，你特别想了解哪些方面？

564718623.en:
some obvious things that come to mind:
1) do you use a debugger vs do you use println?
2) why don't you use a debugger?
3) which debugger do you use? GDB vs LLDB vs ... and on which OS
4) do you debug through CLI or through an IDE?

I think that https://rust-lang.github.io/wg-async/design_docs/async_stack_traces.html are a high-profile item that could improve debugging of async Rust a lot
564718623.zh:
我首先想到的是一些比较显而易见的问题：
1）你会使用调试器，还是使用 println？
2）你为什么不使用调试器？
3）你使用哪种调试器？GDB、LLDB 还是其他调试器？在哪个 OS 上使用？
4）你是通过 CLI 调试，还是通过 IDE 调试？

我认为 https://rust-lang.github.io/wg-async/design_docs/async_stack_traces.html 是一个备受关注的项目，应该能大幅改善异步 Rust 的调试体验。

564770858.en: You should also distinguish using a debugger to get stacktraces from a hung/crashed process vs. step-debugging.
564770858.zh: 你还应该区分这样两种情况：使用调试器从卡死或崩溃的进程中获取堆栈跟踪，以及单步调试。

564775102.en:
Not to hijack the discussion too much, but one thing I miss from gdb + C++ in gdb + rust is that of python replacements for functions: basically something like the indexing operator for a std::vector would also have a python implementation in the debugger.

Rust just have the pretty printers, but if you have a *large* collection (let's say hundreds or more items) gdb will unhelpfully print `...` and not show them all. Plus if you have that many items it is hard to see what is going on visually anyway.

Having an indexing operator that you can *call* from gdb is a game changer to be able to print sub fields of items, or check if an item is in a set, etc.

But for some unfathomable reason it seems the focus so far has only been on the pretty printers.
564775102.zh:
不想过多地带偏讨论，不过我在 gdb + C++ 与 gdb + rust 之间感到遗憾的一点，是后者没有用于替代函数的 Python 实现：基本上，像 std::vector 的索引运算符这样的功能，也应该在调试器中提供一个 Python 实现。

Rust 只有 pretty printer，但如果你有一个很大的集合（比如几百个或更多元素），gdb 会毫无帮助地打印出 `...`，而不会把它们全部显示出来。此外，如果元素数量达到这个程度，仅凭视觉查看也很难弄清楚到底发生了什么。

如果能提供一个可以在 gdb 中调用的索引运算符，就完全改变了游戏规则：你可以打印元素的子字段、检查某个元素是否在集合中，等等。

但不知为何，到目前为止，关注点似乎一直只放在 pretty printer 上。

564776206.en: yeah, better Rust expressions in the debugger would be awesome. RustRover actually implemented support for this recently
564776206.zh: 没错，如果调试器能支持更好的 Rust 表达式，那就太棒了。RustRover 最近实际上已经实现了这项支持。

...

```
I'm imagining 1 and the former part of 3 being combined as a single question along the lines of, "how frequently do you use the following for debugging?" with a listing of GDB, LLDB, etc, (e)print(ln)!, dbg!, and "other (please specify)". Do you think that misses the mark/overcomplicates it? I didn't want to assume people use just one debugger/method.

Similarly I would probably want to ask about the frequency of each OS rather than for a specific choice of OS, though together this might make it difficult to determine which specific pairing is actually most common (as opposed to the pairing of the most common debugger and the most common OS).

同样地，我可能也会想询问用户使用各个 OS 的频率，而不是让他们从中选择一个特定的 OS。不过，这样一来可能就很难判断哪种具体组合最常见了（而不是简单地将最常用的调试器和最常用的 OS 配对）。

```quote
yeah, better Rust expressions in the debugger would be awesome. RustRover actually implemented support for this recently
```

I might be the odd one out but for debugging I actually strongly prefer command line debuggers. I really don't want to debug from an IDE, and for IDEs I prefer something more light weight like vscode. (And yes, it feels strange to call vscode light weight.)

The IDE debuggers never expose the full power, or at least make it quite awkward to interact directly with the underlying debugger to do something like set a hardware memory watchpoint. And woe betide you if you want to write some custom adhoc python or send a custom monitor command to your gdb server (eg. for talking directly to valgrind, or to your hardware debugger hooked up to your microcontroller over JTAG).

Working directly with the command line debugger just has less "impedance mismatch" and it doesn't get in your way.
564779298.zh:
@_**Jakub Beránek|266526** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Soliciting.20opinions.20for.20debugger.20survey/near/564776206)：
```quote
yeah, better Rust expressions in the debugger would be awesome. RustRover actually implemented support for this recently
```

我可能和大多数人不太一样，但说到调试，我确实非常偏好命令行调试器。我真的不想在 IDE 里调试；至于 IDE，我更喜欢 vscode 这种轻量一些的工具。（没错，把 vscode 称作轻量级工具确实感觉有点奇怪。）

IDE 调试器从来不会暴露全部功能；或者至少，在需要直接操作底层调试器来完成某些事情时，会让操作变得相当别扭，比如设置硬件内存观察点。如果你想编写一些自定义的临时 Python 脚本，或者向 gdb 服务器发送自定义监视器命令，那可就更惨了（例如直接与 valgrind 通信，或者通过 JTAG 与连接到微控制器上的硬件调试器通信）。

直接使用命令行调试器的“阻抗不匹配”更小，也不会妨碍你的操作。

566715120.en:
>I don't know if lldb supports that.

In terms of indexing, sortof. The visualizer scripts allow one to index using the variable display command (e.g. `v vec[1]`), but iirc it doesn't work in the expression parser (e.g. `expr vec[1]`) for (slightly stupid) reasons.

The short of it is that visualization is handled ~language-agnostically, whereas expression parsing needs a bespoke plugin for your language. LLDB's expression-parser plugin architecture is like... *really*  hands-off, for better and worse.  It literally hands you a string and the current stack frame and then waits for you to return an object that represents the result of the expression. That means you need to write literally an entire interpreter for it to work as expected. There's an example of that [here](https://github.com/tromey/lldb/tree/a0fc10ce0dacb3038b7302fff9f6cb8cb34b37c6/source/Plugins/ExpressionParser/Rust). One nice thing is it would allow us to just plug in something like MIRI, rustc itself, or [excvr](https://github.com/evcxr/evcxr) pretty easily though.

>The main issue with lldb is that it isn't ergonomic. You can see that in that gdb has all sorts of short names for common operations, like `b` to set a breakpoint, or `c` to continue. While lldb doesn't.

IIRC LLDB's commands can all be abbreviated. If the abbreviation is unambiguous, it will work. It also has a number of hard-coded abbreviations, including `b` for `breakpoint set`, `c` for `continue`, and `v` for `frame variable`, `n` for step over, `s` for step into, etc.

It also has `command alias` that allow users to specify their own command abbreviations.
566715120.zh:
>我不知道 lldb 是否支持这个。

就索引而言，算是吧。可视化脚本允许使用变量显示命令进行索引（例如 `v vec[1]`），但据我所知，在表达式解析器中（例如 `expr vec[1]`）并不能这样做，原因有点蠢。

简单来说，可视化处理基本上与语言无关，而表达式解析则需要为你的语言编写专门的插件。LLDB 的表达式解析器插件架构……怎么说呢，*真的*非常不干涉，优缺点都有。它实际上只会把一个字符串和当前栈帧交给你，然后等待你返回一个表示表达式结果的对象。这意味着，为了让它按预期工作，你实际上需要完整编写一个解释器。这里有一个示例：[https://github.com/tromey/lldb/tree/a0fc10ce0dacb3038b7302fff9f6cb8cb34b37c6/source/Plugins/ExpressionParser/Rust](https://github.com/tromey/lldb/tree/a0fc10ce0dacb3038b7302fff9f6cb8cb34b37c6/source/Plugins/ExpressionParser/Rust)。不过有一点不错：这样一来，我们就能相当容易地接入类似 MIRI、rustc 本身或 [excvr](https://github.com/evcxr/evcxr) 这样的东西。

>lldb 的主要问题在于不够符合人体工程学。你可以看看 gdb：对于常用操作，它有各种简写，比如用 `b` 设置断点，用 `c` 继续执行。而 lldb 没有这些。

据我所知，LLDB 的命令都可以使用缩写。如果缩写没有歧义，就能正常工作。它也有一些硬编码的缩写，包括用 `b` 表示 `breakpoint set`，用 `c` 表示 `continue`，用 `v` 表示 `frame variable`，用 `n` 表示单步跳过，用 `s` 表示单步进入，等等。

它还提供了 `command alias`，允许用户指定自己的命令缩写。

566716809.en:
>it would be awesome if the debugger knew how to call a `Debug` impl of a value if it can't otherwise render it nicely

Within an expression support plugin in LLDB, you can tell it how to call Rust functions, so this should be possible. I don't know if GDB has an equivalent, but i'd assume it does. One issue though is that if the debug impl is never used, iirc doesn't end up in the binary even if compiled in debug mode.

For debug impls that are in the binary though, i think you might even be able to do this right now with lldb's existing commands called from the python visualizer scripts?  `register write rcx <ptr to struct>` -> `jump <debug impl addr>` -> `thread step-out` -> `register read rax`

Saving/restoring the correct registers for the calling convention should be pretty simple, though I'm not sure exactly how you'd handle the `&mut Formatter` that needs to be passed in. I'd need to look into it more
566716809.zh:
>如果调试器在无法很好地渲染某个值时，知道如何调用该值的 `Debug` 实现，那就太棒了。

在 LLDB 的表达式支持插件中，你可以告诉它如何调用 Rust 函数，所以这应该是可行的。我不知道 GDB 是否有对应功能，不过我猜应该有。不过有一个问题：如果某个 debug 实现从未被使用过，据我所知，即使以调试模式编译，它最终也不会被放进二进制文件。

但对于已经存在于二进制文件中的 debug 实现，我觉得你甚至现在就可以借助 lldb 现有的命令，在 Python 可视化脚本中实现这一点：`register write rcx <ptr to struct>` -> `jump <debug impl addr>` -> `thread step-out` -> `register read rax`

按照调用约定保存和恢复正确的寄存器应该很简单，不过我不太确定该如何处理需要传入的 `&mut Formatter`。我得再研究一下。

The motivation was similar to https://blog.rust-lang.org/2025/09/10/rust-compiler-performance-survey-2025-results. Better understand the issues that people are having with one of the top challenges that people have with Rust.

The target audience is t-compiler, but there aren't really (m)any people working on debuginfo, so probably it will be more useful to @**Walnut356**, who is currently doing a GSoC project on debuginfo, and is very interested in it, and also t-infra/t-bootstrap, to let us know which debuggers we should support on CI.

One thing that isn't coming through in the report (and I remember writing it in a free text response or other) is that we lack support (in gdb) for replacing function calls with python code.

For example, if I have a large collection (vector, map or otherwise) and want to print a specific element I can't do `print myMap[someKeyVariable]`, while that works in C++. If the map has thousands of entries (very typical for what I work on), a visualiser is of little use.

622101490.en:
Another one from porting Linux kernel `lib/` code to Rust — smaller than the last one, and this might just be "that's how it has to work," but we wanted to ask rather than assume.

A lot of C code we're translating follows this pattern for a buffer + length pair:

while (len--) { /* use *p, then */ p++; }

When `len == 0`, this never dereferences `p` — so callers routinely pass `(NULL, 0)` to mean "empty buffer, pointer doesn't matter," and it's completely well-defined in C. Translating that pair straight into `slice::from_raw_parts(p, len)` doesn't preserve that, though — even at `len == 0`, a null `p` is UB:

unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts requires the pointer
to be aligned and non-null, and the total size of the slice not to exceed
`isize::MAX`

(silent in release, an abort with `-C debug-assertions=on`). We've found the pattern in roughly 18 already-merged files in our own port so far, from one retroactive review — we assume it's a common shape for anyone porting C buffer-handling code, not just us.

We understand *why* non-null probably matters here — references built from the result presumably want to keep the "a reference is never null" invariant for niche-optimization purposes, so this might be entirely intentional and just a case of "guard the zero-length case yourself before calling it," which is the fix we've landed on going forward. We're not sure if that's considered the expected idiom, though, or if there's a recommended alternative (a dedicated zero-length-safe constructor, a clippy lint pointing people at the guard, something else) for exactly this C-interop shape. Is this a known rough edge, or is "just guard it" genuinely the answer?

Repo (public): [github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux](https://github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux)
622101490.zh:
这是又一个将 Linux 内核 `lib/` 代码移植到 Rust 时遇到的问题——比上一个小一些，而且这可能只是“它就必须这样工作”，但我们还是想先问问，而不是直接假定。

我们正在翻译的大量 C 代码都会对缓冲区和长度这一对参数采用以下模式：

while (len--) { /* use *p, then */ p++; }

当 `len == 0` 时，代码完全不会解引用 `p`——因此调用方通常会传入 `(NULL, 0)`，表示“空缓冲区，指针无所谓”，而且这在 C 中是完全定义良好的。不过，直接将这一对参数转换为 `slice::from_raw_parts(p, len)` 并不能保留这一行为——即使 `len == 0`，`p` 为 null 仍然是未定义行为（UB）：

unsafe precondition(s) violated: slice::from_raw_parts requires the pointer
to be aligned and non-null, and the total size of the slice not to exceed
`isize::MAX`

（在 release 构建中不会有提示；启用 `-C debug-assertions=on` 时则会中止）。我们在自己的一次事后审查中发现，仅在目前已经合并的移植代码里，这种模式就出现在大约 18 个文件中——我们猜想，对于任何移植 C 缓冲区处理代码的人来说，这都是一种常见形式，而不只是我们会遇到的问题。

我们理解这里为什么可能需要非 null——由结果构造出的引用大概希望保持“引用永远不会为 null”这一不变量，以便进行 niche 优化，所以这可能完全是有意为之，确实只是“在调用它之前自行处理零长度情况”。这也是我们今后采用的修复方式。不过，我们不确定这是否算是预期的惯用写法，或者针对这种 C 互操作场景，是否有推荐的替代方案（专门对零长度情况安全的构造函数、通过 clippy lint 提醒用户加保护，或其他方案）。这是一个已知的棘手之处吗，还是说“直接加保护”确实就是答案？

仓库（公开）：[github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux](https://github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux)

622100303.en:
We've been porting parts of the Linux kernel's `lib/` to Rust, and ran into something while trying nightly (1.100.0) that we're not sure how to think about, or whether it's even the kind of thing worth raising here — happy to be redirected if there's a better venue.

Moving from 1.98.0 stable to that nightly, our link step started failing:

ld.lld: undefined symbol: fmaximum_numf, fminimum_numf, __gtsf2,
                                                     fmaximum_num,  fminimum_num,  __gtdf2

As far as we can tell, it traces to the new concrete `ClampBounds` impls for `f32`/`f64` in core/src/cmp/clamp.rs — since they're concrete rather than generic, they get codegen'd into `core` unconditionally, and they pull in soft-float runtime calls. The kernel builds `core` against a `-mmx,+soft-float` target with no float builtins supplied, so those symbols have nowhere to resolve.

We genuinely don't know whether this is expected fallout of `core` gaining float functionality that a `no_std`/no-builtins target should just route around somehow (and we're missing the right incantation), or whether it's more of an edge case nobody's hit yet. Is there a recommended pattern for soft-float freestanding targets here, or is this worth tracking as its own thing? We're currently just sitting on 1.98.0 to sidestep it, so no urgency on our end — mostly curious which direction this should go.

Repo (public): [github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux](https://github.com/handyhandymanadam/Rusty-Linux)
622100303.zh:
我们一直在把 Linux 内核的部分 `lib/` 移植到 Rust，在尝试 nightly（1.100.0）时遇到了一些问题，不太确定该如何理解，也不确定这是否属于适合在这里提出的问题——如果有更合适的渠道，也请告知。

从 1.98.0 stable 切换到该 nightly 后，链接步骤开始失败：

ld.lld: undefined symbol: fmaximum_numf, fminimum_numf, __gtsf2,
                                                     fmaximum_num,  fminimum_num,  __gtdf2

据我们目前的判断，问题源于 core/src/cmp/clamp.rs 中新增的针对 `f32`/`f64` 的具体 `ClampBounds` 实现——由于它们是具体实现而不是泛型实现，因此会被无条件地生成代码并编入 `core`，同时引入软浮点运行时调用。内核是在一个带有 `-mmx,+soft-float` 的目标上构建 `core` 的，并没有提供浮点内建函数，因此这些符号找不到解析位置。

我们确实不清楚，这是否只是 `core` 获得浮点功能后，对于应该自行绕开的 `no_std`/无内建函数目标所产生的预期后果（而我们遗漏了正确的配置方式），还是说这是一个此前没人遇到过的边缘情况。对于软浮点的裸机目标，这里是否有推荐的处理方式？还是说值得单独跟踪这个问题？目前我们只是暂时停留在 1.98.0，以避开这个问题，所以我们这边并不着急——主要是想了解这件事应该朝哪个方向处理。

621694624.en:
In [`compiler/rustc_metadata/src/locator.rs#L772`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/main/compiler/rustc_metadata/src/locator.rs#L772) rustc filters out `--extern` files  that do not match `lib*.{rmeta,rlib,rs}`.  I was trying to track down why and i think it traces back to [RFC-109](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/0109-remove-crate-id.html#naming-library-filenames).
I am wondering if it would be possible to loosen the naming requirements to not require `lib`. Would this cause issues?

For context, I've been [experimenting with content addressable storage](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/5931#issuecomment-5498506395) to deduplicate files in Cargo's cross workspace cache. I originally tried just '<HASH>' but that failed. Then I tried '<HASH>.{rmeta,rlib}' and was kind of surprised when that didn't work. I guess worst case scenario I could work around it by adding `lib<HASH>.{rmeta,rlib}` but that would hurt my soul.
621694624.zh:
在 [`compiler/rustc_metadata/src/locator.rs#L772`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/main/compiler/rustc_metadata/src/locator.rs#L772) 中，rustc 会过滤掉文件名不匹配 `lib*.{rmeta,rlib,rs}` 的 `--extern` 文件。我试着追查了一下原因，感觉这可以追溯到 [RFC-109](https://rust-lang.github.io/rfcs/0109-remove-crate-id.html#naming-library-filenames)。
我想知道，是否可以放宽命名要求，不再强制要求 `lib` 前缀？这样会带来什么问题吗？

作为背景，我最近一直在[尝试使用内容寻址存储](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/issues/5931#issuecomment-5498506395)，以便对 Cargo 的跨工作区缓存中的文件去重。我一开始只是用了 `'<HASH>'`，但没成功。后来我尝试了 `'<HASH>.{rmeta,rlib}'`，结果发现这样也不行，着实有点意外。我想最坏的情况下，我可以通过添加 `lib<HASH>.{rmeta,rlib}` 来绕过这个问题，但这会让我良心不安。

621695549.en: I think I'd prefer to only have the hash, but I could live with the file extensions.
621695549.zh: 我还是更倾向于只使用哈希值，不过保留文件扩展名我也能接受。

621718462.en: what's the issue with having the `lib` prefix?

621720957.en:
i guesss technically nothing. 
My thought was it'd be nice to avoid having to add prefixes/suffixes to files so we could have a hash and look up content without needing to be aware of the content type to add the prefix/suffixes.
621720957.zh:
严格来说，我猜其实没什么问题。
我的想法是，如果不用给文件添加前缀和后缀，而是直接使用哈希值，这样会更好：我们就可以查找内容，而不必知道内容类型，也不需要据此添加前缀和后缀。

621746119.en: Without the file extension rustc would have to try to read the file up to three times. One as rmeta, once as rlib and once as dylib. As for the prefix, this reduces the amount of files that need to be looked at for  `-Ldependency` by filtering based on filename prefix, crate name and (together with the recorded `-Cextra-filename`) suffix before the extension. This significantly cuts down the amount of candidates to be looked at. Often to just a single file.
621746119.zh: 如果没有文件扩展名，rustc 就得尝试读取该文件最多三次：一次按 rmeta 读取，一次按 rlib 读取，还有一次按 dylib 读取。至于前缀，它可以通过根据文件名前缀、crate 名称，以及扩展名前、与记录下来的 `-Cextra-filename` 一起使用的后缀进行过滤，从而减少 `-Ldependency` 需要检查的文件数量。这会大幅减少候选文件的数量，很多时候甚至只剩下一个文件。

621795061.zh: 据我所知，为了帮助使用 CAS 的构建系统，我们确实会在几个地方明确避免将符号链接解析为规范路径。

621849700.en:
It’s possible but comes with trade offs. 

Symlinks will break if the cache is moved, which I suspect will be common (e.g. storing cache on another drive) so we’d probably need to account for that.

Hardlinking would also work but make cache GC more complicated since deleting a file from the cache won’t actually save any disc space. So we’d either have to force users to manually keep cleaning up their target dirs, or have some logic that deletes all copy’s of the hardlink (which I don’t know if it would be safe to do so)
621849700.zh:
可以，但需要权衡一些问题。

如果缓存被移动，符号链接就会失效；我怀疑这种情况会很常见（比如把缓存存放在另一块驱动器上），所以我们可能需要对此加以处理。

硬链接也可以奏效，但会让缓存 GC 变得更加复杂，因为从缓存中删除文件并不会实际释放任何磁盘空间。因此，我们要么得强制用户手动持续清理各自的 target 目录，要么加入某种逻辑，把硬链接的所有副本都删除掉（但我不知道这样做是否安全）。

620216483.en:
for problem 2 (locating the same function fast): if the compiler binaries still have their symbol tables, you can go straight by symbol name
```bash
// find the symbol + its size in each binary
llvm-nm -S --size-sort binary1 | grep <fn>
llvm-nm -S --size-sort binary2 | grep <fn>

// disassembling just that symbol instead of the whole binary
llvm-objdump --disassemble-symbols=<symbol> binary1 > f1.asm
llvm-objdump --disassemble-symbols=<symbol> binary2 > f2.asm
diff -u f1.asm f2.asm
```

`--disassemble-symbols` (llvm-objdump) / `--disassemble=<symbol>` (gnu objdump) will only decode that one function instead of walking the entire `.text` section, 
which is almost certainly why full-binary `llvm-objdump` was choking.
could also wrap this in a tiny script: dump both symbol tables with `n`, intersect by name, and loop `--disassemble-symbols` + `diff` over the matches. 

for problem 1 (filtering superficial moves): bindiff, diaphora is the way (idk much about either)
620216483.zh:
针对问题 2（快速定位相同的函数）：如果编译器二进制文件仍然保留着符号表，就可以直接通过符号名来定位：
```bash
// find the symbol + its size in each binary
llvm-nm -S --size-sort binary1 | grep <fn>
llvm-nm -S --size-sort binary2 | grep <fn>

// disassembling just that symbol instead of the whole binary
llvm-objdump --disassemble-symbols=<symbol> binary1 > f1.asm
llvm-objdump --disassemble-symbols=<symbol> binary2 > f2.asm
diff -u f1.asm f2.asm
```

`--disassemble-symbols`（llvm-objdump）/ `--disassemble=<symbol>`（gnu objdump）只会解码这一个函数，而不是遍历整个 `.text` 段，这几乎肯定就是完整二进制文件上的 `llvm-objdump` 会卡住的原因。

也可以把这个过程封装进一个小脚本：用 `n` 转储两个符号表，按名称求交集，然后针对匹配到的符号循环执行 `--disassemble-symbols` + `diff`。

针对问题 1（过滤掉表面上的位置变化）：bindiff、diaphora 是正解（我对这两个工具都不太了解）。

616227738.en: We have observed that `Drop` is not invoked in a stack safe way. Since we have a clear sequence of calling `.drop()` for sub-structures, I imagine drops can be done in a stack safe way, but probably in an `unsafe` way. Has it been locked at? 616261704.en:
Are you suggesting every Drop call should use stacker?

Because that's likely to inhibit a bunch of optimisations. And counter-intuitively, it could make stack overflows more likely, if the process is almost at the top of its stack when Drop is called.

因为这很可能会妨碍一大堆优化。而且反直觉的是，如果调用 Drop 时进程已经几乎用到了栈顶，这反而可能让栈溢出更容易发生。

616295543.en: In general I see it as the responsibility of the person designing a deeply recursive data structure to implement Drop in a way that consumes bounded stack space instead of O(n), and ideally in O(1) space overall (not just shifting it around as stacker does). As dropping is a fairly constrained operation, this is generally more practical to do in O(1) extra space than for “arbitrary tree traversals that are naturally recursive”.
616295543.zh: 总的来说，我认为，设计深度递归数据结构的人有责任以一种只消耗有界栈空间的方式实现 Drop，而不是 O(n) 的栈空间；理想情况下，整体空间复杂度也应该是 O(1)，而不只是像 stacker 那样把开销转移到别处。由于析构操作受到的限制相当多，相比“天然采用递归方式的任意树遍历”，通常更容易将其实现为只使用 O(1) 额外空间。

616420975.en:
What's the minimum support from the compiler/standard library required for a crate to generically  implement this kind of shallow-stack drop?

For example, I'm imagining an algorithm / implementation scheme like:
- each deeply nested type implements an unsafe trait, let's call it `Droppable`
- the `Drop` impls of these types call `Droppable::prepare`
- which returns `Vec<* mut dyn Droppable>` for each of the shallow fields/items in the type
- these are added to a drop list, and then each of them is prepared to the next level
- finally, the drop list is actually dropped
- for ergonomics, `Droppable` can be derived, so no fields are forgotten

I think currently this doesn't work, because once you're in a drop impl, you're committed to recursively dropping all the fields/items. I guess it would work if some of those fields or items were optional, and `prepare` set them to `None` while preparing them.
616420975.zh:
编译器或标准库至少需要提供什么支持，crate 才能通用地实现这种浅栈析构？

比如，我设想的算法／实现方案大致如下：
- 每个深度嵌套的类型都实现一个 unsafe trait，姑且称为 `Droppable`
- 这些类型的 `Drop` 实现会调用 `Droppable::prepare`
- `prepare` 会为类型中的每个浅层字段／元素返回一个 `Vec<* mut dyn Droppable>`
- 将这些指针加入析构列表，然后逐层对它们执行 prepare
- 最后，真正执行析构列表中的析构操作
- 为了提升易用性，`Droppable` 可以通过派生实现，这样就不会遗漏任何字段

我认为目前这种方式行不通，因为一旦进入 drop 实现，就等于必须递归地析构所有字段／元素。我猜，如果其中一些字段或元素是可选的，并且 `prepare` 在准备它们时把它们设为 `None`，那也许就能实现。

We need a way to avoid deeply recursing through nested types, which implicitly allocates via stack frames. And we need to call drop using a depth-first traversal. (Or is that an in-order traversal? I can never remember.)

Storing your un-dropped pointers in the heap lets you traverse them in one stack frame, then traverse their children in that same stack frame using a loop.

616425464.en: doing a depth-first algorithm instead of breadth-first helps with types with many fields since you only need the fields of all your parents on the worklist rather than everything in the tree with depth <current
