616426182.zh: 基本上，可以想象一下：它把一堆“次要的” drop 实现内联进了一个更大的类型。

616426192.en: a few of these require some stack variables allocated, so it allocates all of those
616426192.zh: 其中有一些需要分配栈变量，于是它把这些变量全部分配出来。

616426226.en: and then it has to call into another implementation
616426226.zh: 然后它还得调用另一个实现。

616426251.en: and then the inlining test failed somewhere so we enter another implementation of drop that works similarly
616426251.zh: 接着某处的内联测试失败了，于是我们进入了另一个行为类似的 drop 实现。

616426325.en: so I can imagine the *practical* case is not one where *avoiding the recursiveness* is the problem, but rather where the combination of tackling both breadth and depth in a disorganized way has resulted in somewhat horrendous code
616426325.zh: 所以我可以想象，*实际*的问题并不是*避免递归*本身，而是以一种杂乱无章的方式同时处理广度和深度，最终生成了相当可怕的代码。

616426626.en: if there's enough spare space in the structs you're dropping for a pointer or two, you could make a linked list of structs to finish dropping so you wouldn't need extra space for the worklist nor extra stack space for a recursive drop
616426626.zh: 如果你要 drop 的结构体中有足够的闲置空间来放一两个指针，可以把待完成 drop 的结构体串成一个链表，这样既不需要为工作列表额外分配空间，也不需要为递归 drop 额外使用栈空间。

616426853.en: another alternative is to store all the structs in arenas and use references instead of `Box`/`Vec` for the recursive parts, that way dropping everything is really easy: the arenas just drop it all by walking through their internal arrays of structs, ignoring the recursive links completely
616426853.zh: 另一个办法是把所有结构体存放在 arena 中，并在递归部分使用引用而不是 `Box`/`Vec`。这样一来，drop 所有内容就非常简单了：arena 只需遍历其内部的结构体数组并将它们全部 drop 掉，完全忽略递归链接即可。

616426935.en: tbh that's probably the fastest method by far -- CPUs are very good at linear walks through memory
616426935.zh: 说实话，这大概是快得多的方法——CPU 非常擅长在线性地遍历内存。

```quote
a few of these require some stack variables allocated, so it allocates all of those
```

( this is my expectation primarily because I know LLVM's codegen has a preference for allocating these early if it allocates them at all. )
616437502.zh:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/616426192)：

```quote
其中有一些需要分配栈变量，于是它把这些变量全部分配出来。
```

（我主要是基于这一点做出这样的预期，因为我知道 LLVM 的代码生成器如果要分配这些变量，倾向于尽早完成分配。）

616437574.en: it then tries to do reuse of stack slots, but there are limits to that which I am much less clear on aside from our lifetime.start and lifetime.end annotations guiding that.
616437574.zh: 之后它会尝试复用栈槽，但这方面存在一些限制。除了我们的 lifetime.start 和 lifetime.end 注解会对其进行引导之外，我对这些限制就不太了解了。

616437962.en: that's why I'd be curious to see any *practical* examples, instead of just some shape with a simple "well obviously if you have a type that is nested ~~99999999999999999~~ enough times with enough indirection to hide the drop impl from inlining (and allow it to compile at all..) it can pop the stack", because I'm guessing there *might* be a better solution for the majority of cases that might technically fail an arbitrary-depth-of-recursion test by not exhausting. but maybe I'm wrong.
616437962.zh: 所以我很想看看一些*实际*的例子，而不只是某种结构配上一个简单的“显然，如果某个类型嵌套 ~~99999999999999999~~ 足够多次，并且通过足够多的间接层级来阻止 drop 实现被内联（同时还得让它能成功编译……），它就会导致栈溢出”的说法。因为我猜，对于大多数情况，也许存在更好的解决方案：它们在技术上可能会在任意递归深度测试中失败，但不会因为耗尽资源而失败。不过也可能是我错了。

617039153.en:
sorry for the late reply.

@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/616425398):
```quote
@Jason Hu "we?"
do you know of any example cases that are practical? do these fault even under optimizations?
```
well, practicality is hard to qualified. Given any AST, it is always able to construct a term that is deep enough to blow up the stack, if Drop is simply recursive.  given the knowledge that Drop is recursive, it is always possible to construct a term. 

@_**theemathas|739695** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/616233383):
```quote
How would unsafe help here? I don't quite understand what you're proposing. Are you proposing some new concrete way of running destructors in recursive data structures? If so, what is it?
```
The idea is preliminary, and I am not sure if unsafe would help. The work is done in MIR. First, we know if an enum is recursive. If so, then in MIR, there must be a call loop in Drop. We then perform a CPS transformation on this MIR call sequence to put the stress on the stack to the heap. 

Sure, this solution is messy. The best solution is, ideally, we always use green stack, i.e. heap-allocated stack. This of course is probably guarded against some compiler flag, but the advantage is also obvious: recursion no longer blows up on inputs.
617039153.zh:
抱歉回复晚了。

@_**workingjubilee|281757** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/616425398)：
```quote
@Jason Hu "we?"
你知道有哪些实际可行的例子吗？即使在优化开启的情况下，这些情况也会出错吗？
```
嗯，很难界定什么算“实际可行”。对于任意 AST，如果 `Drop` 只是递归执行的，那么总能构造出一个深度足以耗尽栈的项。既然我们知道 `Drop` 是递归的，那么总能构造出这样的项。

@_**theemathas|739695** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/616233383)：
```quote
unsafe 在这里能帮上什么忙？我不太明白你的提议。你是在提议一种新的、具体的方式来运行递归数据结构中的析构函数吗？如果是，具体是什么？
```
这个想法还只是初步设想，我也不确定 `unsafe` 是否会有帮助。相关工作是在 MIR 中完成的。首先，我们判断一个枚举是否具有递归性。如果是，那么在 MIR 中，`Drop` 里必然存在一个调用环。接着，我们对这个 MIR 调用序列执行 CPS 转换，把原本施加在栈上的压力转移到堆上。

当然，这个方案比较麻烦。理想情况下，最好的解决方案是我们始终使用 green stack，也就是分配在堆上的栈。当然，这可能需要通过某个编译器标志来控制，但它的优势也很明显：递归不再会因为输入数据而耗尽栈。

617039790.en: In general, I feel that the language should perform some help. For recursive data structure, an iterative destructor always looks similar. there really isn't a reason for boilerplate. Rust has gone far in other aspects, and missing this part appears to me rather strange.
617039790.zh: 总的来说，我觉得语言应该提供一些帮助。对于递归数据结构，迭代式析构函数通常都大同小异，确实没有理由让大家重复编写样板代码。Rust 在其他方面已经走得很远了，唯独缺少这一部分，在我看来相当奇怪。

617040272.en: I wouldn't regard stacker as a solution frankly, but I am developing something different. I will announce when it is materialized.
617040272.zh: 坦率地说，我不认为 stacker 是解决方案，不过我正在开发一些不同的东西。等它成形后我会公布。

617046332.en: one other method I saw mentioned is if you have a binary tree structure, you can linearize it by using tree rotations so you can drop all of it in a single loop without needing extra stack/heap for recursion
617046332.zh: 我看到有人提到的另一种方法是：如果你有一个二叉树结构，可以利用树旋转将其线性化，这样就能在单个循环中释放全部内容，而不需要为递归额外使用栈或堆。

````quote
We then perform a CPS transformation on this MIR call sequence to put the stress on the stack to the heap.
````

Both of these approaches involve heap allocations. It is unlikely that a *language* feature which performs implicit heap allocations would be accepted.
617060323.zh:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/617039153)：


这两种方案都涉及堆分配。让一种会隐式执行堆分配的*语言*特性被接受，可能性不大。

617060689.en: However, it occurs to me that it would be possible to offer functionality like this as a *derive macro* which derives a `Drop` impl and a supporting trait impl for the child types.
617060689.zh: 不过我突然想到，也许可以通过 *derive macro* 提供类似的功能：为子类型派生一个 `Drop` 实现以及一个配套的 trait 实现。

617060914.en: an iterative destructor generally needs heap allocations. if all users are expected to write destructors in such pattern for maximal blowup safety, I don't see why it's a bad idea for the language to take the responsibility over.
617060914.zh: 迭代式析构函数通常需要堆分配。如果为了最大限度地避免栈溢出，所有用户都必须按这种模式编写析构函数，那我不明白为什么让语言来承担这份责任会是坏事。

617061115.en: a derive could also make sense, if it can be pushed to the macro level (which I feel more comfortable injecting unsafe code during heap deallocation for performance purposes).
617061115.zh: 如果能把它放在宏层面实现，derive 也可能是个合理的选择（出于性能考虑，我觉得在堆释放期间注入 `unsafe` 代码会更让人放心）。

617063191.en:
a major reason for this to be explicit is to ensure that code can continue to work without an allocator, as necessary for no_std crates.  making a data structure potentially recursive should not *automatically require* an allocator to be present.

something like a RecursiveDropHeap derive would be more explicit about the fact that it requires the global (system?) allocator, and could be encouraged for use in alloc-present binaries, or libraries with specific purposes that already need alloc, or otherwise are expected to only be used in an alloc context.
617063191.zh:
之所以要明确 opt-in，一个主要原因是要确保代码在没有分配器的情况下仍能运行，因为这对于 no_std crate 是必要的。让一个数据结构具备潜在的递归性，不应该*自动要求*必须存在分配器。

类似 `RecursiveDropHeap` derive 的东西会更明确地表明它依赖全局（系统？）分配器，也可以鼓励在存在 alloc 的二进制程序中使用，或在本来就需要 alloc、用途明确的库中使用，或者用于那些预期只会在 alloc 上下文中使用的场景。

617353089.en:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/617324451):
```quote
do I submit a feature request on github? it seems that the derive trait is a good idea.
```

It would be a library API Change Proposal (ACP) because you would be proposing adding a new derive macro. However, there is another factor: this derive *doesn’t need* to be a standard library feature. This means that it can and *should* be developed in a library separate from the standard library. Then, once the design has been tested out in practice (does it actually solve people’s problems? is the API correct?), it could be considered for standard library inclusion.
617353089.zh:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/617324451)：
```quote
我应该在 github 上提交 feature request 吗？我觉得 derive trait 是个好主意。
```

这属于 library API Change Proposal (ACP)，因为你提议添加一个新的 derive macro。不过还有一个因素：这个 derive *不需要*成为标准库特性。这意味着它可以、也*应该*在标准库之外的独立库中开发。之后，等这个设计在实践中经过验证（它是否真的解决了人们的问题？API 是否合理？），再考虑将其纳入标准库。

617795372.en: if you want to use deep stack recursion because you're a functional programmer type person and you can't wait for `become` then you make the stack bigger

617796247.en: My ultimate practicality requires (1) mutually recursive data types, and (2) type-level fixed point operator, or in more cryptic categorical term, a polynomial functor, c.f. https://docs.rs/yaspar-ir/latest/yaspar_ir/ast/alg/enum.Term.html . Ideally, `#[derive(RecursiveDrop)]`would correctly drop any instance of this type (or maybe this derive alone is not enough? I am not sure at this moment).
617796247.zh: 对我来说，真正实用的方案需要：（1）相互递归的数据类型；（2）类型级别的定点算子，或者用更晦涩的范畴论术语来说，就是多项式函子，参见 https://docs.rs/yaspar-ir/latest/yaspar_ir/ast/alg/enum.Term.html 。理想情况下，`#[derive(RecursiveDrop)]` 应该能够正确释放这种类型的任意实例（不过也许光靠这个 derive 还不够？我目前还不确定）。

617796824.en: I frankly think that this problem has something to do with how much ambient typed information we can fetch during the derive. If the current rustc architecture only permits purely syntactic, untyped transformation, I am convinced that little can be done.
617796824.zh: 坦率地说，我认为这个问题与我们在 derive 期间能够获取多少环境中的类型信息有关。如果当前 rustc 架构只允许进行纯粹的语法层面、无类型信息的转换，那我确信能做的事情非常有限。

617801260.zh: 我正在实现一个 CPS 转换过程宏，用来将所有一般递归转换为迭代。我正在走开源流程。我认为这至少可以为如何实现安全的 drop 提供一些经验。等真正完成开源后，我会回来汇报。

621215779.en:
The open source process has finally gone through, and a crate is published: https://docs.rs/crate/yaspar-macros/latest

TLDR;
> Tag all your recursive functions with `#[stack_safe]` and enjoy stack-overflow freedom! The transformation is **almost** zero-cost!
> 
> Caveats:
> 
> 1. Trait impls cannot get involved in recursion.
> 2. Certain recursive styles require special unsafe options, which are documented in the page above.
621215779.zh:
开源流程终于完成了，现在已经发布了一个 crate：https://docs.rs/crate/yaspar-macros/latest

简而言之：
> 给所有递归函数加上 `#[stack_safe]`，从此不再担心栈溢出！这种转换几乎**零成本**！
>
> 注意事项：
>
> 1. trait impl 不能参与递归。

621286708.en: JSON is a good example of another point, too: it’s not enough to be able to drop the deeply recursive value without stack overflow, you also have to be able to do the actual work you wanted to do on it. If that’s naturally recursive too, then you need to rewrite all of that other code too, or you’ll get stack overflows before you even get to drop the values. For JSON processing there’s usually a ton of different application specific code by various authors, which means you can’t just fix the five or ten places that are exposed to the recursion, so a depth limit is an extremely reasonable default.
621286708.zh: JSON 还是另一个很好的例子：能够在不栈溢出的情况下释放深度递归的值还不够，你还必须能够对它执行你真正想做的操作。如果这些操作本身也天然具有递归性，那么你还得重写其他所有相关代码，否则甚至还没开始释放这些值，就会先发生栈溢出。对于 JSON 处理，通常有大量由不同作者编写的、特定于应用的代码，这意味着你不能只修复暴露递归的五到十个地方，所以将深度限制作为默认设置是非常合理的。

You've demonstrated that a crate can solve it *without* the compiler, too.
So why does it need to be in the compiler?

If the aim is to automatically apply this transform (something only the compiler can do), then:
- [the drop order changes](https://github.com/yaspar-org/yaspar-macros/blob/main/README.md#limitations) are a blocker
- automatically transforming unsafe code could cause unsoundness
- adding to heap usage might not be desirable (or possible, as Vorpal said)
- performance could be impacted

If the aim is to add an attribute/macro to the compiler (or the standard library), then the bar is high. The feature needs to do things that can only be done in the compiler / standard library, or extend standard library types (or traits/lang items, in this case). Otherwise "just use the crate" will be the answer.

But all those decisions might not need to be made yet.

If you're looking at the compiler, then the process would be a lang experiment:
https://lang-team.rust-lang.org/how_to/experiment.html

For the standard library, the first step is a design iteration discussion: https://std-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/development/feature-lifecycle.html#suitability-for-the-standard-library

There's also a note at the top of that page about focusing on real problems people are encountering. Do you have data on how prevalent stack overflows are in practice in Rust?

- [drop 顺序的变化](https://github.com/yaspar-org/yaspar-macros/blob/main/README.md#limitations) 是一个阻碍；
- 自动转换 unsafe 代码可能导致不健全；

- 性能可能会受到影响。

不过，所有这些决策也许还不必现在就做出。

```quote
That is an interesting example crate, but the docs immediately talk about the heap. How would this work in no-std (which I presume would be desirable for a compiler based implementation)?
```

Stack frame needs to come from somewhere. If system stack size is fixed, then it needs to come from somewhere else. For no-std, I can only think of two solutions:

1. Define your own allocator or memory management mechanism that can consume all memory physically possible. 
2. Bound your recursion depths as @**Hanna Kruppe** mentioned.

However, I would raise a point that, for many applications, a recursion bound is a simple idea but not necessarily a good solution. The root problem in this discussion is how to resolve a fixed stack size from the ambient environment setup, let it be your OS or your embedded system. Again, it is the stack size that is bound. A limit on the recursion depths is only an abstraction. Each recursion could have a different frame size, and the same recursion depth might or might not cause stack overflow depending on its initial call sites. In practical, blowing up stack with the same data in different call sites might be rare, but not entirely impossible. The right solution should be a peace in mind. The only limitation should be how much memory you have.

If anyone has ideas about how to make no-std work, I am happy to incorporate.
621481350.zh:
@_**Vorpal|743310** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621296831)：
```quote
这是一个很有意思的示例 crate，但文档一上来就谈到了堆。在 no-std 中这要怎么实现？（我猜对于基于编译器的实现来说，这应该是比较理想的方案？）
```

栈帧总得从某个地方来。如果系统栈大小是固定的，那就只能从别的地方来。对于 no-std，我只能想到两种解决方案：

1. 定义自己的分配器或内存管理机制，以便消耗物理上可用的全部内存。
2. 像 @**Hanna Kruppe** 提到的那样，对递归深度设定上限。

不过我想指出的是，对于很多应用来说，限制递归深度虽然简单，但未必是个好方案。这场讨论的根本问题在于：如何解决由外围环境设置所决定的固定栈大小问题，无论这个环境是操作系统还是嵌入式系统。再说一次，受到限制的是栈大小。限制递归深度只是一种抽象。每次递归所需的栈帧大小可能不同，因此相同的递归深度是否会导致栈溢出，取决于它最初的调用位置。在实践中，相同数据从不同调用位置触发栈溢出的情况可能很少见，但并非完全不可能。正确的解决方案应该让人安心。唯一的限制应该是你拥有多少内存。

如果有人知道如何让 no-std 正常工作，我很乐意将其纳入进来。

621486395.en:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621481350):
```quote
However, I would raise a point that, for many applications, a recursion bound is a simple idea but not necessarily a good solution.
```

I don't think unlimited size queues or channels is a good idea in general in any serious program. It is too easy to end up in resource exhaustion. This is why you use back pressure in concurrent systems, rather than unlimited queues. The same goes for stack usage. You shouldn't build unlimited recursive data structures in the first place. You have the wrong abstraction. Or you didn't validate the depth of your untrusted input.

By the time you hit stack overflow it is already too late, your design should have prevented it in the first place.
621486395.zh:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621481350)：
```quote
不过我想指出的是，对于很多应用来说，限制递归深度虽然简单，但未必是个好方案。
```

我认为，在任何严肃的程序中，无限制大小的队列或 channel 通常都不是个好主意。它们太容易导致资源耗尽了。这就是为什么在并发系统中要使用背压，而不是无限制的队列。栈的使用也是同理。你一开始就不应该构造无限递归的数据结构。说明你选错了抽象，或者没有验证不可信输入的深度。

等到发生栈溢出时，一切都已经太迟了；你的设计本来就应该从一开始避免这种情况。

621487798.en:
@**teor** I don't mean it's compiler's sole responsibility. I think I would rephrase it a bit: providing a universal solution to stack overflow requires significant inputs from the compiler. What the crate does at this moment is somewhere in the middle; it is what a proc-macro can do the best for the few iterations I did. 

What I demonstrated in the crate is, that this is purely a program transformation problem. However, in practice, this is more than a **syntactic** transformation problem, due to how much information a proc-macro is exposed to. All the limitations or caveats the crate has can be resolved if the compiler provides that information. For example, to address the drop order issue, the transformation algorithm needs to know the drop order prior to the transformation, and then drop calls can be inserted in that exact order. This information, of course, cannot be obtained at this moment in a proc-macro. Hence this is a compiler limitation.  

I am not saying the compiler should always perform this transformation. This is not the message I am trying to convey. What I am trying to explain here, is that the compiler should (and must) do something to enable a fully generalized, graceful solution to this problem. It is OK to let a separate crate to do the job (and it's OK to not be part of stdlib too), but the compiler so far lacks functionality to resolve this problem.

Coming back to the title, what can I do if the compiler is not helping me to prevent stack overflow from drop calls? Drop calls are largely inserted by the compiler, but the compiler goes hands-off when an automatically generated and inserted function blows up my stack? This doesn't sound right.
621487798.zh:
@**teor** 我并不是说这完全是编译器的责任。我想稍微换一种说法：要提供一个通用的栈溢出解决方案，需要编译器提供大量支持。这个 crate 目前所做到的处于两者之间；就我做过的几轮尝试而言，这是 proc-macro 能做到的最佳程度。

我在这个 crate 中展示的是，这纯粹是一个程序变换问题。然而在实践中，由于 proc-macro 能够获取的信息非常有限，这不仅仅是一个**语法上的**变换问题。如果编译器能够提供这些信息，crate 目前的所有限制或注意事项都可以得到解决。例如，为了解决丢弃顺序的问题，变换算法需要在变换之前知道丢弃顺序，然后就可以按照完全相同的顺序插入 drop 调用。当然，这些信息目前无法在 proc-macro 中获取。因此，这是编译器的限制。

我并不是说编译器应该总是执行这种变换。这不是我想传达的意思。我想说明的是，编译器应该（也必须）做些什么来支持一个完全通用且优雅地解决这个问题的方案。让一个独立的 crate 来完成这项工作是可以的（不放进 stdlib 也没问题），但到目前为止，编译器缺少解决这个问题所需的功能。

回到标题：如果编译器不帮我避免由 drop 调用导致的栈溢出，我能怎么办？drop 调用很大程度上是由编译器插入的，可当某个自动生成并插入的函数撑爆我的栈时，编译器却撒手不管了？这听起来不太对。

````quote
However, I would raise a point that, for many applications, a recursion bound is a simple idea but not necessarily a good solution.

I don't think unlimited size queues or channels is a good idea in general in any serious program. It is too easy to end up in resource exhaustion. This is why you use back pressure in concurrent systems, rather than unlimited queues. The same goes for stack usage. You shouldn't build unlimited recursive data structures in the first place. You have the wrong abstraction. Or you didn't validate the depth of your untrusted input.

By the time you hit stack overflow it is already too late, your design should have prevented it in the first place.
````

I wouldn't really go this far in a discussion. A universal argument against a deep recursion without considering the actual problem is unfruitful. I am not looking into a problem just because it's there. Drop call stack overflow is a problem many have hit and wonder a solution to. A search on the internet reveals tons on reddit, dated back many years ago. The little support in compiler to resolve this issue is surprising to me. 

Your parallel to concurrency also makes little sense. Job queue implies limited CPU resources, which could lead to problems like starvation; it's a resource management problem. But recursion has nothing to do with resources. It is a mathematically graceful style to organize programs, nothing more and nothing less. It ought to be a choice, if the ambient system permits. Stack overflow is just a side product, a limitation due to the ambient environment, and there is a solution to it, which I have demonstrated. If the claim is that a stack overflow implies a bad design, then does a long running loop imply one as well? I could have hand translate a stack overflowing recursion into a long running loop. They are equivalent.

In practice, our program needs to accommodate user inputs as much as possible. If we were to give a bound on user inputs, it should be for some explainable business reason, not "sorry, our system only allocates 4MB stack size, so we don't allow you to build a term over a 128 depth".

````quote
等到发生栈溢出时，一切都已经太迟了；你的设计本来就应该从一开始避免这种情况。
````

在讨论中，我不会把话说得这么绝对。不考虑实际问题就笼统地反对深度递归，是没有意义的。我并不是因为某个问题客观存在，就专门去研究它。由 drop 调用导致的栈溢出，是很多人都遇到过、也一直想找到解决方案的问题。网上一搜就能发现 Reddit 上有大量相关讨论，最早的甚至可以追溯到很多年前。编译器在解决这个问题上的支持如此之少，令我感到惊讶。

你拿并发来类比也不太恰当。作业队列意味着 CPU 资源是有限的，这可能导致饥饿之类的问题；这是一个资源管理问题。但递归与资源无关。递归是一种在数学上很优雅的程序组织方式，仅此而已。只要外围系统允许，它就应该成为一种可供选择的方式。栈溢出只是副作用，是外围环境带来的限制；而这个问题是有解决方案的，我已经演示过了。如果说栈溢出意味着设计不佳，那么长时间运行的循环是不是也意味着设计不佳？我完全可以手动把一个会导致栈溢出的递归改写成长时间运行的循环。两者是等价的。

在实践中，我们的程序需要尽可能适应用户输入。如果要对用户输入设定上限，也应该出于某个可以解释的业务原因，而不是说“抱歉，我们的系统只分配了 4MB 的栈空间，所以不允许你构造深度超过 128 的项”。

I would suggest defining the minimal necessary compiler features to achieve what you want, for example:
- [Control over drop semantics project goal](https://goals.rust-lang.org/2026/manually-drop-attr.html) - if it does what you need
- full detection of recursive calls
- macro-generated unique names
- panic elision
- *anything else you need*

Then asking what's already available, what's in development, and what would be accepted as an experiment.

To be honest, I find the docs hard to summarise, because they are very verbose, and low-information. (Or low in relevant information density.)
621505691.zh:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621487798)：

```quote
……
我并不是说编译器应该总是执行这种转换。这不是我想要表达的意思。我想说明的是，编译器应该（也必须）做些什么，来支持一个完全通用且优雅地解决这一问题的方案。让单独的 crate 来完成这项工作是可以的（不属于标准库也没关系），但到目前为止，编译器缺少解决这个问题所需的功能。
```

621518777.en:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621490885):
```quote
If the claim is that a stack overflow implies a bad design, then does a long running loop imply one as well?
```

Depending on the problem domain, yes. My background is in hard realtime software, and recursion (especially unbounded) in that domain is just a no-go. But even looking at other fields I have worked in, such as writing reliable high performance server software it is not desirable.

What about single user programs? Well, again my experience is that when I have come across deeply recursive data structures that my representation has been wrong. For example when dealing with ASTs, flattening the structure according to data oriented design principled has resulted in a faster program than a pointer chasing recursive structure. And dropping then is just dropping the underlying Vec or arena, which is no longer recursive. It becomes at worst linear complexity in time and constant in RAM usage (and if drop is trivial, the time can also be constant complexity).

Just because you have something that is logically recursive doesn't mean that it has to be structurally recursive. And on modern CPUs with cache the linearised approach is genrally superior thanks to better prefetching.
621518777.zh:
@_**Jason Hu|320010** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621490885)：
```quote
如果说栈溢出意味着设计不佳，那么长时间运行的循环是不是也意味着设计不佳？
```

这取决于问题领域，答案是肯定的。我的背景是硬实时软件，在这个领域，递归（尤其是无界递归）是绝对不可接受的。但即使放眼我工作过的其他领域，比如编写可靠的高性能服务器软件，递归也并不理想。

那单用户程序呢？嗯，根据我的经验，当我遇到深度递归的数据结构时，通常意味着我的表示方式有问题。例如，在处理 AST 时，按照面向数据设计的原则将结构扁平化，得到的程序往往比使用指针追踪的递归结构更快。而此时的丢弃只需要丢弃底层的 Vec 或 arena，结构本身不再是递归的。最坏情况下，它的时间复杂度是线性的，RAM 占用是常数级的（如果 drop 很简单，时间复杂度也可以是常数级的）。

某个东西在逻辑上具有递归性，并不意味着它在结构上也必须是递归的。而且在带缓存的现代 CPU 上，线性化方案通常由于预取效果更好，性能也更优。

621522305.en: I agree with most of what you said about practice, Vorpal. Recursion is nevertheless an elegant model. A lot of time, an iterative algorithm is not necessarily natural either.  Again, it is not one or another. We can have the best of both worlds: an automatic transformation is here, turning recursive functions into iterative ones. Deep recursion = long iteration. It is healthy mental model + good performance. My empirical study shows that, a stack_safe transformed program can perform slightly better than the original recursive function, and win over an iterative rewrite by a clear margin.
621522305.zh: 我同意你所说的大部分实践方面的观点，Vorpal。不过，递归仍然是一种优雅的模型。很多时候，迭代算法也不一定自然。再说，这并不是非此即彼。我们可以两者兼得：现在已经有一种自动转换，可以把递归函数转换为迭代函数。深度递归 = 长时间迭代。既符合良好的心智模型，又有良好的性能。我的实证研究表明，经过 stack_safe 转换的程序，性能可以略优于原始递归函数，并且明显胜过手写的迭代版本。

621525443.en:
Recursion is an elegant mathematical model on paper, sure. But code is not math. Code is engineering, which is all about being practical, within whatever constraints you have. (No, I could never get along with Haskell, I tried, but all the books just get lost in endless abstractions like applicative functors or whatever.) 

I agree with teor above. It is better to look at what fundamental feature are needed to be able to write such a transform outside of std reliably. To me this feature really is a bit of a code smell, but sometimes the engineering constraints you operate in are that you don't have time to fix that code smell right now. So it is a useful, if temporary, bandaid. Of course, if it is temporary and it works...
621525443.zh:
递归在纸面上确实是一种优雅的数学模型。但代码不是数学。代码是工程，而工程最重要的就是在各种约束条件下讲求实用。（不，我始终没法喜欢 Haskell。我试过，但那些书总是陷入 applicative functors 之类没完没了的抽象中。）

我同意上面 teor 的观点。更好的做法是先研究：要具备哪些基础功能，才能在标准库之外可靠地编写这种转换。对我来说，这个功能确实有点像代码异味，但有时你所面临的工程约束就是眼下没有时间修复这个代码异味。所以它虽然是临时的创可贴，却仍然有用。当然，前提是它确实是临时的，而且确实能正常工作……

621526578.en:
@**teor** It also really depends on what your question is. If the question is about how to prevent Drop from causing stack overflow, then I am not sure Control over Drop is the way to go for the drop problem alone. In general, a recursive data's drop requires touch data as large as its size, so an iterative version of drop should also be able to keep track of all data too. The crux is the size of data is unknown without a thorough traversal, so some memory allocation is needed to maintain dynamic data structure.  

However, the way I see this drop problem, is that it is not different from tackling stack overflow due to any recursion. Ideally, the transformation is the best performed on MIR. This is the timing where all resolution has happened. Here, a CPS transformation is the most accurate and the guarantee of program equivalence is the easiest.

I see that's probably not possible for what rustc is today. The next best solution is the perform the transformation on type-checked HIR. In general, to perform accurate transformation, both type and borrow information needs to be available. To name a few:
1. Name resolution. This is to handle trait impls, where `Trait::<S>foo` and `Trait::<T>foo` are distinguished. Fully detection of recursive call sites also requires this.
2. Life time information. This is to maintain drop order consistency.
3. Access to all function bodies. This is to handle recursions in lambda expressions passed into other function bodies.
621526578.zh:
@**teor** 这也确实取决于你问的是什么。如果你的问题是如何避免 Drop 导致栈溢出，那么我不确定 Control over Drop 是否是单独针对 drop 问题的正确方向。一般来说，递归数据的 drop 需要触及与其大小相当的数据，因此，迭代版本的 drop 也应该能够记录所有这些数据。关键在于，不经过彻底遍历就无法得知数据的大小，所以需要分配一些内存来维护动态数据结构。

不过，在我看来，这个 drop 问题与处理任何由递归导致的栈溢出并没有区别。理想情况下，转换最好在 MIR 上进行。这时所有解析工作都已经完成；在这一层，CPS 转换最为准确，也最容易保证程序等价性。

我看这对如今的 rustc 来说可能还做不到。下一个最佳方案是在完成类型检查的 HIR 上执行转换。一般来说，要进行准确的转换，必须能够获取类型和借用信息。举几个例子：
1. 名称解析。这是为了处理 trait impl，因为需要区分 `Trait::<S>foo` 和 `Trait::<T>foo`。要完整检测递归调用点，也需要这一点。
2. 生命周期信息。这是为了保持 drop 顺序的一致性。
3. 访问所有函数体。这是为了处理传递给其他函数体的 lambda 表达式中的递归。

621551066.en:
> Recursion is an elegant mathematical model on paper, sure. But code is not math. Code is engineering

I think you can frame both of these positions as being engineering ones. Handling unbounded recursion via allocation is the engineering position of "The program should complete its work if the memory required fits in available memory, without needing to transform every tree-traversing algorithm or tune the stack size". And, in fact, `rustc` does this with `stacker`. A difference in context that this is a reasonable option for “trusted input” batch jobs, whereas strictly bounded resource consumption is important for "untrusted input", servers, and real-time applications.
621551066.zh:
> 递归在纸面上确实是一种优雅的数学模型。但代码不是数学。代码是工程

我认为，这两种立场都可以看作是工程立场。通过分配内存来处理无界递归，体现的是这样一种工程观点：“只要所需内存能够装入可用内存，程序就应该能够完成工作，而不需要转换每一个遍历树的算法，也不需要调整栈大小。”事实上，`rustc` 已经通过 `stacker` 这么做了。区别在于具体场景：对于处理“受信任输入”的批处理任务，这是一种合理的选择；而对于“未受信任输入”、服务器和实时应用，严格限制资源消耗则很重要。

621551159.en: Also, Rust already has a thing *like* a CPS transform built in: `async`.
621551159.zh: 另外，Rust 已经内置了一个*类似于* CPS 转换的东西：`async`。

621551283.en: If you write your recursive code as `async fn`s, you are forced to insert `Box`es wherever they are needed to prevent unbounded “stack” usage.
621551283.zh: 如果你把递归代码写成 `async fn`，那么为了防止无界的“栈”使用量，你就必须在需要的地方插入 `Box`。

621551516.en: This is often a bad idea, today, because the `async` transform has situations where it [uses exponentially more memory than necessary](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/62958), but that’s a performance bug that can and should be fixed for the benefit of all async code.
621551516.zh: 如今这么做往往不是个好主意，因为 `async` 转换在某些情况下会使用远超必要量的内存（见 [https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/62958](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/62958)），但这是一个为了所有 async 代码的利益而应该修复的性能 bug。

621552314.en: I agree that handling general recursion precisely requires what async transformation would require. if all information from async is provided, then what i am trying to do here is trivial. the current barrier is really missing type information. but I don't think any box is necessary, other than a fixed number of vec's, all bound by the depths of recursion.
621552314.zh: 我同意，要精确处理一般递归，就需要 async 转换所需的那些信息。如果 async 的所有信息都能提供，那么我在这里想做的事情就很简单了。当前真正的障碍是缺少类型信息。但我认为除了固定数量的 vec 之外，并不需要任何 box；这些 vec 的数量都由递归深度限制。

621552427.en: Yes, I should say, you’re not forced to use `Box` *specifically*; you could use a growable arena. `Box` is just the *simplest* thing that breaks recursion turning into infinite type size, and is common practice in async code that needs it but isn’t concerned with high performance.
621552427.zh: 是的，我应该说清楚：你并不是非得使用 `Box`；也可以使用可增长的 arena。`Box` 只是最简单的办法，它能打破递归，避免类型大小无限增长；对于需要这种处理、但不关注高性能的 async 代码来说，这也是常见做法。

```quote
o be able to drop the deeply recursive value without stack overflow, you also have to be able to do the actual work you wanted to do on it. If that’s naturally recursive too, then you need to rewrite all of that other code too, or you’ll get stack overflows before you even get to drop the values. For JSON processing there’s usually a ton of different application specific code by various authors, which means you can’t just fix the five or ten places that are exposed to the recursion, so a depth limit is an extremely reasonable default.
```

The point I want to make is: I can take care of doing all the processing in a iterative, rather than recursive manner, but I cannot take care of `Drop` as that's a built-in thing.
621605376.zh:
@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Drop.20causes.20stack.20overflow.20for.20deeply.20nested.20data.20structures/near/621286708)：
```quote
要想在不发生栈溢出的情况下释放这个递归层级很深的值，你还得能够以同样的方式完成原本想对它执行的实际操作。如果那部分操作本身也是自然递归的，那么你还得把其他所有相关代码也重写掉，否则还没开始释放这些值，就会先发生栈溢出。对于 JSON 处理来说，通常会有大量由不同作者编写的、特定于应用的代码，这意味着你不能只修复暴露在递归面前的五处或十处代码，所以将深度限制作为默认值是非常合理的。
```

我想表达的重点是：我可以负责以迭代而非递归的方式完成所有处理，但我没法处理 `Drop`，因为那是内置机制。

621682781.en:
I’m not sure what you mean by “built-in”. The `impl Drop for Value`, if any, is library code in serde_json. There is compiler generated drop glue that can recurse, but this can be defused by doing the (iterative) dropping in `impl Drop` while replacing `*self` with a simple value for which the drop glue won’t recurse.

It’s true that you can’t write that `impl Drop` in another library, but the same is true for every other operation implemented in serde_json — in general you need the library’s cooperation for handling deeply nested values without stack overflow. In this particular case, since it’s a fully public enum, you can probably do whatever you need without running any serde_json code (e.g., you can side-step the recursive drop problem for any type of your own that owns a `Value`). But if the type is more opaque, you probably have a similar problem for both Drop and for other APIs that can’t be implemented outside the library. For example, if the `PartialEq` or `Debug` impl for nested Values overflows the stack, you also can’t fix that from the outside, other than by avoiding it and re-implementing it iteratively, which is only possible for `Value` because it doesn’t hide any variants/fields/other types that could be involved in the recursion.
621682781.zh:
我不太确定你说的“内置”是什么意思。即使存在 `impl Drop for Value`，它也是 serde_json 中的库代码。确实有编译器生成的 drop glue 可能会递归，但可以通过在 `impl Drop` 中执行迭代式释放，同时将 `*self` 替换成一个不会触发递归 drop glue 的简单值，来避免这个问题。

确实，你无法在另一个库中编写那个 `impl Drop`，但 serde_json 中实现的其他所有操作也都是如此——一般来说，要处理深度嵌套的值而不发生栈溢出，都需要库本身的配合。就这个具体情况而言，由于它是一个完全公开的枚举，你大概可以在不运行任何 serde_json 代码的情况下完成所需操作（例如，对于任何持有 `Value` 的自定义类型，你都可以绕开递归释放的问题）。但如果这个类型更加不透明，那么对于 Drop 以及其他无法在库外实现的 API，你可能都会遇到类似的问题。比如，如果嵌套 `Value` 的 `PartialEq` 或 `Debug` 实现导致栈溢出，那么除了避开它并以迭代方式重新实现之外，你也无法从外部修复；而之所以对 `Value` 可行，只是因为它没有隐藏任何可能参与递归的变体、字段或其他类型。

621684895.en: Ah, per https://github.com/serde-rs/json/issues/440 it would be semver breaking for serde_json to add a `impl Drop for Value`. Unfortunate. But also doesn’t need compiler magic to *rewrite the drop glue*, if we want to enable serde_json to fix this we can discuss ways to make the impl non-breaking. And avoiding running the `Value` drop glue should still be an option for libraries that wrap/use serde_json (it’s hard to get 100% right and test, but not fundamentally less possible than eliminating all other arbitrary recursion).
621684895.zh: 啊，根据 https://github.com/serde-rs/json/issues/440，serde_json 添加 `impl Drop for Value` 会造成 semver 破坏，属于不兼容变更。真遗憾。不过，如果我们希望让 serde_json 能够修复这个问题，也不需要编译器魔法来“重写 drop glue”——我们可以讨论如何让这个实现不破坏兼容性。而且，对于那些封装或使用 serde_json 的库来说，避免运行 `Value` 的 drop glue 仍然应该是一个可行选项（要做到 100% 正确并完成测试确实很难，但从根本上说，这并不比消除其他所有任意递归更不可能）。

613817866.zh:

613940777.en:
The CRATE_HASH regex in compiletest doesn't care about the length, so it's only triggered in specific circumstances:
- the compiletest regex doesn't match
  - compiletest seems to match the UI test "crate" disambiguator reliably, but not other positions like Type<alloc[hex chars]::Box>
- the UI test uses v0 demangling
- the UI test uses a custom normalization regex that expects exactly 16 hex characters
- the crate disambiguator is 15 characters (happens on 1/16 changes to each crate hash)

It's possible it was dismissed as a spurious failure, and then a subsequent rollup modified the crate hash so it had 16 characters again. It's also possible no tests existed that triggered it until I added this line:
https://github.com/teor2345/rust/blob/511d2920c48fac1afc67b628a5b5125c880f243b/tests/ui/splat/splat-mangling.rs#L185

It's also possible we changed LowerHex formatting to omit leading zeroes at some point. Or omit a single leading zero. (If it was only omitting leading zero *bytes*, then it would only happen in 1/256 changes to the crate hash.)
613940777.zh:
compiletest 中的 CRATE_HASH 正则表达式并不在意长度，所以它只会在特定情况下触发：
- compiletest 正则表达式匹配不上
  - compiletest 似乎能可靠地匹配 UI 测试中的 “crate” 消歧标识，但匹配不了其他位置，例如 Type<alloc[十六进制字符]::Box>
- UI 测试使用了 v0 反混淆
- UI 测试使用了要求恰好 16 个十六进制字符的自定义规范化正则表达式
- crate 消歧标识有 15 个字符（每次 crate 哈希发生变化时，有 1/16 的概率出现这种情况）

也有可能它被当成了偶发性失败而忽略了，随后某次 rollup 又修改了 crate 哈希，使它重新变成了 16 个字符。也有可能在我添加下面这行之前，根本没有能触发它的测试：
https://github.com/teor2345/rust/blob/511d2920c48fac1afc67b628a5b5125c880f243b/tests/ui/splat/splat-mangling.rs#L185

还有一种可能是，我们在某个时候修改了 LowerHex 的格式化，使其省略前导零，或者只省略一个前导零。（如果它只省略前导零字节，那么每次 crate 哈希发生变化时，只有 1/256 的概率出现这种情况。）

613950551.en:
Your example uses padding, rustc-demangle doesn't currently: https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/blob/f36e2988643d7db47a6aa6e328cc7ffd61343651/src/v0.rs#L808

So it would be useful to know if unpadded `LowerHex for u64` has recently started leaving out leading zero hex digits, or changed from leaving out leading zero bytes to leaving out a single leading zero hex digit. (Some hex formatting implementations are per-byte rather than per-nibble.)
613950551.zh:
你的示例使用了填充，但 rustc-demangle 目前没有使用：https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/blob/f36e2988643d7db47a6aa6e328cc7ffd61343651/src/v0.rs#L808

所以，弄清楚未填充的 `LowerHex for u64` 是否最近才开始省略前导零十六进制数字，或者是否从省略前导零字节变成了只省略一个前导零十六进制数字，会很有帮助。（有些十六进制格式化实现是按字节处理的，而不是按半字节处理。）

613950627.en: It's also possible the formatter hasn't changed, and our test coverage just wasn't good enough to reliably catch this.
613950627.zh: 也有可能格式化器从未改变，只是我们的测试覆盖率不够好，没能可靠地捕获这个问题。

@_**teor|325209** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950551):
```quote
So it would be useful to know if unpadded `LowerHex for u64` has recently started leaving out leading zero hex digits, or changed from leaving out leading zero bytes to leaving out a single leading zero hex digit. (Some hex formatting implementations are per-byte rather than per-nibble.)
```

in that case idk why you think it's broken, it always leaves out leading zeros (as intended) if you don't ask for padding (unless the whole value is `0`).
613963962.zh:
@_**teor|325209** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950551)：
```quote
所以，弄清楚未填充的 `LowerHex for u64` 是否最近才开始省略前导零十六进制数字，或者是否从省略前导零字节变成了只省略一个前导零十六进制数字，会很有帮助。（有些十六进制格式化实现是按字节处理的，而不是按半字节处理。）
```

既然这样，我就不知道你为什么觉得它坏了；如果你不要求填充，它本来就总是会省略前导零（除非整个值是 `0`）。

613998595.en:
@_**teor|325209** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950551):
```quote
rustc-demangle doesn't currently: https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/blob/f36e2988643d7db47a6aa6e328cc7ffd61343651/src/v0.rs#L808
```

yeah, that's just wrong, it depends on the surrounding code to be setting up the `Formatter` properly to include zero padding and set the width (and if it is set properly for the crate hash, it's almost certainly set improperly for other parts that you want to format (e.g. strings or decimal numbers)).
613998595.zh:
@_**teor|325209** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950551)：
```quote
rustc-demangle 目前没有使用：[https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/blob/f36e2988643d7db47a6aa6e328cc7ffd61343651/src/v0.rs#L808](https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/blob/f36e2988643d7db47a6aa6e328cc7ffd61343651/src/v0.rs#L808)
```

对，那确实不对；它依赖周围的代码正确设置 `Formatter`，以包含零填充并设置宽度（而且即使 crate 哈希的设置完全正确，你想要格式化的其他部分，例如字符串或十进制数字，也几乎肯定会被设置得不正确）。

614462818.en:
@_**teor|325209** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950627):
```quote
It's also possible the formatter hasn't changed, and our test coverage just wasn't good enough to reliably catch this.
```

That's it, there weren't any tests that formatted the crate hash in rustc-demangle until this PR:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/pull/94#issuecomment-5175108604

And our CI mostly normalises crate hashes of any length, so we have very few tests that require them to be 16 characters. Add to that a 1/16 probability of the bug on each crate hash change (which is rare), and I can see why we didn't catch this.
614462818.zh:
@_**teor|325209** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/crate.20disambiguator.20drops.20leading.20zeroes.20in.20demangling/near/613950627)：
```quote
也有可能格式化器从未改变，只是我们的测试覆盖率不够好，没能可靠地捕获这个问题。
```

就是这样，在这个 PR 之前，rustc-demangle 中根本没有测试会格式化 crate 哈希：
https://github.com/rust-lang/rustc-demangle/pull/94#issuecomment-5175108604

而且我们的 CI 基本上会把任意长度的 crate 哈希都规范化，因此要求它们必须是 16 个字符的测试非常少。再加上每次 crate 哈希发生变化时，这个 bug 只有 1/16 的概率出现（而 crate 哈希的变化并不常见），我能理解为什么我们之前没发现它。

620917525.en:
The infra team wants to remove all individual and team ownership from `rust-lang` crates.io crates, to reduce the attack surface of someone's account being compromised. The idea is that we will:
- Enable trusted publishing for these crates, so that they can only be published from CI of their repositories.
- Remove all team and individual access, so that only `rust-lang-owner` actually owns the crate on crates.io.
- Track which teams (virtually) "own" the corresponding crates in the `team` database.
- Implement a Zulip command for yanking/unyanking a crate in a public Zulip topic, which will only be allowed for members of teams attached to those crates in the `team` database.

I wanted to give a heads-up to the Compiler team about this plan, and ask if you have any feedback/concerns. Currently, the Compiler team owns 16 crates on crates.io (https://crates.io/teams/github:rust-lang:compiler).
620917525.zh:
基础设施团队希望移除 `rust-lang` 在 crates.io 上所有 crate 的个人和团队所有权，以减少因某个账户遭到入侵而带来的攻击面。我们的设想是：
- 为这些 crate 启用可信发布，这样它们只能通过各自仓库的 CI 发布。
- 移除所有团队和个人访问权限，使 crates.io 上实际拥有这些 crate 的只剩 `rust-lang-owner`。
- 在 `team` 数据库中记录哪些团队（以虚拟方式）“拥有”对应的 crate。
- 在公开的 Zulip 主题中实现一个用于撤回/取消撤回 crate 的 Zulip 命令，但只有 `team` 数据库中与这些 crate 关联的团队成员才能使用该命令。

我想提前向编译器团队说明这一计划，并询问你们是否有任何反馈或顾虑。目前，编译器团队在 crates.io 上拥有 16 个 crate（https://crates.io/teams/github:rust-lang:compiler）。

620921412.en: There are probably a few that can be archived
620921412.zh: 其中可能有几个可以归档。

620921690.en: Not sure how that should work in team yet, w.r.t. archived repos and archived crates. Crates are currently attached to repos; probably archiving a repo owning a crate should archive that crate too? (but archiving a crate doesn't really mean anything, right?)
620921690.zh: 我还不确定这在 team 中应该如何处理，包括已归档的仓库和已归档的 crate。现在 crate 是关联到仓库的；拥有某个 crate 的仓库被归档后，可能也应该把该 crate 归档？（不过，归档 crate 其实也没什么实际意义，对吧？）

620988544.en: From a security perspective, archiving and ownership seem orthogonal. You might not need trusted publishing set up for archived crates (they could go no-publishing instead). But what if you want to release a security fix?
620988544.zh: 从安全角度来看，归档和所有权似乎是相互独立的。已归档的 crate 可能不需要设置可信发布（也可以改为 no-publishing）。但如果你想发布安全修复呢？

621001916.en: there is not really any concept of archived crates
621001916.zh: 实际上并没有“已归档 crate”这一概念。

621290313.en: Some crates have not been released for some time, e.g. https://github.com/rust-lang/odht. Would it be okay if we remove all access from them (and keep only `rust-lang-owner`), without necessarily implementing a way for them to be released? infra admins could do an emergency release if needed, but what would be more likely is that if we need a release, we'd implement the release mechanism at that time
621290313.zh: 有些 crate 已经有一段时间没有发布过了，比如 https://github.com/rust-lang/odht。如果我们移除它们的所有访问权限（只保留 `rust-lang-owner`），同时不一定为它们实现发布方式，这样可以吗？如果有需要，基础设施管理员可以进行紧急发布；但更可能的情况是，如果我们确实需要发布，到那时再实现发布机制。

621290386.en: to avoid creating many new CI workflows and publish mechanisms if the crates don't get any new releases anyway
621290386.zh: 这样可以避免在这些 crate 反正不会有新版本发布的情况下，创建大量新的 CI 工作流和发布机制。

621352387.en: I don't have any problem with infra going ahead with this for compiler repos
621352387.zh: 对于编译器仓库，我不反对基础设施团队直接推进这项工作。

t|t-compiler|Removing team crate ownersh.zh: 取消团队对 crate 的所有权

609536510.en: The other option is to support eager expansion through something like `${eager(include!("foo.txt"))}`. Proc-macros already have unstable support for it. Rust-analyzer doesn't support it though and doesn't have an easy path to support it either.
609536510.zh: 另一个选择是通过类似 `${eager(include!("foo.txt"))}` 的形式支持提前展开。过程宏已经有不稳定支持了。不过 rust-analyzer 还不支持它，而且也没有什么简单的支持路径。

609548741.en: Right, excepting the issues that bjorn3 mentioned.
609548741.zh: 对，不过要考虑 bjorn3 提到的那些问题。

609549580.en: I suppose though that things like `${eager($($tt)*)}` are a nice convenient way to get the same functionality as a callback but without the need to add the pattern(s) for that explicitly? But I dunno, I kind of like macros being a bit more functional-like in the way that they are now.
609549580.zh: 不过我想，`${eager($($tt)*)}` 之类的写法，确实是一种很方便的方式，可以在不显式添加相应模式的情况下，获得与回调相同的功能？但我也说不准；我有点喜欢宏目前这种更偏函数式的风格。

609553750.en: `${eager(...)}` means you don't have to adapt all macros everywhere to use continuation-passing-style for everything, so it works without having to modify all macros to accept callbacks
609553750.zh: `${eager(...)}` 意味着你不必为了所有事情都采用延续传递风格去调整各处的所有宏，因此无需修改所有宏来接受回调也能工作。

609560105.en: It also means that macros have less privacy, though.
609560105.zh: 不过这也意味着宏的隐私性会变弱。

609560723.en: Right now, you can never write a macro that *inspects* another macro’s expansion, and many macros are written with the corresponding assumption that the expansion can use implementation details and can be non-breakingly arbitrarily changed as long as the behavior is the same.
609560723.zh: 目前，你永远无法编写一个能够*检查*另一个宏展开结果的宏；而且许多宏的编写都基于这样一个假设：只要行为不变，其展开结果就可以使用实现细节，并且可以任意修改而不会造成破坏性影响。

609561127.en: It would be nice if eager expansion were a thing but opt-in, so that non-cooperating macros' expansions can't be matched, sort of like the current “invisible parentheses” in `macro_rules`.
609561127.zh: 如果提前展开能够存在，但需要显式选择启用，那就好了。这样，不配合的宏的展开结果就无法被匹配，有点像 `macro_rules` 目前的“不可见括号”。

609565249.en: ignoring proc-macros, eager expansion to opaque ast could definitely work. I think the opt-in should only be needed if you want to match non-opaquely or maybe if feeding the output into a proc macro
609565249.zh: 不考虑过程宏的话，将宏提前展开成不透明 AST 肯定是可行的。我认为，只有当你想要以非不透明的方式进行匹配，或者可能要把输出传给过程宏时，才需要显式选择启用。

609565385.en: tbh I think proc-macros should also gain opaque expressions/items/etc. where the proc-macro knows it's an expression but can't inspect its tokens
609565385.zh: 说实话，我认为过程宏也应该获得不透明的表达式、条目等。这样，过程宏知道它拿到的是一个表达式，但无法检查其中的 token。

609602930.en: expand_expr only works for macros that expand to literals, like include_str, to what degree would this address your use cases?
609602930.zh: `expand_expr` 只对展开结果为字面量的宏有效，比如 include_str；这在多大程度上能满足你的使用场景？

609608286.en: It doesn't really help too much, unfortunately. I'd like to see this on things like `include!` as well, which only expands to literals in very specialised cases.
609608286.zh: 遗憾的是，它并没有太大帮助。我也希望 `include!` 之类的宏支持这一点，而 `include!` 只有在非常特殊的情况下才会展开成字面量。

610925242.en:
@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Interest.20for.20callbacks.20in.20.60core.3A.3A.60.2F.60std.3A.3A.60.20.28builtin.29.20macros.3F/near/609561127):
```quote
It would be nice if eager expansion were a thing but opt-in, so that non-cooperating macros' expansions can't be matched, sort of like the current “invisible parentheses” in `macro_rules`.
```

I've done some thinking on this and I think that having a callback as part of a macro's syntax does at least satisfy the opt-in part, but it doesn't keep someone from inspecting the expansion of a macro. I suppose the nice thing here is that it's a non-breaking change (at least in the case of the stdlib macros) and doesn't require any new language features.
610925242.zh:
@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/Interest.20for.20callbacks.20in.20.60core.3A.3A.60.2F.60std.3A.3A.60.20.28builtin.29.20macros.3F/near/609561127)：
```quote
如果提前展开能够存在，但需要显式选择启用，那就好了。这样，不配合的宏的展开结果就无法被匹配，有点像 `macro_rules` 目前的“不可见括号”。
```

我对此思考了一下，觉得把回调作为宏语法的一部分，至少确实满足了“显式选择启用”这一点，但它并不能阻止别人检查宏的展开结果。不过，这种方案的好处在于它不会破坏现有代码（至少对于标准库宏来说是这样），而且不需要引入任何新的语言特性。

621047764.en:
Since this is being brought up offline by @**Aurorans Solis** (who I know somewhat unrelated to the Rust project), I think my stance here is that we should do something to make this less necessary rather than easier to do/better supported. I think that's what the `${eager()}` suggestion and subsequent discussion was about (but apparently that's not how it was taken so I'm being more clear about it).

In functional programming, it's fairly well-known that continuation passing style is hard to write and read, and I don't think that it being macro-based makes this any better (actually, I think it makes it worse).
621047764.zh:
既然 @**Aurorans Solis**（我认识他，但和 Rust 项目基本无关）是在私下提出这个问题，我的看法是：我们应该想办法让这件事变得没那么必要，而不是让它更容易实现或得到更好的支持。我觉得 `${eager()}` 的提议以及后续讨论本来就是这个意思（但显然大家并不是这么理解的，所以我在这里说得更明确一些）。

在函数式编程中，续延传递风格（continuation-passing style）难写难读是众所周知的，我不认为采用宏实现会让情况变得更好（事实上，我觉得反而会更糟）。

620098234.en:
Recently, I have been looking at removing unnecessary allocations from rustc. One thing that comes up repeatedly is an opportunity to use a simple ever-growing arena, instead of using repeated nested allocations on the heap. Using a `Vec` for that is fine, but often we don't even really need to produce a slice of the items in the arena, and moving all the inner things when reallocating can be a waste.

The canonical solution for that is to have a Vec of chunks, where you allocate a chunk (of the same size, if you want to support random indexing access), and then when you run out of space, you allocate a new chunk, and thus you don't need to move all the previous items.

This is implemented e.g. in the `segmented_vec` crate, but I was wondering whether there is anything like that already in the compiler? It seems like a very useful thing, but I wasn't able to find a generic data structure in rustc that would implement something like this already. It doesn't help that this (AFAIK) doesn't have a clear nomenclature in the data structure world (it can be called chunked vec, segmented vec, etc.).
620098234.zh:
最近我一直在研究如何从 rustc 中移除不必要的分配。其中反复出现的一种机会是：可以使用一个简单的、不断增长的 arena，而不是在堆上反复进行嵌套分配。使用 `Vec` 完全没问题，但很多时候我们甚至并不需要生成 arena 中这些元素的切片，而且重新分配时移动所有内部元素也可能是一种浪费。

对此，标准解决方案是使用一个由多个 chunk 组成的 Vec：分配一个 chunk（如果希望支持随机索引访问，可以让它们大小相同），空间用完后再分配一个新的 chunk。这样就不需要移动之前的所有元素。

`segmented_vec` crate 中就实现了这种结构，不过我想知道编译器中是否已经有类似的东西？这看起来是个非常有用的结构，但我没能在 rustc 中找到已经实现此类功能的通用数据结构。更麻烦的是，据我所知，数据结构领域对它似乎没有一个明确的术语（可以叫 chunked vec、segmented vec 等）。

620098895.en: Isn't that [`rustc_arena::TypedArena`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_arena/struct.TypedArena.html)? It has chunks of data.
620098895.zh: 这不就是 [`rustc_arena::TypedArena`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_arena/struct.TypedArena.html) 吗？它里面有数据 chunk。

620099332.en: On this subject, note that "same-sized chunks" is not necessary for random access indexing. The other kind of segmented vector with O(1) indexing has exponentially growing segments (segment `i` holds `1 << i` elements). This removes or reduce the need to manage a variable-sized collection of segment pointers since you can always allocate ceil(log2(max capacity)) segment pointers up-front (though you may want not want to do that for small vectors). And if you do it right, it basically just replaces the div/mod by pow2 for indexing with ilog2 (ca. same cost as count leading zeros), shift, subtract.
620099332.zh: 说到这个，顺便一提，随机访问索引并不要求使用“大小相同的 chunk”。另一种支持 O(1) 索引的分段向量使用的是指数增长的段（第 `i` 段存放 `1 << i` 个元素）。这样可以减少，甚至不需要管理大小可变的段指针集合，因为你总是可以预先分配 ceil(log2(max capacity)) 个段指针（不过对于较小的向量，可能不希望这么做）。如果实现得当，索引时基本上只是把除法/取模换成了 ilog2、移位和减法，成本大致与计算前导零的数量相同。

620108173.en: I just struggle to imagine a scenario where memcpy due to Vec reallocation *specifically* is the bottleneck and replacing that with more calls into the global allocator, more indirection, and more complicated indexing and iteration is worthwhile. I don't want to stop you, but I would be really curious to see the use case where it's a good trade-off (in part for learning, in part because I suspect it'll be something where we could do even better by doing something else)
620108173.zh: 我只是很难想象这样一种场景：Vec 重新分配导致的 memcpy *本身* 是瓶颈，而用更多次全局分配器调用、更多间接访问，以及更复杂的索引和迭代来替代它，居然值得这么做。我不是想阻止你，但我确实很想看看在哪种使用场景下这是个好的权衡（部分是为了学习，部分是因为我怀疑这种场景下我们通过做些别的事情，可能还能做得更好）。

620108789.en: Speaking of append-only vec, I have experimented in the past (not for rustc) with representing a "`Vec` that you only append to" as pair (pointer to next free slot, remaining capacity) and moving the total capacity into the heap allocation. That relies on a phase separation between appending and indexing/iteration, and in return produces a bit less code for the "append" parts than passing `&mut Vec` around (mostly because you can pass two words in registers and so can arrange for APIs that don't round-trip the Vec fields through memory so much). But I never finished that because it didn't help as much as I hoped without `extern "rust-cold"` ABI and without extensive (mechanical) rewrites of the code that appends to the vector.
620108789.zh: 说到只追加的 vec，我以前曾经做过一些实验（不是针对 rustc）：把“只进行追加操作的 `Vec`”表示为一对值（指向下一个空闲位置的指针、剩余容量），并把总容量移入堆分配中。这要求追加和索引/迭代之间存在阶段划分，但作为回报，相比于到处传递 `&mut Vec`，它能让“追加”部分的代码稍微少一些（主要是因为两个字可以通过寄存器传递，因此可以设计出一些 API，避免频繁地让 Vec 的字段在寄存器和内存之间来回转换）。不过我最终没有完成这个实验，因为在没有 `extern "rust-cold"` ABI、也没有对向量追加代码进行大量（机械式）重写的情况下，它带来的帮助没有我希望的那么大。

453845868.en:
Someone on Reddit was complaining about incremental build times on large projects, and made the brave claim that they would be okay with no inlining at all in the changed code.

So I'm going to try to clean up the monomorphization code so that it is possible to configure the compiler to lower everything (or nearly everything) as GloballyShared, with 1 item per CGU. Right now the logic for deciding on the instantiation mode is spread across the compiler, and I'm going to try to centralize it into `cross_crate_inlinable` or a companion function that takes an `Instance` instead.

As far as I can tell so far, this is going to involve landing a lot of small cleanup-y probably-perf-sensitive PRs. I intend to land basically the entire effort in little PRs that are merged on their own merits, because I know others have pointed out that the instantiation mode selection needs some love. I'm just starting this topic to let people know what I'm up to :smile: 

The first two of these PRs are
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/128165
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/128170
453845868.zh:
有人在 Reddit 上抱怨大型项目的增量构建时间，并大胆地表示，他们可以接受变更代码完全不进行内联。

所以我打算尝试整理单态化代码，使编译器能够配置为将所有内容（或几乎所有内容）都降级为 GloballyShared，并且每个 CGU 只包含 1 个条目。目前，决定实例化模式的逻辑散落在编译器的各个地方；我打算尝试将其集中到 `cross_crate_inlinable` 中，或者集中到一个接收 `Instance` 的配套函数中。

就目前看来，这将涉及大量小型的、偏清理性质且可能对性能敏感的 PR。我打算基本上把整个工作拆成许多小 PR，每个 PR 都凭自身价值合并，因为我知道已经有人指出，实例化模式的选择需要好好改进一下。我开这个话题只是想让大家知道我在做什么 :smile:

其中最先提交的两个 PR 是：

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/128170

608316049.en:
It dictates things like stack alignment at function entry, or the alignment of functions themselves, and also it dictates FPCSR and MXCSR's value at function entry. A function that is publicly callable must have certain values set in those registers at function entry to be conformant to the ABI. This is part of how LLVM can assume the default, or at least how it can get away with it: because actually it has to be.

In particular, on Windows, their "long double", last I checked, is just `f64`. Please feel free to correct me on this. It does, on "x86-32", use the floating point stack to pass values, because that was what was available, so it passes them in 80-bit registers. However, they perform the operations according to FPCSR, which makes the operations happen according to a significantly reduced precision. Namely, they are as close as possible to simply approximating `binary64` as that hardware supports.
608316049.zh:
它规定了函数入口处的栈对齐方式、函数本身的对齐方式之类的事项，也规定了函数入口处 FPCSR 和 MXCSR 的值。一个可以被公开调用的函数，必须在函数入口处将这些寄存器设为特定的值，才能符合 ABI。这也是 LLVM 能够假定默认值的原因之一，或者至少说，它之所以能这么做，是因为实际上它必须这么做。

具体来说，在 Windows 上，据我上次了解，他们的“long double”其实就是 `f64`。如果我说错了，欢迎纠正。它确实会在“x86-32”上使用浮点栈来传递值，因为当时可用的就是这个机制，所以会通过 80 位寄存器传递值。不过，它们会根据 FPCSR 执行运算，这会让运算以显著降低的精度进行。具体而言，就是尽可能地按照该硬件所支持的方式，简单地将 `binary64` 作为近似值来处理。

608316314.zh: 而且，这种做法*极少数情况下*会暴露出一个细微差异：使用浮点栈传递值，与使用 xmm 寄存器传递值之间的差异。

608318376.en: Not like reusing the fp register storage is unheard of (MMX).
608318376.zh: 又不是没人听说过复用浮点寄存器存储（MMX 就是这样）。

608318481.en: Yes. Though unlike MMX, doing it implicitly works better for everyone involved, since most software either doesn't know about the other usage, or definitely gives less than half a damn about what it is stomping on.
608318481.zh: 没错。不过和 MMX 不同，隐式地这么做对所有相关方都更有利，因为大多数软件要么不知道另一种用途，要么根本不太在乎自己踩掉的是什么。

608318488.en: Though touching MMX had architectural consequences for the fpreg state, like setting fsw.TOP=7 and ftw=0x0000.
608318488.zh: 不过，访问 MMX 会对浮点寄存器状态产生架构层面的影响，比如将 fsw.TOP 设为 7，并将 ftw 设为 0x0000。

608318534.en: And if they ever want bigger mask registers then they're just using the other 16 bits plus some.
608318534.zh: 而且如果他们以后想要更大的掩码寄存器，只要再使用另外 16 位，外加一些其他位就行了。

608318975.en:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/608318315):
```quote
Virtually no one using the floating-point stack, leaving about 640 bits lying around, is why there are precisely 8 mask registers for AVX512.
```

There's obviously other reasons like "you usually don't need as many predicates at a time as values". But Arm decided on 16 p regs instead of 8 p regs and, given there are as many zmm regs as there are z regs on SVE, one would imagine they would lean in the same direction if all else were equal, as Intel had plenty of notice of what SVE was going to be like by the time they moved from MVEX to EVEX.
608318975.zh:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/608318315)：
```quote
几乎没人使用浮点寄存器栈，白白闲置着大约 640 位，这就是 AVX512 恰好有 8 个掩码寄存器的原因。
```

显然还有其他原因，比如“通常不会同时需要和数值一样多的谓词”。但 Arm 最终决定使用 16 个 p 寄存器，而不是 8 个 p 寄存器；既然 SVE 中的 z 寄存器数量与 zmm 寄存器数量相同，那么如果其他条件都一样，人们大概会认为 Intel 也会倾向于同一方向，因为到他们从 MVEX 转向 EVEX 时，已经提前充分了解 SVE 会是什么样了。

608319271.en: Also, to be fair, 3 bits fit fairly well into the extra byte of EVEX.
608319271.zh: 另外，公平地说，3 位放进 EVEX 多出来的那个字节里也相当合适。

608319399.en: Right. That is an excellent example of another reason to go with 8 that doesn't cause the pipeline to come to a screeching halt and doesn't explain why the floorplan for x86-64 CPUs seems to never include additional space for the kregs (granted, based on external observation). :^)
608319399.zh: 对。这是另一个选择 8 个寄存器的绝佳理由：它不会让流水线骤然停摆，也解释不了为什么 x86-64 CPU 的版图似乎从来没有为额外的 kregs 预留空间（当然，这只是基于外部观察得出的结论）。:^)

608319609.en: I only mention all this because there was briefly an effort to pass an RFC allowing extended precision operations on floats, which included in its argument that using the x87 FPU would enable faster computation of float things because it used separated pipelines or state, which was like... apparently a true thing on some very ancient x86 machines that only had just acquired xmm registers, and is the opposite of true today.
608319609.zh: 我之所以提到这些，是因为之前曾短暂出现过一项努力，想通过 RFC，允许对浮点数执行扩展精度运算；其中一个论据是，使用 x87 FPU 会让浮点运算更快，因为它采用了独立的流水线或状态。然而这……显然只是在某些极其古老、刚刚配备 xmm 寄存器的 x86 机器上才成立，而如今已经完全相反了。

608328740.en: Anyway, regarding what to do here: I don't think it would be the *worst* thing to say that x87_f80 only exists on platforms where that's what `long double` is, since presumably those coincide with platforms that aren't potentially miscompiled. But I also think that if people are going to expect to be able to occasionally do `c_longdouble + c_longdouble` then we could skip LLVM and call our own routines that save+restore the CW. We already have some code like that https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/blob/1521862f2e486ff58b4ce8c92bfadffbc8736f35/libm/src/math/arch/i586/rounding.rs
608328740.zh: 总之，关于这里该怎么做：我不认为规定 x87_f80 只存在于 `long double` 就是这种类型的平台上会是*最糟糕*的做法，因为想来这应该正好是那些不会潜在地产生错误编译的平台。不过我也认为，如果人们确实会期待偶尔能够执行 `c_longdouble + c_longdouble`，那么我们可以跳过 LLVM，调用自己编写的、会保存并恢复 CW 的例程。我们已经有一些类似的代码了：https://github.com/rust-lang/compiler-builtins/blob/1521862f2e486ff58b4ce8c92bfadffbc8736f35/libm/src/math/arch/i586/rounding.rs

608328896.en: Comes at the cost compared to not changing the CW but :shrug: ask intel where the hardware f128 support is if people want something faster.
608328896.zh: 这相较于不修改 CW，代价就是会有额外开销，不过 :shrug: 如果大家想要更快的实现，那就去问 Intel 硬件 f128 支持在哪儿吧。

608653158.en:
As for i686, I don't think the ABI makes a guarantee in the first place, because DirectX exists.

`IDirect3D9::CreateDevice` takes a `BehaviorFlags` parameter, and one of those flags is `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE`:

> Set the precision for Direct3D floating-point calculations to the precision used by the calling thread. If you do not specify this flag, Direct3D defaults to single-precision round-to-nearest mode for two reasons:
> * Double-precision mode will reduce Direct3D performance.
> * Portions of Direct3D assume floating-point unit exceptions are masked; unmasking these exceptions may result in undefined behavior.

Yes, DirectX used to set the FPCSR precision to _PC_24 by default. It was as fun as you could imagine.
608653158.zh:
至于 i686，我认为 ABI 一开始就没有提供这方面的保证，因为还有 DirectX。

`IDirect3D9::CreateDevice` 接受一个 `BehaviorFlags` 参数，其中一个标志是 `D3DCREATE_FPU_PRESERVE`：

> 将 Direct3D 浮点计算的精度设置为调用线程所使用的精度。如果不指定此标志，Direct3D 默认采用单精度、舍入到最近值的模式，原因有二：  
> * 双精度模式会降低 Direct3D 的性能。  
> * Direct3D 的部分代码假定浮点单元异常已被屏蔽；取消屏蔽这些异常可能导致未定义行为。

没错，DirectX 过去默认会将 FPCSR 的精度设置为 _PC_24。那体验真是糟糕得超乎想象。

in practice if you avoid making assumptions about the precision of float ops in unsafe code you're very unlikely to run into issues. and since these are basically retrocomputing targets I hope nobody runs anything truly important on them...

we should probably demote them to tier 3. but there doesn't seem to be urgency so this can wait until build-std is stable so tier 3 does not entirely exclude them from being used on stable.

@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/611735993)：

```quote
嗯，这还是有点不同，因为你并不是说在错误配置下运行属于 UB。
```

@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/611735993)：

```quote
你说的是，在 ABI 强制规定的标准配置下，平台本身就属于 UB。
```

遗憾的是，错误配置就是标准配置。

@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/611735993)：

```quote
结论就是，这个平台实际上并不是 Rust 目标。
```

我们之所以将 SSE 设为 i686 目标的基线，是有原因的。i586 目标确实有些坏了。就 tier 2 目标而言，如果只考虑稳定特性，它们可能是我们拥有的最不完善的目标。不过 nvptx 也是 tier 2，它同样以一些令人愉快的方式坏得很有特色。^^

619419152.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/611724040):
```quote
but yeah running on i586-\* is pretty much insta-UB in principle. nothing prevents the compiler from emitting its own float instructions and assuming that they behave correctly. this is basically the same as running a Rust program with the rounding mode set up incorrectly.
```
I also question what prevents this assumption on i686 also.
If you're returning f64 from an `extern "C"` function, I'd guess that llvm would emit x87 instructions for simple computations, rather than sse instructions, then spill to memory followed by an fld (the latter of which just absolutely worse perf wise, for some definition of "simple" computation).
I'd assume the compiler would *not* assume an environment that is contradicted by the platform psABI. I'd expect clang would not assume it can use `rep movsb` as though `flags.DF=1`, for example.
619419152.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/.60x87_f80.60.20is.20weird/near/611724040)：
```quote
不过话说回来，运行在 i586-\* 上原则上基本上会立即触发 UB。没有什么能阻止编译器生成它自己的浮点指令，并假设这些指令的行为是正确的。这和运行一个舍入模式设置错误的 Rust 程序，本质上是一样的。
```
我也想知道，在 i686 上是什么阻止了这种假设。  
如果你从一个 `extern "C"` 函数返回 f64，我猜 llvm 会在进行简单计算时生成 x87 指令，而不是 sse 指令，然后溢出到内存，再跟一个 fld（从某种“简单”计算的定义来看，后者的性能简直糟糕得多）。  
我认为编译器不会假设一个与平台 psABI 相矛盾的环境。例如，我预计 clang 不会假设自己可以在 `flags.DF=1` 的情况下使用 `rep movsb`。

619441468.en: I think clang always uses sse if available unless you set the flag, even if it’s less efficient

619456499.en: on i686 the problem is much more limited since we only use the x87 registers for `extern "C"` return values, not for any arithmetic
619456499.zh: 在 i686 上，问题要小得多，因为我们只会将 x87 寄存器用于 `extern "C"` 的返回值，而不会用于任何算术运算。

619651653.en:
> not sure if any of these can happen?

The first two problems would also affect our current workaround for the `"Rust"` ABI. In practice this doesn't happen because if LLVM realises it can change the function signature it will also change the calling convention to `fastcc`, which returns floats in SSE registers and is therefore unaffected by the issue. All LLVM floating point libcalls are for mathematical operations which are allowed to quieten signalling NaNs (`abs`, `copysign` and negation are never libcalls), so the calling convention isn't an issue there.
619651653.zh:
> 不确定这些问题是否有可能发生？

前两个问题同样会影响我们目前针对 `"Rust"` ABI 所采用的变通方案。实际上，这种情况并不会发生，因为如果 LLVM 意识到可以更改函数签名，它也会将调用约定改为 `fastcc`；而 `fastcc` 会通过 SSE 寄存器返回浮点数，因此不受该问题影响。LLVM 中所有浮点 libcalls 都用于数学运算，而这些运算允许将信号 NaN 静默化（`abs`、`copysign` 和取负从来不会使用 libcall），所以这里调用约定并不是问题。

619530816.en:
The MIR for `bad_id` does contain a `Terminator { kind: Drop }` for `c` here.
`Drop` terminators are emitted for almost all variables. Before drop elaboration they're just conditional on whether the place was moved out of.
619530816.zh:
`bad_id` 的 MIR 确实包含一个针对这里的 `c` 的 `Terminator { kind: Drop }`。

几乎所有变量都会生成 `Drop` terminator。在 drop elaboration 之前，它们只会根据对应 place 是否已经被移出而进行条件判断。

619531756.en: Either `-Zdump-mir=fn_name` and go digging through the `mir_dump/` folder for the right compilation stage, or, like in this case, `RustLsp view mir` actually gives you the mir from a good stage (from the `rustaceanvim` plugin, idk if this has a vscode alternative)
619531756.zh: 可以使用 `-Zdump-mir=fn_name`，然后到 `mir_dump/` 文件夹里寻找正确的编译阶段；或者像这个例子一样，`RustLsp view mir` 实际上会提供一个合适阶段的 MIR（来自 `rustaceanvim` 插件，不知道 VS Code 有没有对应的替代方案）。

619533478.en:
`RustLsp view mir` is a bit weird to use and almost never gives you anything useful, because it's only one specific stage (idk which one) and has a really weird output format that replaces variables with their names where possible, while keeping them only refered to by their id in the struct debug syntax.

`...bad_id.-------.nll.0.mir` has the terminator too at the end of `bb2`, written as `drop(_17) -> [return: bb3, unwind: bb13]`
619533478.zh:
`RustLsp view mir` 用起来有点奇怪，而且几乎从来不会给出有用的结果，因为它只展示某个特定阶段的 MIR（不知道具体是哪一个），输出格式也非常奇怪：能替换成变量名的地方就替换成变量名，而在结构体调试语法中又只通过 ID 引用变量。

`...bad_id.-------.nll.0.mir` 在 `bb2` 的末尾也有这个 terminator，写作 `drop(_17) -> [return: bb3, unwind: bb13]`。

sorry i am new to this conversation, but the way i see it, `yeet1` and `yeet2` should probably have different type signatures. 
after all few things make behavior more clear than good typing.

`yeet1` should return a `FakeInhabited` type, with a safe `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` method that calls  `unreacheable_unchecked`, but would not otherwise register as uninhabited to the compiler, meaning producing it would not immediately mark the following code as unreacheable.
that would properly enshrine the fact that the following code is unreacheable (it is not possible to have `FakeInhabited` in safe reacheable code) but the compiler isn't aware of it unless we tell it.

`FakeInhabited` is actually a quite convenient type to have when one whishes to check ghost branches of code without having the borrow checker go "oh, an uninhabited type was produced, let's just ignore everything that follows"

````quote
`yeet1` 或 `yeet2`——因为 `trap` 显然有所不同，它的类型签名也不同
````
抱歉，我刚加入这个讨论，不过在我看来，`yeet1` 和 `yeet2` 可能本来就应该有不同的类型签名。

毕竟，很少有什么东西能比良好的类型设计更能让行为变得清晰。

`yeet1` 应该返回一个 `FakeInhabited` 类型，并提供一个安全的 `ex_nihilo::<T>(self) -> T` 方法，该方法会调用 `unreacheable_unchecked`；但它本身不应被编译器视为无 inhabitant 的类型，这意味着生成它不会立即让后续代码被标记为不可达。

这样就能恰当地确立这样一个事实：后续代码是不可达的（在安全且可达的代码中不可能存在 `FakeInhabited`），但除非我们明确告知编译器，否则编译器并不知道这一点。

当你想检查代码中的幽灵分支，又不希望借用检查器看到“哦，生成了一个无 inhabitant 的类型，那我们直接忽略后面的所有内容吧”时，`FakeInhabited` 实际上是一个相当方便的类型。

622662594.en:
yeet2: whenever you write `breakpoint()` you have to make sure that it's okay for that to be a NOP, and the code that runs after `breakpoint()` returns (if it returns) has to run without UB.
or, equivalently: if your code becomes unsound when I replace `breakpoint()` by a NOP, then your code was already unsound before I did that.
622662594.zh:
yeet2：每当你写下 `breakpoint()` 时，都必须确保即使它实际上是个 NOP 也没问题；并且 `breakpoint()` 返回之后运行的代码（如果它返回的话）必须能够在不触发 UB 的情况下运行。  
或者等价地说：如果把 `breakpoint()` 替换成 NOP 后你的代码就会变得不健全，那么在我这么做之前，你的代码就已经是不健全的。

622662641.en: yeet1: whenever you write `breakpoint()`, you can if you want treat whatever comes after that function as dead code (but the code can make the choice that its okay to continue if it wants -- which means that the compiler will not treat it as dead code, it'll pretend that the code may actually run, so the asm you get is the same as for yeet2)
622662641.zh: yeet1 ：每当你写`breakpoint()`，如果您想将该函数后面的任何内容视为死代码（但代码可以做出选择，如果需要，可以继续--这意味着编译器不会将其视为死代码，它会假装代码实际上可能运行，因此您获得的asm与yeet2相同）

622662849.en: I think that in my head I had a similar summary. But what is the compiler allowed to do with this distinction, if it must be a fence in either case?
622662849.zh: 我觉得我脑海中也有一个类似的总结。但如果无论哪种情况它都必须是一个屏障，那么编译器究竟可以利用这个区别做什么呢？

622662978.en: I'm also in favor of yeet2. yeet1 would not be sound for systems where breakpoint instructions are automatically resumed if no debugger is attached (I don't know if such native systems exist, but it is more logical to me than aborting when no debugger is attached and matches how javascript handles `debugger;`)

622665479.en:
For reference, C++ merely says the semantics of `std::breakpoint` is "implementation-defined". There is a note though:

> *Note 1*: When invoked the execution of the program temporarily halts and execution is handed to the debugger until such a time as: the program is terminated by the debugger or, the debugger resumes execution of the program as if the function was not invoked.  — *end note*
622665479.zh:
供参考，C++ 只说 `std::breakpoint` 的语义是“由实现定义的”。不过有一条注释：

> *注 1*：调用时，程序的执行会暂时暂停，并将执行权交给调试器，直到发生以下情况之一：程序被调试器终止，或调试器恢复程序的执行，就好像从未调用过该函数一样。——*注释结束*

622667935.en: I think it should be only `yeet2`. It doesn't make sense to me to tell people it's okay to pretend debuggers don't have a continue button. If you want things to be guaranteed to stop after the breakpoint, put an abort call there.
622667935.zh: 我认为应该只有 `yeet2`。在我看来，告诉人们可以假装调试器没有继续执行按钮，是没有道理的。如果你希望断点之后一定停止，那就在那儿放一个 abort 调用。

622668470.en: This means that `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` isn't "sound", e.g. it won't save you from the effects of `unreachable_unchecked()` if it's all that's between your code and it,  but that doesn't mean it isn't useful. I could imagine writing a macro that expanded to `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` or something, so that you could get a breakpoint in a case when you thought was impossible.
622668470.zh: 这意味着 `yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked()` 并不“安全”，例如，如果你的代码与它之间只有这一段代码，它也无法保护你免受 `unreachable_unchecked()` 影响；但这并不意味着它没有用。我可以想象写一个宏，展开成 `#[cfg(something)] yeet2(); unreachable_unchecked();` 之类的形式，这样在某个你认为不可能发生的情况下，也能触发断点。

622668599.en:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622664570):
```quote
in that yeet1 fails CTFE and yeet2 succeeds?
```

yes. well for yeet2 we could plausibly make either choice for CTFE. for yeet1, failing evaluation is the only valid choice for CTFE.
622668599.zh:
@_**Trevor Gross|532317** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622664570)：
```quote
在这种情况下，yeet1 在 CTFE 中失败，而 yeet2 成功？
```

是的。不过对于 yeet2，我们完全可以合理地选择让它在 CTFE 中成功或失败。至于 yeet1，在 CTFE 中求值失败是唯一有效的选择。

622669045.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622667935):
```quote
I think it should be only `yeet2`. It doesn't make sense to me to tell people it's okay to pretend debuggers don't have a continue button. If you want things to be guaranteed to stop after the breakpoint, put an abort call there.
```

the argument people gave is to have code after the yeet1  breakpoint still optimized as-if it was reachable, which putting an abort there won't achieve.
why that is so useful is not clear to me.
622669045.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622667935)：
```quote
我认为应该只有 `yeet2`。在我看来，告诉人们可以假装调试器没有继续执行按钮，是没有道理的。如果你希望断点之后一定停止，那就在那儿放一个 abort 调用。
```

人们提出这个观点，是因为希望 yeet1 断点之后的代码仍能按照“它是可达的”来进行优化，而在那里放一个 abort 并不能达到这一点。至于为什么这会如此有用，我并不清楚。

622669359.en: I mean, fine, put `black_box(abort as fn())()` if that's something they care about.
622669359.zh: 我的意思是，如果他们确实在意这个，那就用 `black_box(abort as fn())()`。

622669392.en: The case where you care about this seems very niche to me.
622669392.zh: 在我看来，会在意这种情况的人实在太少了。

622669769.en: Like, realistically the ability to click 'continue' exists in the debugger. And if a program I'm running in a debugger hits a breakpoint, like, I'm probably going to try hitting continue (after looking around a bit)?
622669769.zh: 比如，现实情况是，调试器里确实有“继续”按钮。如果我运行中的程序在调试器里触发了断点，我大概会先四处看看，然后尝试点“继续”吧？

622670259.en: I don't think you can put this onto a user and say 'they should know it's UB to hit continue'. That's very strange. But if that's *really* what you want, it's not like you can't "outside the model" this for cases where you control the program, and put in your documentation "if you run my program in a debugger, pressing the continue button on any breakpoints is unsafe and unsupported". It would be very strange to do this, for sure, but that's why I think it's strange for Rust to have this as an invariant in a stdlib function.
622670259.zh: 我不认为你可以把这件事推给用户，然后说“他们应该知道点击继续会导致 UB”。这非常奇怪。不过，如果这确实是你想要的，也不是不能在你控制程序的情况下把它置于“模型之外”，并在文档中写明：“如果你在调试器中运行我的程序，按下任何断点上的继续按钮都是不安全且不受支持的。”这么做当然会非常奇怪，但这正是我认为 Rust 不应该把它作为标准库函数不变量的原因。

622671853.en: So I haven't finished reading that huge thread and perhaps haven't gotten to the followup, but based on https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2961578385 it seems like the argument for yeet1 is that aborting when a debugger is not attached is desirable, so you don't forget these exist then trap some downstream user's code when they're running `strace`
622671853.zh: 所以我还没读完那个很长的讨论，也许还没看到后续内容；但根据 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/133724#issuecomment-2961578385，yeet1 的理由似乎是：当没有连接调试器时直接中止是更理想的行为，这样你就不会忘记这些断点的存在，之后又在某个下游用户运行 `strace` 时让其代码触发陷阱。

622672121.en: I do kind of get that. But couldn't we theoretically have abort-by-default behavior with yeet2 soundness semantics?
622672121.zh: 我多少能理解这一点。但从理论上讲，我们不能让 yeet2 在保持安全性语义的同时，默认执行中止吗？

622672556.en: totally, yeet2 is compatible both with abort-by-default and continue-by-default
