621519125.en:
Thinking about this some more, I don't think overlapping allocations are necessary to justify most allocation-elision optimisations, as long as you stop assuming that stack allocations *always* succeed. If you change that to assuming that only a limited amount of stack space is always available (because in practise there *is* actually a guard-page worth of space that's guaranteed to be unused), you can still completely elide small allocations, as long as you can prove that they would fit into the remaining amount of stack. So the only change necessary is that optimisations have to prove that the total size of the elided allocations is smaller than the remaining-stack-space constant (i.e. the size of the guard page). But as long as that space *could* have been available, there is no need to *actually* allocate anything in the end (by e.g. modifying the stack pointer in the compiled program).

The benefit of making allocations virtual until their address is observed is that you can then also optimise away some large temporary copies like in the `Box::new([0u8; VERY_LARGE_NUMBER])` case, as you wouldn't need to prove (by virtue of actually allocating) that there is actually enough free memory remaining to hold two `VERY_LARGE_NUMBER`-sized arrays.
621519125.zh:
再想了一下，我觉得只要不再假设栈分配*总是*成功，就没必要用重叠分配来证明大多数消除分配的优化是合理的。如果改成假设始终只有有限的栈空间可用（因为实际上确实有一段至少相当于一个保护页大小的空间能保证不会被使用），那么只要能证明小型分配能放入栈上剩余空间，就仍然可以完全消除这些分配。因此，唯一必要的改动就是：优化必须证明，被消除分配的总大小小于剩余栈空间常量（也就是保护页的大小）。但只要那部分空间*有可能*可用，最终就没必要真的进行任何分配（例如在编译出的程序中修改栈指针）。

让分配在地址被观测到之前保持虚拟状态的好处是，这样还可以消除一些大型临时副本，例如 `Box::new([0u8; VERY_LARGE_NUMBER])` 这种情况，因为你不需要通过实际分配来证明确实有足够的剩余可用内存来容纳两个大小为 `VERY_LARGE_NUMBER` 的数组。

621553716.en:
How does stack overflow fit into opsem? If I write a deeply recursive function my program also misbehaves and segfaults. By what mechanic/logic is this allowed?

Follow-up question: can we interpret the opsem mechanic that allows a bad outcome like segfault on stack overflow to also allow other undefined behavior on stack overflow like shown in the linked issue? If we do so, even if that stack overflow was optimized out by the compiler, it hypothetically 'occurred', allowing the undefined behavior.
621553716.zh:
栈溢出在 opsem 中是怎么处理的？如果我写一个递归很深的函数，我的程序同样会行为异常并发生段错误。这是通过什么机制或逻辑被允许的？

追问：我们能否将允许栈溢出时出现段错误这类坏结果的 opsem 机制解释为：栈溢出时也允许出现链接 issue 中所示的其他未定义行为？如果这样解释，那么即使该栈溢出被编译器优化掉了，它也可以假设“发生过”，从而允许未定义行为。

621554294.en: I don't think stack overflow is considered UB in Rust. But at the same time, I'm not sure how we carve out the allowance for the segfault you'll get on stack overflow on some targets.
621554294.zh: 我不认为栈溢出在 Rust 中会被视为 UB。但与此同时，我也不确定我们是如何为某些目标平台上栈溢出时会发生的段错误留出余地的。

621554809.en: (More concretely, there's no unsafe code, so I don't think calling it UB would be good)
621554809.zh: （更具体地说，这里没有 unsafe 代码，所以我觉得把它称为 UB 不太合适。）

621555206.en: I was under the impression the consensus for normal stack overflow (via locals, recursion, etc) was "the implementation may decide to stack overflow at any time, but if it does, that **will** be an abort so you dont have to worry about it"
621555206.zh: 我的理解是，大家对普通栈溢出（通过局部变量、递归等方式造成）的共识是：“实现可以随时决定发生栈溢出，但如果真的发生，**就一定**会中止，所以你不用担心。”

621555295.en: this is why stack probes are important, otherwise it is truly UB, possibly scribbling on unrelated memory
621555295.zh: 这就是栈探针很重要的原因，否则这确实是 UB，可能会胡乱改写不相关的内存。

621555686.en: Do we have stack probes on all targets? I thought we did not.
621555686.zh: 我们在所有目标平台上都有栈探针吗？我以为没有。

621556209.en: should be all tier-1 though, and many tier-2
621556209.zh: 不过 Tier 1 应该都有，很多 Tier 2 也有。

621556227.en: we do not, but I think that the approach there is to just pretend it's not a problem
621556227.zh: 我们没有，但我觉得这里的处理方式就是假装这不是个问题。

621556531.en: The "bury your head in the sand" strategy proposed above is truly versatile.
621556531.zh: 上面提出的“把头埋进沙子里”策略真是适用范围广泛。

621556617.en: if you can't see it, it can't hurt you, and it doesn't even matter what "it" is!
621556617.zh: 你看不见它，它就伤害不了你，而且“它”到底是什么甚至都不重要！

621556943.en: freestanding targets obviously don't come with stack overflow prevention,  it's up to the implementation -- so in practice, many freestanding/embedded programs have UB on stack overflow
621556943.zh: 显然，独立运行目标不会自带栈溢出防护，这取决于实现——所以实际上，许多独立运行/嵌入式程序在栈溢出时都会产生 UB。

621559163.en:
I do understand we'd like to hold on to the "zero UB in safe code" if possible, I personally would not find it a big loss to define "a stack overflow so big it exhausts the address space" as instant UB. No real-world program ever runs into this (except maybe 8/16-bit targets, not sure about that), and it gets rid of these nasty pigeonhole arguments.

'Regular' stack overflow would still be safe, assuming there's stack probes.
621559163.zh:
我确实明白，如果可能的话，我们希望坚持“安全代码中零 UB”这一点。就我个人而言，把“大到耗尽整个地址空间的栈溢出”定义为立即触发 UB，我并不觉得会损失太多。现实世界中的程序从来不会遇到这种情况（也许 8/16 位目标除外，这点我不确定），而且这样还能解决这些棘手的抽屉原理论证。

假设存在栈探测，“普通的”栈溢出仍然会是安全的。


pointer comparison definitely does not compare provenance. not sure why that assumption would be relevant here though -- I agree that this would likely break stuff. I dont think it's the entire world. but it's certainly breaking most people's intuition way more than provenance already does.

sadly I don't know any other way to explain the optimizations LLVM does. That's why we are stuck with the "bury our heads in the sand" strategy. ;) but this is a genuine unsoundness in the sense that the unsafe code is not violating any rule we wrote down, or any rule I could imagine us writing down.
621761218.zh:
@_**asquared31415|384759** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621450225):
```quote
我相当确定，如果 `ptr_a == ptr_b`（假设指针比较也会比较 provenance）不再意味着它们具有相同的内容，那么整个世界都会崩溃。
```

指针比较肯定不会比较 provenance。不过我不太确定这个假设为什么会与这里有关——我同意这很可能会破坏很多东西。我不认为会破坏整个世界，但它肯定会比 provenance 已经造成的影响，更大幅度地违背大多数人的直觉。

遗憾的是，我不知道还有什么其他办法可以解释 LLVM 所做的优化。这就是为什么我们被困在“把头埋进沙子里”这一策略中。;) 但从这个意义上说，这确实是不健全的：这段 unsafe 代码并没有违反我们明确写下的任何规则，也没有违反任何我能想象出我们会写下的规则。

I don't understand why everyone is freaking out on the OOM fix. If you read the [UCG thread](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/328), the proposal there perfectly allows you to compare pointers. (Unless something changed since the last time I read that thread.) It is just not the same thing as comparing numbers/integers.

If you want to compare pointers then just tell the compiler so, instead of lying by saying you want to compare two numbers. `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` might theoretically give you "nonsense", `ptr1 == ptr2` is what you want. Is that so difficult that we rather want to give up on *dead allocation elimination*, or make `addr()` basically `black_box()`?!

Yes, for `expose_provenance()` we don't really have a good solution, but that is currently specced as "we have no idea what this does" anyway. And it is still better to only make `expose_provenance()` be almost `black_box()` for optimization, rather then also `addr()`.

如果你想比较指针，那就直接告诉编译器，而不是谎称你想比较两个数字。`ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` 理论上可能给出“胡说八道”的结果，但 `ptr1 == ptr2` 才是你想要的。难道这难到我们宁愿放弃*消除死分配*，或者让 `addr()` 基本上变成 `black_box()`？！

621806614.en:
ok what about this opsem?

Any time you have a pointer, its value is always just an allocation id plus an offset.

Somewhere in the AMs global state there is a mapping from allocation id to `Option<usize>` for the actual address. The mapping for a given id can't change after initialization.

At any time during the execution of the program, the AM may stop and then do one of these two operations:
1. Crash the program (let's call this kind of crash "stack overflow")
2. Fill in an address for any allocation id currently assigned to `None`

A typed copy from a byte with provenance to a byte without provenance performs a lookup in this global state. If the value is `None`, the AM has to stop and assign an address or crash the program under a stack overflow crash. (But these may occur at any time, so this can also happen before the typed copy.)
621806614.zh:
好，那这个操作语义怎么样？

任何时候，只要你有一个指针，它的值就始终只是一个分配 ID 加上一个偏移量。

在 AM 的全局状态中的某处，存在一个从分配 ID 到实际地址的 `Option<usize>` 映射。某个 ID 对应的映射在初始化之后不能再改变。

在程序执行期间的任意时刻，AM 都可以暂停，然后执行以下两种操作之一：
1. 让程序崩溃（我们把这种崩溃称为“栈溢出”）
2. 为当前映射为 `None` 的任意分配 ID 填入一个地址

将带 provenance 的字节以类型化方式复制到不带 provenance 的字节时，会查询这个全局状态。如果值为 `None`，AM 就必须暂停，并分配一个地址；或者在发生栈溢出崩溃时让程序崩溃。（不过这些事情可能在任意时刻发生，因此也可能在类型化复制之前发生。）

621818971.en: For the inlining issue, I guess we don't really need the finite restriction. 621880545.en: and `addr`-like conversions wrap around, unless you do some operation (e.g. ffi, or perhaps `<=` on an address) that guarantees that the "real" address lies in the range of a usize.
621880545.zh: 而类似 `addr` 的转换会发生回绕，除非你执行了某个操作（例如 ffi，或者可能是对地址使用 `<=`），从而保证“真实”地址位于 `usize` 的取值范围内。

621880619.en: And whether the address lies in the range of a usize is determined ahead of time, like in @_**Alice Ryhl**'s proposal
621880619.zh: 以及地址是否落在 usize 的范围内，是像 @_**Alice Ryhl** 的提案中那样预先确定的

621883607.en:
@_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621880545):
```quote
and `addr`-like conversions wrap around, unless you do some operation (e.g. ffi, or perhaps `<=` on an address) that guarantees that the "real" address lies in the range of a usize.
```
That makes all integer operations have side-effects, doesn’t it?
621883607.zh:
@_**Max|960514** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621880545)：
```quote
而类似 `addr` 的转换会发生回绕，除非你执行了某种操作（例如 ffi，或者对地址使用 `<=`），从而保证那个“真实”的地址落在 usize 的范围内。
```
这样一来，所有整数运算都有副作用了，不是吗？

621884786.en:
I'd explicitly make `+`/`-`/`==` (and perhaps any operation that is somewhat compatible with the ring homomorphism from the natural numbers to `usize`) not cause the address to become "real", but yeah essentially.
Though the side effect is just that the AM must retroactively choose that the allocation is real, like in Alice's proposal. 
I don't think we can get around making certain operations have side-effects, if we want to keep the current optimizations. That's already how it works in LLVM basically, allocations can get optimized away unless you do something to them that blocks the optimization
621884786.zh:
我会明确规定 `+`/`-`/`==`（以及或许任何与从自然数到 usize 的环同态在某种程度上兼容的运算）不会让地址变成“真实”地址，但基本上确实如此。
不过，这个副作用仅仅是 AM 必须追溯性地选择将该分配认定为真实的，就像 Alice 的提案那样。
如果我们想保留现有的优化，我不认为能避开让某些运算产生副作用这一点。LLVM 基本上就是这么工作的：除非你对分配做了某些会阻止优化的操作，否则分配可能会被优化掉

621885404.en: The problem with that is that now you mustn’t remove those operations, because that would change behaviour.
621885404.zh: 问题在于，这样一来你就不能移除这些运算了，因为那会改变程序行为。

621885581.en: And you definitely have to exclude + and - from your list, otherwise `usize::MAX + 1` might not equal zero anymore.
621885581.zh: 而且你肯定得把 `+` 和 `-` 排除在列表之外，否则 `usize::MAX + 1` 可能就不再等于零了。

621885586.en: I'd hope to do this in a way where if you don't observe the result of the operations, it's still valid to remove them. Yeah the way I phrased my proposal fails to achieve this
621885586.zh: 我希望能以这样一种方式实现：如果你没有观察这些运算的结果，那么移除它们仍然是合法的。没错，我之前描述提案的方式无法做到这一点

621885641.en:
@_**joboet|541962** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621885581):
```quote
And you definitely have to exclude + and - from your list, otherwise `usize::MAX + 1` might not equal zero anymore.
```

`usize::MAX` is not an address. Only addresses you get from allocations behave this way
621885641.zh:
@_**joboet|541962** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621885581)：
```quote
而且你肯定得把 `+` 和 `-` 排除在列表之外，否则 `usize::MAX + 1` 可能就不再等于零了。
```

`usize::MAX` 不是地址。只有从分配中获得的地址才会表现出这种行为

621888922.zh:

621889433.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621792917):
```quote
that may work, would need more study.
that said I also think if we tell people that `ptr1 == ptr2` is not the same as `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()`, they won't be happy...
```

Sometimes you can't have everything... The other options on the table currently are (a) giving up on almost all dead allocation elimination, or (b) making both `addr()` and ptr comparison side-effectful (and therefore almost complete `nounwind` black boxes to the optimizer).
621889433.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621792917)：


有时候你不可能面面俱到……目前摆在桌面上的其他选项是：(a) 放弃几乎所有无效分配消除优化；或者 (b) 让 `addr()` 和指针比较都带有副作用（因此对优化器来说，它们几乎会变成完整的 `nounwind` 黑箱）。

621890158.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621806295):
```quote
I think `ptr1 == ptr2` being hard to optimize is much less bad than it being forbidden, or forbidding removing temporary allocations.
```
The proposal from the [UCG thread](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/328#issuecomment-1134395637) is actually the only proposal where I've seen where you have both dead allocation elimination and ptr comparison being not too much of an optimization barrier. The only thing you have to give up on is that address comparison is different from pointer comparison (ptr comparison gives you what you expect, address comparison not).
621890158.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621806295)：

621900083.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621806295):
```quote
I think `ptr1 == ptr2` being hard to optimize is much less bad than it being forbidden, or forbidding removing temporary allocations.
```

yeah, but I expect to most people it's still worse than the soundness bug it is fixing.

also FWIW the way slice::Iter uses comparison is fine and wouldn't break. it is comparison of pointers to different allocations where things are tricky. slice::iter can use an `unsafe fn ptr_eq_same_alloc` that will continue to be optimized just as much as `==` on pointers today.
621900083.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621806295)：
```quote
我认为 `ptr1 == ptr2` 难以优化，要远没有禁止这种写法，或者禁止移除临时分配那么糟糕。
```

是的，但我觉得对大多数人来说，这仍然比它正在修复的那个健全性漏洞更糟。

另外，顺带一提，`slice::Iter` 使用比较的方式没问题，也不会因此出问题。真正棘手的是比较来自不同分配的指针。`slice::iter` 可以使用一个 `unsafe fn ptr_eq_same_alloc`，这样它仍然能像如今对指针使用 `==` 一样得到充分优化。

621900405.en:

```quote

```

So, I think this is still too abstract to me (is `self.ghost_cap.expose()` supposed to modify `self.ghost_addr`? And a bunch of other questions like this), but the properties seem good.

Basically, the situation is that under this model `a.addr() == b.addr()` breaks when `a` and `b` are from different allocations (have different `ghost_cap`s)?

And presumably `with_exposed_provenance(a.addr()) == with_exposed_provenance(b.addr())` doesn't save you (but while it might not work, but it also isn't UB, which, well, it better not be since it's safe). However, IIUC actually exposing the provenance would (IIUC) *does* save you? (In that it gives you something you can compare?)

The main downsides here that I see are:

1. Compatibility, since existing code may assume that addr behaves the way we've, erm, been saying it does (I could believe that this doesn't actually matter because in practice the cases where that assumption breaks in a visible way are so rare as to never happen[^1]... but I also could be wrong about this).

2. Teachability, since it seems meaningfully harder to explain than what we have currently. I think it also doesn't fit as nicely into a 'tower of weakenings' approach (which works best when the complex stuff is more permissive rather than less). This could perhaps be fixed by rethinking the tower, though. I also am less concerned about this, since the alternatives all see so awful.

3. Detectability, since there's no way to detect that `usize_a == usize_b` are integers that came from an `addr()` call, so we can't warn about this (and could only lint on the simplest of cases). And then it forces you to use `ptr::expose_provenance()` over `ptr::addr()` more of the time (since `addr()` can't be used for comparisons reliably), with all the well-documented downsides that comes with (detectability of other issues). This seems like the worst to me, but also perhaps not that bad?

That said, as always, there's a very real chance I've misunderstood something here.

[^1]: Which seems true, otherwise the 'head in sand' strategy would be far less attractive.

[^2]: Cantor's argument about the countability of rationals implies it can... although what the numerator and denominator are is completely mysterious to me, and if they are assigned in a way where the rational simplification matters for equality... I suppose a rational still could be required? I don't know. That sounds bizarre, so I'm assuming it's just an integer, basically.

我看到的主要缺点有：

1. 兼容性，因为现有代码可能假定 addr 的行为就是我们一直——呃——所描述的那样（我可以相信这实际上并不重要，因为这种假定以一种可见方式失效的情况在实践中极其罕见，几乎不会发生[^1]……但我也可能对此判断有误）。

2. 可教学性，因为这似乎明显比我们目前的方案更难解释。我觉得它也不太适合“逐层弱化”的思路（这种思路在复杂部分更宽松而不是更严格时效果最好）。不过，也许可以重新思考一下这个层次结构来解决。我对此也没那么担心，因为其他方案看起来都糟糕得离谱。

621912209.en:
to summarize, the main pills to swallow with this approach are
- ptr comparison is not the same thing as addr comparison
- `expose_provenance` is it not `willreturn`, i.e., an optimization barrier. but we anyway discussed making it an inline asm blob to stop LLVM from miscompiling it so :shrug:  don't use it in your inner loop, use strict provenance there.
- `expose_provenance` is specified to potentially spontaneously abort the program. I am wondering how bad that is. We already say that the program can abort with a stack overflow basically any time (but as a QoI concern it generally won't), so this could be similar. OTOH it is a bit silly since unlike a stack overflow, we know this will actually *never* happen. There's nothing in the compiler that would introduce such OOM. So why have it in the spec in the first place? I don't have a good answer to this.
621912209.zh:
总结一下，这种方案主要需要接受的代价是：

- 指针比较和地址比较不是一回事；
- `expose_provenance` 不是 `willreturn`，也就是说它会构成一道优化屏障。不过我们之前反正也讨论过，要把它做成一段 inline asm，以防 LLVM 错误地编译它，所以 :shrug: 不要在内层循环里使用它，在那里使用 strict provenance。
- 规范规定，`expose_provenance` 可能会让程序自发中止。我在想这到底有多糟。我们已经基本上承认，程序随时可能因为栈溢出而中止（但作为 QoI 问题，通常不会真的发生），所以这也许可以类似看待。另一方面，这有点荒谬，因为和栈溢出不同，我们知道这种情况实际上永远不会发生。编译器中没有任何东西会引入这种 OOM。那么规范一开始为什么要包含这一点？对此我没有好的答案。

621912307.en: isn't it already super unsound to delete allocations that `expose_provenance` was called on?
621912307.zh: 删除曾经调用过 `expose_provenance` 的那些分配，不是已经极其不健全了吗？

621912363.en: no... if you expose a heap allocation and then immediately free it, for instance, you know nothing could possibly access it
621912363.zh: 不……比如说，如果你暴露了一个堆分配，然后立刻将其释放，你知道之后不可能再有任何东西访问它。

621933677.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621901707):
```quote
I view "ghost_addr" as being part of the provenance.
```

Me too. But all previous conversations here on t-opsem that talk about provenance mean only `ghost_cap`.

```quote
Also why does it have to be a "rational"? it can just be a mathematical integer I think.
```

If you use rationals, the semantics has strictly more behaviours that are allowed. Since I can't think of any reason why unsafe code would prefer integer planes, and I can't oversee the ramifications of rational vs integers planes for optimisations, I opted to use rationals. We can always make them integers later.

```quote
instead of allocation planes I just imagine all allocations having unique IDs
```

~~Yes, that is equivalent (but you need to fix a bijection between AllocIds and rationals except 0, to use for order comparisons).~~ Edit: with comparisons it can actually make a difference.

```quote
but for expose_provenance I recall our discussion to be along the lines of "if it's not forced / on plane 0, then NB".
```

I think both options were discussed in the thread, OOM and NB. The end of the thread tended towards NB indeed, but since then there have been discussions pointing out complications that arise with NB, so I thought I'd opt for OOM. We can always change it to NB later, since `nb()` refines `oom()`. And if we allow a program to OOM at any point (which we probably need to, because of stack overflows), then `nb()` and `oom()` are equivalent programs since you can always avoid the NB by raising OOM.

621936966.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Do.20we.20already.20have.20overlapping.20allocations.3F.20.28OOM.20Edition.29/near/621906074):
```quote
is `self.ghost_cap.expose()` supposed to modify `self.ghost_addr`?
```

It is supposed to expose the provenance of the pointer. So"just" what `expose_provenance()` does without this proposal. No-one knows how it works.

```quote
Basically, the situation is that under this model `a.addr() == b.addr()` breaks when `a` and `b` are from different allocations (have different `ghost_cap`s)?
```

Yes. That comparison might yield `true` even though `a` and `b` point to different allocations. In particular, reading from `a` and `b` could give different answers. However, if you ever called `expose_provenance()` on both pointers, then you are fine (in the sense that if the comparison returns `true` then `a` and `b` actually point to the same allocation; they might still have different provenance of course).

```quote
And presumably `with_exposed_provenance(a.addr()) == with_exposed_provenance(b.addr())` doesn't save you
```

Indeed it doesn't. This is probably just equivalent to `a.addr() == b.addr()`.

```quote
The main downsides here that I see are:
```
* Compatibility.
I know. We should have done this before stabilizing `addr()`. But if "head in the sand" works, then clearly you won't run into trouble due to comparing addresses where you actually wanted pointer comparison.
* Teachability. I think this proposal is quite natural from the strict-provenance point of view.
* Detectability. I would think that many "violations" actually have `a.addr() == b.addr()` as syntactic shape.

(Btw, I don't know what your second footnote refers to. But rationals for me is just rational numbers, not some kind of syntactic fractions or something. 2/4, 1/2 and 0.5 are all the same number.)

```quote
那么，想必 `with_exposed_provenance(a.addr()) == with_exposed_provenance(b.addr())` 也帮不了你
```

确实帮不了。这可能实际上就等价于 `a.addr() == b.addr()`。

```quote
我看到的这里主要缺点是：
```

我知道。我们本来应该在稳定 `addr()` 之前就做这件事。不过，如果“把头埋进沙子里”这种做法行得通，那么你显然不会因为比较了本来想进行指针比较的地址而遇到问题。

Sure, I meant for the cases where you could previously use just addr. The fact that usually you can just compare pointers is why I think it's not so bad.

> We already say that the program can abort with a stack overflow basically any time (but as a QoI concern it generally won't), so this could be similar. OTOH it is a bit silly since unlike a stack overflow, we know this will actually *never* happen

Ah, I had interpreted that as being a legit OOM case where because of the expose, we could no longer remove an allocation (and now something else will OOM, so I guess the fact that the OOM isn't in the right place for that should have tipped me off...).

> I would think that many "violations" actually have `a.addr() == b.addr()` as syntactic shape

I don't think so. I can't imagine when you would ever compare `a.addr()` to `b.addr()` directly. Maybe some arithmetic to avoid going through `ptr::wrapping_{add,sub,offset}` (because those are sometimes seen as less 'correct' for somewhat dubious reasons) or something?

One case I can imagine is `(a.addr() & SOME_MASK) == (b.addr() & SOME_MASK)`. And whether or not that's okay depends on which bits `SOME_MASK` is removing...

...

In the interest of being a bit less abstract, I looked around std a bit for things that either violate this rule or seem dubious under it. Here are some cases where addresses are compared (to things other than constants)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow/thread_info.rs (`errno_location().addr()` used as a thread id in a lock)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/backtrace.rs#L325 (instruction pointer compared to a symbol addr. perhaps these are fine because they're code addresses, not addresses of allocations?)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/windows/mod.rs#L72. This is subtraction and not comparison, although the result of the subtraction does get compared, so it seems similar. My assumption is that this is fine because they're from the same allocation? Or is that only the case for the other model.

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs#L110 This actually compares the faulting address to another address range. It feels like this perhaps could be a case that needs to be expose_addr? Certainly the provenances of the guardpage and the fault address are going to be wildly different... Hmmm... Or perhaps we can just declare that this is a case that is Sufficiently Magic to not be a problem?

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/path.rs#L1666-L1669 (more addr() on pointers from same alloc -> arith -> do stuff with result. there's a lot of this, so I'll omit the rest).

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sync/mpmc/waker.rs#L71-L92 These thread ids are `addr()`s of thread locals, and are absolutely being compared. I guess they need to expose instead? Or stay as pointers (harder sell maybe)

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/thread/tests.rs#L149-L165 A test where the addr of a local is compared. Obviously if the code under test is correct then this is fine (same address), but otherwise ???

- There's... also a few places in std::sync that *seem* fine, but I would probably want to do a real look if this model were accepted. And also the xous sync primitives look like they probably violate it, but I don't care enough to dig into a tier3 platform I've only heard of once. (No offense meant to anybody who cares about it, I suppose.)

Anyway, perhaps figuring out if the usage is "okay" or not will get easier over time, but as it stands just from that cursory review, I would say that this makes reviewing code with `addr()` harder (and the "easiest" fix for that in a lot of cases is just to expose instead, since it doesn't require rewriting the code or carefully maintaining provenance of a pointer).

> 我认为，很多“违规”实际上在语法形式上都是 `a.addr() == b.addr()`。

我不这么认为。我想不出你什么时候会直接把 `a.addr()` 和 `b.addr()` 进行比较。也许会做一些算术运算，以避免经过 `ptr::wrapping_{add,sub,offset}`（因为出于一些相当可疑的理由，人们有时觉得这些函数“不太正确”），或者类似的事情？

我能想到的一种情况是 `(a.addr() & SOME_MASK) == (b.addr() & SOME_MASK)`。而这是否可行，取决于 `SOME_MASK` 移除了哪些位……

……

为了不那么抽象，我稍微看了一下 std，找了些违反这条规则、或者在这条规则下看起来比较可疑的代码。下面是一些会将地址与常量以外的对象进行比较的情况：

- https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/f207aa3913114c3326bc0b88acbd12b10244edf8/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs#L110 这里实际上将触发故障的地址与另一个地址范围进行了比较。感觉这或许是一个需要使用 expose_addr 的情况？保护页和故障地址的 provenance 肯定会相差十万八千里……嗯……又或者，我们可以直接宣布这种情况已经“足够特殊”，所以不构成问题？

622027700.en:
So as far as I can tell, it's *almost* the case that LLVM only removes an allocation if it can prove that the program's behavior is the same no matter which (legal) address it chooses. So the program can convert the pointer to an address and check its lower bits, which are zero in any program due to alignment. It can do math where the base address cancels out (i.e. `x - x` simplifies to `0`). Also, LLVM will optimize `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` to just `ptr1 == ptr2`.

Now the only case where this doesn't apply is that LLVM is happy to constant fold `ptr1 == ptr2` to `false` even if both pointers are removed. This is a bit unfortunate for that model because it means that it removed the allocation even though not *all* choices for `ptr1.addr()` and `ptr2.addr()` lead to the same program behavior, because the choice where both are equal has different behavior.

So because of that, we cannot just inspect all possible choices for the address and require that the program behavior must be the same no matter what the chosen address is.
622027700.zh:
所以据我所知，情况几乎是这样的：只有当 LLVM 能证明无论它选择哪个（合法）地址，程序的行为都相同时，它才会移除分配。因此，程序可以把指针转换成地址并检查其低位，而由于对齐要求，在任何程序中这些低位都是零。它也可以进行基地址会抵消的运算（也就是 `x - x` 会简化为 `0`）。此外，LLVM 会把 `ptr1.addr() == ptr2.addr()` 优化成 `ptr1 == ptr2`。

现在唯一不适用的情况是：即使两个指针都被移除了，LLVM 也很乐意把 `ptr1 == ptr2` 常量折叠为 `false`。这对那个模型来说有点遗憾，因为这意味着它移除了分配，尽管并非 `ptr1.addr()` 和 `ptr2.addr()` 的所有取值选择都会导致相同的程序行为：当两者相等时，程序行为就不同。

因此，我们不能简单地检查地址的所有可能取值，并要求无论选择哪个地址，程序行为都必须相同。

```quote
So as far as I can tell, it's *almost* the case that LLVM only removes an allocation if it can prove that the program's behavior is the same no matter which (legal) address it chooses.
```
LLVM basically only does optimizations for equality and offsets. If you observe the address in any other way, it's not gonna optimize away the allocation. I don't think its optimizations care about how the program behaves depending on the address, beyond that.
It also doesn't need to choose a legal address, which is where the overlapping allocation contradiction comes from :D


LLVM 基本上只会针对相等性和偏移量进行优化。如果你以其他任何方式观察地址，它就不会把分配优化掉。我不认为它的优化会关心程序如何随地址变化而变化，至少不止于此。

它甚至不需要选择合法地址，这正是重叠分配矛盾的来源 :D

622029503.zh: LLVM 当然会做诸如将 `ptr % 8` 简化为零，甚至将 `(ptr1 ^ ptr2) % 8` 简化为零之类的事情，因为它知道低位的值。

566325109.en: what do you mean by "a lot more planning"?
566325109.zh: 你说的“提前规划得多一些”是什么意思？

566325231.en: I assume it means actually choosing a date instead of staying vague and having many dates that could potentially be a meeting.
566325231.zh: 我理解它的意思是，实际选定一个日期，而不是含糊其辞，留下一堆可能作为会议日期的选项。

566325752.en: Yeah. I sometimes am doing scheduling a week or two in advance, and the way its currently being done, I don't always know which thursday this meeting will happen on.
566325752.zh: 是啊。我有时会提前一两周安排日程，但按照目前的做法，我并不总是知道这次会议会在哪个周四举行。

566326603.en: yeah we should schedule this further in advance. I just dont have a lot of capacity for the organizational side of this.
566326603.zh: 是的，我们应该更早安排好。我只是没有太多精力负责组织方面的事情。

566326939.en: I maintain that this would be much easier organizationally if we just have a scheduled slot rain or shine and people can individually declare that they can't make the slot, and come time if there is not enough people around we cancel and wait for the next slot to roll around
566326939.zh: 我认为，如果我们直接安排一个固定时段，不论风雨都照常，然后由大家分别说明自己无法参加；到时候如果现场人数不够，我们就取消，等下一个时段到来，这样在组织上会容易得多。

566327259.en: in other words, we flip from assuming the meeting will not happen unless someone arranges to assuming it will happen unless enough people cancel
566327259.zh: 换句话说，我们要从“除非有人安排，否则默认会议不会举行”，改成“除非有足够多人取消，否则默认会议会举行”。

566327300.en: I feel like that's kind of what we have been doing? we have the Thu slot and then we have the polls to see which slot(s) in a month have sufficient attendance

566327364.en: not really, because that means you need to make a poll every month

566327400.en: and everyone needs to weigh in

566327478.en: what I'm talking about is no polls, just people say "sorry I can't make next week"
566327478.zh: 我说的是不要投票，只要有人说“抱歉，我下周没法参加”就行。

566328041.en: I like the general structure of t-spec meetings, that's once a week so it's easy to plan ahead and it's not a big deal if some of them are cancelled
566328041.zh: 我喜欢 t-spec 会议的整体安排，每周一次，所以很容易提前规划，而且偶尔取消几次也没什么大不了的。

The goal is to get to the point where I can exhaustively enumerate a complete and maximally-fine grained taxonomy of concepts related to language/library UB/soundness/invariant/etc. The hope is that any subsequent discussions about terminology can be expressed as “what sets of these maximally-fine grained terms should we lump together in our final set of official terminology?”

617267912.en:
Quoting from the proposal:

---

## Work this proposal is intended to coordinate

This package is intended to address, amend, or provide a common foundation for:
- [RFC 3845, `repr(ordered_fields)`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3845),
  which separates declaration-ordered Rust layout from a future C layout;
- [RFC 3718, target/system C layouts](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3718),
  together with [RFC 3806, field-level alignment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3806);
- the [zero-sized ABI compatibility work](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/157973),
  the related [`repr(transparent)` array work](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155984),
  and [UCG issue #552](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/552);
- [crABI](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3470), which translates
  higher-level types through a C-based ABI;
- proposals for [C bit-fields](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3113),
  [complex numbers](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/3892-complex-numbers.md),
  and [scalable vectors](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3838); and
- open compiler and language questions around
  [call-ABI representation](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/119183),
  [profile-sensitive `VaList`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/141618),
  and [nominal C types for cross-language CFI](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3296).

The claim is not that all of this work must land together. The claim is that it
should fit one coherent model before individual pieces establish incompatible
assumptions.
617267912.zh: 引用提案中的内容：--- ## 本提案旨在协调的工作 该方案旨在处理、修订以下工作，或为其提供共同基础：- [RFC 3845，`repr(ordered_fields)`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3845)，将按声明顺序排列的 Rust layout 与未来的 C layout 区分开来；- [RFC 3718，目标平台/系统 C layout](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3718)，以及 [RFC 3806，字段级对齐](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3806)；- [零大小 ABI 兼容性工作](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/157973)、相关的 [`repr(transparent)` 数组工作](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/155984)，以及 [UCG issue #552](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/552)；- [crABI](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3470)，通过基于 C 的 ABI 转换高级类型；- 关于 [C 位域](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3113)、[复数](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/3892-complex-numbers.md)和[可扩展向量](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3838)的提案；以及 - 围绕[调用 ABI 表示](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/119183)、[对 profile 敏感的 `VaList`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/141618)和[用于跨语言 CFI 的名义 C 类型](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3296)的编译器和语言层面未决问题。这里并不是说所有这些工作都必须一起合并，而是说，在各个部分确立彼此不兼容的假设之前，它们应该能够纳入一个连贯统一的模型。

621487004.zh: 我在想，IO（尤其是输入部分）在我们的语义中是否会带来某种天使式选择。比如，考虑这段伪代码：```fn f1() { let demonic = freeze(poison); let user = read(); if demonic != user { unreachable(); } }``` UB 能否通过用户输入来避免？也就是说，这个程序是否等价于```fn f2() { let demonic = freeze(poison); let user = read(); unreachable(); }```？如果是，那似乎很令人意外。不过，显然```fn f3() { let user = read(); let demonic = freeze(poison); if demonic != user { unreachable(); } }```与 `f2` 等价。所以不能把 `freeze` 跨过 IO 往后移动？

621502468.en: If the demonic choice does not leak through an observation (like `write(demonic)`) I hope all 3 versions are equivalent, and essentially the trace [read, UB] (assuming no time travel semantics, otherwise just [UB])
621502468.zh: 如果恶魔式选择没有通过某种观测泄露出去（比如 `write(demonic)`），我希望这 3 个版本都是等价的，本质上对应于轨迹 [read, UB]（假设没有时间旅行语义；否则就只是 [UB]）。

621503912.en: one thing to be clear about is whether this is read_can_block_forever, or read_mustreturn? Because actual read syscalls could have the user choose "sleep forever, never reaching UB", and thus timetravelling it forwards would definitely be invalid.
621503912.zh: 有一点需要明确：这是 `read_can_block_forever`，还是 `read_mustreturn`？因为实际的 read 系统调用可能允许用户选择“永远休眠，永远不会执行到 UB”，所以把它通过时间旅行提前显然是不合法的。

621505236.en:
Since `freeze(poison)` is allowed to be different every execution, I can't think of a way that they aren't all the same.

I vaguely feel like if it were `const { freeze(poison) }` then perhaps you could argue that the user running 80 skillion copies of the program to figure out what is being compared against might be considered a way it is visible.
621505236.zh: 既然 `freeze(poison)` 在每次执行中都可以产生不同的值，我想不出它们有什么理由不完全相同。模糊地感觉，如果是 `const { freeze(poison) }`，那或许可以说，用户运行 80 skillion 份程序来搞清楚比较的究竟是什么，可能会被视为一种让它可观测的方式。

621521937.en:
Assuming that the `freeze(poison)` operation just non-deteministically produces a value, you’re basically asking if the non-determinism should somehow go away at the point of doing the IO, right? You say “If yes, that seems surprising” – I assume – because the *real* program of course is not going to be nondeterministic. The “real value” of demonic must be somehow in memory.. the real machine can’t be in a whole set of possible states all at once.

But I think the abstract machine model very well can just do that. Yes non-determinism is kinda weird, but that’s just the way the semantics are defined, and stripping away potential execution paths that emerged from non-determinism is a valid thing the compiler can do during compilation, and it’s a very natural thing [and it *will* happen during compilation just because somehow modeling multiple states at once sounds super expensive and unnecessary] but it’s not a thing that preserves ***equivalent*** semantics. Instead it’s a one-way route.

I hope I’m intuiting this stuff correctly, please correct me if I got this completely wrong.

(In case it wasn’t clear, I agree that f2 is equivalent to f1..)

621607315.en:
My intuition is that f1 and f3 are not equivalent, and f3 is equivalent to f2.

f3 "obviously" can legally be compiled to always executing UB. One way to reasonably implement the freeze(poison) operation is by reusing the register that previously held user input, and using that register to store the `demonic` variable. (Edit: Actually, it would need to have the register's value somehow modified in between, like it being incremented or something, so that the comparison gives the result of "unequal". Still doesn't seem so implausible to happen though.)

If read() produces a random value from an external source, then f1 should have well-defined behavior with probability at least 1/256. After all, we've frozen the poison value, so after the freeze, it better act like a normal integer.
621607315.zh: 我的直觉是，f1 和 f3 并不等价，而 f3 与 f2 等价。f3 “显然”可以合法地被编译成总是执行 UB。实现 `freeze(poison)` 的一种合理方式，是复用之前存放用户输入的寄存器，并使用该寄存器来存储 `demonic` 变量。（编辑：实际上，需要以某种方式修改寄存器的值，比如让它递增之类的，这样比较才能得到“不相等”的结果。不过这种情况发生也并非完全不可想象。）如果 `read()` 从外部来源产生一个随机值，那么 f1 应当以至少 1/256 的概率具有定义良好的行为。毕竟，我们已经冻结了 poison 值，所以在 freeze 之后，它最好表现得像一个普通整数。

@_**Frank Steffahn|280891** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Can.20IO.20provide.20angelic.20choice/near/621521937):
```quote
You say “If yes, that seems surprising” – I assume – because the *real* program of course is not going to be nondeterministic. The “real value” of demonic must be somehow in memory.. the real machine can’t be in a whole set of possible states all at once.
```

Our semantics also isn't in a whole set of states at the same time. The AM can sometimes make a non-deterministic choice, but it *has to choose*. In `f1`, by the time you reach the read, the AM (at least as we specify it currently) has already committed to a value of `demonic`; however that value is not leaked through an observable event.

If you want to make `f1` and `f2` equivalent, you have to specify that input can only depend what is observable so far (which is complicated to make fully precise, but at least includes the trace of observable events to this point). Or you need some way to postpone the choice of the particular value for `demonic`, e.g. by modelling variables to have a set of values instead of a single value (but here I'm thinking of variables as SSA values/registers, not as stack allocated objects, because that would be much more complicated to define such non-det semantics for).

621866355.en:
Here's a (hopefully equivalent) alternative model that hurts my head less to reason about. My understanding is that the wording of the C standard implies this model.

The abstract machine is an interpreter that doesn't just maintain the current program state. It maintains the *set* of all possible current program states, executing them in lockstep.

Each time a nondeterministic operation (such as freeze) is executed on one of the elements of this set, this one element gets forked into multiple elements.

Each time the program produces output (or any observable behavior) the interpreter uses the behavior of one of the current program states in the set, and deletes all states in the set that do not produce this observable behavior.

This model is obviously self-consistent, doesn't require time travel, handles nondeterministic environment with no further complications, and is easier to reason about. It's even potentially implementable as an actual interpreter.
621866355.zh:
这是一个（希望等价的）替代模型，推理起来没那么让人头疼。我理解 C 标准的措辞就是在暗示这个模型。

抽象机是一个解释器，它维护的不只是当前程序状态，还维护当前所有可能程序状态的*集合*，并让它们步调一致地执行。

每当对集合中的某个元素执行一次非确定性操作（例如 freeze）时，这个元素就会分裂成多个元素。

每当程序产生输出（或任何可观察行为）时，解释器就采用集合中某个当前程序状态所产生的行为，并删除集合中所有不会产生这一可观察行为的状态。

这个模型显然是自洽的，不需要时间旅行，处理非确定性环境时也无需额外复杂化，而且更容易推理。它甚至有可能真正实现为一个解释器。

621867073.en: Essentially, this "delays" each demonic decision until some observable program behavior forces a decision to be made.
621867073.zh: 本质上，这会把每一次“恶魔式”决策都推迟到某个可观察的程序行为迫使它必须做出决定时。

621867666.zh: 至于如何处理并发和非行为，就留给读者作为练习了。

```quote
抽象机是一个解释器，它维护的不只是当前程序状态，还维护当前所有可能程序状态的*集合*，并让它们步调一致地执行。

每当对集合中的某个元素执行一次非确定性操作（例如 freeze）时，这个元素就会分裂成多个元素。

每当程序产生输出（或任何可观察行为）时，解释器就采用集合中某个当前程序状态所产生的行为，并删除集合中所有不会产生这一可观察行为的状态。

这个模型显然是自洽的，不需要时间旅行，处理非确定性环境时也无需额外复杂化，而且更容易推理。它甚至有可能真正实现为一个解释器。
```

622424346.en:
I wouldn't describe them as "executing in lockstep" though, because different paths can go through *vastly* different amounts of execution steps before the next point of IO is reached.

Implementing an actual interpreter may run into issues if some paths take long to execute. (You can't exactly solve the halting problem to answer the question of what to expect in the long run.) That, and the state size can get huge of course.
622424346.zh:
不过，我不会把它们描述为“步调一致地执行”，因为不同路径在到达下一个 IO 点之前，可能要经历*天差地别*的执行步数。

如果要真正实现一个解释器，某些路径执行时间过长可能会带来问题。（你不可能恰好解决停机问题，从而回答长期运行后会发生什么。）此外，状态大小当然也可能变得非常庞大。

I'm arguing the transformation is legal, because every possible execution of the transformed program yields results unobservable distinct from the original (under time traveling).  Specifically, it yields a result that cannot be proved incorrect for one of two reasons:
1. The println terminates, the implementation chose 47, and UB lets the implementation do whatever it wants throughout the whole "trace", The fact that the implementation prints the "wrong" value is just a consequence of UB.
2. The println does not terminate, and nothing after it happens - no blah print, no UB. The implementation didn't print the wrong value because it chose the right one.

To be clear, I'm not concerned that this is allowed under non-time travelling. The reasoning depends on time-traveling. The concern I have is: Are we sure that nothing does or relies on similar reasoning?
This was my attempt to create an (albeit contrived) example of an optimization that relies on the ability for UB to "time travel" without relying on any I/O operation to return.

我是在论证这个变换是合法的，因为变换后程序的每一种可能执行，产生的结果都与原始程序不可观测地区分（在允许穿越时间的语义下）。具体来说，它产生的结果不可能被证明是错误的，原因有以下两种之一：

1. println 会终止，实现选择了 47，而 UB 允许实现在整个“轨迹”中随心所欲地做任何事。实现打印出“错误”值这一事实，只是 UB 的结果。
2. println 不会终止，它后面的任何事情都不会发生——既不会打印 blah，也不会出现 UB。实现没有打印错误的值，因为它选择的是正确的值。

明确一点，我并不担心这种行为在不允许穿越时间的情况下是否被允许。这个推理依赖于时间穿越。我担心的是：我们能确定没有任何东西在进行类似的推理，或依赖于类似的推理吗？

这是我尝试构造的一个（尽管很牵强的）例子：某个优化依赖于 UB 能够“穿越时间”，但不依赖任何 I/O 操作返回。

622099030.en:
Contrapositive.
LLVM (and any optimizer that has a non-useless `willreturn`) makes it such that UB must be able to time travel accross wilreturn. So willreturn => time-travelling.
But it's not sufficient to say that ~willreturn => ~time-travelling. ~time-travelling => ~willreturn is correct.
622099030.zh:
逆否命题。

LLVM（以及任何拥有非无用 `willreturn` 的优化器）使得 UB 必须能够跨越 willreturn 进行时间旅行。因此，willreturn => 时间旅行。

但不能据此说 ~willreturn => ~时间旅行。~时间旅行 => ~willreturn 才是正确的。

622100580.en:
By argument is the assumption about the pairing of an execution to an environment. Something the implementation has under its control. Ultimately, a transformation from one Language to another doesn't need to preserve the full semantics of the input, it just needs to respect as-if. The result needs to correspond to one possible execution for a given input, and if for a given input/environment *any* execution exhibits UB, the entire behaviour is undefined.
This is the pre-time-travelling definition of UB.
622100580.zh:
我的论点是，关键在于假设如何将一次执行与一个环境配对。这是实现可以控制的事情。归根结底，从一种语言到另一种语言的变换不需要保留输入的完整语义，只需要遵守 as-if 规则。对于给定的输入，结果需要对应于一个可能的执行；而且，如果对于给定的输入/环境，*任何*执行都会表现出 UB，那么整个行为就是未定义的。

这是时间旅行语义出现之前对 UB 的定义。

```quote
on the level of defining the notion of program executions and when a program refines another, "print will always return" and "UB cannot time travel" are basically 2 ways of saying the same thing.
```

The issue is that not all transformations are pure refinement. Any transformation performed on a given well-defined language (whether it be a surface language, or an IR) is, but transformations are also performed at IR boundaries.
622101277.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Interesting.20Consequence.20of.20time.20traveling.20UB/near/622100880)：

```quote
在定义程序执行以及一个程序何时精化另一个程序的层面上，“print 总会返回”和“UB 不能穿越时间”基本上是同一件事的两种说法。
```

问题在于，并非所有变换都是纯粹的精化。对给定的、定义良好的语言（无论是表层语言还是 IR）所做的任何变换确实都是精化，但变换也会在 IR 边界处进行。

622101773.en: anyway I thunk I refuted your practical concern: it cannot be done on unknown functions, and there's no notion of "I/O primitive" in LLVM. in terms of exploring things for curiosity's sake we could imagine what "being an I/O primitive" would mean to a compiler, but in a time-traveling UB world it would imply `willreturn` so the entire premise of "the compiler knows that it is an I/O primitive but doesnt know that it is willreturn" seems incoherent to me. as I said above I think you are imagining a definition of semantics where UB can time-travel but print may fail to return. Such a definition does not exist to my knowledge, so it is futile to discuss its details until you spell it out, and explain why we should care / worry about such a non-standard definition.


it knows some particular functions are equivalent.
but what plausible property could it assume about print that distinguishes it from an unknown function, that is not willreturn, and that allows your transform? in particular given that the one model we have that justifies time-traveling UB also makes printing willreturn, so there's not even any need to come up with whatever property that may be?

To summarize my understanding of the discussion -- we agree the transform is correct under time-traveling UB (since *all* transforms of that program are correct in that model). you claim the transform is also correct in a model of time-traveling UB where printing is not willreturn. my reply is that the statement is meaningless until you actually define such a model.
622105044.zh:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Interesting.20Consequence.20of.20time.20traveling.20UB/near/622102658)：


总结一下我对这场讨论的理解——我们都同意，在 UB 会穿越时间的模型下，这个变换是正确的（因为在该模型中，对那个程序进行的*所有*变换都是正确的）。你认为，在一种 UB 会穿越时间、但打印操作不具备 willreturn 的模型下，这个变换同样正确。我的回应是：在你真正定义出这样一个模型之前，这个说法没有意义。

622115214.en:
@_**niluxv|401145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Interesting.20Consequence.20of.20time.20traveling.20UB/near/622111310):
```quote
Time-travelling-UB means that `trace + (out(x), UB)` and `trace + (UB)` are equivalent traces for every trace `trace` and value `x`.
```

under some guesses as to what you mean by that notation (I assume that's not a tuple of `out(x)` and `UB`), makes sense. typically what we do is we just say there's a single "UB" trace and when a program triggers UB, the entire trace it emitted so far gets replaced by that "UB" trace.
(we assume here that `out` is the only kind of event on the trace. if there's also `in` things get more complicated.)

> It has nothing to do with whether some function possibly diverges.

Yes it does. if you define UB in the time-traveling way above, then it becomes correct for a compiler to assume that `print` (the primitive that emits the `out` event) is `willreturn`. (`willreturn` here stands for a semantic property of operations that boils down to, the code that after this operation is guaranteed to be executed -- or equivalently, 'pure modulo UB' operations can be moved up across a `willreturn` operation.) if you define UB in a way that it's just an event at the end of a trace, but the events before it in the trace also matter, then it becomes wrong for a compiler to assume that `print` is `willreturn`.
whether or not some function diverges is not part of the definition, but the effect on `willreturn` is a consequence of the definition. this depends on the definition of `willreturn` of course. the property that a compiler cares about when it asks for `willreturn` is reordering stuff from after to before, so that is the definition I would use. I admit I was not explicit about that.
622115214.zh:
@_**niluxv|401145** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Interesting.20Consequence.20of.20time.20traveling.20UB/near/622111310)：
```quote
时间旅行式 UB 意味着，对于任意 trace 和值 `x`，`trace + (out(x), UB)` 与 `trace + (UB)` 是等价的 trace。
```

先不论你对这种记法的具体含义有什么猜测（我猜你不是在表示由 `out(x)` 和 `UB` 组成的元组），这说得通。通常我们的做法是直接说存在一个唯一的“UB” trace；当程序触发 UB 时，它迄今为止产生的整个 trace 都会被替换成这个“UB” trace。
（这里假设 `out` 是 trace 中唯一的一类事件。如果还有 `in`，事情就会复杂得多。）

> 这和某个函数是否可能发散没有任何关系。

有关系。如果你以上述时间旅行式的方式定义 UB，那么编译器假设 `print`（产生 `out` 事件的原语）是 `willreturn` 就是正确的。（这里的 `willreturn` 指的是操作的一种语义属性，大意是：该操作之后的代码一定会执行——或者等价地说，“除 UB 外纯”的操作可以跨过一个 `willreturn` 操作向前移动。）如果你定义的 UB 只是 trace 末尾的一个事件，但 trace 中它之前的事件也会产生影响，那么编译器假设 `print` 是 `willreturn` 就是错误的。
某个函数是否发散并不是定义的一部分，但它对 `willreturn` 的影响是该定义的一个推论。当然，这取决于你如何定义 `willreturn`。编译器关心的 `willreturn` 属性，是把某些东西从后面重排到前面，因此我会采用这个定义。我承认自己之前没有明确说明这一点。

622116011.en: another way to put this is -- if UB is just appended to the trace, rather than replacing the entire trace, that is a model of computation where every prefix of the execution matters and needs to be preserved. which is logically equivalent to saying that we want to preserve program behavior for the case where execution just stops after any given `out`.
622116011.zh: 换一种说法就是——如果 UB 只是追加到 trace 中，而不是替换整个 trace，那么这是一种每个执行前缀都很重要、都必须保留的计算模型。从逻辑上说，这等价于：对于执行在任意一个 `out` 之后就停止的情况，我们也希望保留程序的行为。

If you specify it as possibly returning a different value than is passed in, then your program is incorrect according to that spec. And specifying it as having some side effect doesn't affect how "pure" operations can be compiled around it.
621898220.zh: 至少我看不出，对于一个类似 `black_box` 的内联汇编代码块，能讲出什么样的[故事](https://www.ralfj.de/blog/2026/03/13/inline-asm.html)，从而在这里给你任何有用的保证。如果你把汇编指定为直通（pass-through），那编译器实际上可以做任何事情，不受任何约束。如果你指定它可能返回与传入值不同的值，那么按照这个规范，你的程序就是错误的。而把它指定为具有某种副作用，也不会影响“纯”操作如何在它周围进行编译。

622083651.en: I dont know of something that would be improved if we had an LLVM intrinsic rather than an inline asm block (as it seems the put-it-in-memory is not fundamental for the use of inline asm). I guess there could be cases where there's no register of the right size for the value we want to black_box?
622083651.zh: 我不知道如果 LLVM 有一个 intrinsic 而不是 inline asm 块，什么东西会因此得到改进（因为看起来，把它放进内存并不是使用 inline asm 的本质要求）。我猜可能存在这样的情况：我们想要传给 black_box 的值没有合适大小的寄存器可用？

622181013.en:
Yes, we can't rely on a register of the right size being present, so larger values would either have to still spill, or split into multiple registers if it's still reasonably small (in the linked issue, see how the `16 =>` branch is handled—IDK if it's worth handling more than this, but this much is nice as it means something like `&[T]` stays in registers).

I don't know how hard that is to handle in the intrinsic. When `black_box` was `asm!`, this kind of thing was impossible to do correctly (in generic code), due to `asm!` not supporting `MaybeUninit` input/output. But presumably (hopefully) that's not an issue at the point when we're deciding what the intrinsic turns into.
622181013.zh: 没错，我们不能假定一定存在大小合适的寄存器，所以更大的值要么仍然得 spill，要么在仍然相对较小的情况下拆分到多个寄存器中（在所链接的 issue 里，可以看看 `16 =>` 分支是怎么处理的——我不知道是否值得处理比这更多的情况，但处理到这里很不错，因为这样像 `&[T]` 这样的值就能留在寄存器里）。我不知道在 intrinsic 中处理这个有多难。以前 `black_box` 是 `asm!` 时，由于 `asm!` 不支持 `MaybeUninit` 输入/输出，这类事情在泛型代码中无法正确实现。不过到了我们决定这个 intrinsic 最终要转换成什么的时候，这应该（希望如此）就不再是问题了。

622257553.en: sounds like a good solution is to add support to `asm!` for `MaybeUninit` -- uninit memory doesn't exist at the CPU level (except on weird CPUs like IA64). alternatively you can `freeze` the data and then feed it to `asm!`.
622257553.zh: 听起来，一个好的解决方案是让 `asm!` 支持 `MaybeUninit` 作为输入和输出——未初始化内存在 CPU 层面并不存在（除了 IA64 这类奇怪的 CPU）。另一种办法是先对数据执行 `freeze`，然后再把它传给 `asm!`。

622260386.en:
Last I heard whether or not we add `freeze` was very much still up in the air (although I'm very much in favor of it). Using freeze for this would be possible[^1] if we were to write `black_box` in userspace (err, in library code), but I don't see why we wouldn't keep it as an intrinsic.

[^1]: Note that given that the signature is (likely) `MaybeUninit<T>::freeze(self) -> MaybeUninit<T>` and `MaybeUninit<T>` and `T` have the same ABI (or at least on copy will still deinit the padding bytes of `T`, AFAIK), you would have to first convert `T` to a POD (in the `bytemuck::Pod` sense) type before doing the freeze. So it would be awkward. This is neither here nor there, though, I suppose.
622260386.zh: 我上次听说时，是否要加入 `freeze` 还远未尘埃落定（尽管我本人非常支持）。如果我们在用户空间（呃，也就是库代码中）实现 `black_box`，那么用 freeze 来做这件事是可行的[^1]，但我看不出为什么不把它保留为 intrinsic。[^1]：注意，鉴于其签名（很可能）是 `MaybeUninit<T>::freeze(self) -> MaybeUninit<T>`，并且 `MaybeUninit<T>` 与 `T` 具有相同的 ABI（或者至少据我所知，对其进行 copy 仍会将 `T` 的 padding bytes 解除初始化），你必须先把 `T` 转换成 POD（按 `bytemuck::Pod` 的含义）类型，然后再执行 freeze。所以这样做会比较别扭。不过我想这也不太相关。

622264392.en: `asm!` already supports `MaybeUninit` for inputs and outputs.
622264392.zh: `asm!` 已经支持 `MaybeUninit` 作为输入和输出了。

622264487.en: My bad, my info was out of date.
622264487.zh: 是我的错，我掌握的信息已经过时了。

622264605.zh: 我可能应该说清楚：我已经好几年没关注 black_box 的情况了。

598398274.en:
During the meeting today I learned that @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** is generally doubtful about having any form of subobject provenance.
Context: this is about https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256; the question is whether a reference created via `&blah.foo` is allowed to (unsafely) access any bytes outside that field.

What are the general vibes about that? My assumption was that yes we do want subobject provenance sometimes, for some things (e.g. for fields of repr(Rust) types). If that's not the case then we don't even need to discuss the enum discriminant shenanigans @**Mario Carneiro** has been proposing.

The one argument for subobject provenance is optimizations, though I'd have to re-scan that issue to get a more concrete idea for which optimizations we considered.
598398274.zh:
我在今天的会议上了解到，@**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** 总体上对引入任何形式的子对象溯源都持怀疑态度。
背景是这样的：讨论的是 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256；问题在于，通过 `&blah.foo` 创建的引用，是否允许（以不安全的方式）访问该字段之外的其他字节。

大家对此总体是什么看法？我原本以为，我们确实有时希望具备子对象溯源，用于某些场景（例如 `repr(Rust)` 类型的字段）。如果不是这样，那我们甚至不需要讨论 @**Mario Carneiro** 一直在提议的枚举判别值相关问题。

支持子对象溯源的一个理由是优化，不过我得重新浏览一下那个 issue，才能更具体地想起我们当时考虑的是哪些优化。

598398745.en: the [first example](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256#issuecomment-725638217) I mention here... sounds like nonsense? we can do that optimization in Tree Borrows even without subobject provenance...
598398745.zh: 我在这里提到的[第一个例子](https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256#issuecomment-725638217)……听起来像是无稽之谈？即使没有子对象溯源，我们也可以在 Tree Borrows 中进行那项优化……

598399798.en: reading through the issue I only see people posting usecases for the &Header pattern, not motivations for subobject provenance...
598399798.zh: 通读这个 issue 后，我只看到大家在发关于 `&Header` 模式的使用场景，而不是关于子对象溯源的动机……

598399894.en: one motivation is the enum discriminant optimization we talked about (for non-niched enums)
598399894.zh: 其中一个动机是我们讨论过的枚举判别值优化（针对没有 niche 的枚举）。

598406007.en: It's surprising to me that whether or not the type is `#[repr(Rust)]` would matter for this. My mental model has always been that `#[repr(Rust)]` and `#[repr(C)]` were essentially just inputs to the layout algorithm, and not properties that matter after that algorithm produces its result.
598406007.zh: 在我看来，类型是否为 `#[repr(Rust)]` 会影响这一点，这很令人意外。我的理解一直是，`#[repr(Rust)]` 和 `#[repr(C)]` 本质上只是布局算法的输入，而不是布局算法得出结果之后仍然会产生影响的属性。

598406046.en: Admittedly I don't feel that strongly about this.
598406046.zh: 不过说实话，我对此也没有特别强烈的看法。

598406428.en: Typical example for useful subobject provenance in C is arrays in a struct with other members, or multi-dimensional arrays. Though this seems a lot less relevant in Rust because of bounds checks.
598406428.zh: 在 C 中，一个有用的子对象溯源的典型例子是：结构体中包含数组以及其他成员，或者多维数组。不过由于 Rust 有边界检查，这似乎在 Rust 中没那么重要。

598407914.en: How do bounds checks relate to this?
598407914.zh: 边界检查和这个有什么关系？

598408051.en: Are you saying that the check itself provides the same optimization? Or that the check blocks the desirable optimization?
598408051.zh: 你的意思是，检查本身提供了同样的优化？还是说，检查会阻碍我们想要的优化？

598408570.en: If LLVM had a way of expressing subobject provenance, we could use that for bounds-checked array accesses, without requiring subobject provenance in the aliasing model itself.
598408570.zh: 如果 LLVM 有办法表达子对象溯源，我们就可以把它用于经过边界检查的数组访问，而不需要在别名模型本身中引入子对象溯源。

598412108.zh: 所以，类似于 Rust 专用的 intrinsic？

598413294.en: So, I was thinking about this. I wonder how much read access needs to be limited, compared to the potential usefulness of write access.
598413294.zh: 我刚才在想这个问题。我在琢磨，相比于写访问潜在的实用性，读访问究竟需要受到多大限制。

598415849.en:
My unsubstantiated gut feeling is that subobject provenance is probably not worth it for the long tail of capricious gotchas when writing unsafe code that it would likely cause. On the other hand, more than once I've stared at some code that passes a pointer to one field of an ADT into a function, and looking at some access to *other* fields around the call, and thinking that subobject provenance would be really nice for letting LLVM optimize those other accesses better.

For example, [this code](https://github.com/hanna-kruppe/chacha8rand/blob/fbd14b30f7030e7d0a227db177a7630687c6e177/chacha8rand/src/lib.rs#L823-L824) does an indirect call to refill a buffer that's a field of `self`, then resets another field of `self` (index into that buffer) to zero. Semantically, the order of these two steps doesn't matter. But at least for rustc+LLVM as it stands now, it's not clear that the indirect call can't change the counter, so the current order is better because it makes obvious that the counter will be zero after a refill. I'm not sure if protectors or other parts of a Rust aliasing model would help with this.
598415849.zh:
我未经证实的直觉是，考虑到它很可能在编写不安全代码时带来一长串变幻莫测的坑，子对象溯源大概不值得引入。另一方面，我不止一次盯着这样的代码看过：它把一个 ADT 中某个字段的指针传给一个函数，然后观察调用附近对其他字段的访问，并想着，如果有子对象溯源，就能让 LLVM 更好地优化对那些其他字段的访问，那该多好。

例如，[这段代码](https://github.com/hanna-kruppe/chacha8rand/blob/fbd14b30f7030e7d0a227db177a7630687c6e177/chacha8rand/src/lib.rs#L823-L824) 间接调用了一个函数来填充 `self` 的一个字段（缓冲区），然后把 `self` 的另一个字段（该缓冲区的索引）重置为零。从语义上说，这两个步骤的顺序并不重要。但至少就目前的 rustc+LLVM 而言，间接调用不能修改计数器这一点并不明确，因此当前的顺序更好，因为这样显然可以看出，填充完成后计数器会是零。我不确定 protectors 或 Rust 别名模型的其他部分能否解决这个问题。

598436674.en: I think arrays/slices are a bigger issue in practice for sub-object provenance than structs. There's a lot of code out there that takes the address of one element of an array, turns it into a raw pointer and then expects to be able to access any element of the array with it. Ideally such code should be using `&raw`, but that syntax is relatively new and a lot of existing code just creates a normal reference and casts that to a pointer.
598436674.zh: 我觉得，在实践中，相比结构体，数组/切片涉及的子对象溯源问题更大。有大量现存代码会获取数组某个元素的地址，将其转换为裸指针，然后期望通过这个指针访问数组中的任意元素。理想情况下，这类代码应该使用 `&raw`，但这种语法相对较新，许多现有代码只是创建一个普通引用，再把它转换成指针。

598438266.en: An interesting data point is Swift which is [even stricter](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html) than what is being proposed here. In Swift taking the address of a field "materializes" that field only for the scope of the borrow. Not only does this mean that you can't access other fields through that pointer, it also means that if you take the address of 2 fields adjacent of a local then there is no guarantee that they have consecutive addresses.
598438266.zh: 有一个有趣的参考点是 Swift：它甚至比这里提议的方案[更加严格](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html)。在 Swift 中，获取字段的地址只会在借用的作用域内将该字段“实体化”。这不仅意味着你不能通过那个指针访问其他字段，还意味着，如果你获取了一个局部变量中两个相邻字段的地址，就不能保证它们的地址是连续的。

598440392.en:
I think for structs there's still code that does this. For example, when I started with Rust I did stuff like
```rs
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Vec3 {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub z: f32,
}
```
And then use `&v.x as *const f32` (or mut) to access all 3 elements of `v` like an array. This is not strictly allowed in C/C++ either, but doing it is common. That said, I haven't written code like this in a long time (I'm well aware that `v as *const _ as *const f32` is the way to do that), but it wouldn't surprise me at all if there's code out there that does this. In fact, it would surprise me quite a bit if there is not.
598440392.zh:
我觉得结构体也存在这么做的代码。例如，我刚开始接触 Rust 时，会写类似这样的代码：
```rs
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Vec3 {
    pub x: f32,
    pub y: f32,
    pub z: f32,
}
```
然后使用 `&v.x as *const f32`（或 mut）像访问数组一样访问 `v` 的全部 3 个元素。这在 C/C++ 中严格来说也不允许，但这样做很常见。话虽如此，我已经很久没写过这样的代码了（我很清楚 `v as *const _ as *const f32` 才是正确的做法），但如果外面确实存在这么做的代码，我一点也不会觉得意外。事实上，如果不存在这样的代码，我反而会相当惊讶。

@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598415849)：
```quote
For example, [this code](https://github.com/hanna-kruppe/chacha8rand/blob/fbd14b30f7030e7d0a227db177a7630687c6e177/chacha8rand/src/lib.rs#L823-L824) does an indirect call to refill a buffer that's a field of `self`, then resets another field of `self` (index into that buffer) to zero. Semantically, the order of these two steps doesn't matter. But at least for rustc+LLVM as it stands now, it's not clear that the indirect call can't change the counter, so the current order is better because it makes obvious that the counter will be zero after a refill. I'm not sure if protectors or other parts of a Rust aliasing model would help with this.
```

不行，它们帮不上忙；这个问题确实需要子对象溯源。

@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598438266)：
```quote
An interesting data point is Swift which is [even stricter](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html) than what is being proposed here. In Swift taking the address of a field "materializes" that field only for the scope of the borrow. Not only does this mean that you can't access other fields through that pointer, it also means that if you take the address of 2 fields adjacent of a local then there is no guarantee that they have consecutive addresses.
```

这还挺酷的。

598567318.en: like, a bunch of `repr(C)` structs with a common prefix
598567318.zh: 比如说，一堆具有相同公共前缀的 `repr(C)` 结构体。

598567443.en: so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types

598567564.en: if we also want to take as axiom that the repr shouldnt affect such things (which I agree is a reasonable principle), then the only option left is that we could say enum fields are different than struct fields

598567644.en: Sure we can, we just need to tell people to use `&raw` for this. The question is, how much ecosystem breakage are we willing accept?
598567644.zh: 当然可以，我们只需要告诉大家在这种情况下使用 `&raw`。问题是，我们愿意接受多大程度的生态破坏？

598567842.en: it's also so easy to accidentally use an intermediate reference
598567842.zh: 而且，一不小心使用中间引用也实在太容易了。

598567984.en: and the ergonomics of using only raw ptrs are still terrible, pushing people towards using references
598567984.zh: 仅使用裸指针的便利性仍然很差，这会把人们推向使用引用。

598568507.en: there's work on improving these ergonomics
598568507.zh: 目前有人在努力改善这方面的便利性。

598568641.en: yes. but that's too late for all the code that was already written.

598710279.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598567443):
```quote
so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types
```

I think the proper fix for `&Header` is extern types, so we indeed better not enforce subobject provenance for `repr(C)` structs until those have been stabilized and been stable for a while.

*Technically*, it is something that we could change on an edition boundary, right? So that `repr(C)` only disables subobject provenance for a struct if that struct is defined in an edition < 20xy crate. And even before extern types stabelize, disabling subobject provenance could be made into its own attribute.
598710279.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598567443):
```quote
so I don't think we can realistically enforce subobject provenance on repr(C) types
```

我认为，解决 `&Header` 的正确方式是使用 extern 类型，因此在 extern 类型稳定并稳定运行一段时间之前，我们确实最好不要对 `repr(C)` 结构体强制执行子对象来源。

*严格来说*，我们可以在 edition 边界进行这种改变，对吧？也就是说，只有当某个结构体定义于 edition < 20xy 的 crate 中时，`repr(C)` 才会让该结构体禁用子对象来源。而且，即使 extern 类型尚未稳定，也可以将禁用子对象来源设计成一个单独的属性。

598717531.en: maybe after enough years of unsafe coding guides writing "don't mix references and raw pointers unless you really know what you're doing" in bold we'll be able to not have to guarantee things we never allowed :relieved:
598717531.zh: 也许再过上足够多年，unsafe 编程指南一直用粗体写着“除非你真的知道自己在做什么，否则不要混用引用和裸指针”，我们就可以不用再保证那些我们从未允许过的事情了 :relieved:
