598958553.en:
more evidence that we dont want subobject provenance on arrays:
https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/pull/6262
598958553.zh:
更多证据表明，我们不希望对数组引入子对象来源：
https://github.com/rust-bitcoin/rust-bitcoin/pull/6262

598964850.en: evidence that ppl make the mistake, not that they have code patterns that require not having it
598964850.zh: 这证明了人们会犯这种错误，而不是证明他们有必须取消子对象来源才能使用的代码模式。

598967173.en: evidence that if we enforce subobject provenance on arrays we'll have lots of UB in existing code out there
598967173.zh: 这证明了，如果我们对数组强制执行子对象来源，那么现有代码中会有大量 UB。

598967197.en: I've seen enough of that kind of evidence to consider this not a viable option
598967197.zh: 这类证据我已经看得够多了，足以认为这不是一个可行的选择。

598967359.en: What does lack of subobject provenance mean for split_at_mut, if anything? Both split sides retain write permissions to the full slice, they just cannot produce overlapping &mut's without the use of unsafe and therefore the API is sound?
598967359.zh: 如果有的话，缺少子对象来源对 split_at_mut 意味着什么？分割后的两部分都保留了对完整切片的写权限，只是如果不使用 unsafe，就无法生成彼此重叠的 &mut，因此这个 API 是健全的，对吗？

598984027.en: it means that if you extremely carefully write unsafe code you can access parts of slice A from slice B and vice versa. though it is still UB to access the same slice element from both parts (unless you are only reading).
598984027.zh: 这意味着，如果你极其谨慎地编写 unsafe 代码，就可以从切片 A 访问切片 B 的部分内容，反之亦然。不过，从两部分访问同一个切片元素仍然是 UB（除非你们都只是读取）。

599021852.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598967197):
```quote
I've seen enough of that kind of evidence to consider this not a viable option
```

it seems to me that you could opt-in to subobject provenance to enable optimizations though, right? e.g., perhaps structs defined in a future edition crate would need an attribute to opt out of assumptions here. (Maybe that's repr(linear/C), maybe not).

It'd be nice to allow opt-in at least inside std for e.g. Vec and similar data structures where we currently sometimes write code to manually copy len/capacity out while doing allocations, iterating, etc. to gain this optimization (at the cost of some extra stack bytes/registers).
599021852.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598967197):
```quote
I've seen enough of that kind of evidence to consider this not a viable option
```

在我看来，你们可以选择启用子对象来源来开启优化，对吧？例如，未来 edition 的 crate 中定义的结构体，可能需要一个属性来选择退出这里的相关假设。（也许这个属性是 repr(linear/C)，也许不是。）

至少允许在 std 内部为 Vec 及类似数据结构选择启用会很不错。对于这些数据结构，我们目前有时会在分配、迭代等操作期间，手动将 len/capacity 复制出来，以获得这项优化（代价是额外占用一些栈空间/寄存器）。

599023040.en:
sure we can always add more attributes later that add more UB.

@_**simulacrum|116122** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/599021852):
```quote
It'd be nice to allow opt-in at least inside std for e.g. Vec and similar data structures where we currently sometimes write code to manually copy len/capacity out while doing allocations, iterating, etc. to gain this optimization (at the cost of some extra stack bytes/registers).
```

that also assumes that we have some way to actually tell LLVM about this subobject provenance.
599023040.zh:
当然，我们以后总是可以添加更多会引入额外 UB 的属性。

@_**simulacrum|116122** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/599021852):
```quote
It'd be nice to allow opt-in at least inside std for e.g. Vec and similar data structures where we currently sometimes write code to manually copy len/capacity out while doing allocations, iterating, etc. to gain this optimization (at the cost of some extra stack bytes/registers).
```

这还假设我们有办法真正将这种子对象来源告知 LLVM。

599048394.en: I would very much like to be able to tell LLVM about subobject provenance for the move elimination optimization. The optimization has a tendency to replace locals with projections into a larger local. When this happens, I would like to be able to tell LLVM alias analysis that references into the larger local (that were originally references to an unmerged local) are guaranteed to only access a subset of that larger local.
599048394.zh: 我非常希望能把子对象来源信息告知 LLVM，以便进行消除移动优化。该优化倾向于用对一个更大局部变量的投影来替代局部变量。发生这种情况时，我希望能够告诉 LLVM 的别名分析：对这个更大局部变量的引用（原本是对某个未合并局部变量的引用）保证只会访问该更大局部变量的一个子集。

599048435.en: Essentially, I can see this being useful in MIR even if we never expose it in the surface language.
599048435.zh: 本质上，即使我们永远不在表层语言中暴露它，我也能看出它在 MIR 中会很有用。

599106666.en: General subobject provenance in LLVM is kind of Hard, because it adds a lot of intrinsics on the pointer path, and everything needs to learn to look past them (correctly), otherwise you lose optimizations. I think your case might be handled more easily if we add allocator provenance intrinsics (I guess this also more directly represents what you are doing, where multiple sub-allocations are serviced from one larger one). In that case looking through the intrinsics shouldn't be important. (The subobject provenance issue may become simpler if we add ptr_provenance path as part of full restrict.)
599106666.zh: LLVM 中通用的子对象来源信息有点难处理，因为它会在指针路径上加入大量 intrinsic，而所有东西都需要学会（正确地）越过它们进行分析，否则就会损失优化机会。我认为，如果我们添加分配器来源信息 intrinsic，或许能更容易地处理你的场景（我猜这也更直接地表达了你正在做的事情：从一个更大的分配中提供多个子分配）。这样一来，分析时是否越过这些 intrinsic 就不那么重要了。（如果我们把 `ptr_provenance` 路径作为完整 restrict 的一部分加入，子对象来源信息的问题或许会变得更简单。）

602695929.en:
Stumbled across this and these are my thoughts from the CHERI world:

CHERI can support this in the architecture, and so in CHERI LLVM it is a compile-time option to enable (for C/C++), with various type and member annotations, and builtins, to opt out in specific cases when otherwise enabled. This does brush up against language semantics issues (e.g. &a[x] is defined to be equivalent to a + x in C so shouldn't be restricted, and yet there are clearly reasons why that might be useful to do), as well as just de-facto use (e.g. embedding linked list nodes into larger structures), so our default is to turn it off, and if you want to turn it on you can, with varying degrees of aggressiveness that increasingly violate ISO C yet have clear benefits for certain use cases (like the array example, which you have to dial things up quite a bit to get). For our CheriBSD kernel we turn it on, as there is a non-zero number of past CVEs for overflowing within a struct, but only at the lowest level. Even then it is a decent source of friction (the cause of most of our panics these days when exercising previously-untested device drivers etc), but we currently view it as a worthwhile thing to do. I would hope that Rust would be better poised to be able to have a subobject provenance story in its semantics, but I know well the pain that can come from imposing such constraints on systems code...
602695929.zh:
偶然看到了这个话题，以下是我从 CHERI 领域得到的一些想法：

CHERI 可以在架构层面支持这一点，因此在 CHERI LLVM 中，对于 C/C++，这是一个可以在编译时启用的选项；同时还提供各种类型和成员注解，以及 builtins，以便在默认启用时针对特定情况选择退出。这确实会触及语言语义问题（例如，在 C 中，`&a[x]` 被定义为等价于 `a + x`，所以不应受到限制，但显然，限制它又有充分的理由），也会涉及实际上的使用方式（例如，将链表节点嵌入更大的结构体中）。因此我们的默认设置是关闭它；如果你想开启，可以自行开启，并根据需要选择不同程度的激进设置。这些设置越激进，就越偏离 ISO C，但对某些使用场景有明显好处（比如数组示例——要实现这一点，你得把设置调得相当激进）。对于 CheriBSD 内核，我们会开启它，因为过去确实有不少 CVE 是由于在结构体内部发生溢出导致的，不过我们只在最低层级启用。即便如此，这仍然会带来相当大的摩擦（如今，在测试之前未测试过的设备驱动等代码时，我们大多数 panic 都是由此引起的），但目前我们认为这样做是值得的。我希望 Rust 在其语义中建立一套子对象来源信息机制时能更有优势，但我也很清楚，给系统代码施加这类约束可能会带来多大的痛苦……

602701062.en:
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598408051):
```quote
Are you saying that the check itself provides the same optimization? Or that the check blocks the desirable optimization?
```

I don't know if this is the same thing, but one problem we had (still have? dunno) with the `array::IntoIter` was that it was really hard to SRoA because offsetting into the *array* field -- which basically always happens for any interesting consumer -- looks extremely similar to offsetting to read the start/end fields of the iterator itself so it needed *some* way to know that `array_intoiter.as_slice()[i]` isn't allowed to read the start/end fields.

IIRC we ended up moving the array after the start/end so that as long as one only uses known-positive GEP offsets it worked well enough?  But `array::IntoIter<usize, 10>` is a place where the `Range<usize>` and `[usize; 10]` being UB to intermingle would be handy.

(Said without thinking about practicality of it as an overall rule.)
602701062.zh:
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598408051)：
```quote
你是说检查本身提供了同样的优化吗？还是说这个检查阻止了我们所希望的优化？
```

我不知道这是不是同一回事，但我们之前（现在还存在吗？不知道）在处理 `array::IntoIter` 时遇到的一个问题是：它很难进行 SRoA，因为对 *array* 字段进行偏移——任何有趣的使用者基本都会这样做——看起来和对迭代器自身的 start/end 字段进行读取时的偏移极其相似，所以它需要某种方式来知道 `array_intoiter.as_slice()[i]` 不允许读取 start/end 字段。

如果我没记错，我们最后把 array 放到了 start/end 之后，这样只要只使用已知为正的 GEP 偏移量，效果就还算不错？不过，`array::IntoIter<usize, 10>` 确实是一个这样的场景：如果规定 `Range<usize>` 和 `[usize; 10]` 之间不能混用且这会触发 UB，那将会很有帮助。

（这里没有考虑把它作为一条总体规则的实际可行性。）

602795996.en: @**Jessica Clarke** is the point that enforcing subobject provenance is useful to find real bugs (that would be bugs even if the language had no subobject provenance)?
602795996.zh: @**Jessica Clarke** 的意思是，强制执行子对象来源信息，是为了找出实际的 bug（即使语言没有子对象来源信息，这些问题本来也会是 bug）吗？

602796104.en: one could consider turning some forms of subobject provenance violations into EB not UB, so we couldnt use it for optimizations (and there is no risk of miscompilations) but a strict enforcement mode could still error on such code
602796104.zh: 可以考虑把某些形式的子对象来源信息违规行为改成 EB，而不是 UB。这样我们就不能利用它进行优化（也不会有错误编译的风险），但严格执行模式仍然可以对这类代码报错。

602796210.en: that said, I am fairly convinced that we dont want any such EB or UB for array indexing
602796210.zh: 话虽如此，我相当确信，我们不希望数组索引存在任何这类 EB 或 UB。

602796244.en: (i.e., we want to match the C semantics there)
602796244.zh: （也就是说，我们希望在这里匹配 C 的语义。）

602796352.en: that would also mean no official rust tool should ever complain about code that "violates" array subobject provenance
602796352.zh: 这也意味着，任何官方 Rust 工具都不应因为代码“违反”了数组子对象来源信息规则而报错。

602853007.en:
I am outside of opsem and only a little chic of a Rust developer so I don't think my vibes count for much but... I must say I actually do find myself thinking that I'd prefer having subobject provenance.

I find myself thinking that lacking subobject provenance sounds harder to reason about in unsafe code, or harder to teach maybe...? Like, you have an unsafe operation that takes some `&T` and its safety condition is that this must have been created in a particular way / from a particular struct, and also must not have had its provenance restricted, but none of that is visible in the type system. Effectively, the safest of safe types can now have fairly gnarly variance to when they're actually safe, and Rust just says: "yes, this is fine and if you want to write your unsafe code to work with references to a field of type T that just looks like a normal reference to a T, then knock yourself out."

Compared to having subobject provenance, where a reference is a reference is a reference, and if you want to do fancy and unsafe things with eg. field pointers then you have to write specific wrappers over field pointers and carefully carry the provenance over. A `&u32` is always just a `&u32` in this world, never a `&u32<MyStruct::field>`.
602853007.zh:
我不属于 opsem 领域，也只是个对 Rust 略懂皮毛的开发者，所以我不觉得自己的直觉有多大参考价值，不过……我得说，我确实发现自己更倾向于拥有子对象来源信息。

我总觉得，缺少子对象来源信息会让 unsafe 代码更难推理，也可能更难教学……比如，有一个 unsafe 操作接受某个 `&T`，它的安全条件是：这个引用必须以特定方式创建，或者必须来自某个特定结构体；同时，它的来源信息还不能被限制，但这些要求在类型系统中完全不可见。实际上，就连最安全的安全类型，现在也可能在什么情况下才真正安全这件事上存在相当棘手的差异，而 Rust 只会说：“没问题；如果你想让自己的 unsafe 代码处理指向某个字段的引用，而这个引用看起来就只是普通的 `T` 类型引用，那你尽管去做吧。”

相比之下，如果存在子对象来源信息，那么引用就是引用；如果你想对字段指针之类的东西做一些复杂而不安全的操作，就必须为字段指针编写专门的封装，并谨慎地传递其来源信息。在这个世界里，`&u32` 永远只是 `&u32`，而不会是 `&u32<MyStruct::field>`。

602856751.en: The main way that people run up against subobject provenance is with the `&Header` pattern. That's quite different from `&u32`. The user-defined `Header` types have safety invariants directly tied to the extra data (beyond what `size_of_val` says) existing. Sometimes you can't even statically write down the type that the header is part of. I don't think it's obvious that that kind of unsafe code would become much simpler to reason about by enforcing subobject provenance.
602856751.zh: 人们遇到子对象来源信息问题的主要方式，是使用 `&Header` 模式。这和 `&u32` 很不一样。用户定义的 `Header` 类型，其安全不变量直接依赖于额外数据的存在，而这些数据并不在 `size_of_val` 所反映的范围内。有时，你甚至无法静态地写出这个 header 所属对象的类型。我不认为，强制执行子对象来源信息，显然就能让这类 unsafe 代码变得更容易推理。

602856923.en: You are making the mistake of pinning library requirements to language requirements. Stricter preconditions do not make unsafe code easier to write.

602857234.en: The kind of reasoning you are try to engage in is hazardous because if it was valid, would forbid removing UB from the language. Adding UB to the language is already a breaking change, so if we were to also forbid removing UB, the opsem would be fixed and immutable.
602857234.zh: 你试图进行的这种推理很危险，因为如果它成立，就会禁止从语言中移除 UB。向语言中添加 UB 本身就已经是一项破坏性变更；所以，如果我们还要禁止移除 UB，那么 opsem 就会被固定下来，永远不可改变。

602863390.en:
I'm not smart enough and probably too tired to really understand but... In a sense I feel like this makes _safe_ code harder to write.

```rust
fn do_with_type_erased_t(t: &Header) { ... }
```

Is this function safe? Or did we make a mistake and it should actually be `unsafe`? That depends:
1. If it does not read anything beyond the Header then it is safe.
2. If it does read beyond the Header and we do not have subobject provenance it is also safe.
3. Exception: If we have a safe `fn restrict_provenance` in which case it must be unsafe.
4. Exception to 3: If we have a marker trait `Restrictable` that a type can opt out of which is required to call `fn restrict_provenance` then it is safe.
5. Alternative exception to 3: If `fn restrict_provenance` is unsafe then the function is again safe. The safety precondition on `restrict_provenance` is going to be pretty rough though; "reference must not be used to access data out of its bounds". That just feels like it's on the wrong end of the stick - proving a negative instead of giving a positive guarantee.

It just seems complicated to me that `&(mut )T` of all types would have a potentially viral safety condition like this.
602863390.zh:
我不够聪明，而且可能也太累了，实在没法完全理解，但……从某种意义上说，我觉得这会让编写 _safe_ 代码变得更困难。

```rust
fn do_with_type_erased_t(t: &Header) { ... }
```

这个函数安全吗？还是说我们犯了错，它实际上应该是 `unsafe`？这取决于具体情况：
1. 如果它不会读取 Header 之外的任何内容，那么它是安全的。
2. 如果它确实会读取 Header 之外的内容，而我们又没有子对象 provenance，那么它也仍然是安全的。
3. 例外：如果我们有一个安全的 `fn restrict_provenance`，那么它就必须是 `unsafe`。
4. 对第 3 点的例外：如果我们有一个标记 trait `Restrictable`，类型可以选择不实现它，而调用 `fn restrict_provenance` 又要求实现该 trait，那么它就是安全的。
5. 对第 3 点的另一种例外：如果 `fn restrict_provenance` 是 `unsafe` 的，那么该函数又重新变得安全了。不过，`restrict_provenance` 的安全前置条件会相当棘手——“不得使用该引用访问其边界之外的数据”。这给人的感觉就是方向完全反了：不是提供一个正向保证，而是要求证明某件事不会发生。

在我看来，所有类型的 `&(mut )T` 都可能带有这样一种会传染开的安全条件，实在太复杂了。

602869888.en:
I had generally been having similar thoughts to @_**Aapo Alasuutari** but this conversation is making it clearer how `&Header` can be a sensible thing even in safe code.

* Unambiguously true: When we attribute a type `T` to a piece of memory, such as by passing an `&T`, we make a claim about the contents of that memory.
* Potential extension: When we attribute a type `T` to a piece of memory, we make a claim about the contents of *adjacent* memory.
602869888.zh:
我之前总体上也有和 @_**Aapo Alasuutari** 类似的想法，但这次讨论让我更清楚地认识到，即使在安全代码中，`&Header` 也可以是合理的。

* 毫无疑问：当我们把类型 `T` 归属于一块内存时，比如传入一个 `&T`，我们是在对这块内存的内容做出某种断言。
* 可能的扩展：当我们把类型 `T` 归属于一块内存时，我们是在对*相邻*内存的内容也做出某种断言。

602870362.en: …hm, wait, what about [`std::slice::from_ref()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_ref.html)? This implies that, if it is valid to unsafely access the adjacent memory from an arbitrary provided `&Header`, then it must also be valid to unsafely access the adjacent memory from the last element of `&[Header]` (because safe code may transform `&Header` to `&[Header]` and back). This seems like it might have bad consequences for the optimizability of slice accesses.
602870362.zh: ……嗯，等等，那 [`std::slice::from_ref()`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/slice/fn.from_ref.html) 怎么办？这意味着，如果从任意给定的 `&Header` 访问相邻内存在 unsafe 情况下是有效的，那么从 `&[Header]` 的最后一个元素访问相邻内存在 unsafe 情况下也必须是有效的（因为安全代码可以将 `&Header` 转换成 `&[Header]`，再转换回来）。这似乎可能会对 slice 访问的优化能力造成不良影响。

602870801.en:
@_**Aapo Alasuutari|699208** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602869588):
```quote
they'll just be unsound in a more subtle manner (cannot have `restrict_provenance` called on `&(mut )Header`)
```

Yes, `restrict_provenance` is essentially incompatible with the `&Header` pattern. That is a good point. Though it's not so surprising to me: we know the `&Header` pattern is incompatible with subobject provenance, and having `restrict_provenance` essentially means "we have subobject provenance, but it's applied only sometimes instead of automatically for every `&T` that is created" which of course makes no difference for soundness.

602871624.en: In a similarly reductive manner, the `&T <-> &[T]` case seems to boil down to: if we don't have subobject provenance, we don't have subobject provenance for slice elements in particular. 602927687.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602795996):
```quote
@**Jessica Clarke** is the point that enforcing subobject provenance is useful to find real bugs (that would be bugs even if the language had no subobject provenance)?
```

It's about closing security vulnerabilities that are due to intra-object overflows, like https://projectzero.google/2021/12/this-shouldnt-have-happened.html. In theory if you turn on subobject bounds with CHERI LLVM when compiling that code then (ignoring that the next step in the chain was to inject a function pointer which we'd also break, but surely there are other interesting data-oriented things you could do) CHERI could have prevented it. Sometimes there are good reasons why you don't want subobject provenance, but I generally take the view that it's the exception not the rule and it's not too onerous to require opting into the less-secure form, but at least in the case of C there is a lot of existing code that would break so the story is more awkward. With Rust though I imagine (or at least naively hope...) people are generally better about not doing things that go against subobject provenance than your average overly-cunning C programmer.
602927687.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/602795996)：
```quote
@**Jessica Clarke** 的意思是，强制执行子对象 provenance，是因为这有助于发现真正的 bug（即使语言没有子对象 provenance，这些问题也仍然会是 bug）吗？
```

这关系到修复由对象内部溢出导致的安全漏洞，例如 https://projectzero.google/2021/12/this-shouldnt-have-happened.html。理论上，如果你在用 CHERI LLVM 编译那段代码时启用子对象边界，那么（先不考虑攻击链的下一步是注入一个函数指针，而这同样会被我们阻止；不过肯定还可以进行其他有趣的面向数据的攻击）CHERI 本来是可以阻止它的。有时你确实有充分理由不希望使用子对象 provenance，但总的来说，我认为这属于例外而不是常态；要求用户显式选择安全性较低的形式，负担并不算太大。不过至少对于 C 来说，已经存在大量会因此无法工作的代码，所以情况要棘手得多。至于 Rust，我想（或者至少天真地希望……）人们通常比那些平均水平上过于狡猾的 C 程序员更不容易写出违背子对象 provenance 的代码。

603475659.en:
by that I mean that just like the compiler can't put `T` in read-only memory if it contains an `UnsafeCell` ignoring stuff behind pointers, I think the compiler shouldn't enable subobject provenance if `T` contains any type with subobject provenance disabled, ignoring stuff behind pointers. I'm not saying that some other unrelated field of `T` gets disabled subobject provenance too, which is the undecided part of `UnsafeCell`. e.g.:
```rust
pub struct T {
    pub unrelated: Unrelated,
    pub field: TypeWithoutSubobjectProvenance,
}
```
so with `t: T` -- `&t` doesn't use subobject provenance, neither does `&t.field`, but `&t.unrelated` can use subobject provenance since `Unrelated` doesn't disable it.
603475659.zh:
我的意思是，就像编译器不能把包含 `UnsafeCell` 的 `T`（忽略指针背后的内容）放入只读内存一样，我认为如果 `T` 包含任何禁用了子对象来源的类型（同样忽略指针背后的内容），编译器也不应该启用子对象来源。我并不是说 `T` 的其他无关字段也应该禁用子对象来源；这正是 `UnsafeCell` 尚未决定的部分。例如：
```rust
pub struct T {
    pub unrelated: Unrelated,
    pub field: TypeWithoutSubobjectProvenance,
}
```
因此，对于 `t: T`——`&t` 不使用子对象来源，`&t.field` 也不使用，但 `&t.unrelated` 可以使用子对象来源，因为 `Unrelated` 并不会禁用它。

```quote
An interesting data point is Swift which is [even stricter](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html) than what is being proposed here. In Swift taking the address of a field "materializes" that field only for the scope of the borrow. Not only does this mean that you can't access other fields through that pointer, it also means that if you take the address of 2 fields adjacent of a local then there is no guarantee that they have consecutive addresses.
```

In an old thread (https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Varargs.20SROA.20sadness/), I really wanted this for variadic generics. Not just for performance, but when bringing `unsized_fn_params` into the mix, it's necessary for certain varargs designs to work at all
603954424.zh:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/598438266)：
```quote
一个有趣的参考点是 Swift，它甚至比这里提议的方案更加严格。[在 Swift 中](https://www.cocoawithlove.com/blog/2016/02/16/use_it_or_lose_it_why_safe_c_is_sometimes_unsafe_swift.html)，获取字段地址只会在借用的作用域内“实体化”该字段。这不仅意味着你不能通过那个指针访问其他字段，还意味着如果你获取了局部变量中两个相邻字段的地址，就无法保证它们的地址是连续的。
```

在一个较早的讨论串（https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Varargs.20SROA.20sadness/）中，我非常希望变参泛型能具备这一点。不仅仅是为了性能；当把 `unsized_fn_params` 也考虑进来后，某些变参设计要想正常工作，这甚至是必需的。

604215119.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/603950737):
```quote
C's flexible array member pattern is commonly used from Rust in a way that would violate subobject provenance: https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html
```

They don't inherently violate subobject provenance, and you can still restrict references in the abstract machine to be only to the array, but you do need a way to talk about the size of that subobject in the semantics (and, for enforcement, obtain it somehow). For us, C flexible array members (and I think zero-sized ones as well, since zero-sized arrays are a GNU extension that often get used for flexible arrays in pre-C99 code) with subobject bounds enabled notionally get bounds of the entire flexible array member, which we realise by leaving the upper bound from the surrounding object as-is, only increasing the lower bond, which is a conservative over-approximation (since depending on where that capability came from there may be other objects beyond the end of that flexible array member which will end up within bounds, but it's the best we can do without further annotations like the `__counted_by` used by Apple's -fbounds-safety software bounds enforcement).
604215119.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/603950737)：
```quote
C 的柔性数组成员模式在 Rust 中很常见，但其用法会违反子对象来源：https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html
```

它们并非从根本上违反子对象来源；在抽象机中，你仍然可以将引用限制为只能指向数组。但你确实需要一种方式，在语义中描述该子对象的大小（而在实施检查时，也需要以某种方式获取这个大小）。对我们来说，启用了子对象边界的 C 柔性数组成员（我认为零大小数组也一样，因为零大小数组是 GNU 扩展，在 C99 之前的代码中经常被用作柔性数组）在概念上会获得整个柔性数组成员的边界。我们的实现方式是保留外围对象的上界，只增大下界；这是一种保守的过度近似（因为根据该能力的来源，柔性数组成员末尾之后可能还有其他对象，而这些对象最终也会落在边界内），但如果没有进一步的注解——例如 Apple 的 `-fbounds-safety` 软件边界检查所使用的 `__counted_by`——这已经是我们能做到的最好结果。

这样就只剩下枚举了。  
（还有联合体，但我想不出那里有什么可能的子对象 provenance。）

605657693.en: Could still do it over an edition boundary? (I.e. implicitly add the magic no-subobject-provenance marker to all structs in the old edition.)
605657693.zh: 不过，能不能通过 edition 边界来实现？（也就是说，隐式地给旧 edition 中的所有结构体加上那个神奇的“无子对象 provenance”标记。）

605657942.en: At least assuming that's possible, I'd rather not conflate the question of "what are our ideal semantics here going forward" with "how compatible is existing code with those semantics".
605657942.zh: 至少假设这是可行的，我不太希望把“从今往后我们理想中的语义是什么”和“现有代码与这些语义的兼容性有多高”这两个问题混为一谈。

605673952.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605637366):
```quote
so, that pretty much means no subobject provenance for both arrays and structs.
which only leaves enums.
(and unions, but I cant think f any possible subobject provenance there.)
```

it seems odd to not do structs and do enums, then; i think going for an edition change and making it actually work on both (maybe even with arrays, though that seems more ingrained) seems more reasonable than settling for this weird half support
605673952.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605637366)：  
```quote
所以，这基本上意味着数组和结构体都不能采用子对象 provenance。
这样就只剩下枚举了。
（还有联合体，但我想不出那里有什么可能的子对象 provenance。）
```

那么，不支持结构体却支持枚举，似乎就很奇怪了；我觉得，与其接受这种奇怪的半支持状态，不如通过 edition 变更，让它在这两者上都真正可用（甚至数组也支持，尽管数组的这种用法似乎更加根深蒂固），这样更合理。

605828833.en:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605657693):
```quote
Could still do it over an edition boundary? (I.e. implicitly add the magic no-subobject-provenance marker to all structs in the old edition.)
```

So if I have a crate that uses an old edition and is written with old code and it gets passed a struct defined in a new crate, the old code needs to uphold subobject provenance?
605828833.zh:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605657693)：  
```quote
不过，能不能通过 edition 边界来实现？（也就是说，隐式地给旧 edition 中的所有结构体加上那个神奇的“无子对象 provenance”标记。）
```

那么，如果我有一个使用旧 edition、由旧代码编写的 crate，而它接收了一个定义在新 crate 中的结构体，那么旧代码就需要遵守子对象 provenance 规则吗？

605829019.en: This seems like it's not contained to the crate boundary which I feel like is part of the requirement for editions
605829019.zh: 这似乎意味着规则并不局限在 crate 边界之内，而我觉得 edition 的要求之一就是应该以 crate 边界为界。

605836820.en: Kind of, but I think at least in contexts like https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html subobject provenance violations are very tightly bound to the struct being passed in? Accessing beyond the subobject only makes sense for specific structures that are specifically designed with that usage in mind, not generically.
605836820.zh: 某种程度上是这样，但我认为至少在 https://rust-lang.github.io/rust-bindgen/using-fam.html 这类场景中，子对象 provenance 违规行为与所传入的结构体有非常紧密的联系。只有针对特意为这种用法设计的特定结构体，访问超出子对象的部分才有意义，而不是对所有结构体都适用。

605855277.en: IMO the edition change should take effect at the point where the reference is created, not based on the type. So `&x.y` in 2024 returns a reference with whole-allocation provenance, but in 2027 edition returns a reference restricted to the `y` field.
605855277.zh: 我认为，edition 变更应该在创建引用的地方生效，而不是取决于类型。因此，2024 中的 `&x.y` 会返回具有整个分配 provenance 的引用，而在 2027 edition 中则会返回一个 provenance 受限于 `y` 字段的引用。

605861584.en: so then if you use a struct from a 3rd-party crate that is edition 2024 in edition 2027 code, there is no way to return a `&Header` with provenance for the data after the header since creating a reference causes sub-object provenance, but you can do that in edition 2024? that seems like the wrong way to me
605861584.zh: 那么，如果你在 edition 2027 的代码中使用一个来自第三方 crate、且该 crate 使用 edition 2024 的结构体，就无法返回一个具有 header 之后数据 provenance 的 `&Header`，因为创建引用会导致子对象 provenance；但在 edition 2024 中却可以做到？这在我看来似乎不是正确的做法。

605861990.en: it works much better if it's based on which edition the struct is defined in so `Header` from an edition 2024 crate still works when used in an edition 2027 crate, and when the struct definition is changed to edition 2027 it can have the opt-out of subobject provenance attribute, so keeps working
605861990.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，效果会好得多：这样，来自 edition 2024 crate 的 `Header` 在 edition 2027 crate 中使用时仍然可以正常工作；而当结构体定义改为 edition 2027 时，可以通过属性选择退出子对象 provenance，从而继续保持正常工作。

605866400.en: Making it based on the edition where the struct is defined means it's a breaking change for the defining crate to update its edition without opting every single one of its types out of subobject provenance
605866400.zh: 如果根据结构体定义所在的 edition 来决定，那么定义该结构体的 crate 在更新 edition 时，如果不为它的每一个类型都选择退出子对象 provenance，就会构成破坏性变更。

605867169.en: That only applies to types with public fields as you can't create a reference to private fields outside of the defining crate, right?
605867169.zh: 不过，这只适用于字段为 public 的类型，对吧？因为在定义它的 crate 外部无法创建指向私有字段的引用。

605867878.en: Suppose a crate provides `fn as_header(&self) -> &Header` and `unsafe fn from_header(&Header) -> &Self`.
605867878.zh: 假设某个 crate 提供了 `fn as_header(&self) -> &Header` 和 `unsafe fn from_header(&Header) -> &Self`。

605870750.en:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605855277):
```quote
IMO the edition change should take effect at the point where the reference is created, not based on the type. So `&x.y` in 2024 returns a reference with whole-allocation provenance, but in 2027 edition returns a reference restricted to the `y` field.
```

On top of this, there could be a way for individual structs to opt out of subobject provenance on all editions. So you get best of both worlds
605870750.zh:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605855277)：  
```quote
我认为，edition 变更应该在创建引用的地方生效，而不是取决于类型。因此，2024 中的 `&x.y` 会返回具有整个分配 provenance 的引用，而在 2027 edition 中则会返回一个 provenance 受限于 `y` 字段的引用。
```

除此之外，还可以让单个结构体在所有 edition 中都选择退出子对象 provenance。这样两全其美。

605879515.en: having two sets of rules for unsafe code interacting seems tricky to reason about, in the best case scenario, and potentially unreconcilable
605879515.zh: 让不安全代码交互时存在两套规则，即使在最理想的情况下也很难推理，而且还有可能根本无法协调。

605883845.en: reconciling them seems easy, it's just `if has_attribute || edition <= 2024 { disable_subobject_provenance() }`, it's not like both methods have to agree
605883845.zh: 协调起来似乎很容易，只要是 `if has_attribute || edition <= 2024 { disable_subobject_provenance() }` 就行了；又不是两种方式必须达成一致。

605884848.en: that said, I think we need some way to create references without subobject provenance on all editions, so if `&v.header` doesn't work in edition 2027, then you can use `unsafe { *&raw const v.header }` or something
605884848.zh: 话虽如此，我认为我们需要一种能在所有 edition 中创建不带子对象 provenance 的引用的方式。因此，如果 `&v.header` 在 edition 2027 中无法使用，那么你可以改用 `unsafe { *&raw const v.header }` 之类的写法。

605889301.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605884848):
```quote
that said, I think we need some way to create references without subobject provenance on all editions, so if `&v.header` doesn't work in edition 2027, then you can use `unsafe { *&raw const v.header }` or something
```

Yes, there should be a macro for this
605889301.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605884848)：  
```quote
话虽如此，我认为我们需要一种能在所有 edition 中创建不带子对象 provenance 的引用的方式。因此，如果 `&v.header` 在 edition 2027 中无法使用，那么你可以改用 `unsafe { *&raw const v.header }` 之类的写法。
```

是的，应该为此提供一个宏。

605903358.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605883845):
```quote
reconciling them seems easy, it's just `if has_attribute || edition <= 2024 { disable_subobject_provenance() }`, it's not like both methods have to agree
```

sorry, i meant the models for unsafe code of "enable subobject provenance" and "no subobject provenance restrictions" as the two sets of rules, not whatever mechanisms are used to do it in the compiler.

i don't see how code that wants to take advantage of subobject provenance could ever interact with any other code, without needing to manually audit every use of unsafe in all dependencies to be sure that they don't perform operations incompatible with subobject provenance.
605903358.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605883845)：  
```quote
协调起来似乎很容易，只要是 `if has_attribute || edition <= 2024 { disable_subobject_provenance() }` 就行了；又不是两种方式必须达成一致。
```

抱歉，我指的是“启用子对象 provenance”和“不施加子对象 provenance 限制”这两种不安全代码模型，也就是那两套规则，而不是编译器用来实现它们的机制。

我看不出，想利用子对象 provenance 的代码要如何与其他代码交互，同时又不必手动审查所有依赖中的每一处 unsafe 用法，以确保它们没有执行与子对象 provenance 不兼容的操作。

605908096.en: Not sure if it's been answered yet, but, how much of the existing dependant code uses repr(Rust) containers.
605908096.zh: 不确定之前是否已经有人回答过了，不过，现有的依赖代码中有多少使用了 `repr(Rust)` 容器？

605908310.en: I mean, as far as *code* goes, that's as much a question of the default soundness contracts, not "what is UB?". This question I think is generally more about enabling optimizations. But also it's hard to imagine dependent code that would cause a problem there? (Or rather, doing so without being obviously unreasonable by whatever default contract people settle on)
605908310.zh: 我的意思是，就 *代码* 而言，这更多是默认健全性契约的问题，而不是“什么是 UB？”。我觉得这个问题通常更多是在讨论如何启用优化。不过，也很难想象依赖代码会因此造成什么问题？（或者说，很难想象在不明显违背人们最终确定的默认契约的情况下做到这一点。）

606054234.en:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605657693):
```quote
Could still do it over an edition boundary? (I.e. implicitly add the magic no-subobject-provenance marker to all structs in the old edition.)
```

that's a new language feature. for now we're busy enough figuring out the semantics of existing lang features so I consider new features out of scope.
but yeah we are not permanently closing the door to any kind of subobject provenance. (that's trivially true for basically any decision we can make -- we can add new lang features late that make different choices.)
606054234.zh:
@_**Nikita Popov|133224** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605657693)：
```quote
是否仍然可以跨 edition 边界实现？（也就是说，隐式地给旧 edition 中的所有结构体添加神奇的 no-subobject-provenance 标记。）
```

这是一个新的语言特性。目前我们光是弄清楚现有语言特性的语义就已经够忙了，所以我认为新特性不在讨论范围内。

不过，我们确实没有永久关闭任何形式的 subobject provenance 的大门。（对于我们基本上能做出的任何决定，这一点都显然成立——我们以后可以添加新的语言特性，从而做出不同的选择。）

606054495.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605866400):
```quote
Making it based on the edition where the struct is defined means it's a breaking change for the defining crate to update its edition without opting every single one of its types out of subobject provenance
```

only if the crate allows you to do such things to its types. typically you cant just raw ptr stuff into types you dont control.
606054495.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605866400)：
```quote
根据定义结构体所在的 edition 来决定，会导致定义该结构体的 crate 在更新 edition 时产生破坏性变更，除非它为自己的每一种类型都明确选择不采用 subobject provenance。
```

只有当该 crate 允许你对它的类型做这类操作时才是这样。通常情况下，你不能直接把 raw pointer 操作塞进自己无法控制的类型里。

606054756.en:
@_**Opale|908867** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605673952):
````quote
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605637366):
```quote
so, that pretty much means no subobject provenance for both arrays and structs.
which only leaves enums.
(and unions, but I cant think f any possible subobject provenance there.)
```

it seems odd to not do structs and do enums, then; i think going for an edition change and making it actually work on both (maybe even with arrays, though that seems more ingrained) seems more reasonable than settling for this weird half support
````

enums -- or at least, their discriminant field -- are quite special. so it could make sense to treat them differently. that's the subobject of the model @**Mario Carneiro** has been working on that we talked about at the all-hands.
606054756.zh:
@_**Opale|908867** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605673952)：
````quote
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/605637366)：
```quote
所以，这基本上意味着数组和结构体都不采用 subobject provenance。
这样就只剩下枚举了。
（还有联合体，但我想不出那里有什么可能的 subobject provenance。）
```

既然如此，不支持结构体却支持枚举似乎很奇怪；我觉得，与其接受这种奇怪的半吊子支持，不如通过 edition 变更，让它在两者上都真正可用（甚至数组也支持，尽管数组看起来更加根深蒂固）。
````
枚举——或者至少它们的判别字段——非常特殊。因此，区别对待它们是有道理的。这正是 @**Mario Carneiro** 一直在研究的模型中的一个子部分，我们在全员会议上讨论过。

607108666.en:
based on the discussion above and at the recent t-opsem meeting, it seems like at least 3 out of 5 opsem members would be fine with saying "there is no subobject provenance on types that currently exist in the language, except maybe for enums". The main arguments are
- a bunch of existing code assumes this already for arrays and slices
- a lot of code generated by bindgen assumes this at least for repr(C) structs
- `#[repr]` shouldn't affect the opsem in such subtle ways
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** you weren't at that meeting -- I wonder what your thoughts on this are?
607108666.zh:
根据上面的讨论以及最近的 t-opsem 会议，至少 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位似乎都可以接受这样的说法：“对于语言目前已有的类型，不存在 subobject provenance；枚举或许例外。”主要论据如下：

- 大量现有代码已经假定数组和切片不存在这种 provenance
- bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 `repr(C)` 结构体做了这样的假定
- `#[repr]` 不应该以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem
- 这种 UB 的收益并不明确。我们可以设想一些它有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这种信息，这让人觉得它在实际有用的优化方面并没有多少可发挥的空间。

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——想知道你们对此有什么看法？

607112709.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666):
```quote
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.
```

imo that's more of LLVM being designed for C where they use TBAA instead of subobject provenance. if rustc can do SRoA in MIR, that would be a useful optimization enabled by subobject provenance that isn't limited much by LLVM's current lack of support for subobject provenance.
607112709.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666)：
```quote
- 这种 UB 的收益并不明确。我们可以设想一些它有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这种信息，这让人觉得它在实际有用的优化方面并没有多少可发挥的空间。
```

我觉得这更多是因为 LLVM 的设计是面向 C 的，而 C 使用 TBAA，而不是 subobject provenance。如果 rustc 能在 MIR 中执行 SRoA，那么 subobject provenance 就能启用一种很有用的优化，而且不会受到 LLVM 当前缺乏 subobject provenance 支持的太大限制。

607113158.en: SRoA is one of those optimizations that doesn't do much on its own but enables major optimizations since it allows the rest of the compiler to know when fields can be treated as independent variables so it knows that opaque function calls can't clobber or read them
607113158.zh: SRoA 属于那种单独来看作用不大、但能启用重大优化的优化，因为它让编译器的其余部分知道哪些字段可以被当作相互独立的变量处理，从而知道不透明的函数调用不会覆写或读取它们。

607115859.en: Isn't the allocator provenenace RFC also a form of subprovenance?
607115859.zh: allocator provenance RFC 不也是一种 subprovenance 吗？

607125347.en: Example of where C++ using TBAA can optimize code more than Rust can (removing the store in the loop), but I expect Rust can trivially recover that by using SRoA with subobject provenance: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/M836Ke61d
607125347.zh: 这是一个例子：使用 TBAA 的 C++ 能够执行比 Rust 更多的优化（移除循环中的 store），但我预计 Rust 通过结合 subobject provenance 使用 SRoA，就能轻松做到同样的优化：https://rust.godbolt.org/z/M836Ke61d

607194023.en: I'm not very bothered about enabling it for everything except repr(C) and slices/arrays, feels like an unsurprising carveout
607194023.zh: 我并不太在意是否对除了 repr(C) 和切片/数组之外的所有类型启用它；这算是一个不出人意料的例外。

607198225.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607112709):
```quote
imo that's more of LLVM being designed for C where they use TBAA instead of subobject provenance.
```

C has both TBAA and subobject provenance. but no compiler I know of makes much use of the subobject provenance part. presumably because it's not very useful.
Rust has an aliasing model that gives us a lot more information than TBAA. If subobject provenance is not useful in C, why would it be useful in Rust?
607198225.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607112709)：
```quote
我觉得这更多是因为 LLVM 的设计是面向 C 的，而 C 使用 TBAA，而不是 subobject provenance。
```

C 同时拥有 TBAA 和 subobject provenance。不过，据我所知，没有哪个编译器真正大量利用 subobject provenance 这一部分，大概是因为它并不太有用。

Rust 的别名模型能提供比 TBAA 多得多的信息。如果 subobject provenance 在 C 中没有什么用，那为什么在 Rust 中会有用呢？

607198348.en:
@_**The 8472|330154** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607115859):

607202157.en: I don't think LLVM's SRoA currently does this, but it's possible to promote some fields of an aggregate to SSA values while still keeping the original local, if subobject provenance proves that the escaping pointers can only access a subset of fields. For example, for a local `pair: (u32, f32)` where only `&pair.0` escapes, all mentions of `pair.1` could be redirected to a separate local `pair_1: f32`. This effectively takes subobject provenance reasoning and recasts it into separate objects to help LLVM's object-based provenance reasoning.
607202157.zh:
我不认为 LLVM 当前的 SRoA 会这样做，不过，如果 subobject provenance 能证明那些逃逸的指针只能访问字段的一个子集，那么就有可能在保留原始局部变量的同时，将聚合类型中的某些字段提升为 SSA 值。

例如，对于一个局部变量 `pair: (u32, f32)`，如果只有 `&pair.0` 会逃逸，那么所有涉及 `pair.1` 的地方都可以重定向到一个单独的局部变量 `pair_1: f32`。这样实际上就把 subobject provenance 的推理重新表述成了独立对象，从而帮助 LLVM 进行基于对象的 provenance 推理。

In the Rust version LLVM can't prove that accesses through `elements` don't also access `start`, which means that on every loop iteration it must write `start` back to memory so that the access via `elements` sees the correct value. The C++ version with TBAA doesn't have this problem because the individual elements of `elements` and `start` have different types. If you change the C++ code to have an array of `size_t` instead of `double` then it also loses the optimization and has to write back `start` on every loop iteration.

607255273.en:
We could say that if a local of an SRoA-eligible struct type does not have its address taken at any point, then its individual fields are treated as separate locals and can have offsets that differ from what the struct layout would prescribe. ("Does not have its address taken at any point" would be defined syntactically; e.g. an `&local` anywhere in the source, even in dead code, amounts to "taking the address".)

There are plenty of reasons why this particular approach might not be a good idea—making `&local` have spooky-action-at-a-distance among them—but hopefully it demonstrates that this is *possible* to support, and maybe there's a cleaner way.
607255273.zh:
我们可以规定：如果某个符合 SRoA 条件的结构体类型局部变量在任何时候都没有获取其地址，那么它的各个字段就被视为独立的局部变量，并且其偏移量可以不同于结构体布局所规定的偏移量。（“在任何时候都没有获取其地址”将通过语法来定义；例如，源代码中的任何位置出现 `&local`，即使位于死代码中，也算作“获取地址”。）

这种具体做法有很多理由可能并不是好主意——让 `&local` 产生令人难以预料的远距离影响就是其中之一——但希望这能说明，支持这一点是*可能的*，也许还存在更简洁的方式。

Not exactly: in that example, the address of individual fields is taken, but not the whole struct. We need subobject provenence to allow fields whose address is not taken to be extracted into separate locals *and not have to write back any modifications into the original struct*.
607428119.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607416415)：````quote @_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607255273)：```quote 如果某个符合 SRoA 条件的结构体类型的局部变量在任何时候都没有被获取地址，```那么这种情况下 SRoA 就是很简单的，也不需要子对象来源信息。```` 不完全是：在那个例子中，单个字段的地址被获取了，但整个结构体的地址没有被获取。我们需要子对象来源信息，以便将那些地址未被获取的字段提取到单独的局部变量中，*而且不必将任何修改写回原始结构体*。

607454829.en:
@_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607428119):

```quote
, the address of individual fields is taken,
```

oh -- "local does nit have its address taken" to me implied that none of its fields has the address taken either
607454829.zh: @_**Amanieu d'Antras|143274** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607428119)：```quote “单个字段的地址被获取，”```哦——“局部变量没有被获取地址”在我看来意味着它的任何字段也都没有被获取地址。

607455108.en: but again, because there are various ways to observe whether one truly is in an allocation, I dont think any of that works. and the answer IMO is to do better analyses -- if the address is passed to a function that, in some sense, "does not care" about the address, and dosnt access things outside the field, then we can still do $whatever

607522513.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607415902):
``````quote
it always did. C only allows pointer arithmetic within an array. arithmetic between fields is UB.
``````
Yes, but for things like sroa across unknown functions you need to allow for char* (and uintptr_t) casts. And as that linked q&a mentions it is at most unclear if there is any subobject stuff going on in any of the old C specs. The original actual-provenance proposals that are intended to clarify things didn't have any subobject provenance.

And that q&a is really inconsistent about the situation in c2x proposals in general - it says "c2x proposal: yes", but then in the text says that while they could, their current proposal doesn't. And then their actual proposal doesn't seem like it would allow any of the optimizations anyway because "Then on any cast, we'd expand the subrange to that of the original allocation", so any escaped subobject pointer has to be considered an escaped allocation pointer.
607522513.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607415902)：``````quote 它一直都是这样。C 只允许在数组内部进行指针算术运算。字段之间的算术运算是未定义行为。`````` 是的，但对于跨越未知函数进行 sroa 之类的情况，你需要允许 char*（以及 uintptr_t）转换。而且，正如那个链接中的问答所提到的，旧版 C 规范中是否存在任何子对象相关的内容，最多只能说是不明确。那些旨在澄清这一点的、最初提出的真实来源信息方案中，并没有任何子对象来源信息。 另外，那个问答对于 c2x 提案整体上的情况也说得非常不一致——它写着“c2x 提案：是”，但正文又说，虽然他们可以这么做，但当前的提案并没有这样做。而且，他们实际提出的方案似乎无论如何都不允许这些优化，因为“然后在每次转换时，我们都会将子范围扩展为原始分配的范围”，这样一来，任何逃逸的子对象指针都必须被视为逃逸的分配指针。

```quote
you need to allow for char* (and uintptr_t) casts.
```

```quote
based on the discussion above and at the recent t-opsem meeting, it seems like at least 3 out of 5 opsem members would be fine with saying "there is no subobject provenance on types that currently exist in the language, except maybe for enums". The main arguments are
- a bunch of existing code assumes this already for arrays and slices
- a lot of code generated by bindgen assumes this at least for repr(C) structs
- `#[repr]` shouldn't affect the opsem in such subtle ways
- the benefits of this UB are unclear. there are optimizations one can sketch where this is useful, but the fact that LLVM has no way of even representing this makes it look like there's no that much to be had here in terms of practically useful optimizations.

@**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** you weren't at that meeting -- I wonder what your thoughts on this are?
```

Well considering that my enum proposal depends on subobject provenance, you should expect I'm in favor of having it in at least those cases (with or without niche optimization, i.e. subobject provenance for `Option<u8>` too). I have already written extensively on the benefits to UB I perceive for this
607568542.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607108666)：```quote 基于上面的讨论以及最近一次 t-opsem 会议上的讨论，看起来至少有 5 位 opsem 成员中的 3 位愿意接受这样的说法：“对于目前语言中已有的类型，不存在子对象来源信息，枚举类型或许除外。”主要理由如下：- 现有的一些代码已经假定数组和切片是这样的 - bindgen 生成的大量代码至少对 repr(C) 结构体作了这样的假定 - `#[repr]` 不应以如此微妙的方式影响 opsem - 这种未定义行为的好处并不明确。我们可以设想出一些在这种情况下有用的优化，但 LLVM 甚至没有办法表示这一点，这似乎说明从实际有用的优化角度来看，这里并没有太多可得之处。 @**Crystal Durham** @**Mario Carneiro** 你们当时没参加那次会议——我想知道你们对此有什么看法？``` 考虑到我的枚举提案依赖于子对象来源信息，你们应该能预料到，我赞成至少在这些情况下保留它（无论是否进行 niche 优化，也就是说，`Option<u8>` 也应具有子对象来源信息）。我已经详细阐述过，我认为这种未定义行为有哪些好处。

607568625.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607568542):

how? having it just specifically for discriminants should still be possible, no?

607568706.en: I don't know what that means
607568706.zh: 我不知道你这是什么意思。

607568751.en: I don't want you to be able to take a reference to the u8 and then write outside the bounds to clobber the discriminant
607568751.zh: 我不希望你能够获取那个 u8 的引用，然后越界写入，把判别值破坏掉。

607568864.zh: 是的。那这怎么依赖于数组和结构体字段投影限制引用，使其只能访问对应的字段或元素呢？

607569091.en: and in a 2-field enum, how do you rely on pointers to one field not being allowed to access the other field?
607569091.zh: 而对于一个有两个字段的枚举，你又是如何依赖于“不允许指向其中一个字段的指针访问另一个字段”这一点的呢？

607569170.en: it's unclear to me whether you've been talking about projection operators or types
607569170.zh: 在我看来，目前还不清楚你说的是投影运算符，还是类型。

607569237.en: the last messages sounds like projections but the discussion about repr(C) etc is about types
607569237.zh: 你最后几条消息听起来像是在说投影，但关于 repr(C) 等内容的讨论说的是类型。

607569267.en: subobject provenance is something that "happens" during projections -- the newly created reference gets a provenance that is restricted to just the bytes inside the field
607569267.zh: 子对象来源信息是在投影过程中“产生”的——新创建的引用会获得一个来源信息，而这个来源信息被限制为仅涵盖字段内部的字节。

607569381.en: I agree that this "should" be about projections
607569381.zh: 我同意，这件事“应该”是关于投影的。

607569393.en: since each projection has a base type we can talk about all projections to fields of repr(C) types etc
607569393.zh: 由于每次投影都有一个基础类型，我们可以讨论对 repr(C) 类型字段的所有投影，等等。

607569466.en: which is tedious to spell out and it seemed sufficiently obvious that that's what we mean when we talk about "subobject provenance for repr(C) types"
607569466.zh: 只是把这些都明确说出来很麻烦；而且当我们谈论“repr(C) 类型的子对象来源信息”时，这样的含义已经足够明显了。

607569625.en: I understand that's what you mean, but the framing suggested that we should be looking at classification of types into good and bad rather than projections
607569625.zh: 我明白你的意思，但这种表述让人觉得我们应该关注的是把类型分类为好和坏，而不是关注投影。

607569752.en: but, taking a step back -- your enum proposal adds a bunch of extra state and checks specifically for enum discriminants. that seems enough to achieve your goals even if we dont *also* set up the Tree Borrows state machine in a way taht it restricts access to certain bytes?
607569752.zh: 不过退一步说——你的枚举提案专门为枚举判别式增加了一堆额外状态和检查。即使我们不以限制对某些字节的访问的方式来设置 Tree Borrows 状态机，这似乎也已经足以实现你的目标了，不是吗？

607569907.en: so I dont understand how your poposal relies on subobject provenance -- where by "subobject provenance" I specifically mean "when creating a reference, mark only some bytes as being permitted to be read/written via this reference, and make it insta-UB to read/write any other bytes"
607569907.zh: 所以我不明白你的提案是如何依赖子对象 provenance 的——这里我所说的“子对象 provenance”特指：创建引用时，只标记某些字节允许通过该引用进行读写，并且一旦读写其他任何字节就立即产生 UB。

607569951.en: No, that *only* works on niche optimized enums. If you do it without subobject provenance, non-optimized enums are subject to the same problem
607569951.zh: 不，那只对经过 niche 优化的枚举有效。如果不采用子对象 provenance，未优化的枚举也会遇到同样的问题。

607569984.zh: 而且解决方案也是一样的，对吧？

607570018.en: to make the enum thing work we need a solution for this that works without subobject provenance
607570018.zh: 要让枚举这件事可行，我们需要一个不依赖子对象 provenance 的解决方案。

607570032.en: we might as well use that solution for all enums then?
607570032.zh: 那我们干脆把这个解决方案用于所有枚举，不就行了？

607623522.zh:
我猜你指的是“移植到 C 的 Foo 示例”。
我不知道（3）的情况，但（1）和（2）是“是”——这也算是支持（3）为“是”的一些证据。

607623724.en: and furthermore I *know* that the amount of UB this introduces in real-world code is very large (it's the most common SB violation AFAIK), so the performance benefits would have to be pretty big and impossible to recover in other ways (smarter compiler / slightly adjusting the code)
607623724.zh: 而且我*知道*，这种做法在现实世界代码中引入的未定义行为非常多（据我所知，这是最常见的 SB 违规行为），所以它带来的性能收益必须足够大，而且无法通过其他方式（更智能的编译器／稍微调整代码）获得，才值得这么做。

607624326.en: I just don't agree with that assertion. Almost all the time you aren't doing shenaniganry with &Header et al
607624326.zh: 我就是不同意这个断言。几乎所有时候，你都不会对 &Header 之类的东西做这些花招。

607624401.en: which assertion? we have data to show that this kind of UB is common.
607624401.zh: 哪个断言？我们有数据表明，这种未定义行为很常见。

607624526.en: The safety invariant already expects that you don't do this, so I don't understand why you would expect that programmers would use it commonly
607624526.zh: 安全不变量本来就要求你不要这么做，所以我不明白你为什么会认为程序员会经常这么做。

607624551.en: TB has way less real-world UB than SB, and a good chunk of that is the lack of subobject provenance
607624551.zh: TB 中现实世界的未定义行为远少于 SB，而其中相当一部分原因就是缺少子对象来源信息。

607624710.en: I think we lack alternative mechanisms which make it easier to avoid the bad case
607624710.zh: 我觉得我们缺少能让人更容易避开这种糟糕情况的替代机制。

607624779.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624526):
```quote
The safety invariant already expects that you don't do this, so I don't understand why you would expect that programmers would use it commonly
```

I dont expect it, I know it. it's all over the place in @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** 's and our crater-at-home miri runs.
607624779.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624526)：
```quote
安全不变量本来就要求你不要这么做，所以我不明白你为什么会认为程序员会经常这么做。
```

我没这么认为，我是知道事实如此。在 @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** 的运行结果以及我们自己的 crater-at-home miri 运行结果中，这种情况到处都是。

607624808.en: to me this isn't an argument for setting our bad design in stone
607624808.zh: 在我看来，这并不能成为把我们的糟糕设计永久固定下来的理由。

607624873.en: if "this breaks tons of existing real-world code" isnt an argument then I dont know what is :shrug:
607624873.zh: 如果“这会破坏大量现有的现实世界代码”都不能算理由，那我就不知道还有什么能算理由了 :shrug:

607624935.en: again, I'm thinking about eventual future rust
607624935.zh: 再说一次，我考虑的是 Rust 更遥远的未来。

607624974.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624710) in #**t-opsem>Vibes on subobject provenance**:
```quote
I think we lack alternative mechanisms which make it easier to avoid the bad case
```
given 10 years of precedent I dont think the theoretical existence of such mechanisms is relevant
607624974.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** 在 #**t-opsem>Vibes on subobject provenance** 中[说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607624710)： “我觉得我们缺少一些替代机制，让人更容易避开糟糕的情况。” 鉴于过去 10 年的先例，我不认为这类机制在理论上的存在具有什么相关性

607624984.en: I understand there are problems at present
607624984.zh: 我明白目前确实存在一些问题

607625141.en: Im not going to sacrifice our current users on the altar of a hypothetical ideal future Rust
607625141.zh: 我不会为了一个假想中的理想 Rust 未来，而牺牲我们当前的用户

607625177.en: this is a "better things aren't possible" argument
607625177.zh: 这是一种“做不到更好”的论证

607625187.en: we're talking about an opsem for *current* Rust
607625187.zh: 我们讨论的是针对*当前* Rust 的操作语义

607625304.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625177):
```quote
this is a "better things aren't possible" argument
```

no, it's a "the real world of existing code matters" argument
607625304.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625177)： “这是一种‘做不到更好’的论证。” 不，这是在说“现实世界中已有的代码很重要”

607625390.en: I am okay with taking an opsem for current rust which lacks subobject provenance if we couple this with some amount of thinking on how we can get away from it in the next edition or w/e
607625390.zh: 如果我们同时花些精力思考如何在下一个版本或之类的时机摆脱它，那么我可以接受采用一种缺少子对象来源的当前 Rust 操作语义

607625569.en: I just worry that this will become part of the stable surface and it will become even more impossible to change in the future
607625569.zh: 我只是担心它会成为稳定接口的一部分，以后就更加不可能改变了

607626882.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625390):
```quote
I am okay with taking an opsem for current rust which lacks subobject provenance
```
that is good to hear

> if we couple this with some amount of thinking on how we can get away from it in the next edition or w/e

various avenues for evolving this exist, though of course as you know evolving things around unsafe is particularly tricky. it pretty much has to be opt-in, or all "old" types would have to get the opt-out attribute during the transition which would be a gigantic amount of churn.
do you see any alternative option for the current opsem that would make future evolution easier without risking breaking tons of existing code? the only option I can imagine is to make it dependent on the `repr` of the struct that contains the projected field, but there are pretty good argument against that.
607626882.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607625390)： “我可以接受采用一种缺少子对象来源的当前 Rust 操作语义。” 听到你这么说真不错。> 如果我们同时花些精力思考如何在下一个版本或之类的时机摆脱它，演进它的路径有很多，不过当然，正如你所知，围绕 `unsafe` 进行演进尤其棘手。它基本上必须是选择加入的；否则，在过渡期间，所有“旧”类型都得加上选择退出的属性，那将造成巨量的改动。对于当前的操作语义，你能想到什么替代方案，既能让未来的演进更容易，又不会冒着破坏大量现有代码的风险吗？我能想到的唯一方案，是让它取决于包含被投影字段的结构体的 `repr`，但反对这样做的理由也相当充分。

607627129.en: are there any patterns which exist in the wild which weren't already dubious at best?
607627129.zh: 现实世界中有没有什么模式，至少不是从一开始就很可疑的？

607627185.en: whether they are dubious heavily depends on your PoV
607627185.zh: 它们是否可疑，很大程度上取决于你的视角

607627388.en: at the very least something that would be written after knowing that subobject provenance is a thing and failing to find a better option
607627388.zh: 至少得是那种在知道子对象来源确实存在之后，找不到更好方案才会写出来的代码

607627422.en: we never gave any indication to programmers that references should be considered to be "contained to their fields" even when turned into raw pointers
607627422.zh: 我们从未向程序员暗示过：即使引用被转换成原始指针，也应该认为它们是“局限于各自字段之内的”

607627470.en: rather than just "I thought this was C with better syntax"
607627470.zh: 而不只是“我以为这就是语法更好的 C”

607627622.en: you can't leap allocations using raw pointer offsets though
607627622.zh: 不过，使用原始指针偏移也无法跨越分配

607627740.en: it doesn't seem to be that different to me unless you are designing a formal checker
607627740.zh: 在我看来，这似乎并没有什么不同，除非你是在设计形式化检查器

607627883.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607626882):
```quote
various avenues for evolving this exist,
```

FWIW I quite like the idea of providing people extra tools they can use in hot loops to help the optimizer, rather than inflicting extra UB on everyone everywhere, so a dedicated `fn restrict_provenance<T>(x: &mut T) -> &mut T` (not even unsafe!) sounds like a pretty nice option to me
607627883.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607626882)： “演进它的路径有很多，” 顺便说一句，我相当喜欢这样一种思路：提供一些额外工具，让人们可以在热点循环中使用它们来帮助优化器，而不是把额外的 UB 强加给所有人、所有地方。所以，提供一个专用的 `fn restrict_provenance<T>(x: &mut T) -> &mut T`（甚至不需要是 unsafe）对我来说听起来是个相当不错的选择

607628073.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607627740):
```quote
it doesn't seem to be that different to me unless you are designing a formal checker
```

it's very different (at least when considering arrays and repr(C) types) since you cant predict the distance between allocations
607628073.zh: @_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说道](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607627740)： “在我看来，这似乎并没有什么不同，除非你是在设计形式化检查器。” 差别非常大（至少在考虑数组和 repr(C) 类型时），因为你无法预测各个分配之间的距离

607628102.en: maybe this is the difference, I don't see it as inflicting extra UB on everyone everywhere, I see it as inflicting a weird model of validity on everyone everywhere
607628102.zh: 也许这就是区别所在：我不认为这是把额外的 UB 强加给所有人、所有地方；我认为这是把一种奇怪的有效性模型强加给所有人、所有地方

607628310.en: if anything the model with subobject provenance is "weird", it needs some extra state and complexities to generate the extra UB
607628310.zh: 如果说有什么的话，带有子对象溯源的模型才是“怪异”的；它需要额外的状态和复杂性，才能产生额外的 UB

607628450.en: certainly a flat model would be easier
607628450.zh: 当然，扁平模型会更简单

607628507.en: but we've already committed to that extra state anyway
607628507.zh: 但反正我们已经决定采用那种额外状态了

607628642.en: no? TB as-is has no subobject provenance
607628642.zh: 不是吧？按现状来看，TB 没有子对象溯源

607628715.en: TB is much harder than a flat memory model with bytes at positions
607628715.zh: TB 比那种在各个位置存放字节的扁平内存模型要难得多

607628764.en:
true. I never said it wasnt so... not sure why you're bringing this up.
but even compared to that we need to make it even weirded to get subobject provenance.
(that's obviously the baseline I was comparing with above.)
607628764.zh: 没错。我从没说过不是这样……不太明白你为什么要提这个。即便与那种模型相比，我们还得把它弄得更怪，才能实现子对象溯源。（显然，我上面比较的基准就是那个。）

607628899.en: I think this perspective is something that only a TB maintainer would have
607628899.zh: 我觉得，这种视角恐怕只有 TB 维护者才会有

607629059.en: I would rather explain TB in terms of the properties it ensures rather than by its mechanistic behavior
607629059.zh: 我更愿意从 TB 所保证的性质来解释它，而不是从它的机制行为来解释

607629126.en: like "if you take a reference you get access to those bytes"
607629126.zh: 比如说，“如果你拿到了一个引用，你就能访问那些字节”

607629154.en:
eh, happy to consider an alternative aliasing model as baseline.
but currently it just sounds like you trying to invalidate my arguments based on them being made by me :shrug:
607629154.zh: 呃，我很乐意考虑把另一种别名模型作为基准。不过目前听起来，你只是因为这些论点是我提出来的，就想让它们失效 :shrug:

607629305.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629059):
```quote
I would rather explain TB in terms of the properties it ensures rather than by its mechanistic behavior
```

that sounds like you're thinking about a type system and safety invariants. we're not in that world here though.
607629305.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629059)：
```quote
我更愿意从 TB 所保证的性质来解释它，而不是从它的机制行为来解释
```

听起来你是在用类型系统和安全不变量的思路考虑问题。但我们现在讨论的并不是那个语境。

607629401.en: I mean that TB vs TB+epsilon is not distinguishable to the outsider
607629401.zh: 我的意思是，对于局外人来说，TB 和 TB+epsilon 是无法区分的

607629464.en: it is if their code gets miscompiled / flagged by miri ;)
607629464.zh: 如果他们的代码被错误编译，或者被 miri 标记出来，那当然能区分 ;)

607629471.en: it's already got more moving parts than the average person can keep in their head
607629471.zh: 它包含的组成部分已经比一般人能记住的还多了

607629614.en: I don't think that optimizing that model is necessarily a primary goal, because explaining the model to a layman is not its primary purpose
607629614.zh: 我不认为优化这个模型一定是首要目标，因为向外行解释这个模型本来就不是它的首要用途

607629620.en: and subobject provenance is not an "epsilon" change to how much code gets flagged by miri, it's a pretty significant change
607629620.zh: 而且，子对象溯源并不是对有多少代码会被 miri 标记这种情况做出的“epsilon”级别的改动，而是相当重大的变化

607629787.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629614):
```quote
I don't think that optimizing that model is necessarily a primary goal, because explaining the model to a layman is not its primary purpose
```

very strong hard disagree on that. enough people will want to / have to dig to the bottom of our "tower of weakenings" that it's definitely important to keep this in mind.
607629787.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607629614)：
```quote
我不认为优化这个模型一定是首要目标，因为向外行解释这个模型本来就不是它的首要用途
```

对此我强烈不同意。会想要或不得不深入探究我们“层层弱化的塔”的人足够多，所以牢记这一点绝对很重要。

607629907.en: it is rather intended to balance good properties for optimization with an easy mental model
607629907.zh: 它的目标本来就是在有利于优化的良好性质和易于理解的心智模型之间取得平衡

607629957.en: (also, here the simpler low-level model aligns with less UB on the high-level which means it's also easier to use even without knowing the details)
607629957.zh: （而且，在这里，更简单的底层模型意味着高层的 UB 更少，这也意味着即使不了解细节，它也更容易使用）

607630022.en: so I would rank ease of description at 2 or 3, it's important but not most important
607630022.zh: 所以我会把易于描述排在第二或第三位；这很重要，但不是最重要的

607630128.en: having a useful tower of weakenings is IMO even more important
607630128.zh: 在我看来，拥有一套实用的弱化层级甚至更加重要

607630286.en: every weaker tower floor that's valid on TB + subobject provenance is also valid on TB - subobject provenance, so "having a useful tower" cannot possibly ever be an argument for subobject provenance
607630286.zh: 任何在 TB + subobject provenance 上有效的更弱层级，在 TB - subobject provenance 上也同样有效，因此“拥有一套实用的层级”不可能成为支持 subobject provenance 的论据

607630510.en: I'm not sure I agree with that, at a higher level of the tower of weakenings how do you explain that the code I gave can fail?
607630510.zh: 我不确定是否同意这一点。在弱化层级中处于更高层级时，你要如何解释我给出的代码为什么会失败？

607630620.zh: 这是一个相当显然的定理

607630679.en: because a weaker tower level can only ever say "dont do X", it can never say "X is definitely UB"
607630679.zh: 因为更弱的层级只能说“不要做 X”，永远不能说“X 肯定是 UB”

607630733.en: if my rule is "pointers can't access out of your region" then that code should not be able to fail
607630733.zh: 如果我的规则是“指针不能访问你所在区域之外的内容”，那么那段代码就不应该能够失败

607630910.en: also that sounds like a safety invariant thing
607630910.zh: 而且这听起来像是安全性不变量的问题

607630927.en: it's an incomplete explanation of what is happening
607630927.zh: 这是对实际发生情况的不完整解释

607631029.en: so yes it is a weakening IMO, although I understand that I'm basically exploiting a contravariance issue here
607631029.zh: 所以，是的，我认为这确实是弱化，尽管我明白自己基本上是在利用这里的一个逆变问题

607631148.en: but I think programmers do both kinds of reasoning (what can I do, what can I trust others will not do)
607631148.zh: 但我认为程序员会进行这两种推理（我能做什么，以及我可以相信别人不会做什么）

607631208.en: we dont use the opsem to restrict what others will do
607631208.zh: 我们不会用操作语义来限制别人会做什么

607631250.en: that's not even valid reasoning since we always can remove UB from the opsem
607631250.zh: 这种推理甚至不成立，因为我们始终可以从操作语义中移除 UB

607631317.en: only the type system can restrict what others will do, so it's not really part of this discussion
607631317.zh: 只有类型系统才能限制别人会做什么，所以这其实不属于本次讨论的内容

607631406.en: I don't see how types help here
607631406.zh: 我看不出类型在这里能提供什么帮助

607631453.en: the code I wrote is 100% safe
607631453.zh: 我写的代码是 100% 安全的

607631486.en: ~~maybe they dont, but the opsem surely doesnt^^~~
607631486.zh: ~~也许类型系统不会，但操作语义肯定不会这样做^^~~

607631708.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607631453):
```quote
the code I wrote is 100% safe
```

yes and for soundness if it calls an arbitrary opaque function the code can entirely rely on that function not mutating outside the reference
607631708.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607631453)：
```quote
我写的代码是 100% 安全的
```

是的；而为了保证健全性，如果它调用了任意的不透明函数，那么代码完全可以依赖于该函数不会修改引用所指范围之外的内容

607631725.en: the type system already ensures that
607631725.zh: 类型系统已经保证了这一点

607631761.en: the function only receives ownership of the field in question
607631761.zh: 该函数只获得了相关字段的所有权

607631837.en: but all that is safety invariant / type system reasoning
607631837.zh: 但这些都属于安全性不变量／类型系统推理

607631910.en: so please explain to me why we go from "this is unsound" to "everyone does this" when discussing subobj prov
607631910.zh: 所以，在讨论 subobj prov 时，请你解释一下，为什么我们会从“这是不健全的”转而说“大家都这么做”

607632005.en: I hope everyone doesn't break the rules, otherwise rust wouldn't be a very useful language
607632005.zh: 我希望不是所有人都会违反规则，否则 Rust 就不会是一门很有用的语言了

607632042.en: people dont do this *across APIs calling arbitrary unknown functions*
607632042.zh: 人们不会在跨 API 调用任意未知函数时这么做

607632112.en: but that's the case I'm talking about?

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607567862):
````quote
I dont see any thing in the standard permitting those to be used to do ptr arithmetic outside of arrays
````

[6.3.2.3 Pointers, item 7](https://www.iso-9899.info/n3047.html#6.3.2.3)
```quote
When a pointer to an object is converted to a pointer to a character type, the result points to the lowest addressed byte of the object. Successive increments of the result, up to the size of the object, yield pointers to the remaining bytes of the object.
```
Which yes, relies on &x.foo not being a restricted to a subobject (otherwise you could argue that it doesn't even let you access the next array element). While I agree with that q&a that this is unclear rather than clearly unrestricted, certainly the default assumption by programmers has been that it is unrestricted.

uintptr_t would rely on Footnote 73, which is just a footnote - "The mapping functions for converting a pointer to an integer or an integer to a pointer are intended to be consistent with the addressing structure of the execution environment." Otherwise pointer/int casting is at least allowed to be encrypt/decrypt, which would break using it for pointer math (since uintptr_t is only required to work for the same value pointer->int->pointer).
607670945.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607567862)：
````quote
我没看到标准中有任何内容允许使用这些指针在数组之外进行指针算术
````

[6.3.2.3 Pointers, item 7](https://www.iso-9899.info/n3047.html#6.3.2.3)
```quote
当指向某个对象的指针被转换为指向字符类型的指针时，结果指向该对象地址最低的字节。对结果依次递增，直到达到该对象的大小，就会得到指向其余字节的指针。
```
这确实依赖于 `&x.foo` 不被限制为只能指向一个子对象（否则你可以认为它甚至不允许访问数组中的下一个元素）。虽然我同意那个问答所说的：这与其说是明确不受限制，不如说是不明确；但程序员长期以来的默认假设确实是它不受限制。

`uintptr_t` 则依赖于脚注 73，而脚注终究只是脚注——“用于将指针转换为整数，或将整数转换为指针的映射函数，其意图是与执行环境的寻址结构保持一致。”否则，指针／整数转换至少可以被实现为加密／解密，这会破坏将其用于指针算术的做法（因为 `uintptr_t` 只被要求保证同一个值经过指针→整数→指针转换后仍能正常工作）。

we allow *tons* of things the safety invariant strictly forbids. we have a "memory contains untyped bytes" model even though our safety invariants would naturally give rise to "memory contains typed objects" -- but we recognize that people need to work with those bytes so we get out of their way to the extent that we can. your arguments based on naturality of subobject provenance only make sense to me if we assume a framework of typed memory. in a world where untyped memory has been accepted as the natural state of affairs, I cannot see at all how subobject provenance leads to a *less* weird model of validity.

I guess that the answer changes in the `fn bar` case by "forking" the original `x: &mut _` reference into multiple references `&mut x[0]` and `&mut x[1]` - in a world without subobject provenance both of these would have write access to the entirety of the array `x` but that "other forked reference" limits what they can actually do without triggering UB. Compared to just holding the original `&mut x` and a derived `&mut x[1]`, we of course do not consider these two references aliasing since the original one is "turned off" while the derived one lives.

I personally cannot really say I like this from a surface language point of view, ... but at least we (hopefully) don't lose optimisations like in the last `fn inner` if we can argue that forking references does effectively produce a restricted form of subobject provenance.
607756036.zh:
我猜，在 `fn bar` 这个例子中，答案会因为把原始的 `x: &mut _` “分叉”为多个引用 `&mut x[0]` 和 `&mut x[1]` 而发生变化——在没有子对象 provenance 的世界里，这两个引用都会对整个数组 `x` 拥有写权限，但那个“另一个分叉出来的引用”会限制它们实际上能做什么，否则就会触发 UB。相比之下，如果只是持有原始的 `&mut x` 和一个派生出的 `&mut x[1]`，我们当然不会认为这两个引用存在别名关系，因为在派生引用存活期间，原始引用处于“关闭”状态。

就表层语言而言，我个人确实不能说喜欢这种设计……但至少，如果我们能够论证引用分叉实际上产生了一种受限形式的子对象 provenance，那么我们（希望如此）就不会像最后那个 `fn inner` 示例那样损失优化机会。

607843047.en:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607833205):
```quote
I don't think this is a hard model to teach
```

And that's essentially CHERI's model: flat memory where capabilities are mostly an address and a window where that address is usable. The question is what's the window of a new pointer?

Today it's the allocation for pointers returned by the global allocator, and that same allocation for derived pointers. The rationale being what Ralf said: offsets between allocation is dynamic, offsets within allocations is (usually) static. Of course if you implement an allocator within an allocation (like a custom allocator), then that rationale doesn't work anymore because offsets between custom allocations are dynamic but still share the same window inherited from the global allocation they are drawn from.

The second question is whether we can change that, to which there's at least 2 options:
1. Explicit: the user may shrink the window when creating a new pointer (by default it inherits the window), which could be in the form of `restrict_provenance`.
2. Implicit: pointers (or maybe just references, TBD) get a window based on their type (possibly depending on attributes on the outer/inner types).

The problem of "implicit windowing" is legacy code (if the attributes are not opt-in). The problem of "explicit windowing" is optimizations (which are not "enabled by default"). Which is why it seems to all boil down to how much legacy would break and how much optimization would we get (to which I have no ideas, but according to the thread and AFAICT: non-negligible legacy would break and no clear optimizations except for enums)
607843047.zh:
@_**Mario Carneiro|271719** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607833205)：
```quote
我不认为这是一个难以讲清楚的模型
```

这本质上就是 CHERI 的模型：内存是平坦的，而 capability 主要就是一个地址，以及该地址可以使用的一个范围。问题在于，新指针的这个范围应该是什么？

对于全局分配器返回的指针来说，目前它是整个分配；对于派生出的指针来说，则沿用同一个分配。理由正如 Ralf 所说：分配之间的偏移量是动态的，而分配内部的偏移量通常是静态的。当然，如果你在一次分配内部实现了一个分配器（比如自定义分配器），这个理由就不再成立了，因为自定义分配之间的偏移量是动态的，但它们仍然共享从中分配出来的那个全局分配所继承的同一个范围。

第二个问题是，我们能否改变这一点；至少有两种方案：
1. 显式方式：用户在创建新指针时可以缩小这个范围（默认情况下继承原范围），这可以通过 `restrict_provenance` 来实现。
2. 隐式方式：指针（或者也许只有引用，待定）根据其类型获得一个范围（可能还取决于外层类型或内层类型上的属性）。

“隐式设置范围”的问题在于遗留代码（如果这些属性不是选择启用的）。而“显式设置范围”的问题在于优化（因为它们不会“默认启用”）。所以问题似乎最终都归结为：会破坏多少遗留代码，以及能获得多少优化收益（对此我没有什么想法，但根据这个讨论串以及我的理解：会破坏数量不可忽略的遗留代码，而除了枚举之外，没有明确的优化收益）。

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607832376):

````quote
Maybe that's the best way to put it: flat memory is very intuitive to many people, but also clearly doesnt work. The closest approximation we can have is to be "flat within an allocation". Subobject provenance breaks with that.
````

But of course, that can't be the full model, because the *heap allocator itself* is free to rely on the offset between allocations it creates. There is a natural tree structure here—`malloc` gets access to big chunks of memory from e.g. `mmap`, cuts them into smaller pieces, and hands those to its callers—who are themselves free to slice and dice further
607850239.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607832376)：


但当然，这不可能是完整的模型，因为*堆分配器本身*就可以依赖它所创建的各个分配之间的偏移量。这里存在一种自然的树状结构——`malloc` 从例如 `mmap` 获取大块内存，把它们切分成更小的部分，再交给调用者；而调用者自己也可以继续切分这些内存。

Provenance has taught me that the flat memory model is wrong. The natural model I end up with is "a pointer to a byte range only gives you access to that byte range". The fact that we can sometimes launder a pointer with access to a large range as a pointer to a smaller range feels to me like an exception that needs justification, rather than the other way around.

Sounds like a rule that wouldn't break too much code is "when you take a reference to a place, you get a reference with provenance to not more than the extent of that place, unless (for compatibility) that place is an array/slice index or a `repr(C)` field access, in which case you get provenance not more than you'd get by borrowing the whole array/slice/`repr(C)` struct". Is that accurate?


provenance 让我认识到，平坦内存模型是错误的。我最终形成的自然模型是：“指向某个字节范围的指针，只能让你访问该字节范围。”有时我们可以把一个能够访问较大范围的指针转换成一个指向较小范围的指针；对我来说，这更像是一种需要给出理由的例外，而不是反过来。

听起来，下面这条规则应该不会破坏太多代码：“当你取得一个 place 的引用时，你得到的引用所带的 provenance 不会超过该 place 的范围；但出于兼容性考虑，如果该 place 是数组/切片索引，或者是 `repr(C)` 字段访问，那么你得到的 provenance 不会超过借用整个数组/切片/`repr(C)` 结构体时所能得到的范围。”这样理解准确吗？

但如果你从“原始的系统访问”出发，这就是一个令人意外的限制；所有那些会打破该模型的现存代码就是证明。再说一次，这大概是代码产生 UB 的前三大原因之一。（很难给出精确数字，需要有人进行更精确的数据收集。）

607888912.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607847277):
```quote
I agree. TB has to do extra work (delayed initialization) to *not* have subobject provenance, which I think demonstrates that subobject provenance is the simpler model
```

that's not really true. delayed initialization is not extra work. the only extra work we do is *eager initialization* of the `T` part that an `&[mut] T` points to. the "natural" / simplest possible form of TB (in an ideal language without `UnsafeCell` and without protectors) would have only lazy initialization and nothing else.
607888912.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607847277)：
```quote
我同意。TB 为了不采用子对象 provenance，反而必须做额外的工作（延迟初始化）；我认为这恰恰说明子对象 provenance 才是更简单的模型
```

这其实不对。延迟初始化并不是额外的工作。我们唯一做的额外工作，是对 `&[mut] T` 所指向的 `T` 部分进行*急切初始化*。“自然的”或最简单的 TB 形式（在一种没有 `UnsafeCell`、也没有保护器的理想语言中）只会有延迟初始化，除此之外什么也没有。

