there's no laundering going on, so if your mental model needs laundering to explain "TB without subobject provenance" then it is unnecessarily complicated. no subobject provenance is the natural state of a TB-like model.  (having subobject provenance was natural for SB.)

607941879.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607907508):
```quote
if we expect people to be able to opt-out of subobject provenance and have `&Header` work when passed through safe code, `restrict_provenance` needs to be `unsafe` or do nothing on `&Header`, since otherwise `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` is UB
```

There could be a world in which you have both of:
* a `restrict_provenance` that becomes a no-op when used on `&T where T: NoSubobjectProvenance`, and
* a different such function that *fails to compile* in that case, because that’s a sign that you’ve done something broken with the ownership of a `T` like putting it in a `Box` that has none of the neighboring memory present

Though, hm, that’s another distinction in use cases, that one could want to make explicit, too. “This type may be used in a way which requires no-subobject-provenance” vs. “this type *is always* used in a way which requires no-subobject-provenance". The latter would mean that trying to construct `Box<Header>` is a logical error potentially leading to unsoundness, and the former would not.

Is any of this worth doing instead of using (newtyped) raw pointers? I don’t know. But I am both skeptical about the usability of "just use raw pointers", and wanting to not live in the world where accessing out of bounds of a reference's referent is OK, which means I wish that Rust did have an explicit opt-out (or opt-in!) per type.
607941879.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607907508)：
```quote
如果我们希望用户可以选择不采用子对象来源信息，并且让 `&Header` 在经过安全代码传递后仍然有效，那么 `restrict_provenance` 要么必须是 `unsafe` 的，要么对 `&Header` 不执行任何操作，否则 `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` 就会产生未定义行为
```

也可以存在这样一种设计，同时提供以下两者：
* 一个在用于 `&T where T: NoSubobjectProvenance` 时变成空操作的 `restrict_provenance`；
* 以及另一个在这种情况下无法编译的类似函数，因为这意味着你对某个 `T` 的所有权处理方式有问题，比如把它放进了一个周围没有任何相邻内存的 `Box` 中。

不过，嗯，这又涉及使用场景上的另一种区分，而且这种区分也可能值得明确表达出来：“这个类型可以用在不需要子对象来源信息的场景中”与“这个类型*总是*用在需要不采用子对象来源信息的场景中”。后者意味着尝试构造 `Box<Header>` 是一种逻辑错误，并可能导致不健全；前者则不会。

与使用（通过 newtype 封装的）原始指针相比，这些做法是否值得？我不知道。但我一方面对“直接使用原始指针”的可用性持怀疑态度，另一方面又不想生活在“访问引用所指对象范围之外的内存是可以的”这样的世界里，因此我希望 Rust 确实能按类型提供明确的选择退出（或者选择加入）机制。

608087615.en:

```quote
if we expect people to be able to opt-out of subobject provenance and have `&Header` work when passed through safe code, `restrict_provenance` needs to be `unsafe` or do nothing on `&Header`, since otherwise `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` is UB
```

at least on `&mut` I think it can be safe -- if you take in an `&mut Header` from outside code, you have no way of knowing that there is a tail after that header.
for `&Header` however I think I agree, I committed the cardinal sin of not thinking semantic enough -- one could define a type where we carefully control which shared references a user can obtain to ensure they always have a valid tail. it's very non-trivial to get such an API to be sound though.
608087615.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/607907508)：
```quote
如果我们希望用户可以选择不采用子对象来源信息，并且让 `&Header` 在经过安全代码传递后仍然有效，那么 `restrict_provenance` 要么必须是 `unsafe` 的，要么对 `&Header` 不执行任何操作，否则 `read_after_header(restrict_provenance(get_header()))` 就会产生未定义行为
```

至少对于 `&mut`，我认为它可以是安全的——如果你从外部代码接收一个 `&mut Header`，你没有办法知道这个 header 后面是否还有尾部数据。
不过对于 `&Header`，我认为你的看法是对的。我犯了没有从语义层面充分思考这个问题的大忌——可以定义一种类型，谨慎控制用户能够获得哪些共享引用，从而确保这些引用始终拥有有效的尾部数据。不过，要让这样的 API 保持健全，难度确实非常高。

608097644.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/608087615):
```quote
at least on `&mut` I think it can be safe -- if you take in an `&mut Header` from outside code, you have no way of knowing that there is a tail after that header.
```

Why would there be a difference between `&Header` and `&mut Header`? Either way, you have to encapsulate the type such that outside code can't create a place of type `Header`. And if outside code can create a `&mut Header` without there being a tail, then it can trivially also create `&Header` without tail.
608097644.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/608087615)：
```quote
至少对于 `&mut`，我认为它可以是安全的——如果你从外部代码接收一个 `&mut Header`，你没有办法知道这个 header 后面是否还有尾部数据。
```

为什么 `&Header` 和 `&mut Header` 会有区别？无论哪种情况，你都必须对这个类型进行封装，使外部代码无法创建一个类型为 `Header` 的位置。而且，如果外部代码可以在没有尾部数据的情况下创建一个 `&mut Header`，那么它当然也可以创建一个没有尾部数据的 `&Header`。

608099166.en: If you can get an `&mut Header` with a tail, you can `replace_with` and move the header wherever. So either it's safe to restrict the provenance, or it's unsafe to hand out the `&mut` at all
608099166.zh: 如果你能获得一个带有尾部数据的 `&mut Header`，就可以通过 `replace_with` 将 header 替换掉，并把它移动到任意位置。所以，要么限制来源信息是安全的，要么根本就不安全地提供 `&mut`。

608100296.en: Oh, I see. That's true when there's any non-trivial relation between header values and size/contents of the tail. I think there are some (rare) cases where swapping via `&mut` is safe because the safety invariants w.r.t. tail are the same for all values of the type. For example, if there's a trailing array but the length of that array is stored at a fixed offset before/after the `Header` type. (Don't ask me if there's a good reason for not having such data in the header type itself)
608100296.zh: 哦，我明白了。当 header 值与尾部数据的大小或内容之间存在任何非平凡关系时，确实如此。我认为有一些（少见的）情况，通过 `&mut` 进行交换是安全的，因为对于该类型的所有值而言，关于尾部数据的安全不变量都相同。比如，存在一个尾随数组，而该数组的长度存储在 `Header` 类型之前或之后的固定偏移处。（别问我为什么不直接把这种数据放进 header 类型本身。）

618233165.en: I propose we commit to *not* having subobject provenance for arrays/slices: https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/622.
618233165.zh: 我提议，我们明确承诺不为数组/切片采用子对象 provenance：https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/622。

619691904.en: fwiw I am rather in favor of keeping Rust strict here and abundantly teaching "don't do pointer arithmetic on (stuff derived from) references". Choosing to allow moving between array/slice elements feels more like "trying not to break code written by ppl used to C" than "useful capability that allows code we couldn't otherwise".
619691904.zh: 仅供参考，我比较倾向于让 Rust 在这里保持严格，并且反复强调“不要对（从引用派生出的）东西做指针算术”。选择允许在数组/切片元素之间移动，感觉更像是“尽量不破坏那些习惯了 C 的人写的代码”，而不是“提供一种有用的能力，让原本无法实现的代码得以实现”。

619716211.en: I would describe it as "trying not to break code written in the first 5-10 years of Rust where we didnt much talk about aliasing"
619716211.zh: 我会把它描述为：“尽量不破坏 Rust 最初 5～10 年间编写的代码——那时候我们还不太讨论别名问题。”

619716247.en: to date we still have no docs that clearly say that you cant do ptr arithmetic on (stuff derived from) references, and raw ptr ergonomics are still terrible
619716247.zh: 截至目前，我们仍然没有文档明确说明不能对（从引用派生出的）东西做指针算术，而裸指针的使用体验依然糟糕透顶。

619716292.en: so I dont think we can blame programmers for writing such code

619763660.zh: 也许还要再过 15 年，我们才能利用这个 UB，而不会导致大量错误编译；我觉得这没什么问题。

619800525.en: Maybe we can have a kind of "opsem edition" so that old codes get the more permissive semantics with fewer room for optimizations, but the new edition has more UB and requires the code to conform to new aliasing requirements. In old editions, miri emits a warning that it is going to be UB in future editions, and in new editions it just rejects.
619800525.zh: 也许我们可以引入一种“opsem edition”，让旧代码采用更宽松的语义、牺牲一些优化空间，而新 edition 则包含更多 UB，并要求代码符合新的别名要求。在旧 edition 中，Miri 发出警告，说明未来 edition 中这将成为 UB；而在新 edition 中则直接拒绝。

619808590.en: People who use Miri to check their code are already told not to do this. Our problem is with users who don't, and we can assume they won't notice the edition change if it doesn't raise a warning of some sort
619808590.zh: 使用 Miri 检查代码的人已经被告知不要这么做了。我们的问题在于那些不使用 Miri 的用户，而我们可以假设，如果 edition 变更没有引发某种警告，他们不会注意到这次变更。

619817955.en: It could be a separate number than the normal edition. Then users could ask themselves that what is the effect of the number that I'm bumping, and do I need to fix anything / check with miri? And they can downgrade their edition if they hit any "miscompilations".
619817955.zh: 它可以使用不同于普通 edition 的编号。这样用户就可以问自己：我正在递增的这个编号会带来什么影响？我是否需要修复什么，或者用 Miri 检查一下？如果遇到任何“错误编译”，他们还可以降级 edition。

过去编写了大量代码，而且这些代码很可能不会再更新。永远维护项目是要花钱的，通常没有资金支持的项目负担不起这笔费用。更不用说，并不是每个项目都能在 Miri 中运行。

619827593.en: And doing it via editions would mean that the "true" rust opsem would have to support both. For this, perhaps that is fine (although it does beg the question of whether or not it's worth it to introduce something as complex as 'opsem editions' for this case), but generally this seems very difficult and confusing to me. This 'opsem edition' would also be dangerous to update, especially for projects that can't run under miri. And having the more permissive opsem in the older edition means there would be cases where downgrading opsem editions would be desirable, which seems like something we shouldn't want (AFAIK downgrading normal editions is currently only done for wider compiler version support). This also doesn't even get into the complexity macros would introduce here.
619827593.zh: 而通过 edition 来实现，就意味着“真正的” Rust 操作语义必须同时支持两种情况。对于这个问题，也许这样还行（不过这确实会让人思考：为这个案例引入如此复杂的“opsem editions”是否值得），但总的来说，这对我而言似乎非常困难且令人困惑。这个“opsem edition”在升级时也会很危险，尤其是对那些无法在 Miri 下运行的项目而言。而让旧 edition 保持更宽松的操作语义，意味着会出现一些应该降级 opsem edition 的情况；这似乎不是我们想要的（据我所知，目前降级普通 edition 只是为了支持更广泛的编译器版本）。此外，这还完全没有涉及宏会在这里引入的复杂性。

619966796.en: also what's the rush, we can say "we has subobject provenance", add a bunch of `implicit_operation_near_unsafe_code` lints to flag implicit autoref, let Field Projections solve the ergonomics, and wait 10 years before we exploit that particular UB

619976429.en:

619976429.zh:
到目前为止，我还没看到任何能让我确信这些 bug 不会反复出现的计划。有 field projections 固然很棒，但它并没有解决自动借用相关的任何问题。

我认为，如果我们再让一份规范带着诸如“在 2040 年之前不能利用这个 UB”这样的奇怪脚注存在 10 年，那会非常糟糕——尤其是对于 subobject provenance 这类重要问题。而且这甚至还没有涉及另一点：我觉得，把完全可以避免的 UB（也就是说，我们能够避免引入它）直接施加到遗留代码上，是值得质疑的。

619977172.en: I could imagine delaying the decision until we have better data (compare miri runs of "TB with strict subobject provenance" and "TB with slightly relaxed subobject provenance"). but some Miri work is needed before we can run such an experiment.
619977172.zh: 我可以想象，先推迟决定，等我们有更好的数据后再说（比较“具有严格 subobject provenance 的 TB”和“稍微放宽 subobject provenance 的 TB”的 Miri 运行结果）。不过，在进行这样的实验之前，还需要先做一些 Miri 工作。

619977289.en: I already said this upthread, but I want to see moves like this accompanied with a plan for how to actually reach the desired end state, since otherwise it's just saying "we should lock in now that better things are not possible"
619977289.zh: 我已经在上面的讨论中说过这点了，但我希望看到这类改动时，同时能有一套实际达到理想最终状态的方案；否则，这就只是在说“我们现在就该把现状定死，因为以后不可能有更好的做法了”。

619977463.en: I think in the absence of a plan we should indeed lock in. so I would say the people who argue against allowing such code are the ones I'd expect to come up with a plan for how to deal with the massive footguns caused by the UB they want us to have.
619977463.zh: 我认为，如果没有方案，我们确实应该把现状定死。所以我会认为，那些反对允许此类代码的人，才应该提出方案，说明该如何处理他们希望我们保留的 UB 所造成的大量隐患。

619977503.en: I mean several plans have been proposed and you keep shooting them down for being too long term
619977503.zh: 我的意思是，已经有人提出过好几套方案了，而你一直因为它们的时间跨度太长就把它们否决掉。

619977543.en: there have been sketches of outlines of a plan. and yeah I wasnt a fan of them.

619977733.en: I wanted to get something landed in the Reference because we need to nail down the related https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/621. saying in the Reference "it's UB to ever do an access outside the memory the reference points-to" feels like a huge disservice to our users, introducing an entire new class of UB out of nowhere now for patterns that we have seen again and again in real-world code.
619977733.zh: 我想先把一些内容写入 Reference，因为我们需要明确解决相关的 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/621。在 Reference 中写上“任何时候，只要访问超出该引用所指向的内存范围，就是 UB”，我觉得这会严重损害用户利益：它会凭空引入一整类全新的 UB，而我们明明已经在现实世界的代码中一次又一次地看到这些模式。

619977844.en: okay, but you've already seen that lots of people would like to see a path forward to where that is actually UB. I understand your concerns, but I'm not sure you understand ours. Please engage with the brainstorming on how to make something that satisfies everyone
619977844.zh: 好吧，但你已经看到，很多人都希望能有一条前进路径，最终让这确实成为 UB。我理解你的担忧，但我不确定你是否理解我们的担忧。请参与讨论如何制定一个能让所有人都满意的方案。

619977854.en: yes, Miri has errorred for such code for a long time, but that was an experiment to figure out how much UB we can get away with in this space. and to me the experiment showed that no we can get away with this.
619977854.zh: 是的，Miri 很久以来都会对这类代码报错，但那是一项实验，目的是弄清楚在这个领域我们究竟能容忍多少 UB。而在我看来，实验表明：不，我们不能容忍这种做法。

619991326.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429):
```quote
having field projections is amazing but doesnt solve any of the issues around autoref.
```

For autoref, I'm proposing a `implicit_operation_near_unsafe_code` lint that warns on autoderef/autoref, match ergonomics, and a couple other implicit operations in a function body that also has an `unsafe` block. Does that not address the issues around autoref? Or are you objecting to it on other grounds?
619991326.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429)： “有字段投影确实很棒，但并没有解决围绕自动借用的任何问题。” 针对自动借用，我提议增加一个 `implicit_operation_near_unsafe_code` lint：当函数体中同时存在 `unsafe` 块时，对自动解引用/自动借用、匹配人体学以及其他几个隐式操作发出警告。这样还不足以解决自动借用相关的问题吗？还是说你是基于其他理由反对它？

619991727.en: @**Thom Chiovoloni** , if your comment is directed at me: do you have an argument for not having subobject provenance in the far future which isn't of the form "lots of legacy code exists"? I would really like to hear a positive argument against subobj provenance
619991727.zh: @**Thom Chiovoloni**，如果你的评论是针对我的：你能否提出一个理由，说明为什么在遥远的未来也不应该有子对象溯源，而这个理由不是“遗留代码太多”这种形式？我真的很想听听反对子对象溯源的正面论据。

619991884.en: sometimes "too much legacy exists" *is* also a critical reason why you're locked into something. see: most other systems in the world
619991884.zh: 有时候，“遗留代码太多”*确实*也是让你不得不受制于某种方案的关键原因。参见：世界上大多数其他系统。

619991939.en: I think legacy code is a genuinely good reason. But I also would probably be in favor of having no subobject provenance anyway, since I think it's less error prone.
619991939.zh: 我认为遗留代码确实是一个很充分的理由。但即便如此，我可能还是会支持完全不采用子对象溯源，因为我认为那样更不容易出错。

619991944.en: Of course I recognize it as a constraint, but I also think that "stability without stagnation" is a good principle and if we can find a way to have our cake and eat it too that would be great
619991944.zh: 当然，我承认这是一项约束，但我也认为“在不陷入停滞的前提下保持稳定”是一个很好的原则；如果我们能找到一个两全其美的办法，那就太好了。

619991980.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429):
```quote
I think it would be very bad if we went another 10 years with a spec that has weird footnotes like "cant exploit this UB before 2040"
```

It wouldn't even be part of the spec, only an implementation choice for the sake of not breaking users too much. And even if it was, I don't see why that's a problem? We'd still have the systems language with the best spec.

 We'd make a blog post about "btw, never do pointer arithmetic on references" to make sure everyone is aware. We'd update the nomicon if it's not already clear. Once we settle on TB/SB, we're already squarely in the realm of "opsem of references has subtle provenance" anyway, and that's also something we'll have to document/teach well so it's not a whole new world of problems either.
619991980.zh: @_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619976429)： “如果我们再用一份带有诸如‘在 2040 年之前不能利用这个 UB’之类奇怪脚注的规范过十年，我认为那会非常糟糕。” 这甚至不会成为规范的一部分，只会是为了不至于过多破坏用户代码而采取的一项实现选择。即便它属于规范，我也不明白这有什么问题。我们仍然会拥有规范最完善的系统语言。我们可以写一篇题为“顺便说一句，永远不要对引用做指针算术”的博客文章，确保所有人都知道这一点。如果 Nomicon 里还没有说清楚，我们也会更新它。一旦我们确定采用 TB/SB，我们本来就已经明确进入了“引用的操作语义具有微妙的溯源规则”这一领域；这同样是我们必须充分记录并讲解好的内容，所以也不会凭空带来一整套全新的问题。

619992326.en: put another way, I do not accept "legacy code exists" as a reason to *permanently* block off some design avenue, although the runway to get onto it might be very long. I would like the t=infinity limit of Rust to be a perfect language, so the only thing that will get me off having a design permanently is if there is an argument that it is not good on its own merits
619992326.zh: 换句话说，我不接受“存在遗留代码”作为*永久*封锁某条设计路径的理由，尽管走上这条路径的过程可能会非常漫长。我希望 t=infinity 时的 Rust 能成为一门完美的语言，所以，唯一能让我永久放弃某项设计的理由，就是有人能论证它本身并不好。

619992570.en: I don't think there's such a thing as a perfect language. It's all subject to taste. That means if changes which break old code are okay, then they will be made continuously, since tastes change. That means that people have to maintain software indefinitely, which means that things without indefinite funding will be broken. So I don't agree with that at all.
619992570.zh: 我不认为存在所谓完美的语言。一切都取决于个人偏好。这意味着，只要允许做出会破坏旧代码的改动，那么这种改动就会持续发生，因为偏好会发生变化。也就是说，人们必须无限期地维护软件；而没有无限期资金支持的东西最终都会被破坏。所以我完全不同意这种看法。

619992678.en: Anyway, I think UB should have to justify itself as being worth how error-prone it makes the language. I think this is a case that genuinely makes the language more error-prone (as evidenced by how often this is hit), without benefit to compensate for that.
619992678.zh: 总之，我认为 UB 应该证明自己值得承担它给语言带来的易错性。我认为这确实是一个让语言更容易出错的案例（从它在实践中被频繁触发这一点就能看出来），却没有相应的收益来弥补这一点。

619992701.en: So I would be against it even without the legacy argument.
619992701.zh: 所以，即使不考虑遗留代码这个论据，我也会反对它。

619992784.en: being error-prone is certainly an argument against it on its own merits. I don't think it's a matter of taste, it's an empirical matter
619992784.zh: 容易出错当然本身就是反对它的理由。我不认为这是品味问题，而是一个经验问题。

619992826.en: "references ever existing make more code UB" was one of the most common errors with SB in the past
619992826.zh: “只要引用曾经存在过，就会让更多代码变成 UB”是过去使用 SB 时最常见的错误之一。

619992835.en: I agree with Thom -- even ignoring existing code, I don't think it's obvious that "pervasive subobject provenance for references" would be the best place for Rust to end up in eventually. It seems almost certain that any useful aliasing model will be subtle for many programmers to wrap their heads around. But that doesn't mean further sources of UB are automatically (near-)free. It's still a trade-off how many things unsafe code authors have to be very careful about. At least in today's Rust, this is empirically a very common footgun in the wild. It's not obvious to me if and how a far-future Rust can fully remove these footguns.
619992835.zh: 我同意 Thom 的看法——即使不考虑现有代码，我也不认为“对引用普遍采用子对象溯源”显然会是 Rust 最终最理想的归宿。几乎可以确定，任何有用的别名模型对许多程序员来说都会微妙得难以理解。但这并不意味着增加额外的 UB 来源就自动等于（近乎）零成本。对于不安全代码作者必须格外小心的事项究竟有多少，这仍然是一种权衡。至少在今天的 Rust 中，从实际情况来看，这确实是现实世界中非常常见的坑。我不清楚遥远未来的 Rust 是否能完全消除这些坑，以及要如何做到这一点。

619992967.en: My argument for it is that it's easier to teach, and therefore less error-prone. I know Ralf will argue something about UB monotonicity here but I don't think it's as simple as that, if there is some weird edge case that people may or may not be allowed to exploit in certain circumstances that seems problematic and error-prone to me
619992967.zh: 我的理由是它更容易教授，因此也更不容易出错。我知道 Ralf 会在这里谈论什么 UB 单调性之类的东西，但我不认为事情有那么简单：如果存在某个奇怪的边界情况，导致人们在某些情形下可能被允许、也可能不被允许利用它，那在我看来这就很有问题，也很容易出错。

619993067.en: I don't think ease of teaching automatically corresponds to ease of use.
619993067.zh: 我不认为易于教授就自动意味着易于使用。

619993076.en: references making more code UB than pointers already exists with or without subobj provenance
619993076.zh: 引用比指针让更多代码变成 UB，这种情况无论有没有子对象溯源都已经存在了。

619993219.en: I also think adding UB to code to make things easier to teach is highly dubious.
619993219.zh: 我也认为，为了让东西更容易教授，就给代码增加 UB，是非常值得怀疑的做法。

619993300.en: it's not the UB itself making things easier to teach, it's the simpler model
619993300.zh: 并不是 UB 本身让东西更容易教授，而是更简单的模型。

619993302.en: For education you can still go with a 'tower of weakening' style, where you first teach that you shouldn't do this, even if the reality is that you can.
619993302.zh: 在教学上，你仍然可以采用“逐级弱化”的方式：先教导大家不应该这样做，即便实际情况是你可以这样做。

619993323.en: Yes, you can teach the simplified model without making things that don't fit into the simplified model UB. In fact, we have already officially adopted that approach with the strict provenance / exposed provenance split.
619993323.zh: 是的，你完全可以在不把那些不符合简化模型的行为定义为 UB 的前提下，教授这个简化模型。事实上，我们已经通过 strict provenance / exposed provenance 的区分正式采用了这种做法。

619993361.en: this is to me very similar to strict provenance
619993361.zh: 在我看来，这和 strict provenance 非常相似。

619993523.en: the difference being that we haven't yet attempted to FCP whatever angelic provenance model we need to handle the non-strict provenance stuff
619993523.zh: 区别在于，我们还没有尝试对处理 non-strict provenance 所需的任何 angelic provenance 模型进行 FCP。

619993565.en: we just took the first step in making that code rare
619993565.zh: 我们只是迈出了让这类代码变得少见的第一步。

619993671.en: and right now we haven't taken the first step in making non-subobject provenance code rare
619993671.zh: 而且目前，我们还没有迈出让 non-subobject provenance 代码变得少见的第一步。

619993732.en: I think it's not even clear to me whether those on the other side want to see this code discouraged
619993732.zh: 我甚至不确定另一方的人是否希望看到这类代码受到劝阻。

619993853.en: How is that related to the "it's easier to teach" argument?
619993853.zh: 这和“更容易教授”这个论点有什么关系？

619993857.en: I'm a pragmatist. I only care about discouraging this code if it's ultimately decided to be UB. Strict provenance is different, in that there are actual downsides to not following it (miri support, if nothing else).
619993857.zh: 我是实用主义者。只有在最终决定把这类代码定义为 UB 的情况下，我才会在意劝阻使用它。strict provenance 则不同，因为不遵循它确实有实际的缺点（至少还有 miri 支持这一点）。

619993923.en: I'm confused - miri rejects both kinds of code (subobj provenance and strict provenance violations)
619993923.zh: 我有点困惑——miri 会拒绝这两类代码（subobj provenance 和违反 strict provenance 的代码）。

619994014.en: I think it's pragmatic to discourage code in advance of making it UB
619994014.zh: 我认为，在把某种行为定义为 UB 之前就劝阻使用相关代码，是很务实的做法。

619994042.en: Non-strict provenance will always be hard for miri to support. Non-subobject provenance, to my understanding, is completely possible for miri to support just fine (even if it only does now under a specific flag).
619994042.zh: Non-strict provenance 对 miri 来说永远都会很难支持。据我理解，miri 完全可以很好地支持 non-subobject provenance（即使目前只有在特定标志下才能做到）。

619994147.en: At the moment, I do discourage using non-subobject provenance, partially because it's poorly supported in miri, and partially (more importantly) because it may become UB.
619994147.zh: 目前，我确实不建议使用 non-subobject provenance，一部分原因是 miri 对它的支持很差，另一部分（更重要的）原因是它将来可能会变成 UB。

619994201.en: But if it became defined behavior and were supported fine in miri, I would have no reason to discourage it.
619994201.zh: 但如果它最终成为定义明确的行为，并且 miri 也能很好地支持它，那我就没有理由反对使用它了。

619994259.en: I mean, it's fundamentally unsafe so it's needed to be discouraged in that way. And it may be easy to break library safety requirements too with it. So I don't think it should be used wildly.
619994259.zh: 我的意思是，它从根本上来说是不安全的，所以需要以这种方式加以劝阻。而且，使用它也可能很容易破坏库的安全性要求。因此，我不认为应该泛滥地使用它。

619994291.en: This is going out on a limb, but I suspect that miri could be faster with subobject provenance, because you can use more efficient data structures than TB
619994291.zh: 这可能有点冒昧，但我猜使用 subobject provenance 后，miri 可能会更快，因为你可以使用比 TB 更高效的数据结构。

619994350.en: For me, that's not nearly a good enough reason to make something UB.
619994350.zh: 对我来说，这远远不是把某种行为定义为 UB 的充分理由。

619994378.en: of course not, but since you mentioned miri support I thought I'd mention it
619994378.zh: 当然不是，但既然你提到了 miri 支持，我就想顺便提一下这一点。

619994384.en: Especially something like this, which genuinely makes unsafe Rust harder to write.
619994384.zh: 尤其是像这种确实会让 unsafe Rust 更难编写的东西。

619994403.en: that's the part I'm stuck on

619994465.en: is there code which naturally wants to be written in a subobj provenance violating way?
619994465.zh: 有没有哪类代码，天然就适合以违反子对象来源的方式来编写？

619994477.en: You basically have to use raw pointers everywhere. As mentioned, raw pointers have terrible ergonomics (I don't think this is likely to change hugely). It's also easy to accidentally go through a reference.
619994477.zh: 基本上你到处都得使用裸指针。正如前面提到的，裸指针的使用体验很糟（我不认为这一点可能会有巨大的改变）。而且也很容易一不小心就经过了引用。

619994500.en: that's already the case for separate reasons
619994500.zh: 出于其他独立的原因，目前已经是这样了。

619994521.en: This makes the consequences of not doing it much more likely to be UB
619994521.zh: 这会让不这么做的后果更有可能是未定义行为（UB）。

619994530.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619994477):
```quote
I don't think this is likely to change hugely
```

Field Projections will make a significant difference, fwiw
619994530.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619994477)：
```quote
我不认为这一点可能会有巨大的改变
```

不过，字段投影（Field Projections）会带来显著的改变，顺带一提。

619994606.en:
@_**Nadrieril|245339** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619994530):
````quote
Field Projections will make a significant difference
````

Lack of method call support (or trait dispatch support) will probably be a problem forever, since we probably don't want to give up the ability to add methods to raw pointers
619994606.zh:
@_**Nadrieril|245339** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/619994530)：
````quote
不过，字段投影（Field Projections）会带来显著的改变
````

缺少方法调用支持（或 trait 分派支持）可能会永远是个问题，因为我们大概不希望放弃给裸指针添加方法的能力。

619994653.en: I have to go, though. I'll be back later.
619994653.zh: 不过我得走了。晚点回来。

619994780.zh: 确实如此，而且挺令人遗憾的。

619995085.en: But partially solvable thanks to library code: just needs someone to write a crate with a nice version of `NonNull` that commits to not adding new methods and allows method calls through it
619995085.zh: 不过这部分可以借助库代码解决：只需要有人写一个 crate，提供一个更好用的 `NonNull` 版本，承诺不再添加新方法，并允许通过它进行方法调用。

619997859.en: Many people (including me) are not going to depend on a random library from crates.io and deal with yet another pointer type just to make using raw pointers less of a chore
619997859.zh: 很多人（包括我在内）不会仅仅为了让裸指针没那么难用，就去依赖 crates.io 上随便一个库，再应付另一种指针类型。

619998311.en: If you can’t make the case that it’ll be a first class part of the built-in Rust experience, including all the library API churn that is needed to avoid lots of type conversion clutter, then IMO it’s not a satisfying answer for this concern. And unless we can basically deprecate raw pointers and/or `NonNull` then there is still the cognitive overhead of having even more raw pointer types (we already have too many and other reasons for adding even more, like alignment niches).
619998311.zh: 如果你无法证明它会成为 Rust 内置体验中一等重要的组成部分，包括为了避免大量类型转换杂乱而需要进行的所有库 API 变更，那么在我看来，这就不是对这一担忧令人满意的回答。而且，除非我们基本上能够弃用裸指针和/或 `NonNull`，否则多出更多裸指针类型仍然会带来认知负担（我们已经有太多类型了；当然，也有其他需要增加更多类型的理由，比如对齐方面的利基优化）。

620002845.en: Yea fair I was going a bit far there
620002845.zh: 嗯，有道理，我刚才确实说得有点过头了。

620007415.en: I assume `NonNull` will indeed be a valid receiver, right? So it'll be possible to call methods on `NonNull<MyStruct>` that have a `self: NonNull<Self>`, I assume?
620007415.zh: 我想 `NonNull` 确实会是一个有效的接收者，对吧？所以应该可以在 `NonNull<MyStruct>` 上调用那些具有 `self: NonNull<Self>` 的方法，对吧？

620007665.en: Hotly debated, I believe the current consensus is no (because we want to keep adding methods and can't version std)
620007665.zh: 这件事争议很大。不过我认为目前的共识是否定的（因为我们希望继续添加方法，而 std 又无法进行版本化）。

620009657.en: Put another way: it feels to me that removing subobject provenance makes unsafe Rust and especially FFI related code easier to write, but it risks making performance-sensitive safe Rust harder to write.
620009657.zh: 换句话说，在我看来，移除子对象来源会让不安全 Rust，尤其是与 FFI 相关的代码，更容易编写；但它可能会让对性能敏感的安全 Rust 更难编写。

620011298.en: I'm skeptical that that's fundamental. I also think that if the `is_nice` check is complex enough to be performance sensitive, the compiler will have trouble deduplicating it anyway, and if it's simple then the performance won't matter that much.
620011298.zh: 我怀疑这并不是根本性的问题。我还认为，如果 `is_nice` 检查复杂到足以影响性能，那么编译器无论如何都很难消除重复检查；而如果它很简单，那性能影响也不会太大。

620011421.en: I also think that even if it is true, performant code being easy to write is less important than correct unsafe code being easy to write. (And I say that as someone who has written a lot of performance critical code)
620011421.zh: 我还认为，即使这确实如此，让高性能代码更容易编写，也不如让正确的不安全代码更容易编写重要。（我这么说，是因为我写过很多性能关键型代码。）

620011497.en: Also, given that you often need to dip into unsafe to write high performance code, unsafe code being easier to write will make some kinds of high performance code easier to write anyway.
620011497.zh: 另外，考虑到编写高性能代码时经常需要涉及不安全代码，让不安全代码更容易编写，本来也会让某些类型的高性能代码更容易编写。

620011563.en: My original concern was for getting optimizations in safe code
620011563.zh: 我最初担忧的是如何在安全代码中获得优化。

620011777.en: this issue is about weighing whether to allow "weird" unsafe code being DB or to have all code everywhere paying a performance price unless you have some local information about where your references come from
620011777.zh: 这个问题在于权衡：是允许“奇怪的”不安全代码属于定义明确的行为（DB），还是让所有地方的代码都付出性能代价，除非你掌握一些关于引用来源的局部信息。

620011995.en: it's basically exactly the same argument for why references exist to begin with with their SB style UB attached, it means you can do optimizations on free functions taking references
620011995.zh: 这基本上和“为什么一开始要有引用，并为它们附带 SB 风格的未定义行为”是完全相同的论点：这意味着你可以对接收引用的自由函数进行优化。

620012074.en: which opens up a whole class of optimizations to Rust which are not accessible to C/C++
620012074.zh: 这为 Rust 开启了一整类 C/C++ 无法实现的优化。

620012131.en: which is important *specifically because* this includes boring normal safe code
620012131.zh: 这之所以重要，*恰恰是因为*其中包括了普通、平淡无奇的安全代码。

620012397.en: It's not like rust loses those optimizations. It just won't gain further ones, in the few cases where this can meaningfully prevent them. Also, the case above involves interior mutability, so that example can probably be recovered by saying that only the bytes inside an UnsafeCell have UnsafeCell properties (regardless of subobj provenance)
620012397.zh: Rust 又不是会失去这些优化。它只是在少数确实可能因此受到影响的情况下，无法进一步获得新的优化而已。另外，上面的例子涉及内部可变性，因此或许可以这样解决：只有 `UnsafeCell` 内部的字节才具有 `UnsafeCell` 的属性（不论子对象来源如何）。

620013558.en:
Hot take: Rust already has subobject provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

Allocations essentially are a particularly strict form of subobjects. Using allocators on top of other allocators, you can have a build a whole tower of nested sub"objects" (allocations). The rules around how this nesting works are seriously underspecified and full of open questions—but there's (AFAICT) broad agreement that we want to give the compiler broad latitude to optimize around allocations, despite the challenges that poses.
620013558.zh:
我的一个大胆看法：Rust 已经有子对象来源了 https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

分配本质上是特别严格的一种子对象。通过在其他分配器之上使用分配器，你可以构建出一整套嵌套的“子对象”（分配）。关于这种嵌套如何运作的规则，目前严重缺乏明确规定，也存在大量悬而未决的问题——但（据我所知）大家普遍同意，我们希望给编译器足够大的自由度，围绕分配进行优化，尽管这会带来不少挑战。

620013776.en: I've always found it confusing that we consider "allocations" to be super-special and totally distinct from subobjects in general. I think we should have one model that encompasses both
620013776.zh: 我一直觉得奇怪：我们把“分配”看得非常特殊，认为它与一般的子对象完全不同。我认为我们应该有一个能够同时涵盖二者的模型。

620014128.en:
I think I saw suggested an option to have subobject provenance on structs but not on arrays/slices before. I have lost track of this conversation at this point, so I don't know if that is still on the table, but if it is, wouldn't that cover most reasonable use cases.

The "having a reference to head and getting the tail" case wouldn't be covered. Nor would "I'm an allocator and I stashed metadata before the object and want to use it during free", but that last one should probably use raw pointers anyway.
620014128.zh:
我记得以前有人提议过：结构体可以具有子对象来源，但数组/切片不能。我现在已经跟不上这场讨论了，所以不知道这个方案是否仍在考虑之中；但如果还在，那么它不是可以覆盖大多数合理的使用场景吗？

“持有指向头部的引用，然后获取尾部”的情况无法覆盖。“我是一个分配器，在对象前面存放了元数据，并希望在释放时使用它”的情况也无法覆盖，不过后一种情况本来就应该使用裸指针。

620014281.en: That's still on the table, see https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/2338. This discussion is mostly because some people find even this unacceptable (they want more subobject provenance than it).
620014281.zh: 这个方案仍在考虑之中，见 https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/2338。这场讨论主要是因为有些人觉得即使这样也无法接受（他们希望子对象来源的适用范围比这更大）。

620015011.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620013776):
```quote
I've always found it confusing that we consider "allocations" to be super-special and totally distinct from subobjects in general. I think we should have one model that encompasses both
```

The solution for allocators will need to need to work for raw pointers somehow. I think it's a separate topic all together, honestly.
620015011.zh:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620013776)：
```quote
我一直觉得奇怪：我们把“分配”看得非常特殊，认为它与一般的子对象完全不同。我认为我们应该有一个能够同时涵盖二者的模型。
```

分配器的解决方案无论如何都需要能够处理裸指针。我觉得这完全是另一个话题，说实话。

620021038.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620012397):
```quote
It's not like rust loses those optimizations. It just won't gain further ones, in the few cases where this can meaningfully prevent them. Also, the case above involves interior mutability, so that example can probably be recovered by saying that only the bytes inside an UnsafeCell have UnsafeCell properties (regardless of subobj provenance)
```

I've kinda been confused about this: the intention is AFAIU that bytes outside a reference are writable if the referenced data contains cells: so if you get a reference to `struct Foo { a: usize, b: Cell<X> }` and want to mutate `a` then can't you just reference the `&foo.b` and then access out of that to `foo.a`. Because `b` hold a Cell, all bytes out of it are RW and therefore it's not UB to write `a`.

In other words, it seems to me like we can't have both no subobject provenance, and type-deliminated interior mutability. Or we can, but it's nearly meaningless since you can always expand the interior mutability into surrounding fields by going through a plain Cell reference and expanding back out.
620021038.zh:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620012397)：
```quote
Rust 又不是会失去这些优化。它只是在少数确实可能因此受到影响的情况下，无法进一步获得新的优化而已。另外，上面的例子涉及内部可变性，因此或许可以这样解决：只有 `UnsafeCell` 内部的字节才具有 `UnsafeCell` 的属性（不论子对象来源如何）。
```

我一直有点困惑：据我所知，设计意图是，如果引用的数据中包含 cell，那么引用范围之外的字节也是可写的。比如说，如果你获得了一个指向 `struct Foo { a: usize, b: Cell<X> }` 的引用，并且想修改 `a`，那你不能直接引用 `&foo.b`，然后从那里越界访问到 `foo.a` 吗？因为 `b` 持有一个 `Cell`，所以从它向外的所有字节都是可读写的，因此写入 `a` 并不属于未定义行为。

换句话说，在我看来，我们似乎不可能同时做到：没有子对象来源，以及按类型划分的内部可变性。或者说可以，但这几乎没有意义，因为你总是可以先通过一个普通的 `Cell` 引用向外扩展，将内部可变性扩展到周围字段，然后再继续向外访问。

620023028.en:
@_**Jules Bertholet|421518** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Vibes.20on.20subobject.20provenance/near/620013558):
```quote
Hot take: Rust already has subobject provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation
```

620031065.en:
But yeah, my four cents are that lack of subobject provenance (or maybe it should be called "reference access restrictions")

1. does seem to forbid some optimisations that one might consider reasonable (whether they're worth it is another thing),

2. puts pressure on safe Rust to do odd things to regain said optimisations (like create a `&self.foo` and explicitly remove it after a cross-cutting call to prove no mutations, while hoping that the compiler doesn't use a stack slot on it),

3. seems to also be a slippery slope to Cells leaking interior mutability into their surroundings (`&Cell` has to assume bytes outside of it are also interior-mutable, hence `&StructContainingCell` has to kinda assume all of its fields are interior-mutable),

4. seems to be a fairly all-or-nothing thing, in that a hypothetical `fn restrict_provenance` or an attribute to do the same either has to be unsafe, or a function containing reference access expansion has to be unsafe with the precondition of said function or attribute not being used. (The attribute is easier if the library doesn't enable foreign code to create the referenced data.) Effectively, if a `&Header` reference may or may not be restricted (depending on if a `restrict_provenace` was called on it, of if it lives in a restricted struct?) then we have a risky reference validity condition (used by some functions) that is not visible in the type system. (I've generally preferred making newtypes for these cases so that I can see in the type system that I have less restricted access that the pointer referree type suggests.)

But as said above: I'm but a little chick and definitely don't know much about opsem, nor do I know that much about compiler optimisations. I also don't really know or understand if the ~6000? UB cases found with SB Miri is a lot or not, and therefore whether halving that to around 3000? IIRC with TB and no subobject provenance is a big deal or not.
620031065.zh:
不过，我的四点看法是，缺少子对象 provenance（或者也许应该称为“引用访问限制”）：

1. 确实似乎会禁止一些人们可能认为合理的优化（至于这些优化是否值得，则是另一回事）；

2. 会迫使安全 Rust 做一些奇怪的事情来重新获得这些优化（比如创建一个 `&self.foo`，然后在一次跨领域调用之后显式地移除它，以证明没有发生任何变更，同时还要祈祷编译器不要为它使用栈槽）；

3. 似乎还会滑向这样一种局面：Cell 将内部可变性泄漏到周围区域（`&Cell` 必须假定其外部的字节也具有内部可变性，因此 `&StructContainingCell` 在某种程度上就必须假定其所有字段都具有内部可变性）；

4. 似乎是一个相当非此即彼的问题：假设有一个 `fn restrict_provenance`，或者一个能实现相同效果的属性，那么它要么必须是不安全的；要么，包含引用访问扩展的函数就必须是不安全的，并以不得使用该函数或属性作为前置条件。（如果库不会允许外部代码创建被引用的数据，那么使用属性会更容易。）实际上，如果一个 `&Header` 引用是否受限取决于是否曾对它调用过 `restrict_provenace`，或者它是否存储在一个受限结构体中，那么我们就有了一个有风险的引用有效性条件（某些函数会使用它），但这个条件在类型系统中不可见。（对于这类情况，我通常更倾向于使用 newtype，这样我就能从类型系统中看出，我拥有的访问权限比指针所指向的类型所暗示的更受限。）

不过，正如上面所说：我只是只小菜鸟，对 opsem 确实不太了解，对编译器优化也所知不多。我也不太清楚、也不理解 SB Miri 找到的大约 6000 个？UB 案例到底算多还是少，因此也不知道在 TB 下、没有子对象 provenance 时，如果我没记错，能把它减少到大约 3000 个？这件事是否意义重大。

```quote
Hot take: Rust already has subobject provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

Allocations essentially are a particularly strict form of subobjects. Using allocators on top of other allocators, you can have a build a whole tower of nested sub"objects" (allocations). The rules around how this nesting works are seriously underspecified and full of open questions—but there's (AFAICT) broad agreement that we want to give the compiler broad latitude to optimize around allocations, despite the challenges that poses.
```

allocations are *explicitly* created and destroyed. it's hard for the programmer to miss that. that's very different from the kind of subobject provenance people are advocating in this thread.
621794925.zh:

```quote
大胆的观点：Rust 已经拥有子对象 provenance https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/index.html#allocation

分配本质上是一种尤其严格的子对象。通过在其他分配器之上使用分配器，你可以构建出一整座嵌套子“对象”（分配）的高塔。关于这种嵌套如何运作的规则严重缺乏规范，且充满未决问题——但（据我所知）大家普遍同意，我们希望给予编译器围绕分配进行广泛优化的空间，尽管这会带来种种挑战。
```

分配是*显式*创建和销毁的。程序员很难注意不到这一点。这与本主题中人们所主张的那种子对象 provenance 非常不同。

620033100.en: imo the way we should make `Header` patterns work is by putting an extern type as the last field of the header, and define that to mean that there can be more stuff following the header (or preceding, but maybe we'd want the extern type to be first, though otoh that doesn't really work unless the extern type is a ZST), so doing that means references to types structurally containing those extern types don't get subobject provenance, but references to types without those do get subobject provenance.
620033100.zh: 我觉得，让 `Header` 模式生效的方式应该是把一个 `extern type` 作为 header 的最后一个字段，并规定这意味着 header 后面还可以有更多内容（也可以是在前面，不过或许我们会希望把 extern type 放在最前面，但另一方面，除非 extern type 是 ZST，否则这样并不真正可行）。这样一来，结构上包含这些 extern type 的类型的引用就不会具有子对象溯源，而不包含这些类型的引用则会具有子对象溯源。

620033158.en: or some `repr` thing or `PhantomPinned`-like marker type.
620033158.zh: 或者使用某种 `repr` 属性，或类似 `PhantomPinned` 的标记类型。

620033266.en: ~~though that only works for Header, not intrusive lists~~
620033266.zh: ~~不过这只对 Header 有效，对侵入式链表不行~~

620033404.en: how does it not work for intrusive lists? they follow the `Header` pattern where there's extra data before and/or after the `Header`
620033404.zh: 为什么对侵入式链表不行？它们遵循 `Header` 模式，在 `Header` 前面和/或后面都有额外数据。

620033417.en: (or perhaps I guess you just need to chain the tag on everything including the intrusive link, which is fine, so nvm)
620033417.zh: （或者，我想，也许只需要把这个标记串联到所有东西上，包括侵入式链接，这也没问题，所以算了。）

620033539.en: now that I'm thinking about it more, a 1-ZST marker type is probably better than an extern type since you can then easily put your `Header` struct inside another struct without the issue of the extern type not having a size
620033539.zh: 现在仔细想想，大小为 1 的 ZST 标记类型可能比 extern type 更好，因为这样就可以轻松地把你的 `Header` 结构体放进另一个结构体，而不会遇到 extern type 没有大小这一问题。

620034974.en: Alternative idea: sub-objection provenance is a property of the *field projection* so it really should be specified using an attribute on the header field in the struct it is embedded it. This attribute would cause any field projections to that field to retain the provenance of the outer struct.
620034974.zh: 另一种想法：子对象溯源是*字段投影*的属性，所以实际上应该通过嵌入该 header 的结构体中 header 字段上的属性来指定。这个属性会使对该字段进行的任何字段投影都保留外部结构体的溯源。

620037308.en: maybe have subobject provenance active only on types recursively defined in editions after the subobject provenance marker is stable? that way old legacy code isn't broken but rust programs can still benefit from the optimizations after they and their dependencies migrate to a new edition. there could also be a crate-wide attribute to allow opting in on code in old editions for crates that need a lower msrv, which would only make that crate's types act like they are defined on the new edition for the recursive check
620037308.zh: 也许可以规定，只有在子对象溯源标记稳定之后的版本中递归定义的类型，才启用子对象溯源？这样既不会破坏旧的遗留代码，又能让 Rust 程序在自身及其依赖迁移到新版本后享受到相关优化。还可以提供一个 crate 级属性，让需要较低 msrv 的 crate 选择在旧版本的代码中启用它；这样只会让该 crate 的类型在递归检查时表现得像是在新版本中定义的一样。

620037507.en: that would break code using `&u8` as their header type, but we could say a few builtin types opt-out or something, `&()` and `&c_void` in particular should probably opt-out (but not if the `()` is in a new-edition struct)
620037507.zh: 这样会破坏那些使用 `&u8` 作为 header 类型的代码，但我们可以规定有几个内置类型默认选择退出之类的；尤其是 `&()` 和 `&c_void` 可能应该选择退出（不过如果 `()` 位于新版本结构体中，则不应如此）。

620043599.en: Setting aside my comment about legacy code for a moment, that doesn't seem to help the &Header case (https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256), where often the full object doesn't exist as a nameable Rust type.
620043599.zh: 暂且不谈我关于遗留代码的评论，这似乎无法解决 `&Header` 的情况（https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/256）：在这种情况下，完整对象通常并不存在一个可命名的 Rust 类型。

620073041.en:
I feel that an attribute on a field does make sense - it at least explains (to me) how the compiler could even optimise based on subobject provenance in a world where it is not a given. `&foo.header` touches a field with `#[header]`? => can't assume it won't touch `foo.data`. `&foo.part` doesn't have `#[header]`? => can assume it won't touch `foo.data`.

But a type-level opt-out also seems necessary: both for Thom's above case where the full object doesn't exist as a nameable Rust type, but also for `&array[0]` - if the `Type` in `array: Type[]` opts out of subobject provenance then we can happily say that the array does not have subobject provenance.

But none of this really helps existing code. If existing code has to be correct as-it-is while Rust gains opt-outable subobject provenance then it kinda seems like `#[repr(C)]` would be the only reasonable thing to rely on... If `#[repr(C)]` on a type automatically opts it out of subobject provenance but with some `#[get_it_back]` attribute in existence to opt it back then maybe it wouldn't be too odd that `#[repr(C)]` has strong effect on opsem: it's a default but not something that cannot be changed.

Having `#[repr(ordered_fields)]` increases in importance daily.
620073041.zh:
我觉得给字段加属性确实有道理——至少对我来说，在子对象溯源并非既定规则的情况下，这至少解释了编译器如何能够基于子对象溯源进行优化。`&foo.header` 访问了带有 `#[header]` 的字段？=> 不能假定它不会访问 `foo.data`。`&foo.part` 没有 `#[header]`？=> 可以假定它不会访问 `foo.data`。

但类型级别的选择退出似乎也是必要的：既要应对上面 Thom 提到的完整对象不存在可命名 Rust 类型的情况，也要应对 `&array[0]`——如果 `array: Type[]` 中的 `Type` 选择退出子对象溯源，那么我们就可以放心地说这个数组不具有子对象溯源。

不过这些对现有代码都没什么帮助。如果既有代码必须保持原样正确，同时 Rust 又要获得可选择退出的子对象溯源，那么感觉唯一合理的依托就是 `#[repr(C)]`……如果某个类型上的 `#[repr(C)]` 会自动使其选择退出子对象溯源，但同时又存在某种 `#[get_it_back]` 属性可以重新启用它，那么 `#[repr(C)]` 对操作语义产生强烈影响或许也不会显得太奇怪：它是一种默认设置，但并非不可更改。

拥有 `#[repr(ordered_fields)]` 的重要性与日俱增。

620074480.en:
Some examples:

```rust
#[repr(Rust)]
// or #[repr(ordered_fields)]
struct RStruct {
  r___restricted: RField, // Non-repr(C) field in a normal struct -> default to restricted subobject provenance
  #[unrestricted_references]
  r_unrestricted: RField, // Opt out of restricted subobject provenance
  c_unrestricted: CField, // repr(C) field in a normal struct -> default to unrestricted subobject provenance
  #[restricted_references]
  c___restricted: CField, // Opt back into restricted subobject provenance
}

#[repr(C)]
struct CStruct {
  r_unrestricted: RField, // Non-repr(C) field in a C struct -> default to unrestricted subobject provenance
  #[restricted_references]
  r___restricted: RField, // Opt back into restricted subobject provenance
  c_unrestricted: CField, // repr(C) in both sides -> unrestricted
  #[restricted_references]
  c___restricted: CField, // Opt back into restricted subobject provenance
}

#[repr(Rust)]
// or #[repr(ordered_fields)]
struct RField {}
#[repr(C)]
struct CField {}
```

620082598.en:
imo having type-level opt-out is quite useful since we already do that for other things (`PhantomPinned`/`UnsafeCell`) and for any struct type, if you're going to use the `Header` pattern, you'll want to mark the `Header` type since that's only one spot instead of the `N` structs that contain the `Header`.

That also helps Rust tell LLVM the right function argument attributes (which iirc doesn't currently have but could definitely gain -- something like `cant_access_outside(-23, 45)`) when you pass a `&Header` into a function, rather than Rust having to always tell LLVM it-could-be-a-header-pattern because it doesn't know if someone got that pointer from a field access and if that field was properly annotated with the opt-out or not.
620082598.zh:
我觉得类型级别的选择退出非常有用，因为我们已经对其他东西（`PhantomPinned`/`UnsafeCell`）采用了这种做法；对于任何结构体类型，如果你打算使用 `Header` 模式，就会希望标记 `Header` 类型，因为这样只需标记一个地方，而不是包含 `Header` 的 `N` 个结构体。

当你把 `&Header` 传入函数时，这也有助于 Rust 将正确的函数参数属性告知 LLVM（据我所知目前还没有，但完全可以添加——类似 `cant_access_outside(-23, 45)` 的东西）。这样就不用让 Rust 总是告诉 LLVM“它可能是一个 header 模式”，因为 Rust 不知道那个指针是否来自字段访问，也不知道该字段是否正确标注了选择退出属性。

620084411.en: Oh ... I think primitives and much of eg. the std library might want a third attribute option: `#[inherited_references]`. So that if you have a usize struct in a Rust struct that field will by default be restricted, but in a `repr(C)` it'd be unrestricted, and then the same for Mutex or ~~Box~~Cell or whatnot.
620084411.zh: 哦……我觉得，基本类型以及标准库中相当一部分类型可能需要第三种属性选项：`#[inherited_references]`。这样，如果 Rust 结构体中有一个 usize 字段，那么该字段默认会受到限制；但在 `repr(C)` 中则不受限制；Mutex 或 ~~Box~~Cell 之类的类型也是如此。

620088866.en: And that seems to correspond with `#[repr(transparent)]` quite naturally as well (which would then opt you into this default): if you're wrapping transparently over some `T` then you don't really want to mess with the reference restrictions of that `T` any more than what a possible incoming field projection tells you, and what the target `T` says. Otherwise you're not being very transparent.
620088866.zh: 而且这似乎也很自然地对应于 `#[repr(transparent)]`（这样一来就会选择这个默认行为）：如果你对某个 `T` 做透明封装，那么除了可能传入的字段投影以及目标 `T` 本身所规定的内容之外，你通常并不希望进一步干涉 `T` 的引用限制。否则就不能算是非常透明了。

621897599.en:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/marker.20type.20to.20opt-out.20of.20subobject.20provenance/near/621847117):
```quote
though that would only solve the `&Header` problem when the stuff outside the header is an array, instead of an arbitrary struct.
```

Well the whole point is that you don't want (or can't) write out the proper type of the tail, so just use `[MaybeUninit<u8>; ?]` (or `[u8; ?]` if you know that the tail is initialized and doesn't contain pointers/provenance).
621897599.zh:
@_**Jacob Lifshay|229517** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/marker.20type.20to.20opt-out.20of.20subobject.20provenance/near/621847117)：

```quote
不过，这只能在 header 外部的内容是数组而不是任意结构体时，解决 `&Header` 的问题。
```

621903985.en: I guess that works, but it still kinda breaks for fields stored before the beginning of the `Header` type, since you can't have a `[MaybeUninit<u8>; ?]` as the -1st field of your struct. 619859216.en:
From LLVM's LangRef
```quote
Warning

Constant duplication currently makes it unsound to compare pointers if either may be `unnamed_addr`, because each reference to the global in the IR may return a different pointer, and optimization passes may create additional references. Optimization passes can also create pointer comparisons with the expectation that the comparison will return true if the object is the same, which theoretically can make any usage of `unnamed_addr` unsound, but in practice it is unlikely that input IR that does not explicitly compare pointers will be affected by this issue.
```
They obviously have a different meaning of "unsound" here but this still seems crazy to me. I would not expect a read-only `static` to randomly give me different addresses.
619859216.zh:
来自 LLVM 的 LangRef：
```quote
Warning

Constant duplication currently makes it unsound to compare pointers if either may be `unnamed_addr`, because each reference to the global in the IR may return a different pointer, and optimization passes may create additional references. Optimization passes can also create pointer comparisons with the expectation that the comparison will return true if the object is the same, which theoretically can make any usage of `unnamed_addr` unsound, but in practice it is unlikely that input IR that does not explicitly compare pointers will be affected by this issue.
```
显然，他们这里对“不健全”的含义和我们不同，但这对我来说仍然很离谱。我没想到一个只读的 `static` 会随机给出不同的地址。

619859940.en: That also does not track with what the reference says [about `static`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/items/static-items.html#r-items.static.intro). Are you sure that read-only statics emit `unnamed_addr`?

620410726.en:
So now we have both directions ^^
LLVM assumes that it gets to merge `unnamed_addr` globals by telling the linker to do so, but simultaneously will assume that an `unnamed_addr` global living at a certain address is proof about the contents of the memory, even if the load is using a different pointer.
I guess this is what the warning in the LangRef was about?
620410726.zh: 所以现在两个方向都有了 ^^ LLVM 通过告知链接器去合并 `unnamed_addr` 全局变量，假设自己可以合并它们；但与此同时，它又会假设某个地址上的 `unnamed_addr` 全局变量可以证明内存中的内容，即使 load 使用的是另一个指针。我猜这就是 LangRef 中警告所针对的问题？

620413339.en: (or it's incorrect for the linker to merge uninit memory into init memory)
620413339.zh: （或者说，让链接器把未初始化内存与已初始化内存合并本身就是不正确的。）

620592265.en: the linker has no concept of uninit vs init memory
620592265.zh: 链接器没有未初始化内存和已初始化内存的概念。

620592936.en: Sorry, should have phrased it differently (and more precisely): It's incorrect for *LLVM to allow* the linker to merge uninit memory (that has been propagated) with init memory
620592936.zh: 抱歉，我刚才应该换一种更准确的说法：让链接器把（已经传播出去的）未初始化内存与已初始化内存合并，是 *LLVM 允许这样做* 才不正确。

620593238.en: Because that implies that the memory at that address has different content depending on what pointer you read it from, i.e. this is the memory model question
620593238.zh: 因为这意味着同一地址上的内存内容会根据你从哪个指针读取它而有所不同，也就是说，这正是内存模型的问题。

620775259.en:
At a face value I would say we cannot merge them, at least not under the as-if rule. In the opsem, that is, before any optimizations apply, if two pointers have the same address and you perform a load from both, then assuming neither load triggers UB, the two loads must return the same value. So from this you can conclude that the second allocation is also initialized *in the opsem*.

At least that is my understanding of the current opsem models.
620775259.zh:
乍看之下，我会说我们不能合并它们，至少不能依据 as-if 规则合并。在 opsem 中，也就是在任何优化生效之前，如果两个指针的地址相同，并且你分别通过它们执行加载，那么假设这两次加载都不会触发 UB，它们就必须返回相同的值。因此可以得出结论：第二次分配在 *opsem 中* 也已经初始化了。

至少这是我对当前 opsem 模型的理解。

620775501.en: And so merging leads us to conclude that the memory of the second allocation is initialized *in the opsem*. That is, programs assuming the value is initialized will not be UB under the opsem, and so such programs cannot be considered to rely on refinement of an execution with UB in the opsem.
620775501.zh: 因此，合并会让我们得出这样的结论：第二次分配的内存在 *opsem 中* 已经初始化。也就是说，假定该值已初始化的程序在 opsem 下不会产生 UB，所以不能认为这类程序依赖于对 opsem 中带有 UB 的执行进行细化。

620778568.en: I think that just depends on how you define the opsem
620778568.zh: 我认为这完全取决于你如何定义 opsem。

620809586.en: I hope that we don't have an opsem where the value behind a pointer depends on how we got the pointer. I suppose avoiding the issue might not be *that* much more difficult than reasoning about whether or not you're allowed to read from the ptr in the first place, but still it's deeply unintuitive. I don't know how I could possibly teach it besides explaining this optimization.

https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/328

573945032.zh: 我的意思是，这属于未定义行为（UB）。

573945046.en: Since you violated the Frozen/SharedReadOnly tag.

573947026.en: Suppose that, in lcnr's code, `foo` also calls `call_foo` (mutual recursion). It would be possible to have two `foo` calls simultaneously in a single stack in a single thread. With the supposed optimization, it would then be possible to observe two references to two different locals to have the same address, within a single thread.
573947026.zh: 假设在 lcnr 的代码中，`foo` 还会调用 `call_foo`（相互递归）。这样一来，在单个线程的同一个栈中，就可能同时存在两个 `foo` 调用。按照这个假设的优化，随后就可能在单个线程中观察到，指向两个不同局部变量的两个引用具有相同的地址。

573959378.en:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573945046):
```quote
Since you violated the Frozen/SharedReadOnly tag.
```

If there wasn't an immutable shared borrow there, the compiler would have the burden of proving that overlapping the allocations does not cause operations on one to interfere with the other. However, the compiler can ignore, for the purposes of upholding that burden, any operation that would be UB, such as writing through a shared reference to bytes not inside an `UnsafeCell`.
573959378.zh:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573945046)：
```quote
因为你违反了 Frozen/SharedReadOnly 标记。
```

如果那里不存在不可变共享借用，编译器就有责任证明，让这些分配重叠不会导致对其中一个分配执行的操作干扰另一个分配。不过，为了履行这一证明责任，编译器可以忽略任何会导致 UB 的操作，例如通过共享引用向不在 `UnsafeCell` 内的字节写入。
