```quote
I suppose the more correct statement is that `x` and `y` *must* have different addresses *if* `foo` observes such.
```

that's equivalent to saying they must have different addresses. everything is up to observatios in the spec.
574049838.zh:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573938458)：
```quote
我想，更准确的说法是：如果 `foo` 能观察到这一点，那么 `x` 和 `y` *必须*具有不同的地址。
```

这等同于说它们必须具有不同的地址。规范中的一切最终都取决于可观察性。

574050024.en:
@_**lcnr|216206** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573924378):
````quote
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573924244):
```quote
`x` is initialized to a single bit pattern then only reachable through a shared reference. The optimization seems fine and rather indistinguishable from const propagation.
```

my question is: is it valid for the example in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/49206#issuecomment-3902441529 to have the same ptr value in different threads for a type that is not `Sync`
````

FWIW that post got edited -- they dont actually have the same ptr value
574050024.zh:
@_**lcnr|216206** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573924378)：
````quote
@_**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)|120827** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573924244)：
```quote
`x` 被初始化为单一的位模式，之后只能通过共享引用访问。这个优化看起来没问题，而且与常量传播很难区分。
```

我的问题是：对于 https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/49206#issuecomment-3902441529 中的示例，如果某个类型不是 `Sync`，那么让它在不同线程中具有相同的 ptr 值是否有效
````

顺便说一下，那条帖子后来编辑过了——它们实际上并不具有相同的 ptr 值。

574091334.en: Yes, I am asking whether this *would* be a valid optimization right now
574091334.zh: 是的，我想问的是：现在这种优化是否会是有效的。

574091418.en: like, it seems desirable to me that we are allowed to deduplicate immutable allocations this way
574091418.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得允许我们以这种方式对不可变分配进行去重似乎是件好事。

574091617.en: A slight reframing is: are there other reasons outside of "breaks users  who rely on pointers to not `Sync` values not overlapping per thread" why we wouldn't want this optimization?
574091617.zh: 换个说法：除了“会破坏那些依赖于同一线程内指向非 `Sync` 值的指针互不重叠的用户”之外，还有其他不希望采用这种优化的理由吗？

574091741.en: Because I would like to close this type system unsoundness by telling users they are generally not allowed to assume that the compiler wont just deduplicate immutable values
574091741.zh: 因为我希望通过告诉用户，他们通常不能假定编译器不会直接对不可变值进行去重，来修复这个类型系统的不健全性。

574094817.en: I would expect that a local variable is guaranteed to have a distinct address from any other local variable
574094817.zh: 我本来会认为，一个局部变量保证具有不同于其他任何局部变量的地址。

574094883.en: I don't think you can just promote a local variable to a static
574094883.zh: 我不认为你可以直接把一个局部变量提升为静态变量。

574163915.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574049838):
````quote
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573938458):
```quote
I suppose the more correct statement is that `x` and `y` *must* have different addresses *if* `foo` observes such.
```

that's equivalent to saying they must have different addresses. everything is up to observatios in the spec.
````

No, because the current solutions to the memory problem say that maybe observering the address of an allocation is not the same as observing its uniqueness.
574163915.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574049838)：
````quote
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/573938458)：
```quote
我想，更准确的说法是：如果 `foo` 能观察到这一点，那么 `x` 和 `y` *必须*具有不同的地址。
```

这等同于说它们必须具有不同的地址。规范中的一切最终都取决于可观察性。
````

不，因为当前针对内存问题的解决方案认为，观察一个分配的地址可能不等同于观察到它的唯一性。

574164022.en: (At the very least, merely taking a reference/pointer is insufficient to observe uniqueness)
574164022.zh: （至少，仅仅获取一个引用/指针不足以观察到唯一性。）

574184586.en:
@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574094817):
```quote
I would expect that a local variable is guaranteed to have a distinct address from any other local variable
```

yeah, agreed. (if they are live at the same time.) this has nothing to do with `Sync`.
574184586.zh:
@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574094817)：
```quote
我本来会认为，一个局部变量保证具有不同于其他任何局部变量的地址。
```

是的，同意。（如果它们同时处于存活状态。）这与 `Sync` 毫无关系。

574184706.en:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574163915):
```quote
No, because the current solutions to the memory problem say that maybe observering the address of an allocation is not the same as observing its uniqueness.
```

you are referring to https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/328 ? There is no current solution for that, and it is highly confusing to implicitly assume one of the experimental sketches of a model discussed there when talking in a different thread.
574184706.zh:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574163915)：
```quote
不，因为当前针对内存问题的解决方案认为，观察一个分配的地址，可能并不等同于观察它是否具有唯一性。
```

你指的是 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/328 吗？目前并没有针对这个问题的解决方案；而且，在另一个讨论串里发言时，想当然地默认为那里讨论的某个实验性模型草案已经成立，会让人非常困惑。

574185044.en:
@_**lcnr|216206** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574091741):
```quote
Because I would like to close this type system unsoundness by telling users they are generally not allowed to assume that the compiler wont just deduplicate immutable values
```

IOW you are proposing to close the soundness hole by declaring it not-a-soundness-hole by fiat.
that's tempting but also it makes reasoning about correctness of unsafe code another new level of crazy difficult. *someone* has to carry the burden of dealing with this and I am not convinced that it should be "everyone who writes unsafe code that somehow cares about addresses". I literally have no idea how one would build a version of RustBelt that works in the world you are proposing.
574185044.zh:
@_**lcnr|216206** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574091741)：
```quote
因为我想通过告诉用户，他们通常不可以假定编译器不会直接对不可变值进行去重，来解决这个类型系统的不健全性问题。
```

换句话说，你是在提议：通过武断地宣布这不是一个健全性漏洞，来“解决”这个健全性漏洞。

这确实很诱人，但同时也会让推理不安全代码的正确性变得更加疯狂、更加困难。总得有人承担处理这个问题的负担，而我并不确信这个人应该是“所有编写某种程度上依赖地址的不安全代码的人”。我完全不知道要如何构建一个能够在你所提议的世界中工作的 RustBelt 版本。

574185132.en: I'd much rather confine this radioactive mess to consts (where address identity is already... challenged) than extending it to all let-bound variables
574185132.zh: 我宁愿把这摊放射性垃圾限制在 const 中（在那里，地址身份本来就已经……很成问题了），也不想把它扩展到所有通过 let 绑定的变量。

574185626.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574184586):
````quote
@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574094817):
```quote
I would expect that a local variable is guaranteed to have a distinct address from any other local variable
```

yeah, agreed. (if they are live at the same time.) this has nothing to do with `Sync`.
````

I would not expect locals to be different if they are immutable because guaranteeing difference prevents most stack slot deduplication optimizations.
574185626.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574184586)：
````quote
@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574094817)：
```quote
我会认为，一个局部变量的地址一定不同于其他任何局部变量的地址。
```

对，同意。（如果它们在同一时间处于存活状态的话。）这和 `Sync` 毫无关系。
````

如果局部变量是不可变的，我不会认为它们的地址必须不同，因为保证地址不同会阻碍大多数栈槽去重优化。

574185889.en: like the entire process for tail call elimination requires you to be able to partially reuse the stack, no? if taking `&i32` prevents reuse of a local then that seems likely to make things pretty rough on actual benefits from that.
574185889.zh: 比如说，尾调用消除的整个过程都要求你能够部分复用栈空间，对吧？如果获取 `&i32` 会阻止局部变量被复用，那看起来很可能会让这种优化在实际中难以获得什么收益。

574186053.en: What sort of unsafe tricks depend on multiple identical immutable variables not sharing address? It seems extremely niche to me, but then again I have written *that* much unsafe rust yet.
574186053.zh: 有哪些不安全技巧依赖于多个相同的不可变变量不共享地址？在我看来，这似乎极其小众，不过话说回来，我写过的 Rust 不安全代码还没有多到那种程度。

574186123.en: What I'm getting at, is this even something real reasonable code depends on?
574186123.zh: 我的意思是，这真的会是某些合理的实际代码所依赖的东西吗？

574186609.en: I would especially not expect deduplication of consts to be a property unique to them and not also applied to let-bindings.
574186609.zh: 我尤其不认为，对 const 的去重会是 const 独有的属性，而不会同样应用于 let 绑定。

574186796.en:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574185889):
```quote
like the entire process for tail call elimination requires you to be able to partially reuse the stack, no?
```

It's okay for the locals to have the same address if they don't exist at the same time.
574186796.zh:
@_**workingjubilee|281757** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574185889)：
```quote
比如说，尾调用消除的整个过程都要求你能够部分复用栈空间，对吧？
```

如果局部变量不在同一时间存在，那么它们拥有相同的地址也没关系。

574186858.en: @**RalfJ** doesn't requiring let uniqueness, as long as we model temporaries as being equivalent to let bindings, also massively complicate optimizations like common subexpression elimination the moment someone looks sideways at it with `&`?
574186858.zh: @**RalfJ**，只要我们把临时值建模为等同于 let 绑定，要求 let 绑定具有唯一性，难道不会在有人通过 `&` 留意到这一点时，立刻让公共子表达式消除之类的优化变得极其复杂吗？

574186923.en: As someone working on embedded systems, I want rustc to optimise to reduce memory usage as much as possible. Both RAM and code size matter. So again: what sort of unsafe tricks actually depend on this? Because it seems extremely obscure to me to depend on different immutable and identical variables not being merged.
574186923.zh: 作为一名从事嵌入式系统开发的人，我希望 rustc 尽可能优化，以降低内存使用量。RAM 和代码大小都很重要。所以我还是想问：究竟有哪些不安全技巧真的依赖于这一点？因为在我看来，依赖不同的、相同的不可变变量不被合并，实在是太晦涩、太罕见了。

574187131.en: For one, I think whether a binding is marked `mut` is mostly treated along the lines of a lint. Yeah it may be a hard error, but I don't believe miri considers it UB to write to it.
574187131.zh: 首先，我认为绑定是否标记为 `mut`，在很大程度上只是按 lint 的方式处理的。没错，它可能会导致硬错误，但我不认为 Miri 会把向其中写入视为 UB。

574187257.en: for instance drop gets a mut ref to it
574187257.zh: 例如，drop 会获得指向它的可变引用。

574187487.en: That *is* a fair point actually for stack locals. But presumably this optimisation can only be done if we know the variable isn't written to anyway. So given that we know the variable isn't written to, but adress might be taken, what sort of in-the-wild unsafe tricks would get broken?
574187487.zh: 对于栈上的局部变量来说，这确实是个合理的观点。不过，想必只有在我们知道变量不会被写入的情况下，才能进行这种优化。所以，既然我们知道变量不会被写入，但可能会获取它的地址，那么现实世界中究竟有哪些不安全技巧会因此被破坏？

574189565.en: Idea is that you can create an `Owner` on the stack, and you can lock it multiple times by passing the same owner.
574189565.zh: 这个想法是，你可以在栈上创建一个 `Owner`，然后通过传入同一个 owner 多次对它加锁。

574189618.en: Since `Owner: !Sync`, reentrant locks are all on the same thread.
574189618.zh: 由于 `Owner: !Sync`，可重入锁操作都会发生在同一个线程上。

574190280.en: And this is relying on locals on different threads having unique addresses, yes?
574190280.zh: 而这依赖于不同线程上的局部变量拥有唯一地址，对吧？

574191242.en: I think that guaranteeing such may much more deeply complicate compiler targets which expect that disjoint threads can share more data than that, moving them from having odd edge-cases in their conformance to a nigh-impossibility in their support.
574191242.zh: 我认为，做出这样的保证，可能会让那些原本预期不相交的线程能够共享更多数据的编译器目标变得复杂得多，使它们从一致性上存在一些古怪的边界情况，变成几乎不可能支持。

574192961.en: Is that talking about things like GPU targets?
574192961.zh: 这是在说 GPU 之类的目标吗？

574193170.en: Here is an idea: why not an attribute on the type to control if instances can be merged? (You could bikeshed about opt in/out or attribute vs phantom member etc. That is not really what I want to discuss at this point though.) It seems to me having this under programmer control for the rare occasions where it does matter would be good.
574193170.zh: 我有个想法：为什么不在类型上加一个属性，用来控制实例是否可以合并？（你可以争论到底应该选择加入还是选择退出，或者用属性还是幻影成员之类的。这些并不是我现在真正想讨论的重点。）在少数确实有影响的场合，让程序员能够控制这一点，在我看来似乎是件好事。

574193370.en:
@_**Vorpal|743310** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574192961):
```quote
Is that talking about things like GPU targets?
```

yes.
574193370.zh: @_**Vorpal|743310** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574192961)：```quote 这是在说 GPU 之类的目标吗？``` 是的。

574193643.en: *Generally* I would like more developer control over low level things like merging of variables, linker attributes (ELF visibility for example), and other codegen details. That is one thing that feel restrictive in current stable Rust.
574193643.zh: 总的来说，我希望开发者能够更多地控制变量合并、链接器属性（例如 ELF 可见性）以及其他代码生成细节之类的底层机制。这是当前稳定版 Rust 让人感觉受限的地方之一。

574194381.en: Ah seems recent, the tracking issue was only opened last month. I last lamented the lack of it half a year ago probably. Nice to see things are happening there, even if the implementation isn't yet merged (let alone stable).
574194381.zh: 啊，看来这是最近才有的，跟踪 issue 也是上个月才开的。我大概在半年前还在抱怨缺少这个功能。看到这方面终于有进展真不错，尽管实现还没有合并（更不用说稳定化了）。

574236572.en:
@_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574189565):
```quote
Idea is that you can create an `Owner` on the stack, and you can lock it multiple times by passing the same owner.
```

Incidentally this is also affected by the OP issue: if you make `Owner::new()` const, `&Owner::new()` may get the same address on different threads no?
574236572.zh: @_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574189565)：```quote 这个想法是，你可以在栈上创建一个 `Owner`，然后通过传入同一个 owner 多次对它加锁。``` 顺带一提，这也会受到 OP 所提问题的影响：如果你把 `Owner::new()` 设为 const，那么不同线程中的 `&Owner::new()` 可能会得到同一个地址，对吧？

574236734.en: Yeah, so you probably should not do that.
574236734.zh: 是的，所以你可能不该这么做。

574240830.en: That seems fragile. Having an explicit attribute on the type to opt out of merging seems way simpler to understand as an unsafe author. Is there any reason such a design isn't being considered here?
574240830.zh: 这看起来很脆弱。对于编写 unsafe 代码的人来说，在类型上显式添加一个属性来选择不进行合并，似乎要容易理解得多。有什么理由不考虑这种设计吗？

574242024.en: It seems to me that `!Sync` serves that purpose well
574242024.zh: 在我看来，`!Sync` 已经很好地起到了这个作用。

574242085.en: You should not be able to put it into a static (or anything that is static promoted)
574242085.zh: 你不应该能够把它放进 static（或任何会被提升为 static 的东西）中。

574248416.en: Doesn't this overload what Sync does? Are there use cases for Sync types that don't get merged as well? (Or !Sync types that *do* get merged)
574248416.zh: 这不是把 Sync 的职责扩大了吗？有没有需要使用 Sync 类型、但又不希望它们被合并的场景？（或者有没有希望被合并的 !Sync 类型？）

574250187.en: Merging a !Sync type is never okay
574250187.zh: 合并 !Sync 类型永远都不行。

574250359.en: As for whether there are cases where merging Sync types is wrong, well maybe you can come up with something if you use sentinels that exist only for their address in some other manner.
574250359.zh: 至于合并 Sync 类型是否也有错误的情况嘛，如果你通过其他方式使用只为自身地址而存在的哨兵，也许可以想出某种情况。

574275026.en: I'd also find it surprising if Sync/!Sync affects opsem though.
574275026.zh: 如果 Sync/!Sync 会影响 opsem，我也会觉得很意外。

574277606.en: It doesn't have to affect opsem if you outlaw merging locals.
574277606.zh: 如果禁止合并局部变量，就不必让它影响 opsem。

574283633.en: Yes, sure, but then we lose all those optimisations altogether. @**Vorpal** (and several others) is (are) arguing for having the optimisations.
574283633.zh: 是的，当然可以，但这样一来我们就会彻底失去所有这些优化。@**Vorpal**（以及其他几个人）主张保留这些优化。

574329230.en: How about requiring `ReentrantMutex` to use `UnsafeCell` for the `_not_zst` field? I.e. we would only guarantee unique stack slots for !Freeze. That does allow all the optimisations we want (including supporting GPU targets I guess?). Too much of a footgun?
574329230.zh: 要求 `ReentrantMutex` 在 `_not_zst` 字段中使用 `UnsafeCell`，怎么样？也就是说，我们只对 !Freeze 保证唯一的栈槽位。这样确实可以实现我们想要的所有优化（包括支持 GPU 目标，我猜？）。但这会不会太容易踩坑？

574349836.en:
1. Could LLVM still optimize that if it cold determine the Unsafe Cell was being written to?
2. All of this trying to tie this into existing constructs that are only marginally related seems like footguns to me, in that it makes it hard to discover. It doesn't feel like a clean design, it feels like magic (and not in a good way).
574349836.zh: 1. 如果 LLVM 能确定 Unsafe Cell 会被写入，它仍然可以对其进行优化吗？ 2. 试图把这一切和现有的、关联性很有限的构造绑定起来，在我看来都像是在埋雷，因为这会让人很难发现其中的规则。这感觉不像是一个简洁的设计，更像是魔法（而且不是好的那种）。

574370436.en: this isnt about losing optimizations, it's about *adding* new "optimizations" that fly in the face of basically everything that has been discussed or modeled regarding local variables so far. the optimization would also be unique to Rust I think.
574370436.zh: 这不是在讨论会失去优化，而是在讨论要新增一些与迄今为止关于局部变量的几乎所有讨论或建模都相悖的“优化”。我觉得这种优化可能还是 Rust 独有的。

574370529.en: stack variables are just like heap allocations except they are more efficient to free because they follow a strict discipline
574370529.zh: 栈变量就像堆分配，只不过由于遵循严格的规约，释放起来更高效。

574370577.en: it would be very strange to merge two calls to `malloc`; the same goes for merging two local variables
574370577.zh: 合并两个对 `malloc` 的调用会非常奇怪；合并两个局部变量也是一样。

574370811.en: consts are *values* that inherently dont have an address; playing creative tricks with address identity for them is tricky and we dont now yet how unsafe code could be written to be resilient against this, but it doesnt come entirely out of nowhere
574370811.zh: const 是本质上没有地址的*值*；对它们的地址身份耍一些创造性的花招很棘手，而且我们现在还不知道不安全代码要如何编写，才能抵御这种情况，但这也并非完全没有来由。

574370863.en: but local variables are *places*, and there we really have no business doing anything funny
574370863.zh: 但局部变量是*内存位置*，在这方面我们确实没有理由做任何奇怪的事情。

574370888.en: for statics, we even already enshrined this in the Reference
574370888.zh: 至于 static，我们甚至已经在 Reference 中明确规定了这一点。

574393683.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574370577):
```quote
it would be very strange to merge two calls to `malloc`; the same goes for merging two local variables
```

The compiler is allowed to optimise away a malloc entirely, I would expect it should be allowed to merge two mallocs that are allocated and freed together as well.
574393683.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574370577)：
```quote
合并两个对 `malloc` 的调用会非常奇怪；合并两个局部变量也是一样。
```

编译器可以将一次 `malloc` 完全优化掉，我认为它也应该可以合并两个同时分配、同时释放的 `malloc`。

574399961.en: Also, merging together locals is needed for tailcall optimization to be legal.
574399961.zh: 此外，为了让尾调用优化合法，合并局部变量也是必要的。

574403540.en: TCO only merges locals at their liveness boundaries
574403540.zh: 尾调用优化只会在局部变量的活跃性边界处合并它们。

574445852.en:
@_**Vorpal|743310** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574393683):
````quote
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574370577):
```quote
it would be very strange to merge two calls to `malloc`; the same goes for merging two local variables
```

The compiler is allowed to optimise away a malloc entirely, I would expect it should be allowed to merge two mallocs that are allocated and freed together as well.
````

those are very different things, so I dont see how you jumped from a to b.
also, the compiler is *not* allowed to optimize away malloc if that changes what the program sees/observes.
574445852.zh:
@_**Vorpal|743310** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574393683)：
````quote
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574370577)：
```quote
合并两个对 `malloc` 的调用会非常奇怪；合并两个局部变量也是一样。
```

编译器可以将一次 `malloc` 完全优化掉，我认为它也应该可以合并两个同时分配、同时释放的 `malloc`。
````

这两件事非常不同，所以我不明白你是怎么从 A 跳到 B 的。
而且，如果这样会改变程序所看到或观察到的结果，编译器*不*允许把 `malloc` 优化掉。

574446007.en:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574399961):
```quote
Also, merging together locals is needed for tailcall optimization to be legal.
```

tailcall optimizations is illegal if locals are live until after the fn call. merging locals with disjoint liveness ranges is entirely fine as has already been said above. we are entirely talking about the case of locals with overlapping liveness here, so tail calls are not relevant.
574446007.zh:
@_**Connor Horman|257758** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/.60Sync.60.20and.20deduplicating.20immutable.20allocations/near/574399961)：
```quote
此外，为了让尾调用优化合法，合并局部变量也是必要的。
```

如果局部变量一直活跃到 `fn` 调用之后，尾调用优化就是不合法的。正如上面已经说过的那样，合并活跃性区间互不相交的局部变量完全没问题。我们现在讨论的完全是活跃性重叠的局部变量，因此尾调用与此无关。

574457378.en: I'd say it's not really about whether such optimisation is "old" or "new" or exists in C, but whether the trade-off between UB and performance benefit is worth it.
574457378.zh: 我认为，这真正要讨论的并不是这种优化是“旧的”还是“新的”，或者它是否存在于 C 中，而是 UB 与性能收益之间的权衡是否值得。

574467163.en: true, I just want to oppose the framing about "losing" anything. you cant lose what you never had ;)
574467163.zh: 没错，我只是想反对“失去”任何东西这种说法。你不可能失去从未拥有过的东西 ;)

574467373.en: also this is less about UB and more about extra non-determinism (that can of course lead to UB later). in a sense that's worse since it means even with miri you are unlikely to find such problems.
574467373.zh: 此外，这与其说是 UB，不如说是额外的非确定性（当然之后可能导致 UB）。从某种意义上说，这更糟，因为这意味着即使使用 miri，也不太可能发现这类问题。

574555474.en: Having an attribute/phantom-member to opt in/out of this seems like a good idea then. There are cases where people want this and cases where people don't want it. If there are good arguments for both sides why not allow the developer the freedom to choose?
574555474.zh: 那么，提供一个属性/幽灵成员来选择启用或禁用这种行为，似乎是个好主意。有些情况下人们希望这样做，也有些情况下人们不希望这样做。如果双方都有充分的理由，为什么不把选择的自由交给开发者呢？

574582258.zh: 你可以用 `&const { ... }` 来选择启用。

574598185.en:
That is per call site though. While optimisations like this would be great to apply everywhere possible. Inlining, macros etc often cause duplicate code. And turn things that weren't const before into things that could be const in the inlined context.

So that doesn't feel like a satisfactory answer. I would postulate that opting out is much rarer than places that could opt in.
574598185.zh:
但那是针对每个调用点的。而像这样的优化，如果可能的话，应该能在任何地方应用。内联、宏等经常会导致代码重复，还会把原本不是 const 的东西变成在内联上下文中可以成为 const 的东西。

所以这感觉不是一个令人满意的答案。我认为，需要选择禁用的地方要比可以选择启用的地方少得多。

620100066.en:
Sorry for the long radio silence on this.

I originally intended to respond by proposing an alterative design that unifies the issues addressed in that PR with issues addressed in a number of other proposals. That alternative design is [here](https://gist.github.com/joshlf/2dbca0d5d025cfd0d40424ed3e50e0ed).

After very helpful feedback from @**Crystal Durham** and @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** during the last t-opsem meeting, I realized that I was biting off more than I could chew on my own.

I just finished a [draft proposal](https://gist.github.com/joshlf/8f6751869cd17fd4a0b5695877b05e21) that argues that we need *some* unified model for reasoning about questions of layout, ABI, etc. In particular, I argue that reasoning about these questions piecemeal continues to paint us further into design corners that we then have to make breaking changes to escape. I think we should do at least some thinking about a unified model before we make any more commitments in this space.

My plan is to post a comment to the same effect on that PR, but I first wanted to socialize this in a smaller group before I drop what is admittedly a grenade into the discussion.

(In terms of the PR itself, I am aware of a very minor risk of future incompatibility, which I'll raise. But more to the point, I argue in the proposal that we should be skeptical of our own ability to evaluate these things without a unified model, so I think we should move more carefully until we have such a model. "I can't think of any problems" has historically not been a good predictor of there not being problems.)
620100066.zh:
抱歉，这件事沉默了这么久。

我原本打算提出一个替代设计，将该 PR 所处理的问题与其他若干提案所处理的问题统一起来。这个替代设计见[这里](https://gist.github.com/joshlf/2dbca0d5d025cfd0d40424ed3e50e0ed)。

在上次 t-opsem 会议期间，@**Crystal Durham** 和 @**Ben Kimock (Saethlin)** 提供了非常有帮助的反馈。之后我意识到，单靠自己啃下这么大的问题，实在超出了我的能力范围。

我刚完成了一份[提案草案](https://gist.github.com/joshlf/8f6751869cd17fd4a0b5695877b05e21)，主张我们需要某种统一模型，用来推理布局、ABI 等问题。具体来说，我认为，继续将这些问题拆开来分别处理，只会让我们进一步陷入设计死角，最终不得不通过破坏性变更才能脱身。我认为，在这个领域做出更多承诺之前，我们至少应该先对统一模型进行一定程度的思考。

我的计划是在那个 PR 下发表一条类似内容的评论，但在把一个不可否认会像手榴弹一样砸进讨论区的东西扔出去之前，我想先在一个较小的群体中讨论一下。

（就 PR 本身而言，我知道存在一个非常轻微的未来不兼容风险，我会提出这一点。但更重要的是，我在提案中主张，如果没有统一模型，我们应该对自己评估这些问题的能力保持怀疑。因此，在有这样一个模型之前，我认为我们应该更加谨慎地推进。“我想不出有什么问题”历来都不是“确实不存在问题”的可靠预测指标。）

620108648.en:
I'm trying to thread a tricky needle here, and I don't claim to have the optimal approach:
- I don't want to try to stall everything (the perfect being the enemy of the good)
- I *do* want to get everyone involved in these discussions to start thinking of a unified model as something worth considering

I agree that Rust has historically handled these things incrementally. In some domains, that approach has been successful. However, IMO when it comes to layout, ABI, and other compatibility-with-the-external-world questions, that approach has frequently painted us into corners or resulted in implementations or feature designs which are just *wrong* wrt the external reality.
620108648.zh: 我正在努力在一个棘手的问题上取得平衡，但我不敢说这是最优方案：- 我不想试图拖住所有事情（不能让完美成为优秀的敌人）；- 但我确实希望参与这些讨论的每个人都开始把统一模型视为值得考虑的东西。我同意，Rust 历来都是渐进式地处理这些问题。在某些领域，这种方式确实取得了成功。然而，在我看来，涉及布局、ABI 以及其他与外部世界的兼容性问题时，这种方式经常让我们陷入设计死角，或者导致实现和特性设计与外部现实完全不符。


I do think this is very related in that I think we should also shift opsem/lang towards treating FFI / C interop as a matter of having an explicit mapping from some types and function signatures to C equivalents, and accepting that this sometimes means we don't have such neat, portable answers for memory layout and calling convention of those types as people thought we could have in the early days of Rust.

620116319.en:
In this case, the verbosity was intentional, although maybe a mistake. I tried to structure the post as “brief argument” (Part I) followed by “exhaustive argument” (Part II) that goes through every instance of incompatibility. The exhaustive coverage was meant to demonstrate that the problem is real and persistent, not just the exception that proves the rule.

There are also a number of subtleties that I felt needed to be covered, and I wasn’t sure how to keep them concise, e.g.:
- Arguing that we need to consider forwards-evolvavility (to avoid issues present in some current proposals, which propose to change the semantics of things like `repr(C)`, which risks making unsafe code silently unsound)
- Explaining what a “unified model” might mean, since I explicitly *don’t* want to prescribe that it has to be reified as a model in rustc
- Forecasting future issues like multiple address spaces
620116319.zh:
这次的冗长是有意为之的，不过也许确实是个错误。我试图把帖子组织成“简要论证”（第一部分），后面接“完整论证”（第二部分），逐一讨论每个不兼容实例。之所以要做到如此全面，是想证明这个问题确实存在且持续存在，而不只是某个能够证明规则的例外。

另外，还有一些我认为需要涵盖的细节，而我不确定该如何把它们说得简洁，例如：
- 论证我们需要考虑前向演进能力（以避免一些当前提案中存在的问题；这些提案建议改变 `repr(C)` 等事物的语义，可能会导致不安全代码在不知不觉间变得不 sound）
- 解释“统一模型”可能意味着什么，因为我明确*不*想规定它必须在 rustc 中具体化为一个模型
- 预测未来可能出现的问题，例如多个地址空间

620116361.en: If somebody feels like there’s a more concise presentation that captures all of the subtleties in the current post, I’m very open to that. I definitely don’t like how long the post currently is.
620116361.zh: 如果有人觉得可以用更简洁的方式呈现当前帖子中的所有细节，我非常愿意听取建议。我确实不喜欢帖子现在这么长。

620116708.en: One of the problems I've found with editing LLM generated text is that unless you have background/experience with editing (in particular, knowing when and what to cut, and having the ability to be, well, ruthless about it), it's pretty difficult to do those kind of revisions (most of the time when evaluating technical documentation you evaluate on a different merit, which is just 'does this contain information' and 'is this worded acceptably', which will often be true for LLM text). So, I sympathize with the difficulty here, but I don't think it's reasonable to place the burden for that onto others.

619459339.en: AFAIK in LLVM they both compile to the same ABI, one just has a `nounwind` annotation. that can't be ABI-affecting, can it?
619459339.zh: 据我所知，在 LLVM 中它们最终都会编译成相同的 ABI，只是其中一个带有 `nounwind` 注解。这个不可能影响 ABI，对吧？

619462858.en: I believe that LLVM has incomplete documentation about what function attributes are ABI affecting, but it does say that a mismatch in ABI affecting attributes is undefined.
619462858.zh: 我认为 LLVM 关于哪些函数属性会影响 ABI 的文档并不完整，但它确实说明了：影响 ABI 的属性不匹配会导致未定义行为。

619463477.en: Intuitively this feels like it should be fine, but I don't know if LLVM agrees.
619463477.zh: 直觉上，这应该没问题，但我不知道 LLVM 是否也这么认为。

619498372.en: I fully expect that that's fine, since after all that's exactly what happens when you call C code from C++ code or C++ code from C code -- the `nounwind` attributes don't match since usually all the C code isn't built with exceptions support, but the C++ code usually is. The only problem you should run into is if your function actually unwinds but the compiler thinks it shouldn't be able to since you converted it to a nounwind function pointer.
619498372.zh: 我完全认为这样应该没问题，毕竟这正是从 C++ 代码调用 C 代码，或从 C 代码调用 C++ 代码时发生的情况——两者的 `nounwind` 属性并不匹配，因为通常 C 代码都不是在启用异常支持的情况下构建的，而 C++ 代码通常是。唯一可能遇到的问题是：如果你的函数确实发生了展开，但由于你把它转换成了一个 nounwind 函数指针，编译器认为它不可能发生展开。

614354140.en:
Closures (and coroutines) currently behave almost like normal ADTs. in particular, if they have fields of reference type, those get retagged as the closure / coroutine is moved around. This can cause gnarly surprises since the retags are quite hard to identify, even compared to regular retags that are already entierly hidden from surface Rust.
So I wonder, should we maybe say that these types are effectively implicitly wrapped in a `MaybeDangling`? In other words, the references captures by closures / coroutines are just forwarded entirely unchanged if the closure / coroutine itself is moved around.

(Reminder that MaybeDangling is a bad name as one major usecase is "wont actually dangle but I want to suppress retagging".)
614354140.zh:
闭包（以及协程）目前的行为几乎和普通 ADT 一样。尤其是，如果它们有引用类型的字段，那么在闭包/协程被移动时，这些字段就会被重新标记。这可能会带来非常棘手的意外，因为这些重新标记很难被发现；即使是普通的重新标记，也已经完全隐藏在表层 Rust 代码之外了。

所以我在想，我们是不是应该说这些类型实际上会被隐式包裹在 `MaybeDangling` 中？换句话说，如果闭包/协程本身被移动，那么其中捕获的引用就会完全原样地传递，不做任何修改。

（提醒一下，MaybeDangling 这个名字并不好，因为它的一个主要用例是“实际上并不会悬空，但我想抑制重新标记”。）

614354268.en: now that MaybeDangling is implemented this should be fairly easy to do, by generalizing the checks for MaybeDangling in Miri and codegen to also trigger on closures and coroutines.
614354268.zh: 既然 MaybeDangling 已经实现了，那么这样做应该相当容易：只要把 Miri 和代码生成器中针对 MaybeDangling 的检查泛化一下，让它们在遇到闭包和协程时也触发即可。

618186989.en: Why extend ABI compatibility at all at this point? I feel like the `fn_cast!` idea is just plain better than ABI compatibility, especially the variant that abstracts over actual ABI differences and allows all mismatches that can be transmuted. And once (/if) that’s implemented and stabilized, ABI compatibility seems like a weird legacy thing we can freeze in time and otherwise ignore.
618186989.zh: 事到如今，为什么还要继续扩展 ABI 兼容性？我觉得 `fn_cast!` 的想法明显比 ABI 兼容性更好，尤其是那种能够对实际的 ABI 差异进行抽象，并允许所有可以通过转置（transmute）实现的类型不匹配的方案。而且一旦（如果）它实现并稳定下来，ABI 兼容性就像是一种奇怪的遗留机制：我们可以把它冻结在当前状态，其他方面不再理会。

618187771.en: It makes sense to for example be allowed to define a type that C will call as `extern "C" fn(&mut T)` if it has the invariant that it will always be called with an exclusively owned pointer to reduce the amount of useless boilerplate in the body and to allow defining it as safe function. Without ABI compatibility between `&mut T` and `*mut T`this wouldn't be possible. `fn_cast!` doesn't help with that as there is no place to insert it for `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`.
618187771.zh: 比如说，如果某个类型有这样一个不变量：它总是会接收到一个独占拥有的指针，那么允许将其定义为 C 会调用的 `extern "C" fn(&mut T)` 就是合理的。这样既能减少函数体中无用的样板代码，也能将其定义为安全函数。如果 `&mut T` 和 `*mut T` 之间没有 ABI 兼容性，这就无法实现。`fn_cast!` 也帮不上忙，因为对于 `#[unsafe(no_mangle)]`，没有可以插入它的位置。

618187859.en: that's FFI ABI compat, I am talking only about Rust-to-Rust ABI compat here
618187859.zh: 那是 FFI ABI 兼容性，我这里只谈 Rust 到 Rust 的 ABI 兼容性。

618187898.en: we currently document absolutely nothing about FFI ABI compatibility as the few people that know the details dont have the time to write anything down :/

618188253.en:
@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618186989):
```quote
Why extend ABI compatibility at all at this point? I feel like the `fn_cast!` idea is just plain better than ABI compatibility, especially the variant that abstracts over actual ABI differences and allows all mismatches that can be transmuted. And once (/if) that’s implemented and stabilized, ABI compatibility seems like a weird legacy thing we can freeze in time and otherwise ignore.
```

As I understood fn_cast in the CFI context (but this might have been an earlier draft, I have not checked in recent months) it would generate a shim. For normal non-CFI environments it would instead be a straight pointer cast without overhead (and rely on ABI compatibility).

I assume you don't want the overhead for shims everywhere, in which case the question of ABI compatibility is still highly relevant.
618188253.zh:
@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618186989)：
```quote
为什么事到如今还要继续扩展 ABI 兼容性？我觉得 `fn_cast!` 的想法明显比 ABI 兼容性更好，尤其是那种能够对实际的 ABI 差异进行抽象，并允许所有可以通过转置（transmute）实现的类型不匹配的方案。而且一旦（如果）它实现并稳定下来，ABI 兼容性就像是一种奇怪的遗留机制：我们可以把它冻结在当前状态，其他方面不再理会。
```

据我对 CFI 上下文中的 fn_cast 的理解（不过这可能是更早的草案，我最近几个月没确认过），它会生成一个垫片函数。在普通的非 CFI 环境中，它则会直接进行指针转换，不产生额外开销（并依赖 ABI 兼容性）。

我猜你不会希望到处都为垫片函数付出开销；如果确实如此，那么 ABI 兼容性的问题仍然非常重要。

618188337.en: with the macro the question of ABI compatibility becomes a compiler implementation detail
618188337.zh: 有了这个宏，ABI 兼容性的问题就变成了编译器的实现细节。

618188356.en: we can generate more/fewer shims as we make more/fewer things ABI compatible
618188356.zh: 随着我们让更多或更少的东西具备 ABI 兼容性，我们也可以生成更多或更少的垫片函数。

618189379.en: Yes, by moving the decision whether a shim is needed into the compiler/optimizer, we can omit shims that aren't necessary in reality but would be necessary if you only relied on what is stably guaranteed. That covers both compiler implementation details which aren't (yet / ever) stable guarantees, and also internals of user-defined types.
618189379.zh: 是的，通过将是否需要垫片函数的决定交给编译器或优化器，我们可以省略那些实际上并不需要、但如果只能依赖稳定保证就必须存在的垫片函数。这既涵盖了尚未（或永远不会）成为稳定保证的编译器实现细节，也涵盖了用户自定义类型的内部实现。

618189508.en: I really wish someone would work on that macro :D
618189508.zh: 我真希望有人能着手实现那个宏 :D

618189512.en: (But also, I'd expect that just emitting transmute-based shims for everything would be fine in practice, if the transmutes are no-ops then LLVM *should* be able to merge the functions after some cleanup.)
618189512.zh: （不过话说回来，我觉得实践中直接为所有情况生成基于转置的垫片函数应该也没问题；如果这些转置操作实际上都是空操作，那么 LLVM *应该* 能在经过一些清理后将这些函数合并起来。）

618190840.en: The idea is that fn_cast would only generate a shim if one is needed.
618190840.zh: fn_cast 的设计理念是：只有在确实需要时才生成垫片函数。

618198341.en:
The original RFC specified that the ABI should be the same https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2195-really-tagged-unions.md#guide-level-explanation.

> An enum can currently be adorned with `#[repr(Int)]` where `Int` is one of Rust's integer types (u8, isize, etc). For C-like enums -- enums which have no variants with associated data -- this specifies that the enum should have the ABI of that integer type (size, alignment, and calling convention).

I'd have expected that to be true. That said, I don't actually know of non-FFI use cases that would care. There are plenty of FFI use cases which would, though.
618198341.zh:
最初的 RFC 规定 ABI 应该相同 https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/blob/master/text/2195-really-tagged-unions.md#guide-level-explanation。

> 目前，可以使用 `#[repr(Int)]` 修饰枚举，其中 `Int` 是 Rust 的某种整数类型（u8、isize 等）。对于类 C 枚举——也就是没有带关联数据的变体的枚举——这表示该枚举应当采用对应整数类型的 ABI（大小、对齐方式和调用约定）。

我原本以为确实应该如此。话虽如此，我确实不知道有哪些非 FFI 的使用场景会在意这一点。不过，会在意这一点的 FFI 使用场景倒是很多。

618198628.en: for FFI, if we want to be CFI-compatible, we apparently have to declare it Erroneous Behavior to make a call where one side uses the enum and the other side uses the integer
618198628.zh: 对于 FFI，如果我们希望与 CFI 兼容，那么显然必须将一边使用枚举、另一边使用整数进行调用的行为声明为错误行为（Erroneous Behavior）。

618199485.en: That seems very unfortunate, as bjorn3 pointed out above. For that EB to be viable, there needs to be something like fn_cast but for *exposing* FFI functions
618199485.zh: 正如 bjorn3 上面指出的那样，这看起来非常不理想。要让这种错误行为可行，就需要某种类似 fn_cast 的机制，但它是用于*暴露* FFI 函数的。

618200085.en: I dont think I agree. We will anyway guarantee that we won't "act" on that EB by default, one has to opt-in to having it enforced, e.g. by using CFI.
618200085.zh: 我不认为我同意这一点。无论如何，我们都会保证默认情况下不会“执行”该错误行为；必须显式选择启用强制执行，例如使用 CFI。

618200164.en: tbh I think for the cases where Rust accepts an integer coming from the other side of FFI, using fieldless repr(Int) enums is a bad idea -- more convenient to consume form the Rust side, but causes instant UB when the other side messes up, or the Rust side messes up its enum definition, with no way to detect it
618200164.zh: 老实说，我觉得对于 Rust 接受来自 FFI 另一端的整数这一类情况，使用无字段的 `repr(Int)` 枚举不是个好主意——从 Rust 侧使用起来确实更方便，但一旦另一端出错，或者 Rust 侧错误地定义了枚举，就会立即产生未定义行为，而且没有任何办法检测出来。

618200169.en: does C guarantee that enums are ABI-compatible with their "inner" integer type? I dont think so. So it's fine to declare code that mixes enums and ints as buggy. After all CFI has done this for >10 years.
618200169.zh: C 是否保证枚举与其“内部”整数类型在 ABI 上兼容？我不这么认为。所以，把混用枚举和整数的代码认定为有 bug 是合理的。毕竟 CFI 已经这样做了 10 多年。

618200296.en: It's very common to use Rust enums in FFI (bindgen `rustified_enum` option), and has been for a long time. In the case where the C code isn't fully controlled and the C provides the enum, it is an antipattern, but for cases where it's an input *to* C, or the library is fully controlled, I think it's entirely fine.
618200296.zh: 在 FFI 中使用 Rust 枚举（bindgen 的 `rustified_enum` 选项）非常常见，而且已经这样做很长时间了。如果 C 代码并非完全受控，且枚举由 C 提供，那么这是一种反模式；但对于枚举作为传给 C 的输入，或者库完全由自己控制的情况，我认为这样做完全没问题。

618200686.en: Is there any actual benefit in the input-to-C-only case? If you're just passing values to C, you can just pass non-enum constants instead of enum variants, right? Even if you want an `enum` for your own internal bookkeeping, is there any drawback to just casting explicitly when you call into C?
618200686.zh: 只在“作为传给 C 的输入”的情况下，这样做真的有什么实际好处吗？如果你只是把值传给 C，直接传递非枚举常量而不是枚举变体不就行了吗？即使你想用 `enum` 做内部记录，在调用 C 时显式转换一下，难道有什么缺点吗？

618200698.en:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618200169):
```quote
does C guarantee that enums are ABI-compatible with their "inner" integer type? I dont think so. So it's fine to declare code that mixes enums and ints as buggy. After all CFI has done this for >10 years.
```

In C23 it seems that they are (at least, they're compatible types, which is as close to ABI as the C standard gets):

> The enumerated type is compatible with the underlying type of the enumeration. After possible lvalue conversion a value of the enumerated type behaves the same as the value with the underlying type, in particularly with all aspects of promotion, conversion, and arithmetic.
618200698.zh:
@_**RalfJ|120791** [说过](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618200169)：

```quote
C 是否保证枚举与其“内部”整数类型在 ABI 上兼容？我不这么认为。所以，把混用枚举和整数的代码认定为有 bug 是合理的。毕竟 CFI 已经这样做了 10 多年。
```

在 C23 中，似乎它们是兼容的（至少它们是兼容类型，而这已经是 C 标准能够达到的、最接近 ABI 的表述了）：

> 枚举类型与该枚举的底层类型兼容。经过可能的左值转换后，枚举类型的值与底层类型的值表现相同，尤其是在提升、转换和算术运算的所有方面。

618201107.en: it's the term used for defining when type A can be assigned into a place of type B
618201107.zh: 它是用来定义类型 A 何时可以赋值给类型 B 的存储位置的术语。

618201132.en:
Elsewhere it says:

> All declarations that refer to the same object or function shall have compatible type; otherwise, the behavior is undefined.
618201132.zh:
其他地方还写道：

> 所有引用同一对象或函数的声明都必须具有兼容类型；否则，行为就是未定义的。

618201137.en: No, compatibility is stronger than allowing assignment.
618201137.zh: 不，兼容性比允许赋值更严格。

618201499.en: either way, their notion of "compatible" is non-transitive
618201499.zh: 无论如何，他们对“兼容”的理解都不具有传递性

618201508.en: so it's not really suited as a definition of ABI compatibility
618201508.zh: 所以它并不适合作为 ABI 兼容性的定义

618201522.en: There's no direct mention of ABI in C standards.
618201522.zh: C 标准中没有直接提到 ABI。

618201543.en: I don't think it needs to be transitive for this to hold either.
618201543.zh: 我也不认为要满足这一点就必须具备传递性。

618201579.en: In general, outside of backwards compatibility / churn concerns, I think it would have been better and simpler if Rust was very restrictive about ABI compatibility in the calling convention sense, to the point that there's essentially only one "correct" equivalent of any C type and function signature. Any instance of using using other types on the Rust side than the raw C equivalent would require some explicit opt-in (like `fn_cast!`) for allowing that one function to be called with a specific different signature. That would avoid placing any restrictions on CFI and Miri for finding type confusion bugs, while still allowing *explicit* mapping from C types to richer Rust types when intended and helpful.
618201579.zh: 一般来说，抛开向后兼容性和代码变动方面的顾虑不谈，我认为 Rust 如果在调用约定意义上的 ABI 兼容性方面采取非常严格的限制，反而会更好、更简单——严格到基本上每种 C 类型和函数签名都只有一个“正确”的等价形式。任何在 Rust 侧使用不同于 C 中原始对应类型的类型的情况，都需要显式选择加入（例如使用 `fn_cast!`），以允许某个函数以特定的不同签名被调用。这样既不会限制 CFI 和 Miri 查找类型混淆漏洞，同时也仍然允许在有意为之且确有帮助时，将 C 类型显式映射为更丰富的 Rust 类型。

618201645.en: And I say this as one of the people who originally implemented `repr(transparent)`!
618201645.zh: 我这么说，是因为我正是最初实现 `repr(transparent)` 的人之一！

618201674.en: I think it's useful to be allowed to pass rust enums to FFI functions for the same reason `safe` FFI functions are possible to write.
618201674.zh: 我认为，允许将 Rust 枚举传给 FFI 函数是有用的，理由和可以编写 `safe` FFI 函数一样。

618201851.en: I think it's very unintuitive if we decide that the right way to do this is to tell people to use `fn_cast!` for this. Especially when there's so much code in the wild that does it (which people might see and assume is fine).
618201851.zh: 如果我们决定正确的做法是告诉大家为此使用 `fn_cast!`，我会觉得这非常不直观。尤其是现实世界中已经有大量这样的代码（人们可能会看到这些代码，并据此认为这样做没问题）。

618202081.en: For `extern "C" {}` imports it can be something different than `fn_cast!` specifically. That one's more oriented towards places that take a function pointer. I think it's neat to be able to layer more Rust-friendly typing on FFI even for direct calls, without wrapper boilerplate. But I also think that when the mapping is at all non-obvious, it's also helpful to note the actual C signature and justify any flourish added to it.
618202081.zh: 对于 `extern "C" {}` 导入，具体实现可以不同于 `fn_cast!`。后者更多是面向接收函数指针的场景。我认为，即使是直接调用，也能够在 FFI 之上叠加更符合 Rust 使用习惯的类型系统，而不必编写包装器样板代码，这一点很不错。但我也认为，当这种映射完全不明显时，注明实际的 C 签名，并说明在此基础上添加的任何润色为何合理，也会很有帮助。

618202097.en: Even if we don't care about EB in existing/legacy code, there's still educational material out there that talks about enums and FFI use, and not all of that will be updated.
618202097.zh: 即使我们不在意现有代码或遗留代码中的 EB，外面仍然有一些讲解枚举和 FFI 使用方式的教育材料，而这些材料不可能全部得到更新。

618202155.en: Yes, it's a mess. I am very sympathetic  to that. That's why I explicitly qualified my "it would have been better if" with "outside of backwards compatibility / churn"
618202155.zh: 没错，这确实一团糟。我对此非常理解，也深表同情。这就是为什么我在说“如果当初……会更好”时，明确加上了“抛开向后兼容性和代码变动方面的顾虑”这一限定。

618202185.en: The C standard says that enums are ABI compatible with their inner integer, *but not with each other*. Remember that compatibility is not transitive in C.
618202185.zh: C 标准规定，枚举与其底层整数类型 ABI 兼容，*但不同枚举之间并不兼容*。要记住，在 C 中兼容性不具有传递性。

618202211.en:
>  But I also think that when the mapping is at all non-obvious, it's also helpful to note the actual C signature and justify any flourish added to it.

To be clear: I agree with you on this. But I think it's a style choice, and I think changes like this should be done carefully.
618202211.zh:
>  但我也认为，当这种映射完全不明显时，注明实际的 C 签名，并说明在此基础上添加的任何润色为何合理，会很有帮助。

明确地说：我同意你的看法。但我认为这是一个风格选择，而且我认为这样的改动应该谨慎进行。

618202434.zh: 所以，如果我们说无字段的 repr(Int) 枚举与 Int ABI 兼容，那么 Rust 中任意两个 repr(Int) 枚举（只要使用相同的 Int）也都 ABI 兼容


ABI-compatibility is a transitive notion though so this is still relevant. we cannot say enums are ABI-compat with their inner type without also saying they are ABI-compat with each other.
618202504.zh:

One reason why I’d like to claw back as much ABI compatibility as possible is because anything that we keep as non-EB (because we don’t consider it sufficiently useful to CFI) can come back to haunt us later, if it later turns out to be more useful to make it EB. If we can slowly replace *all* reliance on ABI compatibility with CFI-friendly equivalents, then we won’t ever have to go through a second odyssey of telling people that code from 10 years ago, which we said was fine five years ago when we introduced EB for the sake of CFI, actually should be changed after all.
618203131.zh: @_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618202629)：`对于这种情况，我认为只有在确实存在相称的强烈需求时，我们才应该把它定为 EB。`我之所以希望尽可能收回 ABI 兼容性，是因为我们保留为非 EB 的任何东西（因为我们认为它对 CFI 不够有用），日后都有可能反过来给我们带来麻烦：如果后来发现把它定为 EB 更有用，我们就会陷入困境。如果我们能够逐步用对 CFI 友好的等价方案替代对 ABI 兼容性的所有依赖，那么将来就不必再经历第二次漫长的历程——告诉人们，十年前编写的代码，我们在五年前为了 CFI 引入 EB 时还说它没问题，但现在实际上还是应该改掉。

618225572.en: As I've argued previously, it would be a terrible mistake for Rust to bless a CFI scheme that violates the C standard for no good reason. If we teach users to ignore standards on a whim, they will ignore ours as well
618225572.zh: 正如我之前所论证的，如果 Rust 认可一种毫无正当理由地违反 C 标准的 CFI 方案，那将是一个可怕的错误。如果我们教用户可以随心所欲地无视标准，那他们也会无视我们的标准。

618225657.en: It is CFI that should change to do the sane, standard-compliant thing, not Rust that should add footguns to accommodate CFI's current broken behavior.
618225657.zh: 应该改变的是 CFI，让它采取合理且符合标准的做法，而不是 Rust 为了迁就 CFI 当前有问题的行为而增加容易误用的陷阱。

618227999.en: I wouldn't be particularly against changing CFI to encode enums as their underlying integer type, rather than their struct name. But I don't think CFI can reasonably be changed to fix all of the other C standard divergences, particularly the issues with typedefs of structs with no name.
618227999.zh: 我并不特别反对修改 CFI，让它把枚举编码为其底层整数类型，而不是结构体名称。不过，我不认为 CFI 能合理地修复所有其他与 C 标准的分歧，尤其是那些没有名称的结构体的 typedef 所涉及的问题。

618228266.en:
There, we have an issue that Rust has no way to express the equivalent of an unnamed typedefd C struct, so Rust simply cannot express the ABI of functions using such structs.

Which by the way is similar to the situation around enums in my eyes. If Rust declares that our enums are like the underlying integer, then this means that we have no way in Rust to express the signature of a function that takes a C enum as argument. It's just less bad here since we have a type that is ABI-compatible with said C enum.
618228266.zh: 这里的问题是，Rust 没有办法表达与无名 typedef C 结构体等价的类型，因此 Rust 根本无法表达使用这类结构体的函数的 ABI。顺便说，在我看来，这和枚举的情况很相似。如果 Rust 声明我们的枚举就等同于底层整数，那么这意味着我们在 Rust 中没有办法表达以 C 枚举作为参数的函数签名。这里只是没那么糟，因为我们有一个与该 C 枚举具有 ABI 兼容性的类型。

Sure we do. Because C enums are also ABI-compatible with the underlying integer
618231116.zh: @_**Alice Ryhl|218683** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618228266)：“顺便说，在我看来，这和枚举的情况很相似。如果 Rust 声明我们的枚举就等同于底层整数，那么这意味着我们在 Rust 中没有办法表达以 C 枚举作为参数的函数签名。”当然有办法。因为 C 枚举同样与其底层整数具有 ABI 兼容性。

618231401.en: From the point of view of a Rust program linking against it, C is just an ABI. Whether the C library uses an integer or an enum is a private implementation detail, because the ABI is the same
618231401.zh: 从链接到该库的 Rust 程序的角度来看，C 就只是一个 ABI。C 库使用整数还是枚举，是私有实现细节，因为它们的 ABI 是相同的。

618300991.en: Well, not entirely? In Rust you would come to the conclusion that `fn(enum_foo)` and `fn(enum_bar)` are compatible as long as the enums are backed by the same integer, but they aren't compatible in C according to the standard.
618300991.zh: 嗯，也不完全是这样吧？在 Rust 中，你会得出这样的结论：只要枚举由同一个整数类型作为底层类型，`fn(enum_foo)` 和 `fn(enum_bar)` 就是兼容的；但根据 C 标准，它们在 C 中并不兼容。

618322289.en: if someone is using Rust ABI compatibility rules to conclude things about C ABI compatibility, they are just wrong. not much we can do about that.
618322289.zh: 如果有人利用 Rust 的 ABI 兼容规则来推断 C ABI 的兼容性，那他们就是错的。对此我们也没什么可做的。

618322706.en:
non-transitive ABI compatibility could arise with a CFI scheme that implements some arbitrary "compatibility" check at runtime. not sure if that actually exists but it seems like a useful hypothetical for this discussion.
in that world, a Rust declaration of ``fn(enum_foo)``/``fn(enum_bar)`` would be represented towards that system with the underlying integer type. That's something the Rust frontend would do. In contrast, a C frontend would tell the CFI system about the actual enum. So yeah these would be compatible when called from Rust but not when called from C.
618322706.zh: 如果某种 CFI 方案在运行时执行某种任意的“兼容性”检查，就可能出现非传递性的 ABI 兼容性。我不确定现实中是否真的存在这种情况，但在这次讨论中，它似乎是一个有用的假设。在这种世界里，Rust 对 `fn(enum_foo)`/`fn(enum_bar)` 的声明，会以底层整数类型的形式呈现给那个系统。这是 Rust 前端会做的事情。相比之下，C 前端会把实际的枚举告知 CFI 系统。所以，是的，从 Rust 调用时它们会兼容，但从 C 调用时则不会。

619418215.en:
@_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618202376):
````quote
However, ABI compatibility *in Rust* is transitive

So if we say fieldless repr(Int) enum is ABI compatible with Int, then any two repr(Int) enums (for same Int) are also ABI compatibile in Rust
````

@_**RalfJ|120791** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618202504):
```quote
ABI-compatibility is a transitive notion though so this is still relevant. we cannot say enums are ABI-compat with their inner type without also saying they are ABI-compat with each other.
```
These assume that ABI compatibility in Rust is also **symmetric** (so together with transitivity, an equivalence relation). Is that a given? Transitivity seems obvious, but I don't see why it needs to be symmetric. In fact, the docs at https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html#abi-compatibility seem to contain at least one clearly asymmetric case: 
>The ABI strings are guaranteed to be compatible if they are the same, or if the caller ABI string is `$X-unwind` and the callee ABI string is `$X`, where `$X` is one of the following: ...

In the enum case, for example, it could be reasonable that you can call `fn(int)` as `fn(enum_foo)` or as `fn(enum_bar)`, but not `fn(enum_foo)` as either other type.
619418215.zh: @_**Hanna Kruppe|124289** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618202376)：“不过，*在 Rust 中*，ABI 兼容性是传递的。所以，如果我们说无字段的 `repr(Int)` 枚举与 `Int` 具有 ABI 兼容性，那么在 Rust 中，任何两个使用相同 `Int` 的 `repr(Int)` 枚举也都具有 ABI 兼容性。”@_**RalfJ|120791** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/repr.28Int.29.20enum.20ABI.20compatibility/near/618202504)：“不过，ABI 兼容性本来就是一种传递关系，所以这仍然值得关注。我们不能说枚举与其内部类型 ABI 兼容，却不同时说它们彼此之间也 ABI 兼容。”这些说法假定 Rust 中的 ABI 兼容性也具有**对称性**（因此与传递性结合起来，就构成等价关系）。这是既定事实吗？传递性似乎很明显，但我不明白它为什么必须具有对称性。事实上，https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.fn.html#abi-compatibility 中的文档似乎至少包含一个明显不对称的情况：“如果 ABI 字符串相同，或者调用方 ABI 字符串是 `$X-unwind` 而被调用方 ABI 字符串是 `$X`，则保证二者兼容，其中 `$X` 是以下之一……”以枚举为例，完全可以认为你可以将 `fn(int)` 作为 `fn(enum_foo)` 或 `fn(enum_bar)` 来调用，但不能将 `fn(enum_foo)` 作为其他任一类型来调用。

619419356.en:
If you go a bit further down, it says
```quote
Furthermore, ABI compatibility satisfies the following general properties:
* Every type is ABI-compatible with itself.
* If `T1` and `T2` are ABI-compatible and `T2` and `T3` are ABI-compatible, then so are `T1` and `T3` (i.e., ABI-compatibility is transitive).
* If `T1` and `T2` are ABI-compatible, then so are `T2` and `T1` (i.e., ABI-compatibility is symmetric).
```
619419356.zh: 如果你再往下看一点，文档写道：“此外，ABI 兼容性满足以下一般性质：* 每个类型都与自身具有 ABI 兼容性。* 如果 `T1` 与 `T2` 具有 ABI 兼容性，且 `T2` 与 `T3` 具有 ABI 兼容性，那么 `T1` 与 `T3` 也具有 ABI 兼容性（即 ABI 兼容性具有传递性）。* 如果 `T1` 与 `T2` 具有 ABI 兼容性，那么 `T2` 与 `T1` 也具有 ABI 兼容性（即 ABI 兼容性具有对称性）。”

614944346.en:
All of this talk about atomic-`memcpy`, volatile-`memcpy`, etc. makes me think what we really need is a uber-`memcpy` where you can independently select whether the input and/or output are atomic, volatile, aligned, potentially-overlapping, really a `memset`, etc.

The idea is we propose adding it to LLVM and then it becomes the replacement for `llvm.memcpy`, `llvm.memcpy.element.unordered.atomic`, etc. (though probably with some kind of migration strategy). Because the flags are independently set for the input and output, that prevents problems where both input and output are atomic/volatile so the compiler generates a extra load when all you want is volatile/atomic store, or an extra store when all you want is volatile/atomic store. Being both volatile and atomic allows you to have volatile ops that interact with fences and other atomics.
614944346.zh:
所有这些关于 atomic-`memcpy`、volatile-`memcpy` 等的讨论，让我觉得我们真正需要的是一个超级版的 `memcpy`：可以独立选择输入和/或输出是否具有原子性、易失性、对齐、可能重叠、实际上是 `memset` 等属性。

我们的想法是提议将其加入 LLVM，然后用它替代 `llvm.memcpy`、`llvm.memcpy.element.unordered.atomic` 等（不过可能需要某种迁移策略）。由于可以独立设置输入和输出的标志，这样就能避免输入和输出都具有原子性/易失性时出现的问题：当你只想要易失性/原子存储时，编译器却生成了额外的加载；或者当你只想要易失性/原子加载时，编译器却生成了额外的存储。让操作同时具有易失性和原子性，可以使易失性操作与栅栏及其他原子操作正确交互。

614951405.en: Currently atomic `memcpy` and volatile `memcpy` have no way to say the input or output shouldn't be atomic/volatile so they end up optimizing poorly: https://rust.godbolt.org/z/cjnE76nsz
614951405.zh: 目前，原子 `memcpy` 和易失性 `memcpy` 无法表明输入或输出不应具有原子性/易失性，因此它们最终无法得到良好的优化：https://rust.godbolt.org/z/cjnE76nsz

614983766.en: This seems like a good idea to me, but I'm not really familiar enough with LLVM to say if that's the right way to add it to LLVM. @**Nikita Popov** might have opinions on the topic.
614983766.zh: 我觉得这似乎是个好主意，但我对 LLVM 还不够熟悉，无法判断这是否是在 LLVM 中加入它的正确方式。@**Nikita Popov** 可能对此有自己的看法。

614991974.en: In #58041 it came up that for `volatile_memcpy` there isn't much reason to distinguish whether the src or dst is volatile. You might as well just have one operation that is volatile in both ends, and then that is sufficient for both cases without really hurting any perf.
614991974.zh: 在 #58041 中有人提到，对于 `volatile_memcpy` 来说，区分 src 或 dst 是否具有易失性并没有太大意义。你完全可以只使用一个两端都具有易失性的操作，这样就足以覆盖这两种情况，而且基本不会影响性能。

614993673.en: If you doing a volatile_memcpy from MMIO memory, but never read (part of) the destination, then keeping destination as non-volatile would be a perf improvement. Or if you just created the value to write for a memcpy into MMIO memory, the write it into memory can be optimized out if you keep the source as non-volatile.
614993673.zh: 如果你从 MMIO 内存执行 volatile_memcpy，但从不读取目标内存的（某一部分）内容，那么让目标保持非易失性可以提升性能。或者，如果你只是创建了一个要写入 MMIO 内存的值，并将其用于 memcpy，那么如果源保持为非易失性，这次写入内存的操作就可能被优化掉。

615008920.en: It's also possible you might want to use different atomic orderings for load vs store.
615008920.zh: 你可能还会希望对加载和存储使用不同的原子内存顺序。

615009220.en: Although, to some extent perhaps that can be done using fences separate from the actual copying? I'm not certain (it feels like it could, but it also might fail in an important way that I'm not considering)

```quote
Seems like the byte type will fix a bunch of the known-length versions, since we can atomic store `b192` for example.
```

actually I expect you can't atomic store a `b192` and get the rust semantics you'd want since I'd assume llvm will compile that to the C++ store by locking, just like `i192`.

atomic memcpy is only elementwise atomic, unlike the other LLVM atomic instructions which are guaranteed to be atomic for the whole value no matter how large since they use locking if there isn't a native instruction big enough.
615033492.zh:

615062903.en:
@_**Julien Cretin (ia0)|117910** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Uber-.60memcpy.60/near/615053955):


if you use regular atomics you are modeling the other process as participating in the same AM. that means it can observe atomic accesses and they cant be optimized away.
it also means UB in the other process is UB in your program, which is a Bad Day if you dont actually trust the other process...
615062903.zh:
@_**Julien Cretin (ia0)|117910** [说](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/136281-t-opsem/topic/Uber-.60memcpy.60/near/615053955)：


如果你使用普通的 atomic，那么你就是在将另一个进程建模为参与同一个 AM。这意味着它可以观察到原子访问，而这些访问不能被优化掉。
这也意味着另一个进程中的 UB 会成为你的程序中的 UB；如果你实际上并不信任另一个进程，那可就糟糕了……

614939545.en:
I have several questions/thoughts about how memory accesses interact with signal handlers. (In particular, with async-signal-safe signal handlers that might still access Rust-allocated memory, such as atomics in `static`s... and presumably local variables within a signal handler implemented in Rust are also affected, under a literal reading of documentation.)

# Spurious signals

First, if the signal handler is treated as not semantically guaranteed to be called at the expected time, I *think* we can use inline-asm-style storytelling, even on the current version of rust before https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/610 lands.

In particular, say that some read or write, A, triggers a signal B that causes signal handler C to run. We could tell the story that "signal B can be spuriously raised at any time, and A is not responsible for that". To maintain that story, we can no longer assume that C runs iff A starts to execute, but at least -- as far as I know -- this would make running C sound.

(So long as nothing tries to detect that signal B was in fact caused by memory access A and make some unchecked assumption based on that fact. Nothing in the language itself or in `std` ought to do that, and at *worst* some other crate could go out of its way to include code which is inconsistent with this story, perhaps installing a signal handler and deciding whether to execute UB based on the contents of a `siginfo_t`.)

I don't think this even requires volatile accesses. Any sort of memory access should work.

The cost is that if you try to use this somewhat-simplistic story to justify a segfaulting read (for instance), then you have to accept the possibility of a segfault occurring at any time whatsoever.

It's more useful for memory-mapped files and SIGBUS. We could slightly refine the story to "spurious SIGBUSes can occur during any time that any memory-mapped file is shorter than its mapping". Any operation which changes the length of a file or a mapping (whether from the current process or an external process), which already has externally-observable side effects, can be said to also manage the flag permitting these spurious SIGBUSes. Under this story, reads and writes to shared memory-mapped files are not unsound in the face of external processes being able to truncate files, even if there's a registered SIGBUS handler that accesses Rust-allocated memory and may or may not abort the process (though, realistically, a SIGBUS handler should abort the process). Instead, if such a truncation occurs, the result is well-defined... if less than ideal for the victim process.

Under this story, do the memory accesses to memory-mapped files even need to be volatile? (...separately, there's still the concern of data races, and absent mixed-size atomic accesses, I suppose that volatile reads and writes are the best option.)

(Edge case: maybe the program is statically linked to the responsible OS code, and that code somehow avoids executing an operation which is considered externally observable. Then there could be a problem. This argument requires there to be *something* external to the AM that could hypothetically be tracking the lengths of memory-mapped files and their mappings, and could hypothetically send SIGBUSes based on that state.)

# Guaranteed signals

Once volatile accesses are permitted to trap... can a signal handler access Rust-allocated memory and then abort the process, while still being guaranteed to be called when the access occurs? Or, as in the above scenario, can it not be guaranteed that a custom signal handler would run at the expected time?

I'm trying to think of hypothetical transformations that would break this guarantee, but if the custom signal handler is only reading and writing atomics (and its own local variables), then transformations that break the signal handler would also break any other thread looking at the atomics at the wrong time. (Even if this all occurs moments before the process is terminated.) Thread-local state could hypothetically be clobbered and un-clobbered before and after a volatile operation without breaking other threads, but since signal handlers ought to be treated as running in a different thread, that shouldn't break a sound signal handler.

Note that `std`, on some platforms, [registers a signal handler](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/b070f45ad92ed45b20e57d9483a21657d0d00715/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs) implemented in Rust for SIGBUS and SIGSEGV on some platforms. (Its job is to check if the SIGBUS or SIGSEGV looks like it was caused by a stack overflow, and if so, print a nicer error message and abort the process.) Since that signal handler has local variables in Rust allocations, a literal reading of
> The access is allowed to trap. It can also cause other side-effects, but those must not affect Rust-allocated memory in any way.

indicates that volatile operations are not permitted to result in a SIGBUS or SIGSEGV on those platforms (unless those signal handlers are unregistered first), which doesn't seem intended.
614939545.zh:
关于内存访问如何与信号处理程序交互，我有几个问题和想法。（特别是对于异步信号安全的信号处理程序：它们仍可能访问 Rust 分配的内存，例如 `static` 中的原子变量……而且，按文档的字面意思理解，Rust 实现的信号处理程序中的局部变量大概也会受到影响。）

# 虚假信号

首先，如果我们把信号处理程序视为在语义上并不能保证于预期时间被调用，我*认为*即使在 https://github.com/rust-lang/unsafe-code-guidelines/issues/610 落地之前，当前版本的 Rust 也可以采用类似内联汇编的叙事方式。

具体来说，假设某次读或写操作 A 触发了信号 B，进而导致信号处理程序 C 运行。我们可以这样描述：“信号 B 可能在任何时间被无缘无故地引发，A 对此不负责任。”为了维持这一叙事，我们就不能再假设 C 运行当且仅当 A 开始执行，但至少——据我所知——这样一来，运行 C 就是健全的。

（前提是没有任何东西试图检测信号 B 确实是由内存访问 A 引起的，并据此作出未经检查的假设。语言本身或 `std` 中不应有任何东西这样做；最坏的情况是，某个其他 crate 可能特意加入与这一叙事不一致的代码，比如安装一个信号处理程序，然后根据 `siginfo_t` 的内容决定是否执行 UB。）

我认为这甚至不需要 volatile 访问。任何形式的内存访问都应该可以。

代价是：如果你试图用这种略显简单的叙事来为一次会触发段错误的读取（例如）辩护，那么你就必须接受段错误可能在任何时候发生。

对于内存映射文件和 SIGBUS，这种方式更有用。我们可以将叙事稍微细化为：“只要存在任何长度小于其映射长度的内存映射文件，就可能在任意时刻发生虚假的 SIGBUS。”任何会改变文件或映射长度的操作（无论来自当前进程还是外部进程）本来就具有对外可观察的副作用，因此也可以说它会管理那个允许发生这些虚假 SIGBUS 的标志。按照这一叙事，即使外部进程可以截断文件，即使已注册的 SIGBUS 处理程序会访问 Rust 分配的内存并且可能终止、也可能不终止进程，对共享内存映射文件进行读写也不会因此变得不健全（不过现实中，SIGBUS 处理程序应该终止进程）。相反，如果发生了这种截断，结果是定义明确的……只是对受影响的进程来说不太理想。

按照这一叙事，对内存映射文件的内存访问甚至还需要是 volatile 的吗？（……另外，数据竞争问题仍然存在；而在缺少混合大小的原子访问时，我想 volatile 读写仍是最佳选择。）

（边界情况：程序可能静态链接了相关的操作系统代码，而该代码以某种方式避免执行被认为是对外可观察的操作。这样就可能出现问题。这个论证要求存在某些位于 AM 之外的东西，它理论上能够跟踪内存映射文件及其映射的长度，并且能够根据该状态发送 SIGBUS。）

# 保证的信号

一旦允许 volatile 访问触发异常……信号处理程序能否访问 Rust 分配的内存，然后终止进程，同时仍保证在该访问发生时被调用？还是说，与上面的场景一样，无法保证自定义信号处理程序会在预期时间运行？

我正在设想一些可能破坏这一保证的转换；但如果自定义信号处理程序只读写原子变量（以及它自己的局部变量），那么会破坏该信号处理程序的转换，也会破坏任何其他线程在错误时间查看这些原子变量的行为。（即使这一切发生在进程即将终止的瞬间。）在线程局部状态方面，理论上可以在 volatile 操作前后将其破坏并恢复，而不会影响其他线程；但由于信号处理程序应被视为运行在另一个线程中，这不应破坏一个健全的信号处理程序。

请注意，在某些平台上，`std` 会为 SIGBUS 和 SIGSEGV [注册一个用 Rust 实现的信号处理程序](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/b070f45ad92ed45b20e57d9483a21657d0d00715/library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow.rs)。（它的工作是检查 SIGBUS 或 SIGSEGV 是否看起来是由栈溢出引起的；如果是，就打印更友好的错误消息并终止进程。）由于该信号处理程序在 Rust 分配中拥有局部变量，按下面这句话的字面意思理解：

> 该访问允许触发异常。它也可以导致其他副作用，但这些副作用绝不能以任何方式影响 Rust 分配的内存。

这意味着在这些平台上，volatile 操作不允许导致 SIGBUS 或 SIGSEGV（除非先取消注册这些信号处理程序），但这似乎并非本意。

Well... io_uring in polling mode theoretically can do unbounded amounts of IO running off just atomic operations on shared memory. You can build the entire program's event loop on that. If you're willing to busy-loop you'd not even have to do a syscall when there's no work to do. *most* programs don't actually use it that way because it needs root and burns CPU-cycles, but you could.
Maybe uring libraries would have to sprinkle some volatile atomics around the start/end or something to make this clear that it triggers IO and the entire event loop isn't unobservable?
615058922.zh:
嗯……理论上，轮询模式下的 io_uring 只通过对共享内存执行原子操作，就能进行不受限制的 I/O。你可以据此构建整个程序的事件循环。如果你愿意忙等，那么没有工作要做时甚至不必进行系统调用。*大多数*程序实际上不会这样使用它，因为这需要 root 权限，而且会消耗 CPU 周期，但理论上确实可以这么做。

也许 uring 库需要在开始或结束的位置之类的地方加上一些 volatile 原子操作，以明确表明这里会触发 I/O，从而说明整个事件循环并不是不可观察的？

615063048.zh: 但你不能使用（非原子的）volatile 与另一个线程通信。

615063840.zh: 如果你执行的是 volatile 原子 release 写操作，那么完全可以构造这样一个故事：某处有一个线程在等待这个位置出现新值；它看到这次写入后，就会执行某些操作。

````quote
remember that story code can only be placed where the inline asm was. so which inline asm are you replacing by that story code? the only option I can imagine is saying that there's some story code running before main which spawns a background thread that just arbitrarily triggers SIGBUS in any other thread any time it wants. and then in the refined version the background thread somehow knows whether there is currently any memory-mapped file that is shorter than its mapping.
````

Story code can go where FFI calls are as well, right? Assuming that *some* FFI is involved any time a memory mapping is created (or has its length change) or a file's length changes, you can say that such FFI reports the changes to that background thread. That background thread records the data, and whenever it determines that there is a memory-mapped file shorter than its mapping, it may choose to send SIGBUSes to the thread with the overlong mapping (up until the background thread sees that there is no longer a memory-mapped file shorter than its mapping in that thread, based on the supposed reports from the mmap and file FFI calls).

Any SIGBUSes received from performing memory accesses on a memory mapping whose backing file is too short, even if Rust/LLVM reorder, hoist them, or do whatever else, should be a subset of the SIGBUSes that could have been sent by that background thread (...ignoring fine details like the contents of the signal's `siginfo_t`. Maybe we can pretend that the background thread has some magic OS permissions that let it forge whatever signal it wants; should be equally sound as far as the language is concerned.). Therefore, the actual FFI code refines this story.


故事代码也可以放在 FFI 调用的位置，对吧？假设每当创建内存映射（或其长度发生变化），或者文件长度发生变化时，都会涉及某种 FFI，那么你就可以说，这些 FFI 会把变化报告给那个后台线程。后台线程记录这些数据，并且每当它判断出存在长度短于其映射范围的内存映射文件时，就可以选择向持有超长映射的线程发送 SIGBUS（直到后台线程根据 mmap 和文件 FFI 调用传来的假定报告，发现该线程中不再存在长度短于其映射范围的内存映射文件为止）。

即使 Rust/LLVM 对这些操作进行重排、提升，或执行其他任何操作，在对底层文件过短的内存映射执行内存访问时收到的任何 SIGBUS，都应该只是那个后台线程可能发送的 SIGBUS 的子集（……忽略信号的 `siginfo_t` 内容之类的细节。也许我们可以假设后台线程拥有某种神奇的操作系统权限，可以伪造任意想要的信号；就语言层面而言，这应该同样是健全的。）。因此，实际的 FFI 代码细化了这个故事。

623056258.en:
Hi @JonathanBrouwer, working on the `check_diagnostic_on_move` migration (#153101). I've hit a design question about lint emission from `finalize_check` and wanted to check the intended approach before writing code.

The current `check_diagnostic_on_move` emits a **lint** (`MALFORMED_DIAGNOSTIC_FORMAT_LITERALS`) via `tcx.emit_node_span_lint`. Moving it into `OnMoveParser::finalize_check`, I found that:

- `SharedContext::emit_lint` takes `&mut self`
- `finalize_check` receives `cx: &FinalizeCheckContext` (immutable)
- all existing `finalize_check` impls (`non_exhaustive` in #161482, `rustc_pub_transparent`, `track_caller`, `inline`, `codegen_attrs`, `link_attrs`, etc.) use `emit_err` (error, `&self`) — **none emit a lint**

So it looks like `finalize_check` currently can't emit a lint. The format-string *parsing* lint is already emitted earlier in `diagnostic/mod.rs` via `cx.emit_lint` (in the `&mut AcceptContext` parse phase), but that phase has no access to item generics — only `finalize_check`'s `target_item` exposes AST generics.

How should the generics-matching lint be emitted? Options I see:

(a) add a `&self` `emit_lint` wrapper to `FinalizeCheckContext`/`SharedContext` (mirroring `emit_err`), so `finalize_check` can emit lints
(b) convert this check to an error (changes lint→error semantics, loses `#[allow]` suppression)
(c) keep the generics-matching check in `check_attr.rs` (hir), since it needs hir generics + node-level lint, and only the format-string parsing part (already done in `mod.rs`) moves to the parser — i.e. this subtask may not be fully migratable as-is
(d) another mechanism you have in mind

What's the intended approach? Thanks!
623056258.zh:
JonathanBrouwer ，您好！`check_diagnostic_on_move`迁移(# 153101)。我遇到了一个关于从`finalize_check`并希望在编写代码之前检查预期的方法。

当前`check_diagnostic_on_move`发出* *棉绒* * （`MALFORMED_DIAGNOSTIC_FORMAT_LITERALS` 通过 `tcx.emit_node_span_lint`。将其移动到`OnMoveParser::finalize_check`，我发现：

-`SharedContext::emit_lint`{} 片段`&mut self`
-`finalize_check`收到`cx: &FinalizeCheckContext`(不可变)
-所有现有的`finalize_check`impls (`non_exhaustive`# 161482 ，`rustc_pub_transparent`, `track_caller`, `inline`, `codegen_attrs`, `link_attrs`等）使用`emit_err`错误`&self`） — * *没有人排出棉绒* *

所以看起来`finalize_check`目前无法发出绒毛。格式字符串*解析* lint已在`diagnostic/mod.rs` 通过 `cx.emit_lint` 在`&mut AcceptContext`解析阶段） ，但该阶段无法访问项目泛型—仅`finalize_check`S`target_item`暴露AST泛型。

仿制药匹配的棉绒应该如何排出？我看到的选项：

(a)添加`&self` `emit_lint`包装器到`FinalizeCheckContext`/`SharedContext`镜像`emit_err`所以`finalize_check`可以排出绒毛
(b)将此检查转换为错误（更改lint→错误语义，丢失`#[allow]`抑制）
(c)保持仿制药匹配检查`check_attr.rs`(hir) ，因为它需要hir泛型+节点级lint ，并且只需要格式字符串解析部分（已在`mod.rs`)移动到解析器—即此子任务可能无法按原样完全迁移
(d)您想到的另一种机制

您打算采用哪种方法？谢谢！

Which is useful if you want something compact and usable in a no_std context, and as a bonus is convenient for getting a backtrace about the "shouldn't happen" condition that just happened. If you continue from that point without thinking about it, you may encounter the code the assert guarded against.

622821866.en: Hitting "continue" in a debugger after a breakpoint is like taking a program that accepts filenames and giving it `/proc/self/mem`. Once you're in a debugger, and do something to modify the control flow of the program from what it would have been *without* a debugger, the correct operation of the program is now your responsibility.

622823119.en:
@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622821051):
```quote
My argument is that it's perfectly valid for someone to define a version of assert that uses a breakpoint instruction rather than a panic. Which is useful if you want something compact and usable in a no_std context, and as a bonus is convenient for getting a backtrace about the "shouldn't happen" condition that just happened. If you continue from that point without thinking about it, you may encounter the code the assert guarded against.
```

I'm not sure I agree that it's perfectly valid. It can be fine in some cases I suppose, but the reality is that this *is* a feature that exists and it's so intrinsic to the functionality of the debugger that I think it falls on the program that wants to do it to contend with (and document) the fact that they're doing something odd.

To be clear: People can do this if they want, but as I suggested above, they're taking it upon themselves to apply and document this extra safety requirement for running their program: you must not use a debugger to continue past a breakpoint. There's nothing wrong with a given program having additional safety requirements beyond what Rust provides (we often call this "outside the model"); this is how programs like ripgrep can support mmaping files without it being a violation of Rust's rules. If you do something like this, you are just supposed to communicate to the user what your additional requirements are, such as not truncating certain files, or not stepping in a debugger.

```我不确定我是否同意它是完全有效的。 在某些情况下，我想这是可以的，但现实是，这*是一个*存在的功能，它对于调试器的功能是如此固有，以至于我认为它落在程序上，而程序想要这样做来对抗（并记录）他们正在做一些奇怪的事情。需要明确的是：人们可以根据需要执行此操作，但正如我上面建议的那样，他们将自行申请并记录运行其程序的额外安全要求：不得使用调试器继续通过断点。给定程序除了Rust提供的安全要求之外还有其他安全要求（我们通常称之为“模型外” ） ，这没有什么问题；这就是像ripgrep这样的程序可以支持mmaping文件而不违反Rust规则的方式。如果执行此类操作，则只需向用户传达其他要求，例如不截断某些文件或不步入调试器。

622832331.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622832031):
```quote
You can already use the unstable `std::process::abort_immediate()` for crash explosively. A debugger should catch the SIGILL and allow you to inspect the state of the process.
```

I'd love to see that stabilized *too*, but the difference with `breakpoint` is that *if the particular call site allows*, you have the option of *trying* to continue without even more invasive things. Whether you can do so *successfully* depends on the program, and is your responsibility for continuing, but `breakpoint` makes it convenient to do so.
622832331.zh:

622834063.en: The function josh wants could be implemented as `breakpoint(); let mut crash = true; if read_volatile(&mut crash) { abort(); }`. This requires you to explicitly acknowledge that continuing may not be safe by changing the value of `crash` using your debugger.
622834063.zh: Josh想要的函数可以实现为`breakpoint(); let mut crash = true; if read_volatile(&mut crash) { abort(); }`。这要求您明确承认，通过更改`crash`使用调试器。

622834312.en: I do still sorta think `yeet2(); black_box(abort as fn())()` kinda still works for that. But I don't think it's the case either of these functions is more portable than the other. I think both permit lowering to `abort_immediate()` or `loop {}` (in practice `yeet2` probably permits lowering to a noop if that's *truly* all that can be done).
622834312.zh: 我还是觉得`yeet2(); black_box(abort as fn())()`仍然可以做到这一点。但我不认为这两个功能中的任何一个都比另一个更便携。我认为两者都允许降低到`abort_immediate()` 或 `loop {}`实踐`yeet2`如果这是*真正*可以做的一切，则可能允许降低到noop ）。

622834479.en: Or, alternatively, you could acknowledge that continuing may not be safe by typing `c` or `s` in your debugger. :)
622834479.zh: 或者，您也可以通过键入`c` 或 `s`在调试器中。:)

622834537.en: You can skip over a ud2 in a debugger if you really really want to. I feel that's a rare enough case though.
622834537.zh: 如果您真的想要，可以跳过调试器中的ud2。但我觉得这是一个罕见的案例。

622834728.zh: 我相信miri/ctfe也希望将yeet2实现为noop ，因为它在这种情况下没有意义

622834810.en:
@_**Thom Chiovoloni|209168** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622834312):
```quote
I do still sorta think `yeet2(); black_box(abort as fn())()` kinda still works for that. But I don't think it's the case either of these functions is more portable than the other. I think both permit lowering to `abort_immediate()` or `loop {}` (in practice `yeet2` probably permits lowering to a noop if that's *truly* all that can be done).
```

The fact that `yeet2` permits lowering to a no-op is precisely why I'm arguing against it. I'm not saying I've *never* seen an architecture that has no way to crash, but I've never seen one we're likely to port Rust to. And if you have a way to crash, you have a way to implement `breakpoint()`, as a fallback if there's no explicit breakpoint instruction.

622836539.zh: 此操作的最初目的是替换某人有一大堆`cfg`围绕着各种架构特定的等价物`asm!("int3")`。

622837269.zh: 我已经开发了许多低级操作系统/驱动程序/固件代码，这些代码需要`0xCC`指令为“crash, hand control to the debugger if there is one”。

622837877.zh: 我还使用了各种各样的asm/linker魔术，`0xCC`作为填充字节，前提是如果您点击它，您将中断。

622838404.en: If we want to have an operation that is "breakpoint, but the program *additionally* wishes to make an assertion that it is possible to continue from this point", that would be above and beyond what I've seen breakpoints mean in any other context, but that might still be a potentially useful operation in the spirit of letting programs specify *more*. 622838404.zh: 如果我们希望有一个“断点，但程序*另外*希望断言可以从这一点继续”的操作，这将超出我在任何其他上下文中看到的断点含义，但本着让程序指定*更多*的精神，这可能仍然是一个潜在的有用操作。不过，这不是我默认拼写为“breakpoint”的那个。
