622839822.zh: 我完全支持记录它在每个目标上扩展到什么；这将是一个很好的文档。

622843594.en: Here is an example where SIGTRAP is intentionally ignored to avoid crashing the program when there is no debugger attached: https://github.com/r-lyeh/tinybits/blob/2a735d9717c9da30fa7eb60c2cc158dee46f8d40/tinyassert.c#L34 Same here, but permanently sets the ignore (which would not be sound with yeet1): https://github.com/gan74/Yave/blob/1b37349d4f048884e461b82b39d0faf5c9d55b97/y/y/utils.cpp#L54, and another one: https://github.com/shacklettbp/madrona/blob/86457089d677d94e2826613c8ba62d180b50ab41/src/common/crash.cpp#L60-L62 Also https://github.com/roothide/Bootstrap-basebin/blob/c66454cdeb9c1c4dfefd62500fc54e5f458e1a61/launchdhook/main.m#L269 and https://github.com/tiwai/hda-emu/blob/38272fc445344d5ce9eea7341f6a06a04e3d21e3/hda-emu.c#L1528 Also some anti-debugger methods seem to rely on ignoring SIGTRAP.
622843594.zh: 下面是一个示例，其中SIGTRAP被故意忽略，以避免在没有附加调试器的情况下导致程序崩溃：https://github.com/r-lyeh/tinybits/blob/2a735d9717c9da30fa7eb60c2cc158dee46f8d40/tinyassert.c#L34此处相同，但永久设置忽略（使用yeet1不会发出声音） ：https://github.com/gan74/Yave/blob/1b37349d4f048884e461b82b39d0faf5c9d55b97/y/y/utils.cpp#L54,另一个：https://github.com/shacklettbp/madrona/blob/86457089d677d94e2826613c8ba62d180b50ab41/src/common/crash.cpp#L60-L62你可能还喜欢…https://github.com/roothide/Bootstrap-basebin/blob/c66454cdeb9c1c4dfefd62500fc54e5f458e1a61/launchdhook/main.m#L269和https://github.com/tiwai/hda-emu/blob/38272fc445344d5ce9eea7341f6a06a04e3d21e3/hda-emu.c#L1528此外，一些反调试器方法似乎依赖于忽略SIGTRAP。

622844399.en: @**bjorn3** Interestingly (and I'm currently trying to track down why this is), if you ignore SIGTRAP, int3 will *still* abort the program with SIGTRAP.
622844399.zh: @ * * bjorn3 * *有趣的是（我目前正在尝试追踪原因） ，如果您忽略SIGTRAP ， int3将*仍然*使用SIGTRAP中止程序。

622845165.en: Found it. At least on Linux, int3 will send a SIGTRAP using `force_sig`, which forcibly resets an ignored signal to `SIG_DFL` when sending it.
622845165.zh: 找到了。至少在Linux上， int3将使用`force_sig`，强制将忽略的信号重置为`SIG_DFL`发送时。

622845735.en: You *can* write a handler that explicitly ignores it, though. But it's a bad idea unless you know it's valid for all breakpoints in your program. Anti-debugger methods, to the extent they're legitimate, are essentially saying "we assert that there should never be a breakpoint instruction in this program (because if one is there it means someone's trying to debug us, which we don't want to allow)".
622845735.zh: 不过，您*可以*编写一个明确忽略它的处理程序。但是，除非您知道它对程序中的所有断点都有效，否则这是一个坏主意。反调试器方法在合法的范围内基本上是说“我们断言这个程序中不应该有断点指令（因为如果有断点指令，则意味着有人试图调试我们，这是我们不希望允许的）”。

622846584.en: Leaving aside race conditions on signal dispositions, `signal(SIGTRAP, SIG_IGN); raise(SIGTRAP);` is a valid way to spell "let this breakpoint be explicitly ignorable".
622846584.zh: 撇开信号处理的竞争条件不谈，`signal(SIGTRAP, SIG_IGN); raise(SIGTRAP);`是拼写“let this breakpoint be explicitly ignorable”的有效方法。

622846648.en: `raise(SIGTRAP)` is not the same as a breakpoint instruction.

622846984.en:
SIG_IGN and a handler function are treated differently. And:

@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622845735):
```quote
You *can* write a handler that explicitly ignores it, though. But it's a bad idea unless you know it's valid for all breakpoints in your program.
```
622846984.zh:
SIG_IGN和处理程序函数被区别对待。并且：

@_* * Josh Triplett | 239881 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622845735):
```quote
You *can* write a handler that explicitly ignores it, though. But it's a bad idea unless you know it's valid for all breakpoints in your program.
```

622847189.en: And I disagree that it is a bad idea. With yeet2 it would be completely fine.
622847189.zh: 我不同意这是一个坏主意。使用yeet2完全没问题。

622847291.en:
> SIG_IGN and a handler function are treated differently.

That explains why it worked for me.
622847291.zh:
> SIG_IGN和处理程序函数被区别对待。

这就解释了为什么它对我有用。

622847935.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622847189):
```quote
And I disagree that it is a bad idea. With yeet2 it would be completely fine.
```

Even if we provided a function with that semantic, you have no guarantee that *every invocation of a breakpoint everywhere in your program* follows that semantic. You are free to assume that's the case, but that assumption is not *guaranteed* to be valid.
622847935.zh:
@_* * bjorn3 | 133247 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622847189):
```quote
And I disagree that it is a bad idea. With yeet2 it would be completely fine.
```即使我们为该语义提供了一个函数，您也不能保证*程序中任何地方的每次断点调用*都遵循该语义。 您可以自由地假设情况确实如此，但这种假设并不能*保证*有效。

622848712.en: Someone can always write their own `we_have_breakpoint_at_home()` function.

622850622.en: I don't see someone somewhere using yeet1 in another language as reason to make breakpoint() in rust unsound to resume by defining our version as yeet1 too rather than as yeet2.
622850622.zh: 我没有看到有人在某个地方使用另一种语言的yeet1作为理由，通过将我们的版本定义为yeet1而不是yeet2 ，使rust unound中的breakpoint ()恢复。

622851195.en: It's not "unsound to resume", it's "caller-determined whether it can be resumed".
622851195.zh: 这不是“恢复不当” ，而是“来电者决定是否可以恢复”。

622851267.en: It's up to the code invoking it whether that's okay or not.
622851267.zh: 这取决于调用它的代码是否可以。

622852110.en: A `breakpoint()` in isolation would be unsound to resume, but the surrounding context may make it safe. I didn't say it is UB to resume.
622852110.zh: A`breakpoint()`不宜恢复，但周围环境可能会使其安全。我没有说恢复是UB。

622854231.en: Then I'm not sure why you're saying "would be unsound" rather than "may be unsound, depending on surrounding context".
622854231.zh: 那么我不知道为什么你说“不健全”而不是“可能不健全，取决于周围的背景”。

622855470.en: The surrounding context is what determines if unsound functions are actually UB or not.
622855470.zh: 周围的上下文决定了不健全的函数是否真的是UB。

622857259.en: I see. You're treating it the same way you'd treat a function `fn dereference_pointer(ptr: *const T) -> T`, which can be called in a valid way but is unsound because it's doing something unsafe and exposing it as a safe operation?
622857259.zh: 我明白了。你对待它的方式与你对待功能的方式相同`fn dereference_pointer(ptr: *const T) -> T`，它可以以有效的方式调用，但不健全，因为它正在做一些不安全的事情，并将其暴露为安全操作？

622857979.en: The point of my reference to `/proc/self/mem` earlier is that, in the spirit of "if UB happened there must be *some* unsafe operation somewhere that did something wrong", the debugger and every mutating operation the user uses it to do is essentially `unsafe { debugger(); }`.
622857979.zh: 我所指的是`/proc/self/mem`早些时候是，本着“如果UB发生在某个地方一定有*一些*不安全的操作做错了什么”的精神，调试器和用户用来做的每一个变异操作本质上都是`unsafe { debugger(); }`。

622858105.en: Yeah, in this case it would be something like `fn breakpoint() { notify_debugger(); while !user_continued() {} } unreachable_unchecked()`, which is unsound as `user_continued()` may eventually return true.
622858105.zh: 是的，在这种情况下，它会像`fn breakpoint() { notify_debugger(); while !user_continued() {} } unreachable_unchecked()`，其不健全为`user_continued()`可能最终返回true。

622858451.en: That's only true if you put the soundness burden on the breakpoint operation rather than on the debugger, which is the point of disagreement here.
622858451.zh: 只有当您将稳健性负担放在断点操作上而不是调试器上时，才是真的，这是这里的分歧点。

622859656.en:
> the debugger and every mutating operation the user uses it to do is essentially `unsafe { debugger(); }`.

In my view only modifying memory and registers or manually changing the instruction pointer are unsafe operations in a debugger. Just single stepping or continuing is equivalent to the compiler inserting/removing a very slow nop loop at arbitrary points in the program (aka not observable at all from inside the rust abstract machine, and thus allowed just fine).
622859656.zh:
>用户使用的调试器和每个变更操作本质上是`unsafe { debugger(); }`.

在我看来，只有修改内存和寄存器或手动更改指令指针才是调试器中的不安全操作。 单步或继续相当于编译器在程序中的任意点插入/删除一个非常慢的nop循环（也就是说，从Rust抽象机器内部根本无法观察到，因此可以很好地观察到）。

622860154.en: Single stepping or continuing can be equivalent to changing the instruction pointer. (And, in fact, precisely are on arm, where the trap occurs with a resumption address at the breakpoint rather than after the breakpoint.)
622860154.zh: 单步或继续可以等同于更改指令指针。（而且，实际上，正好在ARM上，其中陷阱发生时在断点处而不是在断点之后使用恢复地址。）

622860900.en: That is changing it in a way that the compiler expects to happen. If it didn't expect it, it would treat breakpoints as aborts and skip codegen of all code after it.
622860900.zh: 这正在以编译器期望发生的方式改变它。如果没有预料到，它会将断点视为中止，并跳过其后所有代码的codegen。

622861367.en: I feel like we're stuck in a loop here. There is, in fact, a third option, other than "must always abort" and "must always be resumable". I appreciate that it's not the option you want. But it's a valid option.
622861367.zh: 我觉得我们陷入了一个循环。事实上，除了“必须始终中止”和“必须始终可恢复”之外，还有第三个选项。我明白这不是您想要的选择。但这是一个有效的选择。

622861827.en: If continuing after a breakpoint compiled into the executable was considered dangerous, debuggers should ask for confirmation, not silently accept it IMO.
622861827.zh: 如果在编译到可执行文件中的断点被认为是危险的之后继续，调试者应该要求确认，而不是默默地接受IMO。

622862014.en: If writing code in C is considered dangerous, C compilers should ask for confirmation, not silently generate machine code. But that's not the era that C compilers were written in and it's not the era that debuggers were written in.
622862014.zh: 如果用C编写代码被认为是危险的， C编译器应该要求确认，而不是默默地生成机器代码。但这不是编写C编译器的时代，也不是编写调试器的时代。

622862064.en: Running a debugger is inherently an unsafe operation.
622862064.zh: 运行调试器本质上是不安全的操作。

622862507.en: Gdb and lldb ask for confirmation when doing several dangerous things like detaching or killing a process.
622862507.zh: Gdb和lldb在做一些危险的事情（如分离或杀死一个过程）时会要求确认。

622862708.en:
@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622862064):
```quote
Running a debugger is inherently an unsafe operation.
```

That is what I disagree with. IMO a debugger is only dangerous when you actively tamper with the state of the program. Not when you single step and inspect the state.
622862708.zh:
@_* * Josh Triplett | 239881 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622862064):
```quote
Running a debugger is inherently an unsafe operation.
```这就是我不同意的地方。 只有当您主动篡改程序的状态时， IMO调试器才是危险的。 当您单步检查状态时不会。

622862736.en: I hope you're not asserting that gdb is written to a standard of "if it doesn't ask for confirmation then it must be completely safe".
622862736.zh: 我希望您不要断言gdb的写入标准是“如果它不要求确认，那么它必须是完全安全的”。

622863534.en: I know there are dangerous commands like setting variables or writing to arbitrary memory. However I would certainly hope that gdb warns me when running a command that is normally safe, but not in this specific case. Gdb doesn't warn when you try to attach to a process, unless doing so would cause another process to be killed or detached from for example. And it will ask before downloading debug symbols from the internet by default. And by default it won't run python scripts embedded in the target executable.
622863534.zh: 我知道有一些危险的命令，如设置变量或写入任意内存。但是，我当然希望gdb在运行通常安全的命令时会警告我，但在这种特定情况下不会。当您尝试附加到一个进程时， Gdb不会发出警告，除非这样做会导致另一个进程被终止或脱离。默认情况下，它会在从互联网下载调试符号之前询问。默认情况下，它不会运行嵌入在目标可执行文件中的python脚本。

622863718.en: I think that *most programmers think* that using a debugger for stepping does not modify anything but the timing of the program.
622863718.zh: 我认为*大多数程序员认为*使用调试器进行步进只会修改程序的时间。

622863807.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622862708):

@_**Josh Triplett|239881** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622862064):
```quote
Running a debugger is inherently an unsafe operation.
```

That is what I disagree with. IMO a debugger is only dangerous when you actively tamper with the state of the program. Not when you single step and inspect the state.
````

I mostly agree with that, with the caveat that resuming from a user provided breakpoint, much like stepping around a divide-by-zero, is potentially tampering with the state of the program. 

I would like to figure out a good way for us to move past the part where we are asserting our axioms at each other, and try to find a useful way to explore that in a fashion that would let us decide which one is correct.
622863807.zh:
@_* * bjorn3 | 133247 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622862708):

That is what I disagree with. IMO a debugger is only dangerous when you actively tamper with the state of the program. Not when you single step and inspect the state.
````我基本上同意这一点，但需要注意的是，从用户提供的断点恢复，就像绕过除以零一样，可能会篡改程序的状态。 

我想找出一个很好的方法，让我们超越我们互相断言公理的部分，并试图找到一种有用的方法来探索这一点，让我们决定哪一个是正确的。

622864165.en: You can't step around a divide by zero without using one of the dangerous commands that arbitrarily changes the instruction pointer  A regular step from a SIGFPE will abort the process.
622864165.zh: 如果不使用任意更改指令指针的危险命令之一，则无法绕过除以零的步骤SIGFPE的常规步骤将中止该过程。

622864335.en:
@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622863718):

Would presenting a program for which that is false be sufficient to provide a counterexample? Because there are any number of ways that having a debugger attached can change the behavior of a program and cause it to misbehave.

622865398.en: Sorry, let me say that a different way. I'm not trying to refute that many or potentially even most programmers think that. Would a counterexample be sufficient to demonstrate "those programmers think incorrectly"?
622865398.zh: 对不起，让我用另一种方式说。我不想反驳许多甚至可能是大多数程序员这样认为。反例是否足以证明“那些程序员思维不正确” ？

622865504.en: I don’t think I need that demonstration.
622865504.zh: 我觉得我不需要那个演示。

622865741.en: I would certainly agree with "most programmers will find it *surprising* that a debugger can affect the operation of their program when not explicitly trying to tamper with it".
622865741.zh: 我当然同意“大多数程序员会发现调试器在没有显式尝试篡改程序时会影响其程序的运行*令人惊讶*”。

622865762.en:
All that said, it occurs to me that there are two different use cases for debuggers that may influence what one assumes about their operation:

1. "My program is behaving incorrectly in a way I do not understand. I need a debugger to slow it down and let me look at the individual states."
2. "My program is crashing, and I need to analyze the crash state better than a single backtrace (or nothing)."
622865762.zh:
尽管如此，在我看来，调试器有两种不同的用例，可能会影响人们对其操作的假设：

1. “我的计划行为不正确，我无法理解。 我需要一个调试器来减慢速度，让我看看各个状态。”
2. “我的程序正在崩溃，我需要比单个回溯（或无）更好地分析崩溃状态。”

622866009.en: And in case 2, continuing is empirically unsafe (it will rarely do anything useful), but in case 1, it is not usually empirically unsafe (the program will keep doing its thing).
622866009.zh: 在案例2中，继续在经验上是不安全的（它很少做任何有用的事情） ，但在案例1中，它通常不是经验上不安全的（程序将继续做它的事情）。

622866240.en: And I wonder if you are assuming work in case 2, while I and @**bjorn3** am assuming work in case 1.
622866240.zh: 我想知道你是否在案例2中假设工作，而我和@ * * bjorn3 * *在案例1中假设工作。

622866504.en: I am not assuming that, no. I've certainly used a debugger for both. I'm suggesting that even in case 1, "Program received signal SIGTRAP, Trace/breakpoint trap" is not a message to which `c` is a universally safe answer.
622866504.zh: 我不这么认为。两者我都用过调试器。我建议即使在1的情况下， “程序收到信号SIGTRAP ，跟踪/断点陷阱”也不是`c`这是一个普遍安全的答案。

622866668.en: Note, in particular, that debuggers will typically loudly distinguish between a breakpoint *they set themselves* and a breakpoint instruction.
622866668.zh: 特别要注意的是，调试器通常会大声区分*他们自己设置的*断点和断点指令。

622867032.en:

If we write it correctly, I would be *surprised* if the word `breakpoint` shows up in the debugger, other than in any Rust-source-level view of the programmer's code calling it. The instruction will be inlined, so the backtrace should show `in function_that_called_it ()` not `in breakpoint ()`.

622868239.en: I now think that: regardless of the "theoretical purity" of `yeet1`, in practice, publishing it under the name `breakpoint` will result in people who do not understand it misusing it (counting debugger interactions as "uses"), which can be avoided by giving it a less straightforward name or by not having it.

@_**Kevin Reid (kpreid)|608145** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622868239):
```quote
I now think that: regardless of the "theoretical purity" of `yeet1`, in practice, publishing it under the name `breakpoint` will result in people who do not understand it misusing it (counting debugger interactions as "uses"), which can be avoided by giving it a less straightforward name or by not having it.
```

Without necessarily agreeing with that, just trying to get an idea of the mental model you have for it: would you say the same about the name `core::arch::breakpoint_instruction`? (That's not an ideal name, not least of which because it assumes the underlying implementation *is* a single instruction, but it's mean to be evocative of "self-documenting name".)
622869107.zh:
@_* * Kevin Reid (kpreid) | 608145 * * [说] (https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622868239):
```quote
I now think that: regardless of the "theoretical purity" of `yeet1`, in practice, publishing it under the name `breakpoint` will result in people who do not understand it misusing it (counting debugger interactions as "uses"), which can be avoided by giving it a less straightforward name or by not having it.
```不一定同意，只是想了解你对此的心智模型：你会对名字说同样的话吗`core::arch::breakpoint_instruction`? （这不是一个理想的名称，尤其是因为它假设底层实现*是*单个指令，但它的意思是让人联想到“自文档化名称”。）

622869574.en: That’d be "scarier", and perhaps sufficiently so, but I am guessing that a lot of people have a mental model in which part of the meaning of "breakpoint" *is that it is resumable*. So I think that the actual word "breakpoint" is a bad choice here, insofar as you want something that specifically implies potential non-resumability.

622870213.en: There's only so much a name can do, compared to a doc comment.

622870822.en: Rust’s audience is not, solely, people who already know what to be scared of.

622871086.en: I very much appreciate and agree with that. But I'm also suggesting that a name doesn't have to supersede a doc comment.

622871118.en: I am theorizing that *using the word “breakpoint”* in the name of `yeet1` is too misleading for the broader audience.
622871118.zh: 我的理论是， *在名称中使用“断点”一词*`yeet1`对更广泛的受众来说太误导了。

622871597.en: I’m *less* worried if it’s spelled with the scarier-overall name `core::arch::breakpoint_instruction`, but also, I feel like this is a footgun we don’t need to manufacture when we can just have `yeet2`.
622871597.zh: 我*不太*担心它是否用更可怕的整体名称拼写`core::arch::breakpoint_instruction`，但我觉得这是一支我们不需要制造的脚枪，当我们可以`yeet2`。

622871844.en: ...I feel like that's going to send us back into the loop in which we are arguing about what semantics people *should* want vs *do* want.
622871844.zh: ...我觉得这会让我们回到循环中，在这个循环中，我们正在争论人们*应该*想要什么语义与*做*想要什么语义。

622871996.en: We "can just" have a lot of things, but this thread would not be nearly as long as it is if we agreed that that was all we needed.
622871996.zh: 我们“可以”有很多东西，但如果我们同意这就是我们所需要的，这个线程就不会那么长了。

622872188.en: I'm not trying to prolong it or go around in circles, here, but it's *not helpful* to keep saying "you should be happy with just yeet2 and shouldn't get to have the operation you actually said you want".
622872188.zh: 在这里，我不是想延长它或绕圈子，但一直说“你应该对yeet2感到满意，不应该得到你实际上说你想要的操作”是“没有帮助的”。

622872623.en: I am weighing "people will blithely hit `c` in a debugger and be *upset* when their debugger then reports the UB they just continued into" versus "provide an operation that does what the underlying breakpoint instruction does and what many people who know exactly what instruction they're expecting it to map to will expect", and not immediately going "oh, the former is obviously more important".
622872623.zh: 我在称重“人们会轻松地打`c`在调试器中，当他们的调试器报告UB时，他们会感到*不安* ，他们只是继续进入“与”提供一个操作，该操作执行底层断点指令的操作，以及许多人确切地知道他们希望它映射到什么指令将期望“，而不是立即开始”哦，前者显然更重要“。

622873685.en: All that said, if there's some straightforward and not especially annoying to deal with name that would solve this with a naming bikeshed, then that might end up being where we land. I'm not looking forward to the resulting hazard of talking to people who *do* know the underlying instruction and saying "here's how rust spells the breakpoint operation you're looking for", but it wouldn't be the only such case rust has. Assuming we can solve the problem that way.
622873685.zh: 尽管如此，如果有一些简单而又不特别烦人的名字可以通过命名自行车来解决这个问题，那么这可能最终会成为我们的目标。我不期待与*确实*知道基本指令的人交谈并说“这是Rust如何拼写您正在寻找的断点操作”所带来的危险，但这并不是Rust唯一的此类情况。假设我们可以用这种方式解决问题。

622874211.en: I don’t entirely follow. Aren't *both* `yeet1` and `yeet2` equivalent to “the underlying instruction”? Isn’t the only difference in what we say what the expectations for using it are?
622874211.zh: 我并不完全遵循。不是*两者兼而有之*`yeet1`和`yeet2`等同于“底层指令” ？我们所说的使用它的期望不是唯一的区别吗？

622874605.en: For one non-trivial cohort of users, `yeet2`, as far as I can tell, is "the breakpoint instruction but people will tell you you're using it wrong if you use it in the way you expect to use the breakpoint instruction". They would expect to respond to someone saying "I hit UB by resuming after your breakpoint" with "don't do that, closed, not a soundness issue".

623196085.en:
More specifically, I want it to be possible to support
* alignment niches in references (`&u16`'s address can't be odd, so odd values are valid niches)
* computing maximum slice length in layout (`&[u16]`'s length can't be more than `isize::MAX / 2`, as otherwise the slice would span more than half the address space) (currently this is done as a hack in cg_llvm)

*参考文献中的对齐位置（`&u16`的地址不能是奇数，因此奇数值是有效的壁龛）
*计算布局中的最大切片长度（`&[u16]`的长度不能超过`isize::MAX / 2`，否则切片将跨越超过一半的地址空间） （目前这是作为cg_llvm中的黑客完成的）

623248283.en:
A "fun" case for handling slice ranges is something like:
```rust
struct Meow {
    val: [&'static Meow],
}
```

To determine the metadata range for `&Meow`, you need to know the layout of `val` to get the size of its elements, which itself depends on the layout of `&Meow` again.  In theory it might be possible to split out a lot of the different "ways" in which things can depend on layout, like pointer types really only care about whether a type is sized or not, not the "full layout", but I'm unsure if that helps.

623259635.en:
There is a similar case for alignment niches:
```
struct Meow {
    val: &'static Meow,
}
```
layout of `Meow` depends on layout of `&Meow`, which (for alignment niches) needs to know layout of `Meow` again. you could *maybe* resolve this by noticing that niches in `&Meow` only depend on alignment of `Meow`, which itself is unaffected by niches, but decoupling different layout properties could lead to inconsistencies between the computations, which is scary.

````quote
```Rust
struct Meow {
    val: [&'static Meow],
}
```

To determine the metadata range for `&Meow`, you need to know the layout of `val` to get the size of its elements, which itself depends on the layout of `&Meow` again. In theory it might be possible to split out a lot of the different "ways" in which things can depend on layout, like pointer types really only care about whether a type is sized or not, not the "full layout", but I'm unsure if that helps.
````

An even "funnier" case is something like this:

```rust
#[repr(packed)] // i.e. disable alignment niches, they are not relevant
struct Meow {
    val: [Option<Option<&'static Meow>>],
}
```

To know the valid range slice metadata (length) for `&Meow` you need to know size of `Option<Option<&'static Meow>>`, which in turn requires knowing the niche amount of `&Meow`... which depends on the valid range of the slice metadata (completing the cycle).

> Another "dumb" idea I had is to just check if a cycle *could* occur. I.e. when wanting to add niches to `&Meow`, check if `Meow` contains a reference to itself (in a field, or recursively in a field's field, etc).

We try to compute layouts for generics and on TooGeneric fallback to computing it at mono-time. Checking whether something could be a cycle would give different answers. And if you start conservatively emitting TooGeneric then you get a perf penalty for having to compute it more often.

623163741.en:
@_**Zoxc|116466** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/131828-t-compiler/topic/rustc-codegen-utc/near/623155964):
```quote
Looks like a poor strategy by Microsoft over improving the wastly superior LLVM and its Rust backend. Lots of wasted effort there.
```

I can't speak for Victor, but my understanding is it's best if the compiled semantics of interoperating languages are identical, particularly when link-time optimisation, sanitisers, debuggers, and similar semantics-reliant functionality is used. (Strictly, the semantics need to be compatible, but "identical" is much easier to reason about.)

Trying to make LLVM and gcc's semantics match is an ongoing project, that's already very hard. So the typical advice has been to compile both languages with the same backend.

This seems like a similar situation, where having matching backends improves the safety and reduces miscompilations for all languages involved.

```我不能代表Victor ，但我的理解是，互操作语言的编译语义最好是相同的，特别是在使用链接时间优化、免疫处理器、调试器和类似的语义依赖功能时。 （严格地说，语义需要兼容，但“相同”更容易推理。）

试图使LLVM和gcc的语义匹配是一个正在进行的项目，这已经非常困难。因此，典型的建议是使用相同的后端编译两种语言。

这似乎是一种类似的情况，具有匹配的后端可以提高安全性并减少所有相关语言的错误编译。

623527723.en:
@_**Max|960514** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Is.20it.20conceptually.20possible.20to.20.22restore.22.20an.20.26own.20reference.3F/near/623159279):
```quote
if `person` is declared as `mut` and you reassign with `person.name = *rejected`.
```

I think it would have to be `person.name = { *rejected };` to ensure there is a temporary, so the original borrow can end in the meantime:

 * I would imagine `place = *own_ref;` trying to do a `copy_nonoverlapping()` from `*own_ref` to `place`, hence the mentioned potential borrow-check error about `own_ref` being borrowed while we access the `place`.
 * Whereas when doing `{ *own_ref }`, it's moved into a temporary, so the borrow on `own_ref` can then end, and only then does it write the temporary (`copy_nonoverlapping`) into `place`, which can be borrowed/accessed without problems.
623527723.zh:
@_* * Max | 960514 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/122651-general/topic/Is.20it.20conceptually.20possible.20to.20.22restore.22.20an.20.26own.20reference.3F/near/623159279):
```quote
if `person` is declared as `mut` and you reassign with `person.name = *rejected`.
```我认为这必须是`person.name = { *rejected };`以确保有一个临时的，所以原来的借款可以在此期间结束：

 *我会想象`place = *own_ref;`尝试做一个`copy_nonoverlapping()` 从 `*own_ref` 到 `place`，因此上述潜在的借款检查错误`own_ref`在我们访问时被借用`place`.
 *而在进行`{ *own_ref }`，它被移动到一个临时的，所以借款`own_ref`然后可以结束，只有这样它才会写入临时（`copy_nonoverlapping`步进`place`，可以毫无问题地借用/访问。

623680947.en:
> The previous attempt by @**Moulins|321122** took a different route: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/113166

Hi, I was mentioned, so I'll ramble a bit about my previous attempt :D

Under-approximating the size and aligment of types behind references (for niching purposes) is IMHO unavoidable, as it isn't at all clear that the layout algorithm can be given a sensible definition in terms of a fixpoint (e.g. see [this comment](https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3204#issuecomment-991830689) on the old reference niches RFC for a case where there are two equally "best" layouts, in addition to all the other examples in this thread).

As such, I believe the "two-phase" approach of my old PR is still the correct one:
1. compute a "naive layout": an underestimate of the size and alignment obtained by running a simplified version of the layout logic;
2. when computing the full layout of a reference (`&Foo, &[Foo]`, etc), use the naive layout of `Foo` to add the corresponding niches.

Much of the implementation complexity came from the few places in the compiler that expect to be able to compute correct(-ish) layouts for generic types (IIRC, the transmute size check and the `improper_ctypes` lint). These force the naive layout query to compute exact sizes and alignments for a large class of types, which both means tracking more information and making the naive layout / full layout refinement more brittle (in fact, if you look at my old PR commit-by-commit, you can see the `NaiveLayout` type gradually getting more and more complex ^^)

If we could remove the need for exact naive layouts and always deal with underestimates, I think most of the "how to keep it in sync" concerns would be addressed, as underestimating the size/align is *really easy*.
623680947.zh:
> @ * * Moulins | 321122 * *之前的尝试采用了不同的路线：https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/113166嗨，有人提到我，所以我会详细介绍一下我之前的尝试: D

IMHO不可避免地会低估引用背后类型的大小和校准（出于细分目的） ，因为布局算法是否可以根据固定点给出合理的定义（例如，请参阅[this comment] （https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/3204#issuecomment-991830689)除了此线程中的所有其他示例之外，还有两个同等“最佳”布局的情况下的旧参考小生境RFC ）。

因此，我认为我的旧公关的“两阶段”方法仍然是正确的：
1.计算“朴素布局” ：低估通过运行简化版布局逻辑获得的大小和对齐；
2.计算参考文献的完整布局时（`&Foo, &[Foo]`等） ，使用朴素的布局`Foo`以添加相应的壁龛。

大部分实现复杂性来自编译器中少数几个地方，这些地方希望能够计算泛型类型的正确（ -ish ）布局（ IIRC ，转换大小检查和`improper_ctypes`lint ）。这些强制朴素布局查询计算大类类型的确切大小和对齐方式，这都意味着跟踪更多信息并使朴素布局/完整布局细化更加脆弱（实际上，如果您查看我的旧PR提交，您可以看到`NaiveLayout`类型逐渐变得越来越复杂^ ^)

如果我们可以消除对精确天真布局的需求，并始终处理低估问题，我认为大多数“如何保持同步”的问题都会得到解决，因为低估尺寸/对齐方式“真的很容易”。

623165637.en:
> This seems like a similar situation, where having matching backends improves the safety and reduces miscompilations for all languages involved.

Unless both backends differ in how exactly a given ABI should be encoded, then the fact that rustc is tailored to the way LLVM expect it to be encoded increases the risk of other backends encoding the ABI wrong and getting ABI mismatches. Interaction between object files compiled by different compilers using different backends that are common on a given platform (which happens all the time) is better tested than replacing backends within a single compiler (which is less common). Already for cg_gcc I believe there are some fundamental mismatches between what LLVM and libgccjit expect. LLVM expects half the ABI to be implemented in the frontend, while I believe libgccjit expects it entirely in the backend, with the frontend only lowering to C like types.
623165637.zh:
>这似乎是一种类似的情况，具有匹配的后端可以提高安全性并减少所有相关语言的错误编译。

除非两个后端在给定ABI的编码方式上有所不同，否则rustc是根据LLVM预期的编码方式进行定制的，这增加了其他后端编码ABI错误并获得ABI不匹配的风险。不同编译器使用给定平台上常见的不同后端（始终发生）编译的对象文件之间的交互比在单个编译器中替换后端（不太常见）更好。对于cg_gcc来说，我认为LLVM和libgccjit之间存在一些根本性的不匹配。LLVM预计一半的ABI将在前端实现，而我相信libgccjit预计它完全在后端实现，前端仅降低到类似C的类型。

623166446.en: I still read this as a decision by Microsoft to not invest into improving rustc_codegen_llvm which is the *primary* rustc backend. Also there's no need for cross-language optimizations, if you want performance you use LLVM, never MSVC.
623166446.zh: 我仍然认为这是微软不投资改善rustc_codegen_llvm的决定， rustc_codegen_llvm是*主要*的rustc后端。此外，无需跨语言优化，如果您想要性能，请使用LLVM ，而不是MSVC。

623167719.en: @**bjorn3** Unless you want LTO (they talk about cross-language inlining).

623168547.en: If you want LTO, then yes you need matching backends. LTO is unrelated to ABI mismatches, other than that LTO increases the amount of ABI mismatches if the frontend doesn't match. Using different backends would actually fix those ABI mismatches by blocking inlining across the ABI boundary.
623168547.zh: 如果您想要LTO ，那么是的，您需要匹配的后端。LTO与ABI不匹配无关，但如果前端不匹配， LTO会增加ABI不匹配的数量。使用不同的后端实际上可以通过阻止跨ABI边界的内联来修复这些ABI不匹配。

There are more general stories to be told, but one thing that's very fresh in my mind has to do with -Zdylib-lto in bootstrap and I think it could be of interest to you. Turns out the way bootstrap performs the LTO of rustc_driver.so is directly via RUSTFLAGS (-Zdylib-lto -Clto -Cembed-bitcode) so the usual cargo mechanism of passing -Clinker-plugin-lto to dependencies of an LTO'd crate doesn't fire (plus cargo would reject that anyway because it doesn't really know that LTO can technically be valid for dylib). As a result even when bootstrapping with LTO the dependencies of rustc_driver end up generating native code, which is then unused because of the whole LTO thing. I added a somewhat hacky workaround on our side that sped up our CI, but this is something that could be relevant to rust-lang/rust assuming my analysis is correct (please correct me if it isn't :) ).

623249158.en:
Regarding the compiler_builtins it's mostly just that the reason for why c-b is excluded from LTO for LLVM doesn't directly apply to UTC. In the end we just added a patch that adds a CodegenBackend fn letting the backend opt into including compiler_builtins in LTO as Aleksey said.
However, while tinkering with that I also encountered an amusing issue (which wouldn't have been a blocker on its own, but still): c-b calls ilog2 from two places, in both of these cases the argument is provably positive, though not necessarily constant. The ilog2 function itself calls the cold panic_for_nonpositive_argument when its argument is non-positive. LLVM is able to inline ilog2, prove that this never happens and eliminates those calls. Our backend managed to do that too, but for some technical reasons the symbol table entry for the panic function was not removed from compiler_builtins.o.
By default c-b doesn't participate in LTO, only in the final link, so if nothing else in the rest of the compile tree roots panic_for_nonpositive_argument then the symbol gets eliminated during LTO. When c-b then gets linked to the result of LTO we get an unknown symbol. IIRC I was able to reproduce this even for LLVM under artifical conditions (LTO + low opt level or something like that).
623249158.zh:
关于compiler_builtins ，大多数情况下， c-b被排除在LLVM的LTO之外的原因并不直接适用于UTC。 最后，我们刚刚添加了一个补丁，添加了一个CodegenBackend fn ，让后端选择在LTO中包含compiler_builtins ，正如Aleksey所说。然而，在修补时，我也遇到了一个有趣的问题（这本身并不是一个障碍，但仍然） ： c-b从两个地方调用ilog2 ，在这两种情况下，论证都是可以证明的积极的，尽管不一定是恒定的。ilog2函数本身在其参数为非正数时调用冷panic_for_nonpositive_参数。LLVM能够内联ilog2 ，证明这种情况永远不会发生，并消除这些呼叫。我们的后端也设法做到了这一点，但由于一些技术原因， panic函数的符号表条目没有从compiler_builtins.o中删除。
默认情况下， c-b不参与LTO ，仅参与最终链接，因此，如果编译树的其余部分中没有其他内容根panic_for_nonpositive_argument ，则符号在LTO期间被消除。 当c-b然后链接到LTO的结果时，我们得到一个未知的符号。IIRC I甚至能够在人工条件下（ LTO +低OPT水平或类似条件）为LLVM复制此功能。

623616683.en:
When discussing the ACP for [`normalize_lexically`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.normalize_lexically), libs-api were very keen for it to limit any `..` to the root of the path, erroring if they would go above.

However, users have raised the concern that this couples two different things: normalization and defence against path traversal attacks. While those can be connected, there are also reasons to want to handle these separately. It has been suggested that `normalize_lexically` should do the one normalization job and security should be handled by other methods (e.g. maybe the `Dir` type can help here). This would also be more composable.

See also the long discussion in #134694.
623616683.zh:
在讨论ACP时[`normalize_lexically`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html#method.normalize_lexically),libs-api非常热衷于限制任何`..`到路径的根目录，如果它们位于上面，则会出错。

然而，用户担心这会带来两种不同的情况：正常化和防御路径遍历攻击。 虽然这些可以连接，但也有理由希望单独处理这些问题。 有人建议`normalize_lexically`应该做一个规范化工作，安全应该通过其他方法来处理（例如，`Dir`类型可以在这里提供帮助）。 这也会更具可组合性。

另请参阅# 134694中的长篇讨论。

623641643.en: Absolutely, just pointing out there is a tradeoff

623648521.en:
A thing I want to avoid is making a "turing tarpit" where it meets every possible need, but is not ergonomic for any of them.

With an enum suggestion we need to pin down boundries for when to make a new varient or not. Normalizing empty path could be it's own case. Windows paths that start with `\\?\` then the path is theorietically already normalized because `..` and `.` resolve literally, so that could be it's own case. (or would we want the lib to remove the `..` in that scenario?) I think if you asked everyone on that thread you would get a LOT of different answers.
623648521.zh:
我想避免的一件事是制作一个“图灵沥青” ，它可以满足所有可能的需求，但不符合任何需求的人体工程学。

对于枚举建议，我们需要确定何时创建新变量的边界。 规范化空路径可能是它自己的情况。 开头为的Windows路径`\\?\`那么路径在理论上已经归一化了，因为`..`和`.`从字面上解决，所以这可能是它自己的情况。（或者我们是否希望lib删除`..`在这种情况下？ ）我认为，如果你在那个帖子上问每个人，你会得到很多不同的答案。

623651771.en: I think if we do go the enum route we should keep it simple as possible so no more than two variants. Or else make it an opaque struct and force people to use methods (though I don't think that's ideal).
623651771.zh: 我认为，如果我们确实走枚举路线，我们应该尽可能保持简单，所以不超过两个变体。或者让它成为一个不透明的结构，迫使人们使用方法（尽管我认为这并不理想）。

623652050.en: But I do want to keep the idea of fully decoupling security from normalization on the table until it's definitely ruled out. So we could have a method that just normalizes and always returns a PathBuf.
623652050.zh: 但我确实希望将安全与正常化完全脱钩的想法保留在桌面上，直到明确排除为止。因此，我们可以有一个方法，该方法只是规范化并始终返回PathBuf。

623767600.en: Hi! I would like to figure out the broader direction first but for specifics I do think think we should resolve paths like `C:foo` and `/foo` (this doesn't require accessing the filesystem). The reason is the defy normal classification as they're not technically absolute paths but neither are they relative to the current directory. We could also simplify `\\?\` (aka verbatim) paths.
623767600.zh: 嗨！我想先弄清楚更广泛的方向，但具体而言，我认为我们应该解决`C:foo`和`/foo`（这不需要访问文件系统）。原因是违背正常分类，因为它们在技术上不是绝对路径，但也不是相对于当前目录的路径。我们还可以简化`\\?\`（又名逐字记录）路径。

623796509.en: Paths are such a weirdly deep topic that seems superficially easy.
623796509.zh: 路径是一个如此奇怪的深刻话题，表面上看起来很容易。

623796865.en: Another alternative to erroring when we escape root of a relative path could be to detect that and make it absolute. Then we would have the same signature as std::fs::absolute. If you pass in an absolute path it would be guaranteed to not hit disk (if we pin to root)
623796865.zh: 当我们逸出相对路径的根时，另一种错误可能是检测并使其成为绝对的。然后，我们将具有与std:: fs:: absolute相同的签名。如果您传入绝对路径，则保证不会击中磁盘（如果我们固定到根）

622875072.en: The same way you're feeling like "we shouldn't call yeet1 `breakpoint`", given the potential implications of yeet2, my reaction is "if we provide yeet2, give it a name that makes sure nobody is inclined to use it who *doesn't* want the guaranteed resumability, lest they get blamed for a soundness issue or end up with unexpected interpretation by miri/CTFE".
622875072.zh: 就像你说的“我们不应该叫yeet1`breakpoint`“，考虑到yeet2的潜在影响，我的反应是“如果我们提供yeet2 ，给它一个名字，确保没有人倾向于使用它，谁不想要保证可恢复性，以免他们因健全性问题而受到指责，或者最终被miri/CTFE意外解释”。

622875125.en: And for I suspect an even larger cohort of users, yeet1 would break their expectations. For the cohort that wants yeet1, they can use a resumable trap instead. That is safer than a breakpoint instruction as you can't accidentally resume it. You need to modify the instruction pointer (possibly with a custom debugger command for convenience)
622875125.zh: 我怀疑有更多的用户， yeet1会打破他们的期望。对于想要yeet1的队列，他们可以使用可恢复的陷阱。这比断点指令更安全，因为你不能不小心恢复它。您需要修改指令指针（可能为方便起见使用自定义调试器命令）

622875332.zh: "我写了断点()。为什么它不等同于`break foo.rs:123`在我的调试器中？ ”

622875402.en: `c` is the convenient unsafe debugging command they were expecting to be able to use.

622875598.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622875332):
```quote
"I wrote breakpoint(). Why is that not equivalent to `break foo.rs:123` in my debugger?"
```

"It absolutely is equivalent, other than that your debugger doesn't know about it. Much like any breakpoint you might have set, continuing after it might result in the results of continuing after it, which may not be the results you want."

622876127.en: Can we back up a couple of steps, and try to *not* run headlong into each other with axioms about what some of the users *we* typically work with will expect?
622876127.zh: 我们是否可以备份几个步骤，并尝试*不要*用关于*我们*通常与之合作的一些用户所期望的公理来直截了当地互相碰撞？

622877012.en:
> Much like any breakpoint you might have set, continuing after it might result in the results of continuing after it, which may not be the results you want.

Do you agree that if your program produces UB when you resume after a breakpoint you set in your debugger, that your program is unsound?
622877012.zh:
>就像您可能设置的任何断点一样，在它之后继续可能会导致在它之后继续的结果，这可能不是您想要的结果。

您是否同意，如果您的程序在调试器中设置的断点后恢复时生成UB ，则表示您的程序不健全？

622877728.en: That is *usually* true. There are exceptions to that, which have less to do with breakpoints and more to do with running under a debugger, which can sometimes change behavior in ways other than just timing. But *usually*, yes, if your program ships without a breakpoint in it, and you set one, and then continue from it, your program's behavior will typically be the same as it would have been without your having set the breakpoint. So if that behavior is UB, in most circumstances that means it would have been UB without the debugger present at all.
622877728.zh: 这*通常*是真的。有些例外情况与断点无关，而与在调试器下运行有关，这有时会以计时以外的方式改变行为。但是*通常* ，是的，如果您的程序在发布时没有断点，并且您设置了一个断点，然后从中继续，那么您的程序的行为通常将与您没有设置断点时的行为相同。因此，如果这种行为是UB ，在大多数情况下，这意味着如果没有调试器，它就会是UB。

622877764.en:
> continuing after it might result in the results of continuing after it”

Hm. This description suggests a semantic (not machine-level!) equivalence to `if !ask_the_user("continue?”) { abort() }`. In this frame, we're arguing about *what question we’re asking the debugger-operating user* — is it “do you want to ignore bugs and continue hazardously?” or “do you want to (not) pause execution here?”
622877764.zh:
>在它之后继续可能会导致在它之后继续的结果”

嗯。这个描述表明语义（不是机器级！ ）等价于`if !ask_the_user("continue?”) { abort() }`。在这个框架中，我们争论的是*我们问调试器操作用户什么问题* —是“你想忽略错误并危险地继续吗？”还是“你想（不）在这里暂停执行吗？”

622878148.en: I wouldn't agree with that framing. I can see what you mean by it, but my argument is that a breakpoint isn't a *question to a user*, it's just a stopping point for a debugger, and the (person running the) debugger is then *taking an action* that is not the response to a question.
622878148.zh: 我不同意这种说法。我可以理解你的意思，但我的论点是，断点不是*对用户的问题* ，它只是调试器的停止点，然后（运行调试器的人）会*采取一个行动* ，而不是对问题的响应。

622878755.en: The framing I'd use is "if the overall system here has UB, and we imagine a world in which the whole system uses a Rust-like framing where UB implies a misused unsafe operation somewhere, is the code after the breakpoint unsafe and not marked as such (making it unsound), or is the debugger unsafe?".
622878755.zh: 我使用的框架是“如果整个系统有UB ，并且我们想象整个系统使用类似Rust的框架，其中UB暗示在某个地方滥用了不安全的操作，断点后的代码不安全且未标记为不安全（使其不健全） ，或者调试器不安全？”。

622878937.en: If you have a program running in a debugger, is detaching from this program safe? (just plain `detach` in gdb)
622878937.zh: 如果您有在调试器中运行的程序，从此程序中分离是否安全？ （只是普通的`detach`以gdb为单位）

622878950.en: yeet2 is claiming "the code after the breakpoint is (potentially) unsafe". yeet1 is claiming "the debugger is (potentially) unsafe".
622878950.zh: yeet2声称“断点后的代码（可能）不安全”。yeet1声称“调试器（可能）不安全”。

622879405.en:
The debugger *as a whole* is certainly unsafe; how do you feel about the following narrowed question?
"What are the safety preconditions for the 'continue' button?"
622879405.zh:
调试器*作为一个整体*肯定是不安全的；您对以下缩小的问题有什么看法？
“'继续'按钮的安全先决条件是什么？”

622879718.en: That is, what things is the user obligated to think about before pushing the continue button, supposing they want to avoid UB too?
622879718.zh: 也就是说，用户在按下“继续”按钮之前有义务考虑什么，假设他们也想避开UB ？

622880091.en:
Sure, that's close to equivalent; it's essentially narrowing the unsafety from the whole debugger to individual debugger operations (the handwaving analogy here ignoring the notion of intermediate states between those operations, for the moment).

Though in practice "obligated to think about" may be "obligated to be willing to keep all the pieces if it breaks because they didn't think about", which is often something people are willing to do if they're already in a debugger. ;)
622880091.zh: 当然，这几乎是等效的；它本质上将不安全因素从整个调试器缩小到单个调试器操作（目前，这里的手工类比忽略了这些操作之间的中间状态的概念）。虽然在实践中， “有义务思考”可能“有义务在碎片坏掉时愿意保留所有碎片，因为他们没有思考” ，这通常是人们愿意做的事情，如果他们已经在调试器中。

622880288.en: *most* of the time I do tend to assume "I'm already in a debugger, *mostly* the worst I'm worried about is a crash".
622880288.zh: *大多数时候*我倾向于假设“我已经在调试器中， *大部分*我最担心的是崩溃”。

622881261.en:
@_**bjorn3|133247** [said](https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622878937):
```quote
If you have a program running in a debugger, is detaching from this program safe? (just plain `detach` in gdb)
```

Would have to think about that for a while, for at least three reasons, though I'm not sure if any of them is relevant to why you're asking.
- If you've modified the state of the program, you're taking responsibility for the state you left it in.
- If detaching would cause something to resume running, you have the same safety obligation as doing that resumption.
- As noted before, having a debugger attached *at all* can affect the operation of a program, even if that program isn't actively trying to detect a debugger.
622881261.zh:
@_* * bjorn3 | 133247 * * [说] （https://rust-lang.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/219381-t-libs/topic/Pushing.20.60breakpoint.60.20over.20the.20finish.20line.3F/near/622878937):
```quote
If you have a program running in a debugger, is detaching from this program safe? (just plain `detach` in gdb)
```必须考虑一段时间，至少有三个原因，尽管我不确定其中是否有任何原因与你问的原因有关。
-如果您修改了计划的状态，则需对您离开时的状态负责。
-如果分离会导致某些东西恢复运行，您有与恢复运行相同的安全义务。-如前所述， *完全*附加调试器可能会影响程序的操作，即使该程序没有主动尝试检测调试器。

622881354.en: I'm guessing you're asking because of the second one, there?
622881354.zh: 我猜你问是因为第二个，对吧？

622881545.en:
So in the “debugger safety precondition” frame:

* when debugging a program containing only `yeet1`s, the safety precondition is “unless this is a debugger-inserted breakpoint, you must treat any stopped condition as cautiously as abort/trap/halt/segfault/...”
* when debugging a program containing only `yeet2`s, the safety precondition is “unless this is a abort/trap/halt/segfault/..., you may continue.”
622881545.zh:
因此，在“调试器安全前提”框架中：

*调试仅包含以下内容的程序时`yeet1`安全前提条件是“除非这是调试器插入的断点，否则您必须像对待abort/trap/halt/segfault/...一样谨慎对待任何停止的条件”
*调试仅包含以下内容的程序时`yeet2`安全前提条件是“除非这是中止/陷阱/停止/分段故障/... ，否则您可以继续。”
